sources.title: IFC Grants Sustainability-Linked Loan To ENGIE Energía Perú To Support Renewable Energy Growth & Emission Reduction Goals

title: Atmos Renewables takes full ownership of 316 MW Hornsdale wind farm
summary: Atmos Renewables bought Neoen's majority interest in the 316 MW Hornsdale wind farm in South Australia, taking full ownership.
details: Atmos Renewables, which already held minority interests in all three stages of the 316 MW Hornsdale wind farm in South Australia, bought Neoen's majority interest to take full ownership. Settlement was expected in the second half of 2025.
context: Atmos says the deal takes its managed portfolio above 1 GW and makes it the only owner-operator with renewable assets in every Australian grid-connected state.

sources.title: Atmos Renewables fully acquires 316 MW Hornsdale Wind Farm

title: ACEN International signs US$100 million facility with MUFG
summary: ACEN International signed a US$100 million facility with MUFG to fund ACEN's renewable investments outside the Philippines.
details: ACEN International signed a US$100 million facility with MUFG Bank's Singapore branch to finance or refinance ACEN's renewable projects outside the Philippines, through subsidiaries and joint ventures, and for general purposes.
context: The Philippines is ACEN's largest market, but it has projects in several other countries in Asia-Pacific; the facility funds that international growth.

sources.title: ACEN unit inks $100m loan for renewable energy projects

title: Polsat Plus secures nearly PLN 953 million for 139 MW Drzeżewo wind farm
summary: Polsat Plus Group secured nearly PLN 953 million of loans for its 139 MW Drzeżewo wind farm in Poland, its largest.
details: Polsat Plus Group secured loans of up to PLN 952.9 million from Polish financial institutions, including a PLN term loan of up to PLN 874 million, to finance or refinance construction of its 139 MW Drzeżewo wind farm. All 63 turbines were installed and test power was flowing from 51 of them.
context: Drzeżewo is Polsat Plus's largest wind farm. Commercial operation was planned once commissioning of all turbines was complete.

sources.title: Polsat Plus Group receives investment loan for Poland wind farm

title: AIIB subscribes ₹1,301 crore of Aditya Birla Capital debentures for renewable lending
summary: The AIIB subscribed INR 13,012.5 million of non-convertible debentures issued by Aditya Birla Capital to expand renewable energy financing in India.
details: The AIIB subscribed INR 13,012.5 million of non-convertible debentures issued by Aditya Birla Capital, which will lend the money to solar, wind, hydrogen, storage and electric mobility projects in India.
context: Lending through a domestic finance company lets the AIIB reach many smaller clean energy borrowers it could not finance directly.

sources.title: AIIB Invests INR 13,012.5 Million in Aditya Birla Capital to Accelerate Renewable Energy Financing in India

title: Exus Renewables closes MUFG financing for 130 MW Cibele solar in Portugal
summary: Exus Renewables closed financing for the 130 MW Cibele solar farm in Alentejo, Portugal, with MUFG EMEA as sole lead arranger.
details: MUFG EMEA, as sole lead arranger, hedge provider, agent and account bank, financed Exus Renewables' 130 MW Cibele solar farm on about 300 hectares in Alentejo, Portugal. It should supply about 69,000 households.
context: It supports Exus's growth in Iberia and its aim to become a broader energy solutions provider. One bank taking every role simplifies the financing.

sources.title: Exus Renewables closes solar financing with MUFG EMEA

title: Citicore secures ₱4.4 billion from Security Bank for 125 MWp solar project
summary: Citicore Renewable Energy secured a ₱4.4 billion loan from Security Bank to complete a 125 MWp solar project.
details: Security Bank and Security Bank Capital Investment lent Citicore ₱4.4 billion to complete the 125 MWp Citicore Solar Pangasinan project in Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan.
context: It is one of the priority projects in Citicore's five-year plan. The company says project finance lets it build faster and manage risk.

sources.title: CREC secures PHP 4.4b financing for 125 MW solar project in PH

title: Energy Vault completes purchase of Stoney Creek battery in New South Wales
summary: Energy Vault completed its acquisition of the Stoney Creek battery project in northern New South Wales after Foreign Investment Review Board approval.
details: Energy Vault completed its purchase of the 125 MW / 1,000 MWh Stoney Creek battery project in northern New South Wales from Enervest after approval by the Foreign Investment Review Board. The deal was first announced in March 2025.
context: It joins Energy Vault's Own & Operate portfolio. At eight hours, it is a long-duration battery able to cover the whole evening peak.

sources.title: Energy Vault acquires Stoney Creek Battery Energy Storage System

title: PNE sells 34 MW Sundern-Allendorf wind farm to Encavis
summary: PNE sold the 34 MW Sundern-Allendorf wind farm under construction in the Sauerland to Encavis on a turnkey basis.
details: PNE sold the five-turbine, 34 MW Sundern-Allendorf wind farm in the Sauerland, under construction, to Encavis on a turnkey basis. It should supply about 22,800 households.
context: Turnkey sales let PNE finish construction before handing over a working farm, while Encavis gains a ready-built asset.

sources.title: PNE sells Sundern-Allendorf wind farm to Encavis

title: Qair closes loan for hybrid solar and battery project in Mauritius
summary: Qair closed a loan for a hybrid solar and battery project in Mauritius, where it has operated since 2008.
details: Qair closed a loan for one of its hybrid solar and battery projects in Mauritius, part of four hybrid projects totalling 60 MWac it won in 2023. Qair has operated in Mauritius since 2008 and runs a 10 MW wind farm at Plaine des Roches and 25.3 MW of solar.
context: The loan supports Qair's growth in the Indian Ocean; its later Stor'SUN financing covered the full hybrid programme.

sources.title: Qair secures financing for hybrid solar + storage project in Mauritius

title: Schroders Greencoat takes 50% of JERA Nex's 395 MW US solar portfolio
summary: Schroders Greencoat acquired a 50% stake in JERA Nex's 395 MW portfolio of US solar assets.
details: Schroders Greencoat bought 50% of JERA Nex's operating US solar portfolio: the 300 MW Oxbow farm in Louisiana, the state's largest, which supplies corporate buyers including eBay, and the 95 MW Happy Solar farm in Arkansas. Both are in the MISO market with long-term PPAs.
context: JERA Nex bought the portfolio from Lightsource bp in 2024 and is now sharing ownership to recycle capital.

sources.title: Schroders Greencoat Takes 50% Stake in JERA Nex’s 395 MW US Solar Portfolio

title: Hindustan Power signs PPA with UPPCL for 435 MWdc solar in Uttar Pradesh
summary: Hindustan Power signed a PPA with Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation for a 435 MWdc solar project in the state.
details: Hindustan Power signed a 25-year PPA with Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation for a 435 MWdc solar plant in Uttar Pradesh, won in a competitive auction in April 2025.
context: The project contributes to the state government's target of 22,000 MW of renewable capacity by 2026–27, and to jobs and energy security in the state.

sources.title: Hindustan Power Signs PPA with UPPCL for 435 MW DC Solar Project in Uttar Pradesh

title: Scatec reaches financial close on 142 MW Minas Gerais solar with BNB
summary: Scatec reached financial close on BRL 150 million of non-recourse debt from Banco do Nordeste do Brasil for a 142 MW solar plant in Minas Gerais, about 30% of the BRL 506 million cost.
details: Banco do Nordeste do Brasil is providing BRL 150 million (US$27 million) of non-recourse debt for Scatec's 142 MW Rio Urucuia solar plant under construction in Minas Gerais, about 30% of the BRL 506 million (US$91 million) cost. Operation is expected in the first half of 2026.
context: BNB's loan covers about 30% of the cost. Scatec says long-term financing strengthens its position in Brazil.

sources.title: Scatec secures long-term project financing for Brazil solar project

title: Pulse Clean Energy secures £220 million green loan for UK battery portfolio
summary: Pulse Clean Energy secured a £220 million green loan facility from banks including Santander, ABN AMRO and CIBC for its UK battery portfolio, with Watson Farley & Williams advising the lenders.
details: Santander, ABN AMRO, CIBC, NatWest, Investec and NORD/LB provided Pulse Clean Energy with a £220 million green loan for six new battery sites in the UK, including converting former diesel generation sites to batteries. Watson Farley & Williams advised the lenders.
context: Reusing old diesel sites gives batteries ready grid connections, and gives the sites a cleaner use.

sources.title: Watson Farley & Williams Advises Lenders On £220m Green Financing Deal For Pulse Clean Energy’s BESS Portfolio

title: JERA and bp complete JERA Nex bp offshore wind joint venture
summary: JERA and bp completed JERA Nex bp, a 50/50 offshore wind company with about 13 GW of net potential capacity, including about 1 GW operating and a 7.5 GW development pipeline.
details: JERA and bp completed JERA Nex bp, their 50:50 offshore wind company. Its portfolio has about 13 GW of net potential capacity: about 1 GW operating, a 7.5 GW development pipeline and 4.5 GW of secured leases.
context: The partners say it will focus first on disciplined development of its existing pipeline, combining bp's and JERA's offshore wind businesses.

sources.title: JERA and bp launch offshore wind joint venture

title: FRV Australia reaches financial close on 250 MW / 500 MWh Gnarwarre battery
summary: Fotowatio Renewable Ventures Australia reached financial close on the 250 MW / 500 MWh Gnarwarre battery in Victoria, funded under its portfolio financing facility.
details: FRV Australia reached financial close on the 250 MW / 500 MWh Gnarwarre battery in Victoria, funded under its portfolio facility from July 2024 by five lenders led by Westpac.
context: With Gnarwarre, FRV Australia's portfolio will reach about 1.4 GW. A portfolio facility lets it add projects under pre-agreed terms.

sources.title: FRV reaches financial close for 250 MW/500 MWh Aussie battery project

title: Fortistar and Epic Star Energy buy Hawaii renewable portfolio from HEI's Pacific Current
target: Pacific Current renewable energy portfolio in Hawaii
summary: Investment firm Fortistar and its portfolio company Epic Star Energy have bought a portfolio of renewable energy projects in Hawaii from Pacific Current, a subsidiary of Hawaiian Electric Industries. The deal closed on August 1, 2025. Price and total capacity were not disclosed.
details: The portfolio includes a utility-scale solar project on Kauai along with several other operating renewable projects, described as a mix of commercial and utility-scale assets. The projects sell their power under long-term contracts, meaning buyers have agreed in advance to purchase the output for many years. Epic Star will manage the portfolio going forward. No financial terms, capacity figures or advisers were named in the release.
context: Epic Star says it plans to use the acquired assets as a base for developing more renewable and battery storage projects in Hawaii, where state goals aim to move away from imported oil and fossil fuel power. HEI said it believes Epic Star is a suitable owner to keep the assets supplying clean power. Epic Star's team previously developed one of Oahu's largest solar and battery projects, now under construction.

sources.title: Fortistar and Epic Star Energy Acquire Renewable Energy Portfolio from HEI Subsidiary

title: BNDES approves about R$1 billion for Atlas Renewable Energy's Draco solar complex
summary: BNDES approved about R$1 billion (about US$179 million) for Atlas Renewable Energy's 11-plant Draco Solar Complex in Minas Gerais, which will supply data centres.
details: BNDES is lending about BRL 1 billion (about US$179 million) for Atlas's Draco Solar Complex in Minas Gerais: 11 solar plants with 505 MWac (579 MWdc), due to start operating in early 2026, plus associated grid works.
context: The complex will supply data centres and create about 2,100 construction jobs. Development bank loans from BNDES carry long tenors suited to solar plants.

sources.title: BNDES Approves BRL 1 Billion Financing for Atlas Renewable Energy’s 11 Solar Plants in Brazil, Powering Data Centers

title: Statkraft sells Enerfín Canada to Atlantica Sustainable Infrastructure
summary: Statkraft agreed to sell Enerfín Canada, its Canadian portfolio of operating wind farms, pipeline and team, to Atlantica Sustainable Infrastructure.
details: Statkraft agreed to sell Enerfín Canada, its operating wind farms, pipeline and team, to Atlantica Sustainable Infrastructure. Statkraft got the Canadian assets when it bought Enerfín in a deal signed in November 2023 and completed in May 2024.
context: Statkraft is refocusing on its priority markets; the Enerfín purchase made it a top-10 wind producer in Spain and Brazil.

sources.title: Statkraft Sells Canadian Renewables Portfolio to Atlantica Sustainable Infrastructure

title: BayWa r.e. sells 199 MW wind and solar cluster near Zaragoza to Encavis
summary: BayWa r.e. sold its 199 MW combined wind and solar cluster near Zaragoza, Spain, to Encavis.
details: BayWa r.e. sold its 199 MW cluster 40 km from Zaragoza to Encavis: three wind farms of about 142 MW co-located with two solar plants of 57 MWp, sharing grid infrastructure.
context: It is BayWa r.e.'s first combined wind and solar installation in Spain and its largest onshore wind development in Europe. Sharing a grid connection cuts costs.

sources.title: BayWa r.e. sells Spanish 199 MW wind and solar project to Encavis AG

title: Iberdrola España and Mercadona sign PPAs for more than 300 MW
summary: Iberdrola España and Mercadona signed new long-term PPAs for more than 300 MW of wind and solar capacity.
details: Iberdrola España signed new long-term PPAs with retailer Mercadona for more than 300 MW of wind and solar, supplying its logistics centres and supermarkets in Spain and Portugal.
context: Iberdrola already runs up to 3,500 EV chargers at 800 Mercadona stores; the PPAs extend a long partnership.

sources.title: Iberdrola España and Mercadona Expand Clean Energy Partnership with Over 300 MW in New PPAs

title: T&H Farms sells tax credits from 590 kW rooftop solar project on North Carolina poultry farm

sellers.name: T&H Farms
sellers.role: tax credit seller and project owner

target: Federal clean energy tax credits from T&H Farms 590 kW rooftop solar array
summary: T&H Farms, a family-owned poultry farm in Fairmont, North Carolina, sold the federal clean energy tax credits generated by a 590 kW rooftop solar system on its poultry houses to an unnamed corporate buyer. Concentro arranged the sale. The deal value was not disclosed.
details: The solar array sits on the roofs of the farm's poultry houses and was developed by RED Renewables. The credits were sold through transferability, a rule that lets project owners sell their federal tax credits for cash to companies that owe taxes. Concentro found the buyer and handled due diligence and legal work. The project also received a grant from the USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) and financing from Rabo AgriFinance.
context: The farm says the system will help offset rising energy costs. Concentro claims that REAP grants can cover up to half of project costs and tax credits another 30 to 40 percent, letting farms adopt solar with little upfront investment. The deal shows how small distributed solar projects are using tax credit sales to fund themselves.

sources.title: T&H Farms Sells Tax Credits from Solar Agrivoltaics Project

title: AfDB approves US$144.27 million loan to Niger for energy sector and solar
summary: The African Development Bank approved a US$144.27 million loan for the first phase of Niger's energy sector programme, including more solar capacity.
details: The AfDB approved US$144.27 million for the first phase of Niger's Energy Sector Governance and Competitiveness Support Program. It aims to raise electricity access from 22.5% to 30% by 2026, with plans to install 240 MW of solar among other measures.
context: Programme loans like this fund reforms and investment together, aiming to tackle Niger's power shortages and improve the sector's finances.

sources.title: Niger Secures $144 Million AfDB Loan to Boost Solar Capacity and Raise Electricity Access by 2026

title: IFC invests about US$45 million debt in CleanMax Thailand
summary: The IFC made a THB 1,476 million (about US$45 million) debt investment in CleanMax Thailand to expand industrial solar.
details: The IFC made a THB 1,476 million (about US$45 million) debt investment in CleanMax Energy (Thailand), a subsidiary of India's CleanMax, to build 35 MWp of new solar and refinance 41 MWp of operating plants.
context: It is the IFC's first debt investment in a Thai developer focused only on commercial and industrial solar.

sources.title: IFC Invests $45 Million in CleanMax Thailand to Boost Industrial Solar Capacity

title: Qualitas Energy buys 100 MW greenfield wind portfolio in Lower Saxony
summary: Qualitas Energy acquired three mid-stage wind projects in Lower Saxony, Germany, with up to 100 MW planned.
details: Qualitas Energy bought three mid-stage wind projects in Lower Saxony with up to 100 MW planned across 14 turbines. Its team will continue developing them.
context: Buying projects in the planning phase gives Qualitas a pipeline in Germany, with development continuing under its own team.

sources.title: Qualitas Energy acquires 100 MW greenfield wind energy portfolio in Germany

title: Planted Solar raises $12 million in round led by Piva Capital
summary: Oakland-based Planted Solar, which makes hardware and software for building solar projects, raised $12 million in a funding round led by Piva Capital. Existing backers Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures and Team Builder Ventures also took part.
details: Planted Solar, founded in 2020, sells an integrated platform combining design software, dense ground-mounted arrays that follow the slope of the land, and robotic installation tools. The company says its system uses half the land and 70% less steel than conventional solar and can be built on slopes up to 27%. It plans to use the money to develop its products, expand installation capacity and form partnerships abroad. It is currently working on US projects ranging from community solar to on-site systems for hospitals and infrastructure. The release does not state the valuation or the stake sold.
context: The company frames the raise against rising US solar demand and growing problems with land, costs and construction delays. It claims its approach lets developers build projects twice as fast at roughly 30% lower energy cost. Planted Solar is also expanding into Asia-Pacific and Europe, where it says demand for land-efficient solar is growing.

sources.title: Planted Solar Secures $12M to Accelerate Solar Deployment

title: JSW Neo Energy signs 25-year SECI PPA for 230 MW FDRE project
summary: JSW Neo Energy signed a 25-year PPA with SECI for a 230 MW firm and dispatchable renewable project at ₹4.98 per kWh.
details: JSW Neo Energy signed a 25-year PPA with SECI for a 230 MW firm and dispatchable project at ₹4.98 per kWh, a load-following design that shapes supply to the buyer's demand. JSW's capacity under construction rises to 12.9 GW.
context: It is JSW Energy's first firm and dispatchable renewable project, a growing segment of Indian auctions that requires storage.

sources.title: JSW Neo Energy Signs 25-Year PPA with SECI for 230 MW Firm Renewable Project

title: Zelestra and EDP sign Spain's first large hybrid solar and battery PPA
summary: Zelestra and EDP signed Spain's first long-term PPA combining a large new solar plant (170 MWdc) with battery storage.
details: Zelestra and EDP signed a long-term PPA for a hybrid project in Trujillo, Extremadura: 170 MWdc of solar with 400 MWh of batteries. The structure ensures the battery can be fully charged by the solar plant every day in all weather.
context: It is the first PPA in Spain to combine large-scale solar and storage. The battery lets EDP receive power in the evening, when Spanish prices are higher than at midday.

sources.title: Zelestra and EDP sign first-of-its-kind large scale hybrid solar and battery storage PPA in Spain

title: Cambridge Power sells Eaton Socon solar and battery scheme to AGR Renewables
summary: Cambridge Power sold a 70 MWp solar and 100 MW battery project next to Eaton Socon substation in Bedfordshire to AGR Renewables.
details: Cambridge Power sold a project next to the Eaton Socon substation in Bedfordshire to AGR Renewables: 70 MWp of solar exporting up to 49.9 MW, and a 100 MW battery. The battery was consented in 2023 and the solar in early 2025; construction was due to start in August 2025.
context: Co-locating solar and storage next to a substation shortens the grid connection. The scheme also includes ecological and landscape improvements.

sources.title: Cambridge Power sells co-located solar and battery scheme to AGR Renewables

title: INVL Renewable Energy Fund I signs €29.3 million Kommunalkredit loan for 71 MW Romanian solar
summary: INVL Renewable Energy Fund I signed a €29.3 million loan with Kommunalkredit Austria to build 71 MW of solar in Romania.
details: INVL Renewable Energy Fund I, managed by INVL Asset Management, signed a €29.3 million loan with Kommunalkredit Austria to build 71 MW of solar in Romania. It is Kommunalkredit's second loan to the fund.
context: The fund's managing partner says steady long-term support from lenders speeds the energy transition in the region.

sources.title: INVL Renewable Energy Fund I secures new Kommunalkredit financing for solar energy projects

title: Ares fund takes 80% of Tango joint venture holding 496 MW of Savion solar projects
summary: Shell subsidiary Savion and a fund managed by Ares Infrastructure Opportunities formed Tango Holdings, a joint venture holding five Savion-developed solar projects totaling 496 MW in Ohio, Kentucky, Oklahoma and Indiana. Ares owns 80% of the venture and Savion keeps 20%.
details: The portfolio includes the Martin County and Kiowa County solar projects plus three further solar projects still under construction. Savion acts as managing member, meaning it runs the venture day to day, while Shell Renewable Asset Management International handles asset management of the projects. The deal was signed and closed at the same time with immediate effect. No price was disclosed.
context: Shell says the deal fits its strategy of developing renewable projects and reducing ownership as they mature, which it says helps improve capital returns and control costs. The 496 MW represents part of Savion's 3,049 MW of solar and storage assets under construction, operating or under contract. Shell plans to keep developing other onshore renewable projects through Savion.

sources.title: Shell subsidiary Savion to streamline five U.S. solar projects through joint venture

title: Pardee Renewable Energy takes 90% stake in 4.6 MW Roanoke school rooftop solar partnerships
target: 90% equity interest in four solar partnerships serving nine Roanoke public schools
summary: Pardee Renewable Energy, a subsidiary of Pardee Resources Company, has agreed to invest $15.2 million for a 90% equity interest in four partnerships building rooftop solar systems. The systems total 4.6 MW and will sit on nine public schools in Roanoke, Virginia.
details: The four partnerships plan to install new rooftop solar photovoltaic systems on nine public school buildings in Roanoke. Part of the investment will be funded by commercial bank loans of $8.3 million taken out at the partnership level, meaning the debt sits with the project partnerships rather than the parent company. The projects qualify for federal investment tax credits, which are tax reductions tied to the cost of building clean energy systems, and Pardee says it will use these credits itself. Installation and start of operation are scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2025. The partner on the projects is Secure Solar Futures, a solar developer based in Virginia.
context: The investment adds to the portfolio of Pardee's Alternative Energy Division, which the company describes as a growing part of its business. The structure lets Pardee capture federal tax credits from the school solar projects while sharing ownership with the developer.

sources.title: Pardee Resources Company: Solar PV Investment

title: OX2 buys Fageråsen wind project in Sweden from Eolus and Dala Vind
summary: OX2 acquired the permitted Fageråsen wind project in Dalarna, Sweden, from Eolus and Dala Vind: up to 34 turbines producing up to 700 GWh a year.
details: OX2 bought the permitted Fageråsen wind project in Dalarna from Eolus and Dala Vind. It will have up to 34 turbines producing up to 700 GWh a year, about 14% of the county's consumption, in price area SE3, with full commissioning planned by early 2028.
context: OX2 will develop, manage and keep long-term ownership of the farm as part of its growing portfolio.

sources.title: OX2 acquires Swedish wind project

title: Candi Solar raises US$24 million from existing investors
summary: Candi Solar raised US$24 million from existing investors, including a US$20 million convertible loan from Norfund, to grow in India and South Africa.
details: Candi Solar raised US$24 million from existing investors: a US$20 million convertible loan from Norfund and STOA and a US$4 million mezzanine top-up from the Energy Entrepreneurs Growth Fund. It has raised more than US$140 million in total.
context: Candi installs solar for businesses in India and South Africa, with 165 installations and more than 132 MWp deployed. The round comes ahead of a planned Series D in 2026.

sources.title: Candi Solar Raises $24M to Expand Clean Energy Operations in India and South Africa Ahead of 2026 Series D

title: Mobi Solar signs PPA with XentroMall operator for 2.5 MWp of mall rooftop solar
summary: Mobi Solar Philippines signed its first major PPA, with XentroMall operator XRC Mall Developer, for 2.5 MWp of rooftop solar across retail malls.
details: Mobi Solar Philippines signed a PPA with XRC Mall Developer, owner of the XentroMall brand, to install 2.5 MWp of rooftop solar on several of its community malls and public markets with no upfront cost.
context: It is Mobi Solar's first major PPA; the company was founded in 2023 and offers zero-capex solar to businesses.

sources.title: Mobi Solar Signs First PPA with XentroMall Operator, Launches 2.5 MWp Solar Project Across Philippine Retail Malls

title: Masdar and Iberdrola reach financial close on 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE
summary: Masdar and Iberdrola reached financial close on the 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE offshore wind farm, a €5.2 billion project, with £3.6 billion of loans from 23 banks and Denmark's export credit agency EIFO.
details: Masdar and Iberdrola closed £3.6 billion (€4.1 billion) of project finance from 23 banks and Denmark's export credit agency EIFO for the 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE offshore wind farm, estimated to cost about €5.2 billion. The facility was more than 40% oversubscribed.
context: It is one of the largest offshore wind financings of the decade and Masdar's largest ever.

sources.title: Masdar and Iberdrola achieve financial close for €5.2 billion offshore wind farm

title: Vena Energy signs India's first 100 MW load-following FDRE PPA with SECI
summary: Vena Energy signed India's first load-following PPA with SECI, for 100 MW under the firm and dispatchable renewable energy scheme.
details: Vena Energy signed a 100 MW PPA with SECI under the firm and dispatchable renewable energy scheme launched in June 2023, in the load-following format, where supply follows the distribution companies' demand profile.
context: Vena calls it India's first load-following PPA. The FDRE scheme also covers assured-peak and round-the-clock supply.

sources.title: Vena Energy Leads Innovation In India By Securing First 100 MW Load-Following PPA With SECI Under Firm & Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) Initiative

title: EDPR NA Distributed Generation signs 20-year solar PPA with California Water Service in Bakersfield
target: 1.75 MWac onsite solar array at Cal Water's Northeast Bakersfield Treatment Plant
summary: EDPR NA Distributed Generation, the distributed solar arm of EDP Renewables North America, has signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with California Water Service. The deal covers a 1.75 MWac onsite solar array at a water treatment plant in Bakersfield, California.
details: The photovoltaic system is rated at 1.75 MWac and 2.35 MWdc, meaning its output after conversion to grid-ready alternating current is lower than the panels' direct current rating. It will sit at Cal Water's Northeast Bakersfield Treatment Plant and is expected to produce about 3,800 MWh of electricity per year. Under the power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity, Cal Water will take the system's output for 20 years. The parties did not disclose the contract price or a commercial operation date.
context: The parties estimate the array will cut Cal Water's grid electricity costs by about $1.7 million over the contract term, based on current rates in the Bakersfield District. Cal Water says the project supports its greenhouse gas reduction targets. The deal adds to EDPR NA DG's California portfolio, which the company says spans more than 180 projects.

sources.title: EDP Renewables North America Announces 20-Year PPA with California Water Service

title: ENGIE North America agrees to buy 22 net-metered solar projects in Pennsylvania from Prospect14
target: Portfolio of 22 net energy metered distributed solar projects in Pennsylvania
summary: ENGIE North America has agreed to acquire a portfolio of 22 distributed solar projects in Pennsylvania from local developer Prospect14. The projects total more than 70 MW. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The portfolio is made up of 22 net energy metered (NEM) solar projects, a setup where the electricity produced is credited against a customer's power bill through the utility meter. They are distributed projects, meaning smaller installations connected to the local distribution grid rather than large transmission-connected plants. The release describes the deal as an agreement, and ENGIE refers to developing the projects, which suggests they are not yet built, though no construction timeline or closing date is given. No advisers or price were named.
context: ENGIE says the purchase extends its distributed solar and storage business in Pennsylvania and claims the projects will bring jobs, local tax revenue and better distribution grid reliability. The parties present the deal as evidence of growing demand for distributed solar in the state and of lenders' willingness to finance NEM projects. Prospect14, founded in 2017, says it has originated over 6.5 GWdc of solar and solar-plus-storage projects across US markets.

sources.title: ENGIE Acquires Portfolio of Net Energy Metered Distributed Solar Energy Projects in Pennsylvania from Prospect14

title: Estuary Power closes tax equity and upsized term loan for 185 MW Escape solar and storage project in Nevada
summary: Estuary Power has started operating the first phase of its 185 MW Escape solar and 400 MWh battery project in Lincoln County, Nevada, and closed further financing for it. Morgan Stanley Renewables made the initial funding under a tax equity commitment, and Denham Capital increased the size of the project's term loan. No amounts were disclosed.
details: The first phase, 70 MW of solar, began delivering power in June to Overton Power District No. 5, Caesars Entertainment and Wynn Las Vegas under long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts to buy the output at agreed terms. The second phase, 115 MW of solar plus 400 MWh of batteries, is due to start supplying MGM Resorts International later in 2025. Tax equity is an investment in which an investor funds part of a project in exchange for using its tax credits. Denham provided construction and long-term debt on behalf of its clients. Bechtel is building the solar arrays, Dashiell built the substation and some transmission upgrades, Tesla is supplying the batteries and JinkoSolar the modules.
context: Estuary, a Reno-based developer backed by the Ullico Infrastructure Fund whose investors are mainly union pension funds, says it delivered the first phase ahead of schedule and in just under two years from site selection. The company says the project created nearly 500 union construction jobs. Overton Power District says the contract supplies power at lower cost than other market sources.

sources.title: ESTUARY POWER COMMENCES OPERATION OF ESCAPE SOLAR AND STORAGE PROJECT AND CLOSES ADDITIONAL FINANCING

title: Exus Renewables North America closes $308.2 million financing for Zia solar and Keystone wind portfolios

buyers.name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

target: Zia Solar Power portfolio (185 MW) and Keystone wind portfolio (169 MW)
summary: Exus Renewables North America has completed $308.2 million of debt financing for two operating US portfolios. The deals cover the 185 MW Zia Solar Power portfolio in New Mexico and the 169 MW Keystone wind portfolio in Pennsylvania.
details: The Zia portfolio consists of nine operating solar farms in New Mexico locations including Deming, Los Lunas, Albuquerque, Moriarty and Rio Rancho, and its $149.6 million financing closed in May, led by ING Capital and PNC Capital Markets. Its output is sold under long-term power purchase agreements (contracts fixing who buys the power and at what terms) lasting 20 to 25 years with Public Service Company of New Mexico, Central New Mexico Electric Cooperative, Columbus Electric Cooperative and the City of Rio Rancho. The Keystone portfolio received $158.6 million and is made up of the 139 MW Twin Ridges and 30 MW Patton wind projects. KeyBanc Capital Markets acted as coordinating lead arranger, with Crédit Agricole CIB and Societe Generale as joint lead arrangers. Vitol is the main buyer of power and renewable energy certificates (tradable proof of green generation) across the wind assets.
context: The Keystone financing supports the repowering of Twin Ridges, meaning older turbines were replaced to extend its life and boost efficiency, with the repowered project starting commercial operation in 2024. Exus presents the financings as evidence of lender confidence in its platform. The company says it has over 5 GW in its total portfolio, with 764 MW operating or under construction.

sources.title: Exus Renewables North America Secures Over $300 Million in Financing for Zia Solar Portfolio and Keystone Wind Projects

title: BayWa r.e. sells 60 MWp Seville solar portfolio to KGAL
summary: BayWa r.e. sold a 60 MWp solar portfolio in Guillena, Seville, Gerena II (about 50 MWp) and Chamorro (about 10 MWp), to KGAL.
details: BayWa r.e. sold two energised solar plants with single-axis trackers in Guillena, Seville, to KGAL: Gerena II (about 50 MWp) and Chamorro (about 10 MWp). They should produce about 125 GWh a year.
context: Selling built plants to an asset manager lets BayWa r.e. reinvest in development.

sources.title: BayWa r.e. sells 60 MWp solar portfolio in Spain to KGAL

title: Qualitas Energy buys three German wind projects for repowering
summary: Qualitas Energy acquired three operating wind projects in Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate and Baden-Württemberg with 17.6 MW, which it plans to repower to about 51 MW.
details: Qualitas Energy bought three operating wind projects in Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate and Baden-Württemberg with 17.6 MW. It plans to replace their turbines with eight modern ones, raising capacity to about 51 MW.
context: Repowering old sites with larger turbines triples output on land that already has permits and grid connections.

sources.title: Qualitas Energy acquires 51 MW wind energy pipeline in Germany

title: Cleantech Solar Asia 2 secures US$70 million green loan for Southeast Asian C&I solar
summary: Cleantech Solar Asia 2 secured a five-year US$70 million term loan to develop up to 150 MWp of commercial and industrial solar across Southeast Asia.
details: Clifford Capital and ING arranged a five-year US$70 million term loan, with a US$30 million greenshoe, for Cleantech Solar Asia 2 to build up to 150 MWp of greenfield commercial and industrial solar in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Vietnam.
context: The greenshoe lets the loan grow if the pipeline expands. The lenders cite confidence in Southeast Asian corporate solar.

sources.title: Cleantech Solar Secures $70 Million Green Loan to Boost Southeast Asia C&I Solar Portfolio

title: Bpifrance lends about €17 million for Wysenergy's 9 MW wind farm in Marne
summary: Bpifrance provided about €17 million for Wysenergy's 9 MW Les Deux Noues wind farm in Faux-Fresnay, Marne, which won a CRE tender.
details: Bpifrance provided about €17 million to Wysenergy to build the 9 MW Les Deux Noues wind farm in Faux-Fresnay, Marne, using Vestas V163 turbines. It won a contract in the CRE's latest PPE2 tender and should produce about 27,000 MWh a year.
context: Winning a CRE tender gives the farm a guaranteed price for its output, which supports the loan. De Gaulle Fleurance advised Wysenergy.

sources.title: De Gaulle Fleurance advises Wysenergy on the financing of a wind farm in France

title: SOFAZ agrees to buy 49% of Enfinity Global's 402 MW Italian solar portfolio

buyers.name: State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan (SOFAZ)

target: 402 MW portfolio of 14 solar PV plants in Italy

advisors.name: EY
advisors.role: financial and tax advisor to SOFAZ

summary: Azerbaijan's sovereign wealth fund SOFAZ has agreed to acquire a 49% equity stake in a 402 MW portfolio of solar plants in Italy from Enfinity Global. Enfinity keeps the 51% majority and will continue managing the assets. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of 14 solar photovoltaic plants in the Lazio and Emilia-Romagna regions, some already operating and some still under construction. Their output is sold under long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts fixing the price buyers pay for the electricity over many years. The companies expect the plants to generate about 685 GWh per year. Enfinity was advised by Mediobanca (financial), Legance (legal) and Fichtner (technical), while SOFAZ was advised by JLL (M&A), Dentons Europe Studio Legale Tributario (legal), EY (financial and tax) and DNV (technical).
context: Enfinity says bringing in a capital partner lets it recycle money into its Italian pipeline of 2.6 GW of solar and 5.3 GW of energy storage. SOFAZ describes the investment as a source of stable, predictable income in line with its long-term mandate and says it wants further investments in Italy and Europe. The deal is an example of a sovereign fund taking a minority stake in contracted operating renewable assets.

sources.title: Azerbaijan's Sovereign Wealth Fund to Acquire Minority Stake in 402 MW of Solar Assets in Italy from Enfinity Global

title: Recurrent Energy closes $260 million financing from U.S. Bank for 94 MW Blue Moon Solar in Kentucky

buyers.name: U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance
buyers.role: tax equity investor and construction lender

summary: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, has closed $260 million in construction financing and tax equity for its 94 MW Blue Moon Solar project in Harrison County, Kentucky. U.S. Bank, through U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance, is providing both parts of the funding.
details: Blue Moon Solar is a 94 MW solar plant under construction in Harrison County, Kentucky, with commercial operation expected in 2026. The financing combines a construction loan, which pays for building the plant, with tax equity, an investment where a bank provides capital in exchange for the project's federal tax benefits. Constellation will buy the electricity and renewable energy certificates, which are credits proving the power came from a renewable source, under a power purchase agreement whose length is not disclosed. Recurrent Energy plans to own and operate the plant once it is energized.
context: The project is Recurrent Energy's first in Kentucky, and the company expects it to create hundreds of construction jobs and new local tax revenue. U.S. Bank says it has financed several Recurrent Energy projects and highlights its ability to provide both equity and debt in one package. The deal reflects Recurrent Energy's shift toward owning and operating its own assets.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Secures $260 Million Financing for Blue Moon Solar Project in Kentucky

title: Masdar transfers its Sharjah waste-to-energy stake to Tadweer
summary: Masdar divested its stake in the Sharjah Waste-to-Energy plant to waste management company Tadweer Group.
details: Masdar agreed to sell its stake in the Sharjah Waste-to-Energy plant, opened in 2022 as the Middle East's first commercial-scale facility of its kind, to Tadweer Group, which joins BEEAH Group as partner in Emirates Waste-to-Energy Company. The sale is subject to closing conditions.
context: Masdar says it is refocusing on scaling its core renewable businesses; Tadweer, a waste manager, is a natural owner for a plant that turns rubbish into power.

sources.title: Masdar Transfers Stake in Sharjah Waste-to-Energy Plant to Tadweer, Boosting UAE’s Renewable Energy Goals

title: Sabanci Renewables buys 120 MWac Project Pepper solar development in Texas from OCI Energy
summary: Sabanci Renewables, a US subsidiary of Turkish conglomerate Sabancı Holding, has acquired Project Pepper, a 120 MWac utility-scale solar project in McLennan County, Texas, from developer OCI Energy. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: OCI Energy developed the project from the start, handling land acquisition, early site studies, permits and the grid connection agreement. Sabanci Renewables will now arrange financing, build, own and run the plant. Commercial operation, meaning the point at which the plant starts selling power, is expected in the third quarter of 2027. Sidley Austin advised OCI Energy and Troutman Pepper Locke advised Sabanci Renewables on legal matters.
context: This is the first deal between the two companies, and they say further transactions are being considered. Sabanci says the addition brings its US solar capacity that is operating or under construction to 660 MWdc, toward a goal of 3,000 MWdc of renewables by 2030. OCI Energy says it has more than 5 GWac of solar and storage projects in development.

sources.title: OCI Energy LLC announces sale of 120 MWac project to Sabanci Renewables, advancing clean power in Texas

title: Cero Generation closes about £200 million for three UK solar and battery projects
summary: Cero Generation and Enso Energy reached financial close on about £200 million from ING, NordLB, Rabobank and Santander UK for three UK solar and battery projects, with room to add more.
details: ING, NordLB, Rabobank and Santander UK provided about £200 million as a green loan, with an accordion for future projects, for three UK solar and battery projects of Cero Generation and Enso Energy, including the 115 MW Bramley co-located project and two others with 245 MW combined.
context: This was the first close under Cero's Gemini portfolio facility; the Bumble Bee project followed in 2026.

sources.title: Cero Generation reaches financial close on UK solar and BESS financing package

title: ACWA Power, Badeel and SAPCO sign PPAs with SPPC for 15 GW of Saudi renewables
summary: ACWA Power, PIF-owned Badeel and Saudi Aramco Power Company signed PPAs with the Saudi Power Procurement Company for several solar and wind projects totalling 15 GW.
details: ACWA Power, PIF-owned Badeel and Saudi Aramco Power signed PPAs with the Saudi Power Procurement Company for five large solar plants and two wind plants totalling 15 GW, a total investment of about US$8.3 billion.
context: The projects reached financial close in December 2025. They are the largest single round of Saudi renewable PPAs in our tracker.

sources.title: ACWA Power, Badeel, and SAPCO sign PPAs for several renewable energy projects

title: Ørsted closes about TWD 90 billion financing for 632 MW Greater Changhua 2
summary: Ørsted reached financial close on about TWD 90 billion (about US$3 billion) from 25 banks and five export credit agencies for the 632 MW Greater Changhua 2 offshore wind farm.
details: Ørsted is also selling an equity stake in the project.

sources.title: Ørsted secures project financing for 632 MW wind farm in Taiwan

title: Sumitomo Corporation of Americas makes strategic investment in Independence Hydrogen
summary: Sumitomo Corporation, acting through its US subsidiary Sumitomo Corporation of Americas, has announced a strategic investment in Independence Hydrogen. The funding is meant to help the Virginia-based company develop more small-scale, local hydrogen production and distribution projects in the United States. The size of the investment and the stake acquired were not disclosed.
details: Independence Hydrogen is a privately held, veteran-founded company that runs a hydrogen production site in Petersburg, Virginia. The site captures hydrogen that would otherwise be released into the air as a waste product and purifies it to fuel cell grade. That level of purity is high enough for use in fuel cells, which turn hydrogen into electricity. The company sells this gaseous hydrogen to customers in material handling, such as forklifts, and in mobility, remote critical infrastructure and industrial gases. Its model, branded DeHy, relies on decentralized supply, meaning many smaller production points near customers rather than one large plant. Existing backers Suburban Propane and Hivers & Strivers remain involved as foundation investors.
context: Sumitomo says it holds a long-term positive view of hydrogen and believes the distributed model can grow in a segment it considers underserved. Independence Hydrogen says the backing will speed up its expansion. The company claims its smaller, decentralized approach addresses reliability and cost concerns while getting supply to market faster. The hydrogen is recovered from waste streams rather than described as made with renewable power.

sources.title: Sumitomo Corporation of Americas Announces Strategic Investment in Independence Hydrogen to Develop Hydrogen Production and Distribution Projects

title: Lydian Energy closes US$233 million for Texas battery storage
summary: Lydian Energy reached financial close on US$233 million, its first institutional project financing, for battery storage in Texas.
details: Lydian Energy's US$233 million funds three Texas batteries in ERCOT, including Pintail (San Patricio County) and Crane (Crane County), each 200 MW / 400 MWh, which account for about US$139 million of financing from ING.
context: It is Lydian's first institutional project financing. Batteries in ERCOT earn money from price swings and grid services.

sources.title: Lydian Energy Secures Major $233M Investment To Strengthen Texas Energy Grid With Battery Storage

title: AMPYR Australia reaches financial close on 300 MW / 600 MWh Wellington Stage 1 battery
summary: AMPYR Australia reached financial close on Stage 1 of the 300 MW / 600 MWh Wellington battery in New South Wales.
details: AMPYR Australia reached financial close on Stage 1 of the 300 MW / 600 MWh Wellington battery in New South Wales. Partners include Fluence, Transgrid, Lumea and ZEN Energy, which signed a ten-year virtual offtake agreement.
context: AMPYR and AGP aim for 6 GWh of operating Australian storage by 2030. A virtual offtake gives the battery a fixed income stream from a retailer.

sources.title: AMPYR Australia reaches financial close for Wellington Stage 1 BESS project

title: ib vogt secures ₱4.49 billion green financing from HSBC for Tantangan solar
summary: ib vogt reached financial close on its Tantangan solar project in the southern Philippines with ₱4.49 billion (about US$80 million) of green financing from HSBC.
details: HSBC provided ₱4.49 billion (about US$80 million) of green financing for ib vogt's 99 MWp Tantangan solar plant in South Cotabato. Construction began earlier in 2025.
context: It is ib vogt's second solar project in Mindanao, supplying affordable renewable power to the region as part of the Philippines' clean energy goals.

sources.title: ib vogt Secures PHP 4.49 Billion (USD 80 Million) Green Financing From HSBC To Power Renewable Projects In Southern Philippines

title: Innova and Atrato Onsite Energy reach financial close on 15 MWp Wrexham Solar Park
summary: Innova and Atrato Onsite Energy reached financial close on the consented 15 MWp Wrexham Solar Park in Wales.
details: Atrato Onsite Energy bought the consented 15 MWp Wrexham Solar Park from Innova and reached financial close; construction starts immediately with energisation in the first half of 2026. Sunnerg is the contractor and OCU Hornbill the connections provider.
context: The plant will supply Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water by private wire, a direct cable that avoids grid charges.

sources.title: Innova and Atrato Onsite Energy Reach Financial Close on 15MWp Wrexham Solar Park

title: SUNOTEC buys 400 MWp solar and 600 MWh battery project in Latvia
summary: SUNOTEC acquired 100% of SIA DSE Lazas Solar from Danish Sun Energy to build a 400 MWp solar plant with a 600 MWh battery in Latvia.
details: SUNOTEC bought all of SIA DSE Lazas Solar from Danish developer Danish Sun Energy to build a 400 MWp solar plant with a 600 MWh battery in Latvia, due to be commissioned in March 2027.
context: SUNOTEC, a builder of utility-scale solar and storage, calls it a pivotal step in expanding into owning its own projects.

sources.title: SUNOTEC acquires large scale co-located park with solar PV and BESS

title: Ecopetrol completes acquisition of 205 MW Windpeshi wind project owner from Enel in Colombia
summary: Colombian state-controlled energy company Ecopetrol has closed its purchase of all shares in Wind Autogeneración S.A.S. from Enel S.A.S. The acquired company owns the Windpeshi wind project in La Guajira, Colombia, planned at 205 MW. The purchase price was not disclosed.
details: Windpeshi sits between the municipalities of Uribia and Maicao in La Guajira and is expected to produce about 1,006 GWh per year on average. Ecopetrol's board approved the deal in December 2024, and closing followed regulatory and antitrust approvals. Ecopetrol plans to restart construction by the end of 2025 and expects operations to begin before 2028, with estimated investment of nearly 350 million (currency as stated in the release, likely US dollars) between 2025 and 2027. The power will be used for self-consumption, meaning Ecopetrol will use the electricity in its own operations rather than selling it.
context: Ecopetrol says the project would cover roughly 8 to 9 percent of its group energy demand and help lower energy costs, with an estimated benefit of about 4.8 million tons of avoided CO2 emissions. The company describes it as the start of its non-conventional renewable projects in La Guajira, a region known for strong wind and solar resources. It also says engagement with local Wayuu indigenous communities will be central to development.

sources.title: Ecopetrol S.A. acquires Wind Autogeneración S.A.S., owner of the Windpeshi renewable energy wind project, located in La Guajira

title: Aneo agrees to buy Bäckhammar wind farm in Sweden from KGAL
summary: Aneo agreed to buy the 31-turbine Bäckhammar wind farm in Kristinehamn, Sweden, from KGAL.
details: Aneo agreed to buy the Bäckhammar wind farm in Kristinehamn, southern Sweden, from KGAL. It has 31 Vestas turbines with 130 MW and has run since 2020. Part of its output is sold under a long-term PPA with a large international technology company, which continues.
context: Aneo says the deal broadens the geographic spread of its Nordic production. The existing tech-company PPA gives the farm contracted revenue.

sources.title: Aneo acquires wind farm in Sweden

summary: TotalEnergies sold 50% of its 604 MW Portuguese wind, solar and hydro portfolio to a consortium including MM Capital Partners 2 and Daiwa Energy & Infrastructure.
details: TotalEnergies completed the sale of 50% of its 604 MW Portuguese wind, solar and hydro portfolio to MM Capital Partners 2, Daiwa Energy & Infrastructure and Mizuho Leasing for €178.5 million, an enterprise value of €550 million for the whole. TotalEnergies keeps 50% and runs the assets.
context: The plants average 16 years old and benefit from regulated tariffs. TotalEnergies is selling stakes to recycle capital.

sources.title: TotalEnergies To Sell 50% Stake In Portugal Renewable Portfolio, Aligning With Its Business Model

title: NORD/LB provides about €110 million for three Capital Dynamics solar farms in Spain
summary: NORD/LB provided about €110 million, in separate transactions, for three solar farms Capital Dynamics is building in Aragón, Spain.
details: NORD/LB provided about €110 million, in separate transactions, for three solar farms Capital Dynamics is building in Aragón: 54.89 MW (88,500 panels), 54.78 MW (87,600 panels) and 50 MW (80,600 panels), more than 250,000 panels in total.
context: Together they should supply nearly 30,000 households. Financing each plant separately lets them proceed on their own timetables.

sources.title: NORD/LB Provides €110 Million Financing For Three Capital Dynamics Solar Farms Under Construction In Spain

title: Arevon closes US$600 million corporate credit facility for US solar and storage growth

buyers.name: Wells Fargo Bank, National Association
buyers.role: Administrative Agent and Joint Lead Arranger

buyers.name: Wells Fargo Securities, LLC
buyers.role: Co-Green Loan Structuring Agent and LC issuing bank

buyers.name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, New York Branch
buyers.role: Co-Green Loan Structuring Agent, LC issuing bank and Joint Lead Arranger

buyers.name: Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
buyers.role: Co-Green Loan Structuring Agent, LC issuing bank and Joint Lead Arranger

summary: Arevon Energy, a US developer and operator of solar and battery storage projects, closed a US$600 million corporate credit facility that can be expanded to US$850 million. A group of banks led by Wells Fargo provided the financing.
details: The facility combines a US$350 million revolving loan and letter of credit line with a US$250 million project letter of credit line. A revolving loan lets the borrower draw, repay and redraw funds as needed, while letters of credit are bank guarantees often required to secure obligations such as grid connection or contract performance. Arevon says the money will support working capital, acquisitions, project development and performance support obligations. The facility includes green loan reporting and sustainability-linked metrics, meaning some terms are tied to environmental targets. Latham & Watkins advised Arevon and Morgan Lewis advised the lenders.
context: The facility is corporate-level financing rather than funding for a single project, giving Arevon flexible capital across its portfolio. The company reports owning and operating more than 4.7 GW of solar and storage in 17 states, building another 1.5 GW and holding a 6 GW development pipeline. Arevon presents the deal as a sign of lender confidence in its portfolio.

sources.title: Arevon Secures $600 Million Credit Facility to Accelerate Renewable Energy Growth in the United States

title: Globeleq and African Rainbow Energy reach financial close on 153 MW/612 MWh Red Sands battery project in South Africa
target: Red Sands battery energy storage project

advisors.name: Sungrow
advisors.role: BESS technology supplier and service provider

summary: Globeleq and its partner African Rainbow Energy have reached financial close on the Red Sands battery storage project near Upington in South Africa. The 153 MW/612 MWh project is backed by about ZAR 5.4 billion (roughly US$300 million) in debt from Absa and Standard Bank.
details: Financial close means all funding agreements are signed and money can be drawn to start building. The standalone battery, which can deliver its full output for about four hours, will cover around five hectares in the Northern Cape and sell power to the National Transmission Company South Africa under a 15-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract fixing the buyer and terms. China Energy Engineering Corporation is the engineering and procurement contractor, while Sungrow supplies the battery technology and a long-term service agreement. The project also includes upgrades to Eskom and NTCSA grid infrastructure, and Globeleq will manage it through its subsidiary Globeleq South Africa Management Services.
context: The companies say Red Sands is the largest standalone battery project in Africa to reach financial close. It was first developed by African Green Ventures and bought by Globeleq in 2023, and will be Globeleq's second utility-scale battery project. The partners expect it to ease grid congestion in the region and create about 250 construction jobs and 80 operational jobs.

title: Globeleq agrees to buy 51% of Zambia's Lunsemfwa Hydro Power Company from Norfund
summary: Globeleq has signed a share purchase agreement with Norwegian development institution Norfund to acquire a 51% stake in Lunsemfwa Hydro Power Company in Zambia. The company runs two hydropower plants with a combined 56 MW and is building a 20 MW solar plant. No price was disclosed.
details: LHPC is based in Kabwe in Zambia's Central Province and sells electricity to state utility ZESCO under a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell power, as well as to private customers such as Copperbelt Energy Corporation and Jubilee Metals. The remaining 49% of LHPC stays with Wanda Gorge Investments, a Zambian infrastructure investor. Completion is expected in the second half of 2025.
context: The deal would mark Globeleq's entry into Zambia and its first hydropower investment in Africa. Globeleq says Zambia is a priority market where it is developing more than 400 MW of new solar, wind, battery and hybrid projects, including the 54 MWp Kafue solar project. Norfund, the seller, is also a co-owner of Globeleq alongside British International Investment.

details: Peak Energy bought 11 MW of ready-to-build high-voltage solar projects in the Chubu, Chugoku, Hokkaido and Kansai regions of Japan. Due in 2027, they should produce more than 13 GWh a year, sold to companies under fixed-price long-term PPAs.
context: Fixed-price corporate PPAs give the projects stable revenue without relying on Japan's feed-in tariff, and should cut nearly 6,000 tonnes of CO2 a year.

sources.title: Peak Energy expands in Japan with 11 MW high-voltage solar acquisition

sources.title: ENOVA acquires 45 MW wind farm from BayWa r.e.

title: LS Power completes acquisition of ENGIE Services U.S., rebranded as OPTERRA Energy Services
target: ENGIE Services U.S. (now OPTERRA Energy Services)
summary: LS Power has completed its purchase of ENGIE Services U.S., an Oakland-based energy services business that now goes back to its former name, OPTERRA Energy Services. The company has delivered about 375 MW of solar and 24 microgrids for public sector customers across North America. No price was disclosed.
details: OPTERRA designs and delivers energy efficiency upgrades, solar systems, battery storage, microgrids, lighting and HVAC work, plus operations, maintenance and savings verification, mainly for cities, schools and government agencies. It says it has completed more than 9,000 projects since 1974, including 8.1 MW of solar across 48 school sites in Chula Vista with a backup microgrid. The business has nearly 300 staff. The deal closed on June 12, 2025 after customary conditions, including US regulatory approvals, were met. The release does not name the seller explicitly beyond the ENGIE brand, nor any advisers.
context: LS Power, which says it has developed or acquired 50,000 MW of generation, describes OPTERRA as a strategic fit for its platform of demand-side services such as efficiency and grid reliability. Its chief executive argues that rising US power demand calls for a broad mix of solutions, with energy services as one part. OPTERRA claims its work has secured more than US$3 billion in guaranteed energy cost savings for customers, meaning contracts where promised savings are backed by the provider.

sources.title: LS Power Acquires ENGIE Services U.S; 50+ Year Legacy Company Returns to Its Roots as OPTERRA Energy Services to Expand Efficiency and Renewables Offerings

title: Redeux Energy closes $30 million letter of credit facility with Macquarie for US solar and storage pipeline

buyers.name: Macquarie Group
buyers.role: Sole issuer and administrative agent (Commodities and Global Markets business)

summary: Denver-based developer Redeux Energy has closed a $30 million revolving letter of credit facility provided by Macquarie. The facility will back development costs for Redeux's US pipeline of about 7 GW of solar and 12 GWh of storage.
details: A letter of credit is a bank guarantee that a developer can post instead of cash to meet obligations, here tied to grid interconnection and power purchase agreements (long-term contracts to sell electricity). The facility is revolving, meaning it can be drawn, repaid and reused. Redeux's pipeline spans the ERCOT, MISO, CAISO, SERC and WECC power markets. Macquarie's Commodities and Global Markets business is the sole issuer and administrative agent. Redeux is also marketing a mid-stage portfolio of 1.5 GW of solar and 3.4 GWh of storage in MISO, ERCOT and SERC, targeting sales in the second half of 2025.
context: Redeux says interconnection costs have risen in many markets after queue reforms under FERC Order 2023, increasing the collateral developers must post. The company says the facility lets it carry projects further through development before selling them to independent power producers, capturing more value. Redeux reports it has sold nearly 700 MW of solar and hybrid projects to date and hopes to expand the facility in future.

sources.title: Redeux Energy Secures $30 Million Letter of Credit Facility to Support Solar and Battery Storage Project Development

title: Origis Energy closes MUFG-led financing for 150 MWac Wheatland Solar in Indiana as part of US$530 million-plus portfolio

buyers.name: MUFG
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger, Green Loan Coordinator and Administrative Agent

target: Wheatland Solar project (150 MWac, Knox County, Indiana)
summary: Origis Energy has reached financial close on its 150 MWac Wheatland solar project in Knox County, Indiana, with a bank group led by MUFG. The loan is part of a portfolio financing of more than US$530 million that also covers the Optimist solar and storage project in Mississippi.
details: Financial close means the loan agreements are signed and money can be drawn to build the project. Wheatland will sell its power to CenterPoint Energy under a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity, and is due for completion in the first half of 2026. The companion Optimist project in Clay County, Mississippi has 200 MWac of solar plus 50 MW of four-hour battery storage, sells power to the Tennessee Valley Authority, and had its share of the financing closed in late 2024. MUFG acted as coordinating lead arranger, green loan coordinator and administrative agent, with Associated Bank, CoBank, National Bank of Canada and NatWest as joint lead arrangers and Amalgamated Bank and Siemens Financial Services as lenders. Latham & Watkins and Taft Stettinius advised Origis, while Milbank and Dentons advised MUFG.
context: Origis develops, owns and operates both projects, and the financing lets it move Wheatland toward construction completion. The company says it sees rapid growth in electricity demand, and MUFG describes the deal as part of its support for US renewable project development. The release does not state the exact amount allocated to Wheatland alone.

sources.title: Origis Energy Secures Financial Close for Wheatland Solar as Part of $530+ Million Portfolio Financing with MUFG

title: Onyx Renewables closes $260 million credit facility for US distributed solar and storage

buyers.name: Apterra Infrastructure Capital
buyers.role: Administrative Agent, Lead Arranger and Sole Bookrunner

buyers.name: Investec
buyers.role: Lender, Letter of Credit and Hedge Provider

summary: Onyx Renewables has closed a $260 million senior secured credit facility to fund its distributed clean energy projects across the United States. The facility can be expanded to $350 million and replaces the company's existing revolving credit line.
details: The financing combines a term loan, a revolving line of credit (a loan that can be drawn and repaid repeatedly) and a $10 million letter of credit facility, which is a bank guarantee used to back project obligations. Senior secured means lenders are repaid first and hold claims on assets. The money will support construction and operation of onsite solar and battery storage projects for commercial, industrial and institutional customers. Apterra Infrastructure Capital, an Apollo affiliate, led and arranged the deal, while Investec and ATLAS SP Partners, majority-owned by Apollo funds, acted as lenders, with Investec also providing hedging.
context: Onyx says this is its largest institutional capital raise so far and presents it as a sign of investor confidence in its development and operating track record. The company argues the funding helps it meet demand for lower-cost, resilient power among business customers. The deal illustrates lenders providing corporate-level credit to scale portfolios of small onsite solar and storage installations.

sources.title: Onyx Renewables Secures $260 Million in Secured Credit Facilities to Support Nationwide Deployment of Localized Clean Energy Solutions

title: Enfinity Global sells c.49% of 380 MW US and Italy battery storage projects to Daiwa Energy & Infrastructure
target: Two battery energy storage projects in ERCOT Houston zone (US) and Veneto (Italy)

advisors.name: Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe
advisors.role: legal adviser to Daiwa Energy & Infrastructure

summary: Enfinity Global has sold a roughly 49% minority interest in two battery storage projects totaling 380 MW to Daiwa Energy & Infrastructure, the alternative asset arm of Japan's Daiwa Securities Group. The projects are located in Texas in the US and in Italy's Veneto region. Enfinity keeps about 51% and control.
details: The US project is a 250 MW, 500 MWh battery in the Houston zone of ERCOT, the Texas grid operator, able to discharge at full power for two hours. The Italian project is a 130 MW, 520 MWh battery with four hours of duration. Enfinity will finish development and construction and act as long-term asset manager for both, and operations are expected to start by 2027. No price was disclosed. Winston & Strawn and DLA Piper advised Enfinity, while Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe, Ensight Energy Consulting and Ernst & Young advised Daiwa.
context: The parties say the projects will support grid reliability and rising electricity demand from data centers, AI and industrial electrification. Daiwa describes the deal as a step in expanding its global renewables and storage portfolio. Enfinity says bringing in long-term co-investors is central to its strategy for funding growth across its reported 35.5 GW pipeline.

title: Canada Growth Fund commits up to C$138 million more to geothermal developer Eavor

advisors.name: Davies Ward Phillips & Vineberg LLP
advisors.role: legal advisor to CGF and CGFIM

summary: Canada Growth Fund has signed a definitive agreement to invest up to about C$138 million in Eavor Technologies, a Calgary-based company developing closed-loop geothermal systems. The money is meant to speed up development and commercial rollout of Eavor's technology, whose first commercial project is being built in Geretsried, Germany.
details: About C$89 million is due at financial close, meaning when the deal's conditions are met and funds are released, with roughly C$48 million more tied to Eavor reaching certain milestones. Eavor-Loop is a closed system that circulates a fluid through underground wells to collect the Earth's heat by conduction, without exchanging fluid with the surrounding rock. Since CGF's first investment, Eavor reports progress at Geretsried including intersecting wells with its magnetic ranging system, insulated drill pipe for hot conditions and a method to seal multilateral wells. Davies Ward Phillips & Vineberg advised CGF, Morgan Stanley and National Bank Financial were placement agents for Eavor, DS Lawyers Canada advised Eavor and A&O Shearman advised the placement agents.
context: This is a follow-on to CGF's C$90 million investment in Eavor's Series B preferred equity round in October 2023. CGF, a C$15 billion government-backed fund managed by a PSP Investments subsidiary, says the funding will help keep most of Eavor's leadership and staff in Canada. CGF reports 13 investments totalling about C$2.7 billion since its 2023 launch.

title: Fifth Third Bank commits $98 million tax equity to Arevon's 265 MWdc Indiana solar projects
summary: Arevon Energy has secured a $98 million tax equity commitment from Fifth Third Bank for two solar projects under construction in Pike County, Indiana. The Ratts 1 and Heirloom projects total 265 MWdc.
details: Ratts 1 is 192 MWdc and Heirloom is 73 MWdc, and both are expected to be fully running later in 2025. Tax equity is money from an investor who receives the projects' federal tax benefits in return. This deal uses the Inflation Reduction Act rule that lets tax credits be sold to other companies, giving Arevon more flexibility in how it structures the capital. It follows a separate $299 million financial close, the point where funding is secured, reached in September 2024. Ratts 1 sells power under a long-term contract to Indiana Municipal Power Agency and Meta buys the output of Heirloom.
context: Arevon says the two projects represent an investment of almost $400 million and will pay more than $86 million to local governments over their lifetimes. The company reports more than $3.8 billion in project financings over the past 18 months and is expanding in the Midwest grid region run by MISO. This is Arevon's first tax equity partnership with Fifth Third Bank.

sources.title: Arevon Secures $98 Million Tax Equity Commitment for its Ratts 1 and Heirloom Solar Projects in Indiana

details: Natixis lent €76 million non-recourse to Elawan Energy for 23 operating mini-hydro plants in Spain, 175 MW in total, mixing dam and reservoir plants with run-of-river. Elawan bought them from Acciona in 2024. Watson Farley & Williams advised Elawan.
context: Elawan runs 2.1 GW in nine countries, with 830 MW under construction. Hydro with reservoirs can shift output to times of higher demand.

title: Ecopetrol agrees to buy Statkraft's Colombian solar and wind portfolio of up to 1.3 GW

sellers.name: Statkraft European Wind and Solar Holding AS

target: Statkraft's Colombian solar and wind portfolio
summary: Colombian oil and gas group Ecopetrol signed an asset purchase agreement on May 20, 2025 to buy Statkraft's renewable energy portfolio in Colombia. The portfolio covers up to 1.3 GW of solar and wind projects. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of one development and operating company, six special purpose entities holding solar projects totalling 614 MW and three special purpose entities holding wind projects totalling 750 MW. A special purpose entity is a company set up to own a single project. The projects sit in the departments of La Guajira, Sucre, Córdoba, Caldas and Magdalena. The companies are held through Statkraft subsidiaries Enerfín Sociedad de Energía and Enerfin Enervento Exterior. Completion depends on conditions precedent, meaning requirements that must be met before closing, and other legal approvals.
context: Ecopetrol says the deal would advance its target of adding 900 MW of renewable self-generation capacity by 2025 under its 2040 Strategy. The company expects the assets to supply low-emission power for its own operations, cutting its reliance on spot market electricity purchases and diversifying its energy mix.

title: Enfinity Global closes up to €100 million bond facility with Eiffel Investment Group for European storage and solar
summary: Enfinity Global has closed a bond facility of up to €100 million provided by Eiffel Investment Group through four of its investment vehicles. The money will support development of Enfinity's battery storage and solar projects in Europe.
details: The facility is Enfinity's first financing tied to its European battery energy storage portfolio, where it is developing a 6.4 GW pipeline split between 5.1 GW in Italy and 1.3 GW in the UK. A bond facility is a form of debt in which investors lend money in exchange for repayment with interest. Eiffel, an asset manager focused on sustainable investment, is lending through its infrastructure debt strategy. The release does not state the bond's maturity, interest terms or which specific projects will be funded.
context: Enfinity says it has now secured €865 million of junior and senior debt for Europe, and it describes itself as one of Italy's ten largest independent power producers, with 232 MW operating, 538 MW under construction and 805 MW of approved solar. The company presents storage as central to its plan to supply round-the-clock renewable power to corporate customers. It also claims to have signed one-third of new Italian solar PPA capacity contracted in 2024.

title: Doral Renewables closes $1.5 billion debt and tax equity package for three Mammoth Solar phases in Indiana
target: Mammoth South, Mammoth Central I and Mammoth Central II solar projects

advisors.name: Milbank LLP
advisors.role: Tax equity legal counsel to Truist

summary: Doral Renewables has closed about $1.5 billion of construction debt and tax equity financing for three 300 MWac phases of its Mammoth Solar complex in Pulaski County, Indiana. KeyBanc, Santander and HSBC led a $1.3 billion debt package, and Truist committed over $200 million of tax equity for the Mammoth South phase.
details: The three phases, Mammoth South, Central I and Central II, total 900 MWac and are part of the wider 1.3 GW Mammoth Solar facility, using ground-mounted single-axis tracking panels. The debt includes $412 million of construction-to-term loans (loans that convert into long-term debt once the plant runs), $614 million of tax equity bridge loans (short-term loans repaid when tax equity investors fund), and a $259 million letter of credit facility. Tax equity means an investor funds part of the project in exchange for its federal tax credits, here Truist for Mammoth South. Each phase has long-term power purchase agreements with utilities, and commercial operation is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.
context: The financing covers the remaining phases of what Doral describes as a 1.3 GW complex expected to power about 275,000 homes. The company says the projects will use about 20,000 tons of Indiana steel and over 1 million US-made modules, and it plans to expand agrivoltaics, meaning farming such as grazing alongside the panels. Doral notes all three lead banks are repeat lenders and this is its first tax equity deal with Truist.

sources.title: Doral Renewables Secures $1.5 Billion of Debt and Tax Equity Financing for the Completion of Mammoth Solar

title: CBRE Investment Management funds buy minority stake in ENGIE's 2.4 GW US battery storage portfolio
target: 2.4 GW portfolio of 31 operating battery storage projects in Texas and California
summary: ENGIE North America has sold a non-controlling stake in a 2.4 GW portfolio of operating battery storage projects to funds managed by CBRE Investment Management. The 31 projects are located in Texas and California. ENGIE keeps a controlling share and will continue to run the assets.
details: The portfolio comprises 31 battery projects already in operation within the ERCOT grid region in Texas and the CAISO grid region in California, the two system operators that manage power markets in those states. ENGIE retains majority ownership and will keep operating and managing the batteries. The size of the stake sold, the price, storage energy capacity and advisers were not disclosed. The release describes the sale as completed.
context: ENGIE describes the deal as one of its largest US partnerships on operating assets and one of the biggest battery storage sales so far. The company says it fits its strategy of capital recycling, meaning selling stakes in finished projects to fund new ones, while bringing in a major investor partner. CBRE IM says the investment matches its focus on infrastructure with contracted revenue that benefits from digitalization and decarbonization trends.

title: Foss & Company buys investment tax credits from 174 Power Global's Ho'Ohana solar and storage project in Oahu

summary: Foss & Company has closed a purchase of investment tax credits generated by Ho'Ohana, a solar plant paired with battery storage on Oahu, Hawaii. The project was developed by 174 Power Global. No price or project size was disclosed.
details: Ho'Ohana combines solar generation and a battery system at the same site on Oahu. The deal is a tax credit transfer, meaning the developer sold the federal investment tax credit (a tax break tied to the cost of building the project) to Foss & Company in exchange for cash, a way of raising money for the project. The release does not give the capacity, storage duration, credit amount, advisers or other financing terms.
context: Foss & Company, a tax equity investor and fund sponsor that says it has deployed over $9 billion, presents the deal as part of its move into large, technology-heavy renewable assets. The parties say the co-located design supports grid stability on an island grid as Hawaii pursues more renewable power. Foss says the battery system's safety profile and long warranties gave it confidence despite the technical and regulatory challenges of island storage.
