context: Ammper Power is a retail electricity provider and scheduling entity in ERCOT, the grid operator covering most of Texas, and is a subsidiary of Ammper Energia. The company says the deal reflects its commitment to the ERCOT market and will help customers meet their renewable energy goals.

sources.title: Ammper Power secures a Solar Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) in Texas

title: ENEOS Renewable Energy buys 20% of GoliatVIND floating wind in Norway
summary: ENEOS Renewable Energy bought 20% of the GoliatVIND floating offshore wind project in Norway, its first overseas offshore wind investment.
details: ENEOS Renewable Energy bought 20% of the GoliatVIND floating offshore wind project in northern Norway, its first overseas offshore wind project, joining Source Galileo (40%), Odfjell Oceanwind (20%) and Kansai Electric Power (20%).
context: The 75 MW farm will use five 15 MW turbines on Odfjell's Deepsea Star semi-submersible foundations in about 400 m of water, aiming for operation in 2028. Floating foundations allow wind farms in water too deep for fixed bases.

sources.title: ENEOS acquires 20% stake in Norwegian floating offshore wind farm

title: Arevon closes $351 million construction financing for 251 MWdc Gibson Solar project in Indiana

buyers.name: CoBank
buyers.role: Coordinating lead arranger, administrative agent, collateral agent, documentation agent and LC issuing bank

summary: Arevon Energy has closed a $351 million financing package to build the 251 MWdc Gibson Solar Project in Gibson County, Indiana. The debt comes from CoBank, Societe Generale and PNC Bank.
details: The package includes a construction loan, which funds building costs before the plant runs, from CoBank, Societe Generale and PNC Bank, plus a letter of credit facility from CoBank. A letter of credit is a bank guarantee that a party will meet its payment obligations. Construction has started, and Signal Energy is the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor. Under a commercial agreement with Arevon, the utility NIPSCO will own and operate the plant once construction is finished. Amis, Patel & Brewer advised Arevon, Milbank advised the lenders and Husch Blackwell acted as local counsel.
context: Arevon says this is its sixth financing in the past year, bringing the total to about $3 billion, and its fourth financed utility-scale project under construction in Indiana. The company expects the project to create more than 250 construction jobs and pay more than $83 million to local governments over its life. The transfer to NIPSCO is presented as part of the utility's shift in its generation mix.

sources.title: Arevon Secures $351 Million Financing Package for its Gibson Solar Project in Indiana

title: Neoen signs four-year PPA with SmartestEnergy for half of Culcairn Solar Farm
summary: Neoen signed a four-year PPA with SmartestEnergy for 50% of the output of its 440 MWp Culcairn Solar Farm in New South Wales, starting in late 2026.
details: Neoen signed a four-year PPA with SmartestEnergy for half the output of its 440 MWp Culcairn Solar Farm on Wiradjuri land in the Riverina, New South Wales, from late 2026 when the farm should start operating.
context: Culcairn also holds a long-term energy services agreement from the NSW Electricity Infrastructure Roadmap tenders, which guarantees a minimum price. It will be Neoen's second-largest solar farm.

sources.title: Neoen, SmartestEnergy ink four-year PPA for Culcairn Solar Farm

title: SUSI Asia Energy Transition Fund to buy 39 MW Dam Nai wind farm from Scatec
summary: SUSI Partners agreed to buy the 39 MW Dam Nai wind farm in Ninh Thuận, Vietnam, and Scatec's Vietnam operating company.
details: SUSI Partners' Asia Energy Transition Fund agreed to buy the 39 MW Dam Nai wind farm in Ninh Thuận province, Vietnam, from Scatec, together with Scatec's Vietnamese operating company.
context: Dam Nai will be the first operating asset of the fund's SARA platform and an anchor for more projects nearby. The fund has seven investments in Vietnam, the Philippines, Thailand and Cambodia.

sources.title: SUSI acquires Vietnamese wind farm

title: X-Caliber Rural Capital closes US$100 million bridge loan for Fervo's Cape Station geothermal
summary: An affiliate of X-Caliber Rural Capital closed a US$100 million bridge loan for Phase I of Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Beaver County, Utah, the world's largest next-generation geothermal project.
details: X-Caliber Rural Capital's affiliate closed a US$100 million bridge loan for Phase I of Fervo Energy's Cape Station geothermal project about 7.5 miles north-east of Milford in Beaver County, Utah: US$65 million for wells, pads and roads and US$35 million for power plants and surface infrastructure.
context: Cape Station is the world's largest next-generation geothermal project. Phase I is 90 MW, due by June 2026, towards 400 MW of firm, round-the-clock power by 2028.

sources.title: Fervo receives loan from X-Caliber Rural Capital affiliate for Utah geothermal project

title: Santander provides €150 million revolving credit facility to Trina Solar's European project unit
summary: Banco Santander has provided a €150 million revolving credit facility to a Luxembourg subsidiary of Trina Solar. The money will fund utility-scale solar and battery storage projects developed by Trina's downstream unit ISBU, mainly in Italy, Spain, the UK, France and Germany.
details: A revolving facility lets the borrower draw, repay and redraw money up to a set limit. This one has two tranches. A non-recourse tranche, meaning lenders are repaid only from the projects themselves rather than the parent company, covers assets under construction. A guaranteed tranche, backed by the company, covers projects still in development and acquisitions. No project capacities or maturity dates were disclosed.
context: Trina says the facility is a first step in moving ISBU from building and selling projects to becoming an independent power producer, a company that owns and operates plants and sells their electricity, including through power purchase agreements. Santander describes the deal as part of its goal to facilitate €220 billion in green financing by 2030.

sources.title: Trina Solar Secures €150 Million Credit Facility to Support IPP Transition

title: NewEnergyBlue buys Inbicon biomass conversion technology and patents from Ørsted
target: Inbicon biomass-conversion technology and international patent portfolio
summary: NewEnergyBlue, a US designer of biomass refineries, has completed its purchase of the Inbicon biomass-conversion technology from Danish renewable energy company Ørsted. The deal includes the international patent portfolio and worldwide licensing rights. No price was disclosed.
details: Inbicon technology turns crop waste such as wheat straw and corn stalks into second-generation ethanol, meaning fuel made from non-food plant residue, along with lignin, a plant material that can replace oil-based products in polymers and binders. NewEnergyBlue previously held an exclusive license covering only the Americas, and now owns the patents with global rights. The technology was first used commercially at a refinery in Kalundborg, Denmark, opened in 2009. NewEnergyBlue plans to open its New Energy Freedom refinery in Mason City, Iowa, in 2026, converting corn stalks into bioethanol and lignin, with ethanol intended for low-carbon fuel markets and conversion into Dow Chemical plastics.
context: The purchase lets NewEnergyBlue pursue projects worldwide rather than only in the Americas. The company argues that large volumes of agricultural waste globally could feed such refineries and replace fossil fuels and chemicals. It also says international companies and scientists have shown interest in the technology and plans a biomass technology campus at the Iowa site after commissioning.

sources.title: NewEnergyBlue acquires Inbicon biomass conversion technology and international patent portfolio

title: OX2 sells two Australian solar projects totalling 137 MWp to European Energy
summary: OX2 sold the project rights for the 106 MWp Lancaster solar farm in Victoria and the 31 MWp Mulwala solar farm in New South Wales to European Energy.
details: OX2 sold the project rights to two Australian solar farms, 137 MWp in total, to European Energy: the 106 MWp Lancaster solar farm in Victoria and the 31 MWp Mulwala solar farm in New South Wales. Both should operate in 2026.
context: Together they should produce about 255 GWh a year. OX2 still has 1,185 MW in development in Australia.

sources.title: OX2 sells two Australia solar projects to European Energy

title: Google signs 128 MW solar PPA with X-ELIO for Bell project in Texas
summary: X-ELIO, a Brookfield-owned renewable developer, has signed a power purchase agreement with Google for 128 MW of electricity from its Bell solar plant in Texas. The power will support Google's operations in the state.
details: The Bell solar plant has a capacity of 128 MW and is expected to begin operating in the second half of 2025. The project will also include a 100 MW battery storage system meant to help supply power around the clock. The deal is a physical PPA, meaning the electricity itself is delivered to Google through a shared network rather than settled only financially. The contract length and price were not disclosed.
context: Google says the agreement supports its goal of running on carbon-free energy every hour of every day on all grids where it operates by 2030, and describes it as an example of a new, more scalable way of buying power. X-ELIO says the US is one of its key markets, citing a pipeline of more than 5 GW with about 1 GW it expects to reach notice to proceed, the go-ahead for construction, by the end of 2024.

sources.title: X-ELIO supports Google on its path to decarbonisation with a 128 MW PPA in Texas

title: Elum Energy raises $13 million Series B led by Energize Capital
summary: Paris-based software company Elum Energy has raised $13 million in a Series B funding round led by Chicago investor Energize Capital. Existing backers Alter Equity and Cota Capital also took part.
details: Elum Energy makes software that monitors and controls solar power plants, including hybrid sites that combine solar with batteries, serving commercial and industrial sites, microgrids and utility-scale projects. A Series B is a company's second major round of venture funding, typically used to scale up a business. The company says the money will fund a launch in the United States and further product development in energy storage and electric vehicle charging integration. Elum reports more than 2,500 projects in 50 countries and over 350 clients, and opened offices in Spain, Nigeria and Madagascar in 2023. Eileen Waris of Energize Capital sits on Elum's board.
context: The company argues that solar sites are becoming more complex as batteries and EV chargers are added, increasing demand for software that can manage several asset types together. Energize Capital, which is anchored by developer Invenergy, says it has backed 28 companies and deployed over $500 million. The round is a corporate software investment rather than funding for specific power projects.

sources.title: Elum Energy Secures $13 Million in Series B Funding to Accelerate Growth and Innovation in Renewable Energy Management Worldwide

title: SolaREIT closes long-term debt facility with MetLife Investment Management for solar and storage land financing
summary: SolaREIT, a Virginia-based real estate investment company focused on land for solar and battery storage projects, has closed a long-term debt facility with MetLife Investment Management. The size of the facility was not disclosed.
details: The facility will fund SolaREIT's real estate products for clean energy developers and landowners, which include buying land, buying out existing leases, and making land loans for solar and battery storage sites across the United States. SolaREIT describes the facility as repeatable and scalable, meaning it can be used again and grown as the company's lending expands. No amount, interest terms or advisers were named in the release.
context: SolaREIT says the facility lets it expand its financing offer quickly and improve the economics of the projects it supports, as solar and storage development becomes more capital-intensive. The company, founded in 2020 as a real estate investment trust (a company that owns or finances property and passes most income to investors), says it has provided real estate financing for more than $2.5 billion of solar and storage projects to date.

sources.title: SolaREIT Announces New Debt Facility for Solar and Battery Energy Storage System Real Estate Lease Financing

title: Civic Renewables acquires Orlando and Tampa solar installer Florida Power Management
summary: Civic Renewables, a parent company for local clean energy businesses backed by private equity firm GEF Capital, has bought Florida Power Management, a solar installer serving Orlando and Tampa. It is Civic's third acquisition since launching in 2024. No price was disclosed.
details: Florida Power Management installs solar systems in the Orlando and Tampa areas of Florida. The release says several large solar finance providers use it as their exclusive or main installer in Florida to finish jobs left by contractors that went out of business. Civic will serve as the parent company, giving FPM access to the resources of a larger group while it keeps its local operations. No deal terms, adviser names or capacity figures were given.
context: Civic earlier bought installers Green Rack Solar and Ipsun Solar in June and says it is looking for more local businesses across the US. The deal comes as, according to FPM's founder, many local solar companies are shrinking, and he expects the backing of a larger group to support growth. GEF Capital is a Washington, D.C. private equity firm focused on climate and pollution.

sources.title: Civic Renewables Acquires Florida Power Management

title: AMS Renewable Energy acquires New York solar construction firm Collective Solar
summary: New York City based solar and storage contractor AMS Renewable Energy has acquired Collective Solar, a solar construction firm in Oswego, New York. Collective Solar reports more than 160 MW of solar construction experience. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: AMS is an EPC company, meaning it handles engineering, procurement and construction of projects for developers and independent power producers, which are companies that own and sell power from plants. Collective Solar, founded in 2019, builds ground mounted distributed generation solar, meaning smaller plants connected to local grids rather than large utility-scale sites. Its founder and CEO Vincent Colletti will become Head of Construction at AMS. AMS says it is currently building over 100 MW of distributed solar in National Grid and NYSEG territories in upstate New York.
context: AMS says the deal brings civil and electrical construction work in-house, which it expects to improve efficiency and help it handle a growing pipeline in the northeast and mid-Atlantic. The company also says it aims to pursue growth opportunities nationwide and compete with other vertically integrated solar contractors. The deal is an acquisition of a construction services business rather than of power generating assets.

sources.title: AMS Renewable Energy Expands its Northeast Capacity with Strategic Acquisition of Collective Solar NY

title: Swift Current Energy closes $300 million revolving credit facility for US renewables pipeline

buyers.name: First Citizens Bank
buyers.role: structuring agent, bookrunner and coordinating lead arranger

advisors.name: Sidley Austin LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Swift Current Energy

summary: US clean energy developer Swift Current Energy has closed a $300 million senior secured revolving credit facility. The money will serve as flexible growth capital for its pipeline of wind, solar and battery storage projects in the United States.
details: The facility is a senior secured revolver, meaning a loan backed by company assets that can be drawn, repaid and drawn again as needed. First Citizens Bank acted as structuring agent, bookrunner and coordinating lead arranger, with Deutsche Bank AG and Truist Securities as coordinating lead arrangers and NatWest and SMBC as joint lead arrangers. Sidley Austin advised Swift Current, while Norton Rose Fulbright advised the lenders. The company says it has a 10 GW pipeline and expects to have commercialized 2.2 GW and to own and operate more than 1 GW of projects by the end of 2024.
context: The facility is corporate-level funding rather than financing for a single project, giving the developer capital to move projects through early stages. It marks Swift Current's first deal with Deutsche Bank, which described the deal as part of its business of providing corporate and pre-construction capital to renewable developers. Swift Current is majority-owned by Buckeye Energy Holdings, with IFM Net Zero Infrastructure Fund and Lookout Ridge Energy Partners as other owners.

sources.title: Swift Current Energy Secures $300 Million Facility to Support Renewable Energy Portfolio Buildout

title: Sunsure Energy secures ₹226 crore from Tata Capital for 75 MWp Uttar Pradesh solar
summary: Sunsure Energy secured ₹226 crore (about US$26.9 million) of long-term debt from Tata Capital for 75 MWp of operating open-access solar in Uttar Pradesh.
details: Sunsure Energy secured ₹226 crore (about US$26.91 million) of long-term debt from Tata Capital across five operating open-access solar projects totalling 75 MWp in Uttar Pradesh.
context: The plants already supply several industrial consumers. Refinancing operating plants frees capital for new projects.

sources.title: Sunsure Energy bags $26.91m loan for Uttar Pradesh solar projects

title: Arevon closes $299 million debt financing for Ratts 1 and Heirloom solar projects in Indiana

buyers.name: Crédit Agricole
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger, Administrative Agent, Green Loan Coordinator, Interest Rate Swap Coordinator

target: Ratts 1 Solar and Heirloom Solar projects
summary: Arevon Energy reached financial close on $299 million of debt financing for two solar projects, Ratts 1 and Heirloom, in Pike County, Indiana. The projects total 264 MWdc and are being financed by four banks led as coordinating lead arrangers.
details: The package includes a $119 million construction-to-term loan (a loan that funds building and then converts into long-term debt), a $159 million tax equity and tax credit bridge loan (short-term money repaid later by tax equity investors or buyers of tax credits), and a $21 million letter of credit facility. It is Arevon's first deal where the bridge takeout is not pre-committed, relying on the Inflation Reduction Act's rules that let tax credits be sold to third parties. BNY Mellon is collateral and depositary agent. Ratts 1 sells power to Indiana Municipal Power Agency under a long-term power purchase agreement and Meta buys the output of Heirloom. Construction is underway with full operation targeted for the third quarter of 2025.
context: Arevon says the structure gives it more flexibility and lets it sell tax credits closer to when the projects start operating, instead of locking in tax equity at close. The company describes this as its fifth financing in a year, bringing its climate finance deals to more than $2.6 billion. The projects sit in the MISO grid region where Arevon is expanding.

sources.title: Arevon Achieves $299 Million Financing Package for its Ratts 1 and Heirloom Solar Projects in Indiana

title: Q ENERGY closes €50.4 million for Europe's largest floating solar plant
summary: Q ENERGY reached debt financial close of €50.4 million, arranged by Crédit Agricole's Unifergie and Bpifrance, for the 74.3 MW Les Îlots Blandin floating solar plant in Haute-Marne.
details: Q ENERGY closed €50.4 million of debt from Crédit Agricole Transitions & Energies (through Unifergie) and Bpifrance for the 74.3 MW Les Îlots Blandin floating solar plant on 127 ha of former gravel pits in Haute-Marne, with 134,649 floating modules.
context: It will be Europe's largest floating solar plant; pre-commissioning is planned for Q1 2025. Floating solar uses water surfaces that have no other use.

sources.title: Q ENERGY raises over €50 million to finance Europe's biggest floating solar project

title: Enfinity Global closes €189.6 million financing for 157 MW Italian solar portfolio
target: Eight utility-scale solar plants in Lazio and Emilia Romagna, Italy
summary: Enfinity Global has closed €189.6 million of financing to build eight solar plants totalling 157.1 MW in Italy. The loans were arranged by BayernLB, ING and Rabobank as a group of lenders.
details: The eight utility-scale plants are located in the Lazio and Emilia Romagna regions and are expected to start operating in 2025. The package includes €127.4 million of non-recourse senior debt, meaning lenders are repaid from project cash flows rather than from the parent company, plus €17.1 million to cover VAT during construction and €45.1 million of letter of credit facilities backing PPAs, solar modules and future dismantling. The three banks lent together as a club deal, a shared arrangement among a small group of lenders. Output will be sold under long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts to sell electricity at agreed terms, with A2A, Nova Aeg and an unnamed Italian industrial customer. Astris acted as financial adviser and the law firms GOP and DWF were involved.
context: Enfinity describes the financing as a major milestone for its Italian business, where it says it holds 4.8 GW of solar and storage projects and leads in permitted capacity and solar PPA sales. The company expects the portfolio to produce about 271 GWh of electricity a year. BayernLB has supported about 400 MW of Enfinity financing in Italy to date, according to the company.

sources.title: Enfinity Global secures € 190 million financing for a 157 MW solar power portfolio in Italy

title: Lightsource bp sells UK solar farm and co-located battery to Schroders Greencoat
summary: Lightsource bp completed its largest UK solar project and sold it, with its co-located battery, to Schroders Greencoat, staying on as asset manager.
details: Lightsource bp completed its largest UK solar project, the 49.9 MWac Tiln Farm near Retford, Nottinghamshire, with a co-located battery, and sold both to Schroders Greencoat. Lightsource bp will provide asset management and O&M.
context: The farm supplies building products maker Forterra under a long-term PPA. Selling built projects lets the developer recycle capital into new ones.

sources.title: Lightsource bp sells first energy storage project

title: CPS Energy signs storage capacity agreements with Eolian for 350 MW of Texas batteries
target: Ferdinand and Padua 2 battery storage projects
summary: San Antonio municipal utility CPS Energy has signed two storage capacity agreements with developer Eolian covering 350 MW of new battery storage in South Bexar County, Texas. The deal adds to a 50 MW agreement the two companies signed in 2023.
details: The Ferdinand project is 200 MW and Padua 2 is 150 MW, and both are four-hour batteries, meaning they can discharge at full power for about four hours. Both will be newly built and are expected to start operating in the first half of 2026. Under a storage capacity agreement, the utility pays for the right to use the battery capacity, here for a 20-year period. A related community benefits agreement commits the project companies to give at least $175,000 per year to CPS Energy sponsored activities and scholarships for five years after operation begins. Dykema Gossett PLLC advised CPS Energy on the negotiations.
context: The agreements bring CPS Energy's contracted battery capacity to 400 MW, excluding 10 MW already operating, as part of its Vision 2027 generation plan. Eolian claims the 350 MW is the largest standalone battery buildout in the ERCOT Texas grid to date and says the sites were chosen to ease transmission congestion and support local reliability near retiring thermal plants. Eolian is employee-owned with funds managed by Global Infrastructure Partners.

sources.title: CPS ENERGY SECURES 350 MW OF FUTURE BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE FOR GENERATION PORTFOLIO

title: Air Products San Fu signs 10-year solar PPA with Tatung Forever Energy in Taiwan

buyers.name: Air Products San Fu Co. Ltd.

summary: Air Products San Fu, the Taiwan unit of US industrial gases group Air Products, has agreed to buy solar electricity from Tatung Forever Energy under a 10-year power purchase agreement. Tatung Forever Energy is a subsidiary of Taiwanese conglomerate Tatung Company.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a generator at set terms. Deliveries under this contract are due to start in the fourth quarter of 2024 and run for 10 years. The solar power will cover part of the electricity Air Products San Fu uses to produce industrial gases. The release does not state the capacity of the solar assets, the volume of power or the contract price.
context: Air Products says the deal will let its Taiwan unit avoid carbon dioxide emissions equal to the electricity-related emissions of more than 80,000 Taiwanese households over the contract term. The company presents it as support for decarbonizing Taiwan's industrial gases sector, which serves semiconductor and display makers. Tatung Forever Energy points to fast-growing corporate demand for renewable power in Taiwan.

sources.title: Air Products and Tatung Forever Energy Sign Power Purchase Agreement for Solar Electricity in Taiwan

title: Enfinity Global closes €500 million club financing for 1.5 GW Italian solar portfolio

advisors.name: Akereos
advisors.role: sole bookrunner, structurer and exclusive debt advisor to Enfinity Global

summary: Enfinity Global has reached financial close, meaning all funding agreements are signed and money can flow, on a €500 million financing from a group of five investors. Combined with project-level debt, the funds will pay for developing and building 1.5 GW of solar plants in Italy.
details: The money comes through a club deal, where a small group of investors lends together on shared terms, made up of Infranity, Schroders Capital, Rivage, BNP Paribas Asset Management and QIC. An accordion feature lets Enfinity increase the facility to €800 million later without negotiating a new deal. The financing will be combined with project finance, which is debt repaid from the cash flows of the individual plants. Akereos was sole bookrunner, structurer and debt adviser to Enfinity, Milbank was Enfinity's legal adviser and Ashurst advised the investors.
context: Enfinity says it owns 4.8 GW of solar and storage projects at various stages in Italy and is building 416 MW across 17 projects with long-term power purchase agreements with investment-grade customers. The company describes itself as one of Italy's leading independent power producers and reports a global portfolio of 25.1 GW. The deal gives it a large pool of capital to move part of its Italian pipeline into construction.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes a €500 million landmark investment to build, own, and operate 1.5 GW of solar power plants in Italy

title: Levanta Renewables buys six small solar projects in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand
summary: Levanta Renewables acquired six solar projects, 9.5 MWp in total, in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand from a regional developer.
details: Actis-backed Levanta Renewables agreed to buy six solar projects of 9.5 MWp from a regional developer: three in Malaysia, two in Indonesia and one in Thailand, all with long-term PPAs with Global 500 companies. Completion was due by end-2024.
context: They should produce over 13 GWh a year. It follows Levanta's deals for 27.8 MWp of rooftop solar in Vietnam and a 139 MWp portfolio in Thailand.

sources.title: Levanta Renewables acquires six solar projects in SEA

title: Lodestone Energy buys two 27 MWp solar sites in Manawatū
summary: Lodestone Energy acquired two grid-scale solar sites of 27 MWp each in the Manawatū region from Kiwi Solar.
details: Lodestone Energy bought two grid-scale solar sites of 27 MWp each in the Manawatū region from developer Kiwi Solar. Both have land options and are well advanced in connecting to Powerco's network; together they should produce about 84 GWh a year.
context: They will be developed with a third, consented Manawatū site, with construction starting in mid-2025. Lodestone runs farms near Kaitaia and Edgecumbe and plans 564 MWp across New Zealand.

sources.title: Lodestone acquires two grid-scale solar sites in Manawatu region

title: Google makes tax equity investment in Swift Current's 800 MWdc Double Black Diamond Solar project in Illinois
summary: Swift Current Energy has closed a tax equity investment from Google for its Double Black Diamond Solar project in southern Illinois. The project is rated at 800 MW of direct-current capacity, or 593 MW in alternating current. The investment amount was not disclosed.
details: The project sits about 30 miles west of Springfield in Sangamon and Morgan counties, is under construction, and is expected to start commercial operation by early 2025. Tax equity means an investor provides money in exchange for the project's federal tax credits, and this deal uses Inflation Reduction Act bonus credits for energy communities and US-made content. MUFG, Societe Generale, Truist and ING previously provided construction loans, and Swift Current will remain the long-term owner and operator. McCarthy Building Companies is the construction contractor, with First Solar modules and Nextracker trackers. Constellation NewEnergy will buy part of the power and renewable energy certificates to serve buyers including the City of Chicago, Cook County, CVS Health, Loyola University Chicago, PPG, State Farm and TransUnion.
context: Swift Current says the project is expected to be the largest solar plant east of the Mississippi River once running. The deal is notable because a large tech company is acting directly as a tax equity investor rather than only as a power buyer. Google says it seeks such partnerships to add clean energy at the pace of growing grid demand, and Swift Current describes the structure as a possible model for other large projects.

sources.title: SWIFT CURRENT ENERGY SECURES INVESTMENT FROM GOOGLE FOR 800 MW SOLAR PROJECT

title: Genesis Energy buys 127 MWp solar project from Helios Energy
summary: Genesis Energy secured an advanced 127 MWp solar project from Helios Energy, part of its plan to build 500 MW of grid-scale solar by FY2028.
details: Genesis Energy bought a consented 127 MWp solar project near Edgecumbe in the Bay of Plenty from Helios Energy. Genesis will own all of it and take all its output, about 230 GWh a year from 220,000 panels on 207 ha.
context: A final investment decision is expected in mid-2025, with generation from 2026. Genesis aims for 500 MW of grid-scale solar by FY2028 and to free up to 1,400 MW at its Huntly power station to support energy security.

sources.title: Genesis Energy acquires 127-MWp solar project in New Zealand

title: JERA Nex buys 395 MW of operating US solar from Lightsource bp
summary: JERA Nex acquired the 300 MW Oxbow solar farm in Louisiana and the 95 MW Happy solar farm in Arkansas from Lightsource bp, its first deal since launching.
details: JERA Nex, JERA's renewables business, bought two operating US solar farms totalling 395 MW from Lightsource bp: the 300 MW Oxbow farm in Louisiana, the state's largest, with corporate PPAs including eBay, and the 95 MW Happy farm in Arkansas, with a PPA with Conway Corp.
context: It was JERA Nex's first deal since its launch in April 2024. Lightsource bp keeps asset management and O&M.

sources.title: JERA renewable energy unit acquires 395 MW solar projects in US

title: Lightsource bp secures NZ$267 million for 168 MWdc Kōwhai Park solar
summary: Lightsource bp secured NZ$267 million for the 168 MWdc Kōwhai Park solar project in Christchurch, developed with Contact Energy.
details: Lightsource bp secured NZ$267 million from Westpac New Zealand, Mizuho, China Construction Bank and Intesa Sanpaolo for the 168 MWdc Kōwhai Park solar project at Christchurch Airport, developed with Contact Energy. It will have about 300,000 panels.
context: It is the first phase of the airport's Kōwhai Park renewable energy precinct and one of New Zealand's largest solar farms, and Lightsource bp's first NZ project to reach this stage.

sources.title: Lightsource bp secures NZ$267 million financing package for Kowhai Park solar farm

title: Birch Creek closes tax equity and debt financing for 42 MW Altona Solar in Missouri
summary: Birch Creek Energy has completed financing for its 42 MW Altona Solar project in Audrain County, Missouri, which is now fully operating. Celtic Bank provided tax equity and West Town Bank & Trust provided permanent debt. No deal value was disclosed.
details: Altona Solar is a 42 MWdc utility-scale solar plant on 208 acres that connects to the Ameren Missouri grid. Celtic Bank supplied tax equity, meaning it invested in exchange for the project's federal tax benefits, and had also backed Birch Creek's 49 MW Earp Solar project in Illinois. West Town Bank & Trust supplied permanent debt, a long-term loan that replaces shorter construction funding. The company says the plant produces enough power for more than 6,300 homes.
context: Altona is Birch Creek's first project to reach full operation in its home state of Missouri and the second of several projects the company plans to bring online this year. The projects support its strategy of acting as an independent power producer, owning and operating plants rather than only developing them. Both lenders indicated interest in financing further Birch Creek projects.

sources.title: Birch Creek Completes Altona Solar Financing

title: AGL agrees to buy Firm Power and Terrain Solar with 8.1 GW pipeline
summary: AGL signed a binding agreement to buy Firm Power and Terrain Solar, with a combined 8.1 GW development pipeline in Australia, for $250 million.
details: AGL Energy agreed to buy all of Firm Power, a battery developer with 21 projects, and Terrain Solar, a solar developer with 6 projects, for A$250 million in cash, a combined 8.1 GW development pipeline in Australia.
context: AGL wants firming capacity, mainly batteries, to back up new renewables as coal plants leave the National Electricity Market.

sources.title: AGL to acquire Australia's Firm Power and Terrain Solar

title: mBank finances European Energy's 70 MW of Polish solar
summary: mBank agreed financing for European Energy's Łobez (16 MW) and Dębnica Kaszubska (54.2 MW) solar farms in Pomerania.
details: mBank is providing €33.3 million to European Energy to build two solar farms in Poland, 70 MW in total: Łobez (16 MW) in West Pomerania and Dębnica Kaszubska (54.2 MW) in Pomerania, due for completion in Q4 2024.
context: They should produce about 67 GWh a year and take European Energy to 200 MW of operating capacity in Poland.

sources.title: European Energy to construct two solar farms in Poland with financing from mBank

title: Dominion Energy wins 176,505-acre offshore wind lease off Virginia Beach for $17.7 million

buyers.name: Virginia Electric and Power Company
buyers.role: lease winner, subsidiary of Dominion Energy

target: 176,505-acre offshore wind lease area off Virginia Beach
summary: Virginia Electric and Power Company, a Dominion Energy subsidiary, won a federal lease auction for a 176,505-acre offshore wind area off Virginia Beach with a bid of $17.7 million. The site sits east of the 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project now under construction.
details: The bid works out to about $100 per acre. The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, the federal agency that leases offshore areas for energy use, says the site could host between 2.1 GW and 4.0 GW of offshore wind. The area lies about 35 nautical miles from the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay. Dominion says it has no estimated timeline or cost for developing the lease. Any project would be regulated, meaning its costs would be recovered through customer rates subject to regulator approval.
context: Dominion says it wants more offshore wind options to meet what it calls unprecedented growth in customer electricity demand, in line with the Virginia Clean Economy Act. The lease follows its July acquisition of the 40,000-acre Kitty Hawk Wind North area from Avangrid, to be renamed CVOW South with a potential 800 MW. The company says its main focus remains finishing the 2.6 GW CVOW project, which it expects to enter service by the end of 2026.

sources.title: Dominion Energy Secures 176,505-acre Lease Area from the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management For Potential Regulated Offshore Wind Development

title: Cero Generation reaches financial close on 244.7 MWp Palencia solar portfolio
summary: Cero Generation reached financial close on five solar projects in Palencia, Spain, 244.7 MWp in total, with Banco Sabadell, Rabobank and ING.
details: Cero Generation reached financial close with Banco Sabadell, Rabobank and ING on five solar projects totalling 244.7 MWp in Palencia, Spain, backed by a 10-year PPA with an international technology company. Elmya and Metlen are EPC contractors and LONGi supplies modules.
context: The plants span several Palencia municipalities including Becerril de Campos and Grijota and should produce over 480 GWh a year.

sources.title: Cero seals financing to develop Spanish renewable energy projects

title: LS Power agrees to buy Algonquin's renewable energy business in the US and Canada
target: Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. renewable energy business
summary: LS Power has agreed to acquire the renewable energy business of Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. The business holds 44 operating assets with more than 3,000 MW of capacity across the US and Canada, plus an 8,000 MW development pipeline. No price was disclosed in the release.
details: The operating portfolio is mostly wind and solar, with about 2,700 MW in the US across the NYISO, MISO, PJM, ERCOT and CAISO power markets and about 300 MW in Canada. The 8,000 MW pipeline covers wind, solar, battery storage and renewable natural gas projects at various stages of development. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2024 or the first quarter of 2025, subject to customary conditions including approval by the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and competition authorities. Milbank is legal adviser and Scotiabank and BMO Capital Markets are financial advisers to LS Power.
context: LS Power describes the purchase as a major expansion of its renewables holdings, adding to a fleet it says exceeds 19,000 MW. The company says it believes the platform will help meet rising electricity demand. The business will sit alongside LS Power's other energy transition platforms such as REV Renewables and Rise Light & Power.

sources.title: LS Power Agrees to Acquire Large Scale Renewable Energy Business from Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp.

title: JBIC lends US$173.4 million via PFC for 300 MW Ostro Kannada wind project
summary: JBIC signed a ¥25.5 billion (about US$173 million) loan with Power Finance Corporation for Ostro Kannada Power's 300.3 MW wind project in Karnataka.
details: JBIC signed a ¥25.5 billion (about US$173.4 million) loan through Power Finance Corporation for Ostro Kannada Power's 300.3 MW wind farm in Karnataka, with JBIC providing ¥13.5 billion and SMBC, Bank of Yokohama, Shiga Bank and Bank of Fukuoka the rest.
context: It draws on JBIC's 2022 credit line with PFC for renewables under its GREEN programme; JBIC also guarantees the private banks' share.

sources.title: India secures $173.4m Japanese loan for wind energy project

title: Origis Energy closes $71 million tax equity deal with U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance for Rice Creek Solar in Florida
summary: Origis Energy has closed a $71 million tax equity financing with U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance, a U.S. Bank subsidiary, for its Rice Creek Solar project. The project is a 74.9 MWac solar plant in Putnam County, Florida.
details: Tax equity is an arrangement where an investor puts money into a project in exchange for the right to use its federal tax credits and other tax benefits. Rice Creek Solar has about 213,000 panels and its output is contracted with the Florida Municipal Power Agency on behalf of 12 member municipal utilities. It is the third site in the Florida Municipal Solar Project, and Origis builds, owns and operates it. The company says completion of construction is imminent. Latham & Watkins and local counsel Akerman advised Origis, while Sheppard Mullin and local counsel Balch & Bingham advised U.S. Bank.
context: Origis says the financing helps it scale its large solar portfolio, and describes the Florida Municipal Solar Project as one of the largest municipally backed solar efforts in the country. The company says the plant will generate enough power for roughly 14,000 homes, helping public utilities meet rising demand in Florida.

sources.title: Origis Energy Closes $71 Million Tax Equity Financing with U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance for Rice Creek Solar in Florida

title: Radial Power acquires 22.3 MW New York community solar portfolio from Galehead Development
target: Four community solar projects in New York totaling 22.3 MW
summary: Radial Power has agreed to buy four community solar projects in New York State with a combined capacity of 22.3 MW from developer Galehead Development. Radial Power will take over final development and construction once each transaction closes.
details: The four projects qualify for New York's Value of Distributed Energy Resources (VDER) program, a state scheme that pays local solar projects based on the value their power provides to the grid. Community solar projects let nearby households and businesses subscribe to a share of a solar farm's output and receive bill credits. Galehead worked with local communities and the utility National Grid to secure approvals. Galehead will keep ownership of the land under 14 MW of the portfolio through its Century LandCo unit and continue managing it. The parties' framework agreement also covers a further 18.3 MW of VDER community solar capacity that is expected to close before the end of 2024. No price was disclosed.
context: The deal adds to Radial Power's portfolio of distributed clean energy assets, which it builds and operates for large real estate owners, and the companies describe it as supporting New York's clean energy goals. For Galehead, which says it has developed and sold 7 GW of solar, wind and storage projects since 2016, the sale reflects its model of developing early-stage projects and selling them to downstream owners while sometimes retaining the land.

sources.title: Radial Power Announces 22.3 MW Community Solar Acquisition from Galehead Development

title: Aypa Power secures $323 million financing for 150 MW Kuna battery storage project in Idaho

buyers.name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, New York Branch

summary: Aypa Power, owned by Blackstone, has lined up $323 million in financing commitments for its Kuna battery storage project near Boise, Idaho. The facility has 150 MW of power and 600 MWh of storage.
details: The package combines a $233 million green loan with $90 million in tax equity, which is investment from a party that receives the project's tax credits in return for funding. The green loan includes a construction and term loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term debt covering the gap until tax equity is paid in), and a letter of credit facility. ING Capital, Société Générale and ICBC New York Branch led the debt, Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas is administrative agent, and U.S. Bank is depositary and collateral agent. The project holds a long-term energy storage agreement with Idaho Power signed in April 2023 and is expected to start operating in mid-2025.
context: The company says Kuna will be the largest battery storage project in Idaho once online, helping meet the state's 2025 capacity needs. Aypa points to rising power demand from data centers and industry in the state. It expects the project to support over 150 construction jobs and about $30 million in local economic development over its life.

sources.title: AYPA POWER SECURES $323 MILLION IN FINANCING FOR MAJOR ENERGY STORAGE PROJECT IN IDAHO

title: Tokyo Gas invests in WindFloat Atlantic operator Windplus
summary: Tokyo Gas agreed with Ocean Winds to invest in Windplus, operator of the WindFloat Atlantic floating offshore wind farm in Portugal.
details: Tokyo Gas agreed with Ocean Winds to invest in Windplus, which runs the WindFloat Atlantic floating offshore wind farm in Portugal, its first overseas floating wind investment.
context: WindFloat Atlantic uses 10 MW-class turbines on Principle Power's WindFloat foundations and has operated in waves up to 20 m. Tokyo Gas wants operating experience for Japan's deep waters.

sources.title: Tokyo Gas makes investment in offshore wind power

title: Generac acquires microgrid controller provider Ageto
summary: Generac Power Systems has bought Ageto, a company that makes microgrid controllers for commercial and industrial sites. The deal closed on August 1, 2024, and financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Ageto's controllers and software coordinate, optimize and monitor different energy assets on a site, such as generators, renewable energy sources, battery storage and electric vehicle chargers, from a single interface. A microgrid is a local energy system that can run alongside or independently of the main power grid. Generac has used Ageto controllers in its battery energy storage systems and generator sets since 2021. The acquisition closed on August 1, 2024, and no price, seller or advisers were named.
context: Generac says adding Ageto's software lets it offer site-level integration and control rather than only hardware to domestic commercial and industrial customers with several energy assets. The company claims the deal will simplify asset management for customers and give it a competitive advantage in the microgrid and storage market.

sources.title: Generac Strengthens Microgrid and Energy Storage Solutions with Acquisition of Ageto

title: ENEOS Renewable Energy signs PPA with Amazon for 9.5 MW Japanese solar
summary: ENEOS Renewable Energy signed a corporate PPA with Amazon for about 20,000 MWh a year from the 9.5 MW Kudamatsu Fourth Mega Solar plant in Yamaguchi.
details: ENEOS Renewable Energy signed a corporate PPA with Amazon for about 20,000 MWh a year from the 9.5 MW Kudamatsu Fourth Mega Solar plant in Kudamatsu City, Yamaguchi, under construction for operation by November 2025.
context: It follows ENEOS's May 2024 solar supply deal with West Japan Railway and Kansai Electric Power.

sources.title: ENEOS inks PPA to supply renewable energy to Amazon

title: FRV Australia refinances 1 GW solar portfolio with A$1.2 billion
summary: FRV Australia closed an A$1.2 billion refinancing for its 1 GW portfolio of operating and under-construction solar plants, including Lilyvale, Moree, Sebastopol and Goonumbla.
details: FRV Australia closed A$1.2 billion (about US$781 million) of refinancing from 11 lenders, including ING, Westpac, MUFG, the Clean Energy Finance Corporation and China Construction Bank, for its 1 GW of operating and under-construction solar at Lilyvale, Moree, Sebastopol, Goonumbla, Metz, Winton, Walla Walla and Dalby.
context: The package combines a term loan replacing existing debt with letter of credit and working capital facilities for new development. Macquarie Capital advised FRV.

sources.title: FRV Australia secures $781m refinancing for 1-GW solar portfolio

title: AXIAN Energy and Fortis Green buy stakes in Gigawatt Global Rwanda solar plant
summary: AXIAN Energy and Fortis Green Renewables acquired stakes in Gigawatt Global Rwanda, the solar plant at the Agahozo-Shalom Youth Village in Rwamagana.
details: Fortis Green Renewables (51%) and AXIAN Energy's NEA Rwanda (49%) completed on 30 July 2024 their purchase of Gigawatt Global Rwanda, a solar plant at the Agahozo-Shalom Youth Village in Rwamagana, from Scatec, Norfund and KLP Norfund.
context: NEA Rwanda also owns Scatec Solar Rwanda and runs the plant's operation and maintenance. The purchase agreements were signed in December 2023 and February 2024.

sources.title: AXIAN Energy and Fortis Green acquire solar plant assets in Rwanda

title: Goldman Sachs Alternatives invests US$440 million in BrightNight
summary: Goldman Sachs Alternatives made a US$440 million strategic investment in BrightNight, which builds dispatchable renewable projects.
details: The Infrastructure business of Goldman Sachs Alternatives agreed a US$440 million strategic investment in BrightNight, a developer of dispatchable renewable power for utilities and commercial and industrial customers. With existing commitments it should fully fund BrightNight's five-year plan; closing was expected in September 2024.
context: BrightNight has a 31 GW portfolio and uses its own AI software, PowerAlpha, to design projects. Dispatchable means the plants, usually paired with batteries, can deliver power when needed.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs invests in BrightNight solar energy

title: ACEN buys 60% of Real Wind Energy from Maraj Energy
summary: ACEN bought Maraj Energy's 60% of Real Wind Energy, which is developing 500 MW of wind in Real, Quezon.
details: ACEN bought 60% of Real Wind Energy from Maraj Energy and Development, making it wholly owned. RWEI is developing 500 MW of wind in Real, Quezon. The cash price was under 10% of book value as of 31 March 2024; ACEN also lent RWEI ₱70 million.
context: ACEN plans to raise US$15 billion to grow its clean energy capacity from 5 GW to 20 GW in six years; the wind project could add 500 MW.

sources.title: ACEN acquires 60% stake in 500-MW wind project developer

title: Great Bay Renewables invests $30 million in Midwest distributed solar developer Nokomis Energy
summary: Great Bay Renewables has completed a $30 million investment in Nokomis Energy, a Minneapolis-based developer of distribution-grid clean energy projects. The funding is intended to help Nokomis grow its project portfolio across the Upper Midwest.
details: Nokomis develops projects of 1 to 30 MW that connect to the local distribution grid rather than high-voltage transmission lines, covering community solar, behind-the-meter systems (installed on a customer's side of the meter) and direct-to-utility projects. Since 2017 it says it has developed more than 45 projects. Great Bay typically provides capital in exchange for royalties, meaning a share of future revenue from generating facilities, though the release does not spell out the exact structure of this deal. No advisers or project capacity totals are disclosed.
context: Great Bay says this is its first dedicated investment in distributed solar and describes it as a diversification away from its utility-scale developer partnerships. The investor reports having committed more than $400 million in royalty financing across over 35 projects totaling nearly 8.2 GW. Great Bay is backed by Altius Renewable Royalties and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo.

sources.title: Nokomis Energy Announces $30 Million Investment from Great Bay Renewables

title: Acciona Energía sells 175 MW Spanish hydro portfolio to Elawan for €287 million
summary: Acciona Energía agreed to sell 100% of Acciona Saltos de Agua, 23 hydro plants totalling 175 MW, to ORIX's Elawan Energy for €287 million, debt-free.
details: Acciona Energía agreed to sell 100% of Acciona Saltos de Agua, 23 hydro plants of 175 MW in Aragón, Cantabria and Catalonia, to ORIX's Elawan Energy for €287 million, debt-free. They produce about 500 GWh a year; 77% of capacity is reservoir and 23% run-of-river.
context: The plants have an average of 23 years left on their concessions, the state licences to use the water. Acciona expects a capital gain of about €170 million from the asset rotation.

sources.title: Acciona sells hydro portfolio

title: esVolta closes $258 million credit facilities for 980 MWh Texas battery storage portfolio

buyers.name: MUFG Bank, Ltd.
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger and Green Loan Coordinator

target: Anole, Desert Willow and Burksol battery storage projects
summary: esVolta has completed $258 million of senior secured credit facilities for three standalone battery storage projects in Texas. The portfolio totals 980 MWh and is led by MUFG with a group of other banks.
details: The financing covers the Anole, Desert Willow and Burksol projects, which are under construction and will sell fast-response energy and ancillary (grid support) services into the ERCOT market. The package includes a construction loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term debt repaid once tax equity investors, who fund projects in exchange for tax credits, come in), letters of credit and a long-term loan. MUFG acted as coordinating lead arranger and green loan coordinator, with Nomura and KeyBanc as coordinating lead arrangers, Investec as joint lead arranger and Cadence Bank participating. Morgan, Lewis & Bockius advised esVolta and Winston & Strawn advised MUFG.
context: esVolta, a Generate Capital portfolio company, says the financing will help it speed up growth and build its large-scale storage portfolio at lower cost. The company reports about 1.5 GWh of operating and in-construction storage. It states the projects aim to reduce congestion and strengthen the Texas grid.

sources.title: esVolta Secures $258 Million Credit Facilities for ERCOT Storage Portfolio

title: Eolian closes $390 million green loan and revolving credit facility with six global banks
summary: Eolian, a US renewable energy and battery storage company whose funds are managed by Global Infrastructure Partners, has closed $390 million of new financing with six international banks. The package is made up of a $315 million green loan and a $75 million revolving credit facility backed by operating US renewable projects.
details: The loan is secured by a varied set of eligible green project assets created by Eolian, and the company says it is backed by cash flows from operating renewable projects across the US. A revolving credit facility is a credit line the borrower can draw, repay and draw again. The deal is described as aligned with the Green Loan Principles, an industry standard for how green loan money is used and reported. MUFG referred to the transactions as the Lipari II and Lipari Royalty Holdco financings. The lenders are Santander, MUFG, National Australia Bank, Natixis, Lloyds Bank and SMBC.
context: The financing follows a $515 million green loan that Eolian closed with the same banks in June 2023, making this a second phase of the arrangement. Eolian says the facilities validate its development strategy, and the banks describe the deal as part of their support for renewable energy growth in the US.

sources.title: Eolian and Group of Global Banks Announce Closing of $390 Million Renewable Energy Financing

title: Hudson Sustainable Group sells Japanese solar PV portfolio to Solar Schumann
target: Hudson Solar Japan solar PV portfolio
summary: Hudson Sustainable Group, through its subsidiary Hudson Solar Japan, has sold its solar PV portfolio in Japan to Tokyo-based asset manager Solar Schumann GK. The price and total capacity were not disclosed.
details: The portfolio traces back to 2019, when Hudson Solar Japan bought 33 solar projects operating under Japan's feed-in tariff scheme, a government program that pays a fixed price for the power produced. The release describes the assets as geographically spread across Japan. Mizuho Securities supported the fundraising on the buyer side. No completion date was given.
context: HSG says this is its second exit in Japan and that the sale lets it concentrate on growing Horizon Energy KK, its business aimed at the post-feed-in-tariff market where projects sell power without fixed government prices. The company presents the deal as evidence that its curated portfolios draw institutional investors.

sources.title: Hudson Sustainable Group Announces Sale of Solar PV Portfolio to Solar Schumann

title: ArcLight launches SkyVest Renewables and acquires 160 MW operating Texas wind farm
target: 160 MW operating wind farm in the Midland Basin, Texas
summary: Infrastructure investor ArcLight Capital Partners has set up SkyVest Renewables, a platform to run and improve operating wind and solar assets, with an initial capital commitment of $500 million. As its first deal, ArcLight closed the purchase of a 160 MW operating wind farm in Texas.
details: The wind farm sits in the Midland Basin in Texas and began commercial operation in 2020. The seller and the purchase price were not disclosed. The $500 million commitment is meant for new acquisitions and brownfield development, meaning upgrades or expansion at existing sites. SkyVest is led by President Michael Murphy, formerly of Clearway Energy, and CFO Michael Current, formerly of JERA Americas, with advisers including Mark Albenze, Tom Kiernan and Scott Hall.
context: ArcLight says SkyVest will target operating utility-scale wind and solar projects in North America and aims to raise their cash flow through better operations and commercial management. The firm argues that the maturing renewables market rewards an operations-focused approach over pure growth. It compares the initiative to its earlier platforms Leeward, TerraGen and Great River Hydro.

sources.title: ArcLight Announces Operating Focused Renewables Initiative and New Wind Investment

title: Ecovyst makes $4.5 million equity investment in hydrogen catalyst maker Pajarito Powder
summary: Ecovyst, a US maker of specialty catalysts and advanced materials, has invested $4.5 million in equity in Pajarito Powder. The Albuquerque, New Mexico company develops catalysts and catalyst supports used in electrolyzers, which split water to make green hydrogen, and in fuel cells.
details: Pajarito Powder plans to use the money to advance its technology, deepen customer relationships and grow its business. As part of the deal Ecovyst will appoint a representative to Pajarito's board of directors. The two companies also plan joint development agreements, including new uses for Pajarito's mesoporous carbon, a porous carbon material, such as carbon capture. The stake size and valuation were not disclosed.
context: Ecovyst says the investment extends its Advanced Materials & Catalysts business into the emerging hydrogen market, citing its belief that electrolytic hydrogen will become a widely used low-carbon fuel for heavy transport and industry. Pajarito, a venture-backed startup, already counts Hyundai Motor Company and N.V. Bekaert among its strategic investors and says Ecovyst's manufacturing and scale-up skills could speed its growth.

sources.title: Ecovyst Announces Equity Investment in Pajarito Powder, a Hydrogen Catalyst Company

title: Frontier Energy mandates Infradebt for Waroona Renewable Energy Project
summary: Frontier Energy signed a $215 million senior debt mandate with Infradebt for the first stage of the Waroona Renewable Energy Project in Western Australia, with a 17-year tenor.
details: Frontier Energy signed an A$215 million senior debt mandate with Infradebt, mostly from its Energy Transition Fund, for stage one of the A$304 million Waroona Renewable Energy Project 120 km south of Perth: a 120 MW solar farm and an 80 MW / 360 MWh battery. The 17-year tenor includes two years of construction.
context: The final debt size depends on the Reserve Capacity Price set by AEMO, which pays plants to be available in Western Australia's grid. Infradebt also agreed to fund later Frontier batteries.

sources.title: Frontier Energy secures $215m loan for Waroona Renewable Energy Project

title: TotalEnergies to buy 50% of 795 MW OranjeWind from RWE
summary: TotalEnergies agreed to buy 50% of OranjeWind, a 795 MW Dutch offshore wind farm under development, from RWE, and will use its share to power green hydrogen electrolysers.
details: TotalEnergies agreed to buy 50% of OranjeWind, a 795 MW offshore wind farm about 53 km off the Dutch coast that RWE won in the 2022 Hollandse Kust West VII tender. TotalEnergies will use its share of the power for 350 MW of electrolysers producing about 40,000 tonnes a year of green hydrogen for its refineries.
context: Replacing refinery hydrogen made from gas should avoid about 400,000 tonnes of CO2 a year, part of TotalEnergies' 2030 target to cut operational emissions 40% from 2015.

sources.title: TotalEnergies acquires stake in OranjeWind offshore wind farm

title: Octopus Energy Generation buys 100 French farm rooftop solar projects from ELECO
summary: Octopus Energy's generation arm acquired Sungen 10, owning 100 rooftop solar projects on French farms, from ELECO.
details: Octopus Energy Generation, for its Sky fund, bought Sungen 10 from ELECO, with 100 rooftop solar projects on French farms, and will work with ELECO to build up to 100 MW more on hundreds of farms by 2030.
context: The partners build sheds with solar roofs on farmland, which farmers use free for storage. Octopus plans to invest €1 billion in France by 2025.

sources.title: Octopus energy invests in French solar

title: Keppel MET Renewables buys two solar projects in northern Italy
summary: Keppel MET Renewables, a joint venture of MET Group and Keppel, bought 100% of two solar projects in Piedmont and another northern Italian region.
details: Keppel MET Renewables, a 50:50 venture of MET Group and Keppel's Infrastructure Division, bought 100% of two ready-to-build solar projects of 20 MWp in Piedmont and Lombardy, developed by ReFeel New Energy, due to operate in 2025.
context: They should produce about 30 GWh a year. KMR also has 277 MWp of early- to mid-stage solar in Italy.

sources.title: Keppel MET Renewables acquires PV projects in Northern Italy

title: Aypa Power closes upsized $650 million corporate credit facility
summary: Aypa Power, a Blackstone-owned developer of battery storage and hybrid renewable projects, has closed a $650 million corporate credit facility. It replaces the company's previous $320 million facility and will fund growth across the United States and Canada.
details: The facility is split into a $350 million letter of credit line (bank guarantees often needed to secure grid connections and contracts), a $100 million revolver (a credit line that can be drawn and repaid repeatedly) and a $200 million term loan. Six banks and lenders acted as coordinating lead arrangers, bookrunners and green loan coordinators, meaning they organized the loan and its green labelling. Kirkland & Ellis was Aypa's legal counsel and PEI Global Partners its financial adviser, while Norton Rose Fulbright advised the lenders.
context: Aypa calls this the largest corporate facility in the energy storage industry. The company says the loan is backed by a 22 GW pipeline of projects at various stages and that it aims to deliver more than 3 GW of battery storage and hybrid projects within the next 24 months.

sources.title: AYPA POWER SECURES $650M IN UPSIZED CORPORATE FACILITY, THE LARGEST IN THE ENERGY STORAGE INDUSTRY

title: IREDA approves ₹290 crore for up to 10% of 900 MW Upper Karnali hydro in Nepal
summary: IREDA approved an investment of ₹290 crore (about US$35 million) for up to 10% of the 900 MW Upper Karnali hydro project in Nepal, with SJVN.
details: IREDA approved an investment of ₹290 crore (about US$35.4 million) for up to 10% of the 900 MW Upper Karnali hydro project in Nepal, in collaboration with SJVN, subject to Indian government and regulatory approval.
context: IREDA is India's state-owned renewable energy lender. IREDA says the project contributes to regional energy security.

sources.title: India to invest $35.4m in Nepal’s 900-MW hydro project

title: Intersect Power closes US$837 million for three Texas batteries
summary: Intersect Power closed two transactions totalling US$837 million of construction debt, tax equity and term debt for three standalone batteries in Texas.
details: Intersect Power closed two transactions totalling US$837 million, including portfolio construction debt, tax equity and term debt, for three standalone Texas batteries, Lumina I, Lumina II and Radian, each 320 MWh with two hours' duration and 86 Tesla Megapacks, due online in 2024.
context: Lumina II and Radian will trade through Tesla's Autobidder platform. They add flexibility to Intersect's Texas fleet of 1.2 GWp of solar and 1 GWh of storage.

sources.title: Intersect Power secures financing for BESS projects in Texas

title: Statkraft signs fixed-price PPA with Boralex for 106 MW Limekiln wind farm
summary: Statkraft signed a fixed-price PPA with Boralex for the 106 MW Limekiln wind farm under construction in the Scottish Highlands.
details: Statkraft signed a fixed-price PPA with Boralex for part of the output and REGOs of the 106 MW Limekiln wind farm south of Reay in the Scottish Highlands, under construction for commissioning by end-2024. Gowling WLG advised Statkraft.
context: REGOs certify that power is renewable. The PPA lets Limekiln curtail itself when prices go negative, avoiding costs and easing grid pressure.

sources.title: Statkraft signs fix-priced wind PPA

title: 3M makes strategic investment in electrolyzer maker Ohmium
summary: 3M has completed a strategic investment of undisclosed size in Ohmium International, a US-based company that builds electrolyzers for green hydrogen production. The amount and stake were not disclosed.
details: Ohmium designs and manufactures proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers, which are machines that use electricity, ideally from renewables, to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. The company is headquartered in the United States, makes its equipment in India and reports a project pipeline of more than 2 GW across three continents. The investment was made through 3M New Growth Ventures. Ohmium previously raised 250 million US dollars in a Series C round led by TPG Rise Climate in April 2023.
context: 3M says the deal fits its push into climate technology and could open collaboration on catalysts and other electrolyzer materials, as well as help it explore decarbonizing its own operations. The company links the investment to the US Department of Energy goal of cutting green hydrogen costs to 1 dollar per kilogram. 3M is also an investor in the TPG Rise Climate fund, which led Ohmium's earlier funding round.

sources.title: 3M invests in green hydrogen leader Ohmium in continuing effort to advance breakthrough climate technologies

title: JinkoSolar, RELC and Vision Industries agree to form Saudi joint venture for 10 GW solar cell and module factory

buyers.name: JinkoSolar Middle East DMCC
buyers.role: 40% joint venture partner, subsidiary of JinkoSolar Holding

buyers.name: Renewable Energy Localization Company (RELC)
buyers.role: 40% joint venture partner, wholly owned by Public Investment Fund

target: Saudi Arabian joint venture for high-efficiency solar cell and module manufacturing
summary: A Middle East subsidiary of JinkoSolar has signed a shareholders agreement with RELC, a unit of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, and Vision Industries to set up a joint venture in Saudi Arabia. The venture plans to build a solar cell and module factory with an expected total investment of about US$1 billion and an annual output of 10 GW of each product.
details: Jinko Middle East and RELC will each hold 40% of the joint venture and Vision Industries will hold the remaining 20%. The facility will make high-efficiency solar cells and the panels (modules) they go into, and is expected to reach 10 GW of yearly production capacity for each. The roughly US$1 billion investment is to be funded by a mix of the venture's own funds and outside financing. Formation of the venture still depends on customary conditions, including regulatory approvals, and the production plan and timeline will depend on market conditions.
context: JinkoSolar presents the venture as a step in its strategy to spread manufacturing across more countries and strengthen its global competitiveness. RELC describes the project as supporting Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 economic diversification plan by bringing JinkoSolar's N-type cell technology into local production. The 10 GW figure refers to factory output, not power generation capacity.

sources.title: JinkoSolar to Form a Joint Venture with RELC and VI in Saudi Arabia for Production of 10 GW of High-efficiency Solar Cells and Solar Modules

title: Enfinity Global secures US$164 million financing for 250 MW Japan solar portfolio
target: 250 MW solar PV portfolio in Japan
summary: Enfinity Global has closed a US$164 million (about JPY 26.24 billion) financing for a 250 MW portfolio of solar plants in Japan. The funding was arranged with Macquarie Capital and a group of investors led by Shinhan Asset Management.
details: The portfolio includes seven utility-scale solar plants already in operation and one still being built. The company states the portfolio has an enterprise value, meaning the combined worth of its equity and debt, of more than US$1 billion. It is expected to generate over 300 GWh of electricity per year, which the company says could supply around 60,000 Japanese homes. The release does not describe the loan structure, offtake contracts or advisers.
context: Enfinity Global says the financing supports further expansion of its platform in Japan. Its CEO linked the deal to growing power demand in Japan, including from data centers. The US-based developer reports a 24.1 GW portfolio of renewable and storage projects across various stages.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes $164 million financing for a 250 MW solar PV portfolio in Japan

title: HSBC refinances Leader Energy's 50 MW Vinh Hao 6 solar plant in Vietnam
summary: HSBC Vietnam lent VND 593 billion (about US$23 million) on a seven-year term loan to refinance Leader Energy's 50 MW Vinh Hao 6 solar plant.
details: HSBC Vietnam signed a VND593 billion (about US$23.13 million) seven-year term loan, as sole lender, to refinance Leader Energy's 50 MW Vinh Hao 6 solar plant in Bình Thuận province, operating since 2019 and fully bought by Leader Energy in 2023.
context: The plant produces about 83,000 MWh a year. Leader Energy targets more than 500 MW of renewables in Vietnam.

sources.title: HSBC, Leader Energy ink $23.13m loan for solar project in Vietnam

title: BayWa r.e. sells 95 MW Almodóvar solar farm in Spain to Encavis
summary: BayWa r.e. sold the 95 MW Almodóvar solar farm near Córdoba, due to connect in late 2025, to Encavis.
details: BayWa r.e. sold the 95 MW Almodóvar solar farm near Córdoba, Andalusia, to Encavis, after selling it the 109 MW Lirios farm earlier. It should connect in Q4 2025 and produce about 187 GWh a year.
context: Almodóvar is covered by a 10-year virtual PPA with Huhtamaki signed in 2021, which with a second farm meets about 80% of the company's European power needs.

sources.title: BayWa r.e. sells 95 MW Spanish solar farm

title: Emeren sells 42 MWp ready-to-build Spanish solar portfolio to CVE España
target: 42 MWp portfolio of eight ready-to-build solar projects in Spain
summary: US-listed solar developer Emeren has agreed to sell a 42 MWp portfolio of eight solar projects in Spain to CVE España, a unit of French independent power producer CVE. One project has already changed hands and the rest are due to close in the third quarter of 2024. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of eight greenfield projects, meaning sites developed from scratch, that Emeren has worked on since 2021, each sized between 5 and 6 MW. They are ready to build, meaning permits and grid rights are in place so construction can begin. Six projects are in Castilla y Leon, one in the Valencia region and one in Andalucia. Emeren states the plants will produce about 92,793 MWh per year, which it equates to the consumption of roughly 28,360 households, and avoid around 20,094 tonnes of CO2 annually.
context: Emeren describes the sale as a milestone for its Spanish business and part of its strategy of developing projects and selling them on. CVE says the deal will roughly triple its installed capacity in Spain to about 65 MWp by late 2025. CVE plans to sell the output as distributed solar power to corporate customers through power purchase agreements, which are long-term contracts to supply electricity at agreed prices.

sources.title: Emeren Group Sells a 42 MWp RTB Solar Project Portfolio in Spain

title: Dominion Energy to acquire Kitty Hawk North offshore wind lease from Avangrid
target: Kitty Hawk North Wind offshore wind lease (to be renamed CVOW-South)
summary: Virginia Electric and Power Company, a subsidiary of Dominion Energy, agreed to buy the Kitty Hawk North Wind offshore lease and related development work from Avangrid for about $160 million. The roughly 40,000-acre lease off the US East Coast could host about 800 MW of offshore wind in the 2030s.
details: The price splits into about $117 million for the lease itself, roughly $3,000 per acre, and about $43 million to reimburse Avangrid for development costs already spent. The site will be renamed CVOW-South and would connect to Dominion's transmission grid if approved and built. Dominion says it has no detailed cost or in-service date estimates yet and will develop them in later phases. Closing requires approvals from the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management and the City of Virginia Beach and is expected in the fourth quarter of 2024.
context: Dominion says electricity demand in its Virginia territory is projected to double over 13 years and presents the lease as an option for more regulated generation, meaning output whose costs are recovered through state-approved customer rates. The site lies about 25 miles south of Dominion's 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project, which the company says is on time and on budget for completion by end of 2026. The company states the deal does not change its 2024-2029 capital plan and acknowledges community concerns about a proposed cable landing site in Sandbridge.

sources.title: Dominion Energy Announces Agreement to Acquire Offshore Wind Lease From Avangrid For Potential Future Regulated Generation Development

title: SolarBank completes all-stock acquisition of Solar Flow-Through Funds in Ontario

advisors.name: Evans & Evans, Inc.
advisors.role: valuation and fairness opinion to SFF board

summary: SolarBank Corporation has closed its all-stock purchase of Solar Flow-Through Funds Ltd., a deal that values the company at up to C$45 million. The target owns more than 70 operating solar sites in Ontario totalling 28.8 MW and three battery storage projects under construction with 14.97 MW of discharge capacity.
details: SolarBank bought all SFF common shares it did not already hold through a court-approved plan of arrangement, issuing up to 5,859,561 of its own shares worth up to C$41.8 million, or C$4.50 per SFF share. About 3,575,632 shares worth C$25.53 million were issued at closing, and up to 2,283,929 more shares worth up to C$16.31 million are tied to contingent value rights, meaning they are only issued once final pricing with the Ontario grid operator IESO, supplier terms and debt financing for the battery portfolio are settled and the portfolio is revalued. The solar sites sell power under Ontario feed-in tariff contracts, which are long-term fixed-price deals with the IESO. SFF shareholders approved the deal on June 19, 2024, and the new SolarBank shares are subject to a staged release over 36 months. Evans & Evans, Inc. provided a valuation report and a fairness opinion to the SFF board.
context: SolarBank says the deal adds cash-generating power assets and moves it into owning battery storage and EV charging, while paying in shares preserves cash for its development pipeline. SFF reported revenue of C$9.2 million in 2023 and C$9.4 million in 2022, and the company states the feed-in tariff rates remain favorable into the 2030s. The two companies have worked together for over a decade, and SFF's CEO joins the SolarBank board.

sources.title: $45 Million Valued All Stock Acquisition of Solar Flow-Through Funds Ltd. Closes

title: Obton and GSSG Solar to take over nine Japanese solar plants totalling 117 MW
summary: Obton and GSSG Solar formed a joint venture to take over nine solar plants in Japan, 117 MW in total, eight of them operating.
details: Obton formed a joint venture with GSSG Solar to take over nine Japanese solar plants of 117 MW: eight operating plants of 104 MW, built between 2017 and 2022, and one 13 MW plant in development.
context: All are under Japan's feed-in tariff programme from 2012. Obton earlier bought GSSG's largest asset, an 82 MW plant in Fukushima.

sources.title: Obton, GSSG Solar to acquire 117MW Japanese solar projects

title: Statkraft signs PPA with Luminous Energy for 28.5 MW Bracon Ash solar farm
summary: Statkraft signed a fixed-price PPA with Luminous Energy for almost all output of the 28.5 MW Bracon Ash solar farm in Norfolk.
details: Statkraft signed a PPA with Luminous Energy for the 28.5 MW Bracon Ash solar farm in Norfolk, whose output is mostly fixed-price through a CfD from Allocation Round 5 and a virtual corporate PPA with Bristol Airport. Statkraft handles balancing and settles the two parts at different prices.
context: It is believed to be one of the first solar farms to combine a CfD and a corporate PPA. Statkraft's downregulation service lets the farm cut output when prices fall below a trigger.

sources.title: Statkraft signs solar PPA with Luminous Energy

title: Genex refinances Kidston and Jemalong solar plants
summary: Genex Power refinanced the senior debt on its 50 MW Kidston and 50 MW Jemalong solar plants with a new five-year $162 million facility.
details: Genex Power refinanced the senior debt on its 50 MW Kidston and 50 MW Jemalong solar plants with a new five-year A$162 million facility from existing lenders DZ Bank and Westpac, replacing one due in December 2024 and maturing in June 2029.
context: Interest is 95% hedged until 2030. The refinancing also lets Genex repay a subordinated loan from Infradebt, simplifying its capital structure.

sources.title: Genex completes $162m refinancing for two solar plants

title: Hydrexia and ICE SEDCE Hydrogen agree to form Malaysian hydrogen refuelling and storage joint venture

buyers.name: Hydrexia Borneo Sdn Bhd
buyers.role: JV partner, subsidiary of Hydrexia Holding Limited

summary: Hydrexia Borneo, a unit of Chinese hydrogen technology firm Hydrexia Holding, has signed a heads of agreement with ICE SEDCE Hydrogen to set up a joint venture in Malaysia. The venture would develop, operate and maintain hydrogen refuelling stations and hydrogen storage, starting with the Rembus depot of the Kuching transit system in Sarawak.
details: A heads of agreement is a preliminary, mostly non-binding document setting out the main terms before final contracts are signed. The first focus is operating and maintaining refuelling and storage at the Rembus depot serving the Automated Rapid Transit system, the first phase of the Kuching Urban Transportation System.
