The work is planned in phases, and the partners will also look for further refuelling and storage opportunities. No financial terms, ownership split or capacity figures were disclosed. ICE SEDCE Hydrogen is itself a joint venture of ICE Petroleum and SEDC Energy, a unit of the Sarawak Economic Development Corporation.
context: Hydrexia says the deal supports its expansion in Malaysia, following a strategic partnership with Lestari the previous month. The company presents local partners as key to entering the Southeast Asian hydrogen market. The release does not state whether the hydrogen involved is produced from renewable sources.

sources.title: Hydrexia and ICE SEDCE Hydrogen Form Joint Venture for Hydrogen Development

title: Recurrent Energy closes US$103 million tax credit transfer with Bank of America for 160 MW North Fork Solar in Oklahoma
summary: Recurrent Energy, a Canadian Solar subsidiary, closed a US$103 million agreement to transfer tax credits from its 160 MW North Fork Solar Project to Bank of America. The project, located southwest of Oklahoma City, has started operating.
details: North Fork Solar is a 160 MW solar plant that Recurrent Energy began developing in 2018 and will keep owning and operating. Under a tax credit transfer, the developer sells federal production tax credits, which are tax incentives earned per unit of electricity generated, to a buyer with tax bills to offset, raising cash in return. The Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority, which serves 42 municipal electric systems, will buy all of the plant's output under a 15-year contract. NordLB and Rabobank provided project loans and Blattner handled engineering, procurement and construction. CRC-IB and Latham & Watkins advised Recurrent Energy on the transfer.
context: The release describes this as Recurrent Energy's first production tax credit deal and its first tax credit transfer, which the company says lets it access funding faster. Bank of America presents the deal as helping build the new market for transferable tax credits. For the power authority, the project is its first large-scale solar resource.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes $103 Million Tax Credit Transfer Agreement with Bank of America for North Fork Solar Project

title: Generac acquires PowerPlay commercial battery storage business from SunGrid Solutions
summary: Generac Power Systems has bought PowerPlay Battery Energy Storage Systems, a division of Canadian storage contractor SunGrid Solutions. PowerPlay supplies complete battery storage systems for commercial and industrial sites of up to 7 MWh. The deal closed on June 26, 2024, and its price was not disclosed.
details: PowerPlay offers turnkey battery systems, meaning packaged solutions delivered ready to operate, for businesses such as retail stores, offices, factories and healthcare facilities. The business will keep operating in Cambridge, Canada, where it will act as a research and development centre for Generac's commercial and industrial battery products. SunGrid keeps its engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) business, in which a contractor designs, sources equipment for and builds projects, serving storage projects from 10 MWh to 1 GWh in the United States and Canada. No advisers were named.
context: Generac says the purchase helps it offer a broader set of energy products to commercial and industrial customers in its home market. SunGrid says the sale lets it concentrate on its utility-scale storage construction work. The release points to rising rooftop solar use, electrification and grid reliability concerns as drivers of demand for on-site battery storage.

sources.title: Generac Expands Energy Storage Solutions with Acquisition

title: Q ENERGY sells 33 MW Whinfield solar farm to AlphaReal
summary: Q ENERGY completed the sale of the 33 MW Whinfield solar farm near Darlington to AlphaReal.
details: Q ENERGY completed the sale of the 33 MW Whinfield Solar farm near Darlington, north-east England, under construction with close to 60,000 ground-mounted modules, to AlphaReal.
context: It could supply more than 8,700 UK households. Q ENERGY is developing a pipeline of over 15 GW across Europe.

sources.title: Q ENERGY sells UK solar farm to AlphaReal

title: Sumitomo Corporation of Americas makes tax equity investment in Pacifico Power solar-plus-storage portfolio
target: Portfolio of six distributed solar PV plus battery storage projects in Massachusetts and California
summary: Sumitomo Corporation, through its US arm Sumitomo Corporation of Americas, has made a tax equity investment in six distributed solar and battery projects led by developer Pacifico Power. The portfolio totals 27 MW of solar and 25 MWh of battery storage across Massachusetts and California.
details: Tax equity is a US financing structure in which an investor provides capital to a project in return for using its federal tax credits and other tax benefits. Two of the projects are low-income community solar sites in Massachusetts developed under the state's SMART incentive program, where local residential and business subscribers get discounted power without installing panels themselves. The other four are behind-the-meter systems in California, meaning they sit on customer premises and supply power directly to commercial and industrial users under long-term energy service agreements. The investment amount and timing of the transaction were not disclosed.
context: Sumitomo says this is its group's first investment in distributed generation and part of building out its Green Power Platform business. The company states it will use the experience to look for ways to expand the community solar model in the US, Japan and other countries. The release cites an expectation that the US community solar market will grow from about 6 GW to roughly 14 GW by 2028.

sources.title: Sumitomo Corporation of Americas Diversifies into Distributed Energy with Solar and Storage Investment, Opportunity to Expand Globally

title: Altus Power buys 8.5 MW New Jersey solar array
summary: Altus Power acquired an 8.5 MW ground-mounted solar array in New Jersey that sells power into PJM and solar renewable energy credits.
details: Altus Power bought an 8.5 MW ground-mounted solar array in New Jersey, with 63 acres of land, taking its New Jersey portfolio to 185.5 MW. It sells power into the PJM market and Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs).
context: SRECs are certificates New Jersey utilities must buy to meet solar targets. Owning the land lets Altus redevelop the site later.

sources.title: Altus Power acquires New Jersey solar array

title: Birch Creek Energy closes tax equity, construction and term debt financing for Earp Solar in Illinois
summary: Birch Creek Energy has completed financing for Earp Solar, a utility scale solar project in Warren County, Illinois, which is now fully operating. Foss & Company provided tax equity, West Town Bank & Trust supplied long-term debt and Pathward funded construction. The release describes the project as 47MW in one place and 49MWdc in another.
details: Earp Solar covers 229 acres and connects to the Ameren Illinois grid, and the company says it produces enough power for more than 7,300 homes. Tax equity, meaning investment from a party that receives the project's tax credits in return for capital, was arranged by Foss & Company using an inverted lease, a structure where the developer leases the project to the investor. West Town Bank & Trust provided the permanent, or long-term, debt, while Pathward, N.A. underwrote and funded the construction loan. No deal value was disclosed.
context: Earp Solar is the first fully financed and operating asset in Birch Creek's independent power producer business, through which it plans to own the projects it builds rather than sell them. The company says it is working to complete six projects in the MISO grid region totaling 342MW, with several expected online this year. Foss & Company said this is its second deal with Birch Creek.

sources.title: Birch Creek Energy Completes Financing for 49MW Earp Solar

title: SC Oscar buys New Zealand solar developer Rānui Generation

buyers.name: SC Oscar (SC Renewable Energy Plus Fund 1)

summary: Singapore's SC Oscar fully acquired Rānui Generation, a New Zealand solar developer with four projects of about 157 MWp.
details: SC Oscar, through its SC Renewable Energy Plus Fund 1, bought all of New Zealand solar developer Rānui Generation and its four projects of about 157 MWp, a total investment of around NZ$135 million. Rānui will start building its first project in Northland.
context: The other three greenfield projects are due to start construction in 2025. Greenfield means projects built from scratch on new sites.

sources.title: SC Oscar acquires NZ solar developer Rānui Generation

title: Recurrent Energy closes $513 million financing for 1,200 MWh Papago Storage project in Arizona
summary: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, has closed $513 million in project financing for its 1,200 MWh Papago Storage battery project in Maricopa County, Arizona. MUFG and Nord/LB led the bank group.
details: The package consists of a $249 million construction and term loan, a $163 million tax equity bridge loan and a $101 million letter of credit facility. A tax equity bridge loan is short-term debt repaid once tax equity investors, who fund projects in exchange for tax credits, put in their money. The project has a 20-year tolling agreement with Arizona Public Service Company, a contract under which the utility pays for the right to use the battery's capacity. Construction is planned to begin in the third quarter of 2024 with commercial operation expected in the second quarter of 2025, and Recurrent Energy will own and operate the facility. Bank of America, CoBank, DNB, Rabobank, Siemens and Zions acted as joint lead arrangers.
context: The company describes Papago Storage as the largest energy storage project in Arizona and says it will supply power equal to about 244,000 homes for four hours each day. Recurrent Energy says it began developing the project in 2016 and that Arizona has since become one of the fastest-growing US storage markets. Nord/LB said this is its 11th standalone storage project financing in the US.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes $513 Million in Financing for 1,200 MWh Energy Storage Project in Arizona

title: Masdar agrees to acquire Greece's TERNA ENERGY from GEK TERNA at €3.2bn enterprise value

buyers.name: Masdar (Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC)

advisors.name: Reed Smith LLP
advisors.role: international legal advisor to GEK TERNA

advisors.name: Potamitis Vekris
advisors.role: Greek legal advisor to GEK TERNA

summary: Masdar has signed a definitive agreement with GEK TERNA and other shareholders to buy an initial 67% of Athens-listed TERNA ENERGY at 20.00 euros per share. The price values the Greek renewables company's equity at 2.4 billion euros and its enterprise value at 3.2 billion euros.
details: TERNA ENERGY develops, builds and operates wind, solar, hydroelectric and pumped storage projects, with 1,227 MW installed and about 2,500 MW in operation, under construction or ready to build. Enterprise value means the equity value plus the company's net debt. After completion, which depends on regulatory approvals and other conditions, Masdar plans an all-cash mandatory tender offer, a legally required offer to the remaining shareholders, aiming for full ownership. Shareholders also receive an agreed dividend of 0.38 euros per share. Rothschild & Co. advised Masdar financially, Morgan Stanley advised TERNA ENERGY, and several law firms advised both sides.
context: The parties describe it as the largest energy transaction ever on the Athens Stock Exchange and one of the largest in European renewables. Masdar says TERNA ENERGY will be a key platform for its European growth toward a 100 GW global target by 2030, while TERNA ENERGY targets 6 GW of operating capacity by 2030. GEK TERNA says the sale fits its plan to become a leading diversified infrastructure group in Greece and Southeast Europe.

sources.title: Masdar and GEK TERNA Strike Landmark €3.2bn¹ Deal: UAE Renewables Champion to Acquire Greece's TERNA ENERGY

title: Sembcorp completes purchase of Gelex wind and solar units in Vietnam
summary: Sembcorp completed its acquisition of three of four Gelex subsidiaries in Vietnam, adding 196 MW of operating wind and solar.
details: Sembcorp Solar Vietnam completed buying three of four Gelex Group subsidiaries, adding 196 MW of operating wind and solar, and agreed to take 73% of a fourth that owns a 49 MW hydro plant, due to complete in the second half of 2024.
context: Once complete, Sembcorp's gross renewable capacity will be 455 MW in Vietnam and 14.4 GW across the group.

sources.title: Sembcorp adds 196MW of wind, solar in portfolio with Vietnam acquisition deal

title: TagEnergy reaches financial close on 577 MW Golden Plains Wind Farm Stage 2
summary: TagEnergy reached financial close on the 577 MW second stage of the 1.3 GW, A$4 billion Golden Plains Wind Farm in Victoria, starting construction.
details: TagEnergy reached financial close on the 577 MW, 93-turbine Stage 2 of the A$4 billion Golden Plains Wind Farm in Victoria with non-recourse loans from the Clean Energy Finance Corporation, CBA, Westpac, Denmark's EIFO, Mizuho, Natixis, Bank of China and Deutsche Bank.
context: Stage 1 (756 MW) was under construction with 25% of turbines installed. At 1,333 MW, the farm should supply 9% of Victoria's power from mid-2027. TagEnergy cites the Capacity Investment Scheme's support.

sources.title: TagEnergy achieves financial close for 577 MW wind project

title: Pattern Energy signs 30-year PPA with Hydro-Québec for 150 MW Broughton Wind
summary: Pattern Energy signed a 30-year PPA with Hydro-Québec for the 150 MW Broughton Wind project in Québec.
details: Pattern Energy signed a 30-year PPA with Hydro-Québec for the 150 MW Broughton Wind project in Saint-Pierre-de-Broughton, Sacré-Coeur-de-Jésus and Thetford Mines, about 40 miles south of Québec City.
context: Broughton is a 50/50 venture between Pattern and local and First Nations partners: the MRC des Appalaches, MRC de l'Érable and the Abenaki councils of Odanak and Wôlinak.

sources.title: Pattern Energy signs Québecois wind PPA

title: Octopus Energy Generation buys Gaucho and Nestlewood solar projects from Vesper Energy
target: Gaucho Solar and Nestlewood Solar projects
summary: Vesper Energy has completed the sale of two operating solar projects, Gaucho Solar in Pennsylvania and Nestlewood Solar in Ohio, to Octopus Energy Generation. The two sites together total about 100 MWac. No price was disclosed.
details: Nestlewood Solar covers 610 acres in Clermont and Brown counties, Ohio, and sells its output to a Fortune 100 e-commerce company under a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity. It qualifies as an energy community under the Inflation Reduction Act, a status that can bring extra federal tax credits. Gaucho Solar sits on 68 acres in Beaver and Allegheny counties, Pennsylvania, has about 55,000 panels, and supplies the University of Pittsburgh's sustainability goals. Both projects are in the PJM grid region, and Vesper Energy will stay on as asset manager, meaning it will keep running day-to-day operations for the new owner.
context: Vesper says this is its second major transaction of 2024 and presents it as a sign of investor confidence in renewable projects. The deal adds US solar assets to Octopus Energy Generation, which the release says manages a global green energy portfolio worth nearly 9 billion US dollars. Vesper, based in Texas, reports a development pipeline of about 17 GW.

sources.title: Vesper Energy Completes Sale of Gaucho and Nestlewood Solar Projects to Octopus Energy Generation

title: Captona makes preferred equity investment in Scale Microgrids portfolio of microgrid and community solar projects
target: Portfolio of microgrid and community solar projects in New York and California
summary: New York investment firm Captona has closed and funded a preferred equity investment in a portfolio of microgrid and community solar projects owned by Scale Microgrids. The assets are located in New York and California. No deal value or capacity was disclosed.
details: All projects in the portfolio are already operating, and Scale Microgrids will keep owning, operating and maintaining them. The portfolio includes a microgrid supplying an off-grid cold storage facility, a microgrid serving a municipal water district in California, and community solar projects that give bill savings to New York utility customers. Preferred equity is a form of investment that gets paid ahead of ordinary equity but does not usually carry full control. Scale says the deal let it monetize investment tax credits under Section 6418, the rule that allows clean energy tax credits to be sold to other parties for cash. Kirkland & Ellis advised Captona and Allen Overy Shearman advised Scale Microgrids.
context: Captona says the deal expands its preferred equity strategy and adds to a portfolio that already includes renewable natural gas, fuel cells, storage and solar. Scale says the transaction helps it unlock value from projects it built through its own development, construction and financing platform. The deal illustrates how the transferable tax credit rules are being used to finance distributed energy projects.

sources.title: Captona Closes Partnership with Scale Microgrids, Completing Preferred Equity Investment in Portfolio of Microgrid and Community Solar Projects

title: Canadian Solar signs 20-year PPA with Toyota Tsusho for two Japanese FIP solar projects
target: 1.2 MWp Tsukuba City and 1.9 MWp Daisen Town solar projects
summary: Canadian Solar has signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Toyota Tsusho covering all output from its first two Japanese solar projects under the feed-in premium scheme. The two projects, totalling about 3.1 MWp in Ibaraki and Tottori prefectures, began commercial operation on June 1, 2024.
details: The portfolio consists of a 1.2 MWp project in Tsukuba City, Ibaraki Prefecture and a 1.9 MWp project in Daisen Town, Tottori Prefecture, both using Canadian Solar bifacial modules, meaning panels that capture light on both sides. The projects originally won feed-in tariff contracts, a fixed government-set price, in 2020 auctions but were switched to the feed-in premium system, where generators sell at market prices plus a premium. Under the 20-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity, Toyota Tsusho takes 100% of the power along with Non-Fossil Certificates, which are tradable proofs of clean generation. Toyota Tsusho, an electricity retailer in the Toyota Group, plans to resell the power and certificates to its corporate customers.
context: Canadian Solar describes this as its first private corporate PPA in Japan, marking a shift away from its long focus on government-backed feed-in tariffs. The company says corporate demand for clean energy is rising and that it aims to help Japanese firms meet those needs. It reports a Japan development business of 240 MWp of solar and 1.675 GWh of storage as of March 31, 2024.

sources.title: Canadian Solar Announces Operation of First FIP Projects in Japan and PPA Signing with Toyota Tsusho

title: Rezolv Energy and Low Carbon secure up to €291 million for VIFOR wind in Romania
summary: Rezolv Energy and Low Carbon secured up to €291 million from eight lenders for Phase 1 of the VIFOR wind farm in Romania.
details: Rezolv Energy and Low Carbon secured up to €291 million from eight lenders led by Erste, UniCredit and the EBRD, with IFC, Intesa Sanpaolo, OTP, Raiffeisen and Garanti BBVA, for the 192 MW Phase 1 of the VIFOR wind farm in Buzău County, Romania, backed by five corporate PPAs.
context: It is the first financing for Rezolv, launched by Actis 18 months earlier. Phase 1 should be online by end-2025; a second phase would take VIFOR to 461 MW, one of Europe's largest onshore wind farms.

sources.title: Rezolv Energy and Low Carbon receive financing for Romanian wind

title: Alternergy takes 74.99% of Olympia Solar Power
summary: Alternergy subscribed for 74.99% of Olympia Solar Power and becomes sponsor of its project in Sultan Kudarat.
details: Alternergy subscribed for 74.99% of Olympia Solar Power, 74,999 shares at ₱1 each, and will sponsor the company's application for a solar energy operating contract for a project of up to 100 ha in Barangay Kalandagan, Tacurong City, Sultan Kudarat.
context: A solar energy operating contract is the Philippine government licence to explore and develop a solar site.

sources.title: Alternergy acquires 74.99% stake in Olympia Solar Power

title: Plus Power closes $133 million financing for 150 MW Cranberry Point battery in Massachusetts

buyers.name: Investec
buyers.role: joint lead arranger and administrative agent

summary: Plus Power has closed $133 million of construction and term financing for its Cranberry Point battery storage facility in Carver, Massachusetts. The standalone project has 150 MW of power and 300 MWh of storage, giving about two hours of discharge at full output.
details: The financing combines a construction-to-term loan, which funds building and then converts to a longer-term loan once the project runs, plus a bridge loan and a letter of credit facility. First Citizens Bank and Nord LB were coordinating lead arrangers, Investec and Siemens Financial Services were joint lead arrangers, Investec serves as administrative agent and U.S. Bank as depositary bank. Construction began in December 2023 and the project is expected online in summer 2025. It won a capacity commitment in the 2021 ISO-NE Forward Capacity Auction, meaning it is paid to be available to the New England grid through 2031.
context: Plus Power says this is the first major financing of a utility-scale project that will earn Massachusetts Clean Peak Energy Certificates, a state incentive that pays resources for supplying clean power during peak demand. The company states the project represents roughly a third of the state's goal of 1,000 MWh of battery storage by 2025. Its sister project Cross Town in Maine, at 175 MW and 350 MWh, is also under construction.

sources.title: First Major Standalone Battery Storage Project in ISO-NE Closes Financing

title: Alternergy secures ₱5.3 billion RCBC loan for 64 MW Alabat wind
summary: Alternergy's Alabat Wind Power secured a ₱5.3 billion (about US$90 million) facility from RCBC to part-fund its 64 MW wind project.
details: Alternergy's Alabat Wind Power secured a ₱5.3 billion (about US$90.3 million) project finance facility from RCBC to part-fund its 64 MW Alabat wind project, RCBC's largest such facility since 2014.
context: RCBC also backs Alternergy's 12.5 MWp Kirahon solar project and CitySun rooftop solar. Alternergy has closed ₱18.4 billion of its ₱21 billion financing plan.

sources.title: Alternergy bags $90.3m loan for 64 MW wind project

title: World Bank approves US$1 billion more for Pakistan's Dasu hydropower
summary: The World Bank approved a second round of additional financing of US$1 billion for Stage I of the Dasu hydropower project in Pakistan.
details: The World Bank approved US$1 billion of second additional financing for Stage I of the Dasu hydropower project, a run-of-river plant on the Indus about 8 km from Dasu Town, Upper Kohistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Stage I is 2,160 MW and should produce 12,225 GWh a year.
context: Dasu is being built in stages towards 4,320–5,400 MW, with Stage II using the same dam. The money also builds WAPDA's capacity to prepare future hydro projects.

sources.title: World Bank approves US$1 billion additional financing for DASU hydropower project

title: Vesper Energy completes US$592 million debt syndication for 600 MWac Hornet Solar project in Texas
summary: Vesper Energy has finished syndicating about US$592 million of construction and term loans for its Hornet Solar project in Swisher County, Texas. Syndication means the original loan was shared out among a wider group of banks. The 600 MWac project is backed by a group of ten lenders led by MUFG, Nord/LB and Santander.
details: Hornet Solar covers more than six square miles and has a capacity of 600 MWac and 745 MWdc, using two-sided (bifacial) solar panels mounted on trackers that follow the sun along one axis. The project reached financial close, the point when funding is committed and construction can proceed, in December 2023, after which the loans were syndicated. MUFG, Nord/LB and Santander acted as coordinating lead arrangers, Societe Generale, BayernLB and KB Kookmin Bank as joint lead arrangers, and Allied Irish Bank, Associated, Radiance Structured Finance and DZ Bank as lenders. A construction loan funds building the plant and a term loan is longer-term debt repaid from operating revenue. Blattner Energy is building the project and its output is sold to four buyers under separate power purchase agreements, which are long-term contracts to buy electricity.
context: Vesper describes Hornet as one of the largest single-phase solar projects in the US and says it can power about 160,000 homes in the ERCOT grid. MUFG said raising this much capital in a crowded lending market reflects the project's credit profile. The developer says its pipeline includes more than 55 renewable and storage assets totaling 17 GW.

sources.title: Vesper Energy Finalizes Hornet Solar Debt Syndication, Representing $592 Million in Financing

title: Qualitas Energy buys 36 MW wind repowering project in Brandenburg
summary: Qualitas Energy acquired a wind repowering project in Brandenburg with 36 MW of potential capacity.
details: Qualitas Energy bought a wind repowering project in Brandenburg, Germany, with development potential of 36 MW, at an advanced planning stage. The existing Enercon turbines, running since 1999, will be replaced by five modern ones.
context: Repowering an old site reuses its grid connection and acceptance; the new turbines could supply more than 24,000 households.

sources.title: Qualitas Energy acquires German wind repowering project

title: Pine Gate Renewables buys 450 MWdc MISO South solar development portfolio from Redeux Energy
target: 450 MWdc three-project solar development portfolio in MISO South
summary: Denver-based developer Redeux Energy has sold a 450 MWdc portfolio of three utility-scale solar projects in the MISO South power market to Pine Gate Renewables. The purchase price was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of three solar projects in development located in MISO South, the southern part of the grid region run by the Midcontinent Independent System Operator. Capacity is stated in MWdc, meaning the direct-current rating of the solar panels. The sale is the first from an eleven-project, multi-state 1.7 GWdc portfolio that Redeux put on the market in late 2023. Marathon Capital acted as adviser representing the portfolio. Pine Gate described the projects as turnkey assets for its MISO pipeline.
context: Redeux says demand for renewables in MISO is rising due to utility decarbonization goals and commercial and industrial load growth. The company, founded in 2021 and backed mainly by family office Cathexis Holdings, claims a pipeline of about 7 GW and 7 GWh of solar and storage and plans to sell further multi-GW portfolios each year. It has also announced a process to raise capital. Pine Gate, which says it operates over 2 GW and has over 30 GW in development, adds the projects to its pipeline.

sources.title: Redeux Energy Announces Sale of Utility-Scale Solar Development Portfolio to Pine Gate Renewables

title: Neoen signs 25-year solar PPA with SNCF Energie for 139 MWp
summary: Neoen signed a 25-year corporate PPA with SNCF Energie for all power and guarantees of origin from 139 MWp of solar, including the Le Couret agrivoltaic project.
details: Neoen signed a 25-year corporate PPA with SNCF Energie for all the power and guarantees of origin from its 139 MWp Le Couret agrivoltaic farm in Haute-Vienne, France's largest solar park under a PPA with SNCF. It is permitted and has a grid connection; construction starts in 2026 with commissioning in 2028.
context: The farm's 150 ha will double as sheep grazing for a local farmer, with a farmhouse and sheepfold built as part of the project. Its output matches the yearly supply of the Paris–Marseille high-speed line.

sources.title: Neoen and SNCF Energie sign solar PPA

title: AMEA Power reaches financial close on 120 MW Doornhoek solar in South Africa
summary: AMEA Power reached financial close on the US$120 million, 120 MW Doornhoek solar project, its first in South Africa.
details: AMEA Power reached financial close on the US$120 million, 120 MW Doornhoek solar project in South Africa, awarded in Bid Window 6 of the REIPPPP. Standard Bank lent US$100 million and the IDC provided US$8 million of equity to local partners Ziyanda Energy and Dzimuzwo Energy, wholly owned by African women.
context: REIPPPP is South Africa's renewable energy IPP procurement programme. It will be AMEA Power's first operating asset in the country.

sources.title: AMEA Power reaches financial close on South African PV plant

title: Lotus Infrastructure Partners acquires US developer PNE USA from PNE AG
summary: Lotus Infrastructure Partners, an energy infrastructure investor based in Greenwich, Connecticut, has completed its purchase of PNE USA from German renewable company PNE AG. PNE USA develops utility-scale wind, solar and battery storage projects in North America and will now operate as Allium Renewable Energy.
details: PNE USA has developed and sold 877 MW of wind and solar projects so far and holds a pipeline of more than 3 GW of projects in development. Utility-scale means large projects that sell power to the grid rather than to individual homes. The existing team, led by CEO Karl Dahlstrom, stays in place under the new Allium name, effective immediately. The purchase price and advisers were not disclosed.
context: Lotus says the acquired team's skills in finding and commercializing projects will expand its own renewable development work. Allium's leadership expects Lotus's experience in financing and operating energy assets to speed up its growth. Lotus reports having raised over $3 billion in equity and completed deals worth more than $8 billion in enterprise value.

sources.title: LOTUS ANNOUNCES ACQUISITION OF PNE USA, A LEADING RENEWABLE DEVELOPMENT PLATFORM

title: Avangrid signs PPA with CPS Energy for 161 MW of Peñascal I wind
summary: Avangrid signed a PPA with CPS Energy for 161 MW of its Peñascal I wind farm in Kenedy County, Texas.
details: Avangrid signed a PPA with CPS Energy for 161 MW of its Peñascal I wind farm in Kenedy County, Texas, extending and expanding a 15-year deal from 77 MW. CPS will take almost 80% of the farm's output.
context: Contracting more output reduces Avangrid's merchant risk, its exposure to volatile spot prices in Texas.

sources.title: Avangrid and CPS Energy sign Texan solar PPA

title: Ellomay closes €10.5 million Bankinter financing for 28 MW Spanish solar plant and completes sale of 9 MW Israeli solar plant

buyers.name: Greenlight Fund Limited Partnership
buyers.role: acquirer (50%) of Talmei Yosef PV plant

buyers.name: Doral Group Renewable Energy Resources Ltd.
buyers.role: acquirer (50%) of Talmei Yosef PV plant

sellers.name: Ellomay Capital Ltd.
sellers.role: seller of Talmei Yosef PV plant and parent of borrower

target: Ellomay Solar PV plant (Talaván, Spain) and Talmei Yosef PV plant (Israel)
summary: Ellomay Capital's Spanish subsidiary reached financial close on a €10.5 million project finance package from Bankinter for its 28 MW solar plant in Talaván, Spain. Separately, Ellomay completed the sale of its 9 MW Talmei Yosef solar plant in Israel to Greenlight Fund and Doral Group in equal shares for net proceeds of about NIS 42.6 million (around €10.6 million).
details: The Spanish plant has been connected to the grid since June 2022, and financial close means the loan agreements are signed and money can be drawn. The financing has a €10 million senior term loan plus a €500,000 revolving debt service reserve facility, a standby credit line used to cover loan payments if cash runs short. The loan runs 16 years with semi-annual repayments, though a cash sweep, which uses surplus cash to repay debt early, is expected to shorten it to about 13 years. Interest is six-month Euribor plus 2.5%, swapped to a fixed rate of roughly 5.5% until June 2037, and Ellomay Solar drew the term loan and passed €9.7 million to its parent. The Talmei Yosef sale closed on June 2, 2024 after closing conditions were met.
context: Ellomay says the cash raised will help speed up construction of its solar projects in the USA and Italy, including about 50 MW in Texas and about 40 MW in Lazio currently being built without outside financing. The company describes a strategy of selling mature operating assets and raising debt on projects it initially funded itself after grid connection.

sources.title: Ellomay Capital Announces Execution and Financial Closing of Project Finance for the Ellomay Solar Project and Consummation of Sale of the Talmei Yosef Project

title: Alternergy signs ₱2 billion green loan with BDO Unibank
summary: Alternergy signed a ₱2 billion (about US$34 million) green corporate loan with BDO Unibank, with BDO Capital as arranger, to fund its renewable projects.
details: Alternergy signed a ₱2 billion (about US$34.2 million) green corporate loan with BDO Unibank, arranged by BDO Capital, for its Tanay and Alabat wind subsidiaries and upcoming projects.
context: The loan sits under Alternergy's Green Finance Framework, set up with ADB technical help to follow ICMA, ASEAN and LMA green standards.

sources.title: Alternergy bags $34.2m loan for wind projects

title: MYTILINEOS signs two Irish solar PPAs with Keppel DC REIT
summary: MYTILINEOS signed two long-term PPAs to supply Keppel DC REIT's two Dublin data centres from solar farms in Gorey, Wexford and Goresbridge, Kilkenny.
details: MYTILINEOS signed two long-term PPAs with Keppel DC REIT to supply its two Dublin data centres from two Irish solar farms of 14.28 MW in Gorey, Wexford, and Goresbridge, Kilkenny, due for completion in summer 2024.
context: The farms should produce about 13.6 GWh a year, about 11% of the data centres' needs; with other PPAs, about 92% will come from Irish renewables.

sources.title: MYTILINEOS signs two Irish PV ppas

title: Apricus Generation takes controlling stake in solar and storage developer Nexus Renewables
summary: Apricus Generation, a Miami-based holding company, has acquired a controlling interest in Nexus Renewables, a Toronto-based solar and energy storage developer. Nexus holds a pipeline of more than 500 MW of North American projects. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Nexus Renewables develops solar and battery storage projects and also acts as an independent power producer, meaning it owns projects and sells the electricity they generate. Its portfolio of over 500 MW spans projects at various stages of development and construction across North America, though specific countries and the capacity split between solar and storage were not given. Apricus bought a controlling interest, not necessarily full ownership, and the exact stake was not stated. Nexus founder Keith Sandor continues to lead the company.
context: This is the first acquisition by Apricus since it launched earlier in 2024 with the aim of building a national distributed solar and battery platform. Apricus says independent developers like Nexus often have more projects than capital, and that its funding and management support will help Nexus bring its pipeline into operation. The deal reflects a model in which holding companies back smaller developers to scale distributed generation.

sources.title: Apricus Generation Acquires Solar and Storage Developer Nexus Renewables

title: Alternergy Tanay Wind secures ₱8 billion of loans from BPI and Security Bank
summary: Alternergy Tanay Wind approved ₱8 billion (about US$137 million) of loans from BPI and Security Bank to part-fund its wind project in Rizal.
details: Alternergy Tanay Wind approved ₱8 billion (about US$137.4 million) of loans from BPI and Security Bank to part-fund its wind project in Rizal, secured on its shares held by Alternergy Wind Holdings and backed by a sponsor undertaking.
context: Alternergy planned to raise about US$211 million for its Tanay and Quezon wind projects, 164 MW in total.

sources.title: Alternergy secures $137.4m loan for Tanay wind project

title: RWE signs two 15-year PPAs with Microsoft for Texas wind
summary: RWE signed two 15-year PPAs with Microsoft for power from two new onshore wind farms in Texas, including Peyton Creek II.
details: RWE signed two 15-year PPAs with Microsoft for two new Texas onshore wind farms, Peyton Creek II, which broke ground, and Lane City, which reached investment decision, 446 MW in total with Vestas V163 4.5 MW turbines.
context: Wanzek Construction, a MasTec Renewables company, and RES will lead construction for RWE. Long-term PPAs with large tech buyers help fund new wind farms.

sources.title: RWE signs two Texas wind PPAs with Microsoft

title: Ørsted closes $680 million tax equity financing from J.P. Morgan for Texas and Arizona solar and storage
target: Eleven Mile Solar Center and Sparta Solar
summary: Ørsted has closed $680 million in tax equity financing from J.P. Morgan for two US projects. The portfolio covers 550 MW of solar and 300 MW of battery storage across Arizona and Texas.
details: Eleven Mile Solar Center in Pinal County, Arizona combines 300 MW of solar with a 300 MW / 1,200 MWh battery that can discharge for four hours, and Sparta Solar is a 250 MW solar project in Mineral, Texas. Tax equity means an investor provides cash in exchange for the right to use a project's federal tax credits. Here the battery earns a one-time investment tax credit, while the solar output earns production tax credits over ten years, and the deal includes an option to transfer (sell) the credits to other buyers. Both projects are expected to start commercial operation in 2024. Latham & Watkins advised Ørsted and Milbank advised J.P. Morgan.
context: The release describes the deal as one of the largest solar and storage tax equity transactions combining production and investment tax credits since the Inflation Reduction Act passed in 2022. It extends J.P. Morgan's existing investment in 1.8 GW of Ørsted's 5.7 GW US onshore portfolio. Eleven Mile is Ørsted's first project in Arizona, and the company says it will have 2 GW of operating US solar by the end of 2024.

sources.title: Ørsted Closes $680 Million in Tax Equity Financing for Solar and Storage Portfolio

title: Recurrent Energy signs up to €1.3 billion green revolving credit facility with ten banks for European solar and storage

buyers.name: ING
buyers.role: Sole issuing bank and sole sustainability coordinator

target: Recurrent Energy European solar and battery storage construction portfolio
summary: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, signed a multi-currency green revolving credit facility of up to €1.3 billion with ten banks. The money will fund construction of solar and battery storage projects in Spain, Italy, the UK, the Netherlands, France and Germany.
details: A revolving credit facility is a loan line the borrower can draw, repay and draw again. This one starts at €674 million and can be enlarged to about €1.3 billion, runs for three years with optional extensions, and can be drawn in euros or British pounds. It covers both contracted projects and fully merchant ones, meaning plants that sell power at market prices without a long-term buyer. At first it will back construction of close to 1 GW of solar, mostly in Spain with the rest in the UK. Bondholders SL is facility and security agent, and the agreement was signed in Seville.
context: Recurrent Energy describes the deal as a milestone for its European growth and its shift toward being an independent power producer. The company says it has a worldwide pipeline of 26 GWp of solar and 56 GWh of battery storage. The green label means ING oversees that the use of funds meets environmental criteria.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Secures Landmark Green, Multi-currency Financing for up to €1.3 Billion to Accelerate European Renewable Energy Portfolio

title: PAG raises US$550 million for first renewable energy fund
summary: PAG raised US$550 million of commitments for PAG REN I, its first renewable energy fund, initially focused on Japanese solar.
details: PAG closed its first renewable energy fund, PAG REN I, with US$550 million from pensions, sovereign wealth funds and fund-of-funds investors in North America, Europe and the Middle East. It will develop and buy renewables in Asia-Pacific, starting with solar in Japan.
context: PAG says Asia-Pacific is the largest and fastest-growing energy market and will need more than US$2 trillion of renewable investment.

sources.title: PAG achieves $550m commitment for APAC renewable energy fund

title: ADB and Masdar sign US$46.5 million loan for Nur Bukhara solar and battery
summary: The Asian Development Bank and Masdar signed a US$46.5 million loan for the Nur Bukhara solar plant with battery storage in Uzbekistan, Central Asia's first with a utility-scale battery.
details: ADB and Masdar signed a US$46.5 million loan, US$26.5 million from ADB and US$20 million from the Private Infrastructure Fund for Asia, for the Nur Bukhara solar plant with battery storage in Uzbekistan. ADB also arranged US$26.5 million from JICA, with IFC and others co-financing.
context: It will be Central Asia's first renewable plant with utility-scale battery storage, producing about 555 GWh a year.

sources.title: ADB and Masdar ink $46.5m loan for Uzbek solar and BESS facility

title: Eurasian Development Bank to finance 300 MW Bishkek Solar project in Kyrgyzstan
summary: The Eurasian Development Bank signed a cooperation agreement with Bishkek Solar to arrange US$210 million of 15-year financing for a 300 MW solar project in Kyrgyzstan.
details: The Eurasian Development Bank signed a cooperation agreement with Bishkek Solar to arrange US$210 million of 15-year financing for a 300 MW solar project in Toru-Aigyr village, Issyk-Kul Region, Kyrgyzstan, due to operate by end-2025.
context: The plant has a 25-year PPA with the National Electric Grid of Kyrgyzstan, a public–private partnership with the Energy Ministry and a 25-year investment agreement with the government.

sources.title: EDB to boost financing for 300 MW Kyrgyz solar project

title: SPPC signs two PPAs with Marubeni-led consortium for 1,100 MW of Saudi wind
summary: The Saudi Power Procurement Company signed two PPAs with a Marubeni-led consortium for 1,100 MW of wind projects at what it called the world's lowest wind power cost.
details: The Saudi Power Procurement Company signed two PPAs with a consortium led by Marubeni, with Al-Ajlan & Bros, for 1,100 MW of wind: the 600 MW Al-Ghat project at a levelised cost of 1.56 US cents/kWh and the 500 MW Wa'ad Al-Shamal project at 1.70 cents/kWh.
context: SPPC says Al-Ghat is a world-record low cost for wind power. The projects support Saudi Arabia's aim of about 50% renewable electricity by 2030. Levelised cost is the average cost per unit over a plant's life.

sources.title: Saudi inks 2 PPAs for 1,100 MW wind projects

title: Renewable Power Capital closes €555 million for 553 MW Swedish wind portfolio
summary: Renewable Power Capital closed €555 million of long-term financing for its 553 MW onshore wind portfolio in Sweden, one of Europe's largest for greenfield onshore wind.
details: Renewable Power Capital closed €555 million of long-term financing for its 553 MW Swedish onshore wind portfolio, four farms under construction in Kramfors and Sollefteå, from CIBC, Danske Bank, Export Development Canada, NatWest and NORD/LB. It covers both construction and operation.
context: Almost all output is contracted under 10-year PPAs: Procter & Gamble for the 140 MW Sörlidberget farm, two with LyondellBasell and one with Ardagh. It is one of Europe's largest greenfield onshore wind financings.

sources.title: Renewable Power Capital closes financing of Swedish onshore wind portfolio

title: Iberdrola and Bayer sign 11-year off-site solar PPA in Italy
summary: Iberdrola and Bayer signed an 11-year off-site PPA in Italy for 33 GWh in total from January 2025.
details: Iberdrola and Bayer signed an 11-year off-site PPA in Italy for 33 GWh in total from January 2025, supplied by Iberdrola's 7 MW Montefiascone solar plant in Lazio, so that Bayer's Garbagnate Milanese site uses only renewable power.
context: It extends the companies' PPA alliance from Spain and Mexico to Italy. Montefiascone is Iberdrola's second solar plant in Italy.

sources.title: Iberdrola and Bayer sign solar energy PPA

title: Genesis Energy and Spark sign 10-year PPA for Lauriston solar farm
summary: Genesis Energy and Spark New Zealand signed a 10-year PPA for the output of the 63 MW Lauriston solar farm in Canterbury.
details: Genesis Energy and Spark New Zealand signed a 10-year PPA for the output of the 63 MW Lauriston solar farm in Canterbury, Genesis's first, due to generate by end-2024. It will cover about 60% of Spark's annual power, with renewable energy certificates.
context: Long-term corporate contracts give new projects the backing to get built. Spark targets a 56% cut in emissions by 2030 from 2020.

sources.title: Genesis Energy and Spark sign 10-year PPA for Lauriston solar farm

title: Vena Energy signs corporate PPA with Mitsubishi Corporation Clean Energy for Maibara Solar
summary: Vena Energy signed a corporate PPA with Mitsubishi Corporation Clean Energy for power from the 31.65 MW Maibara Solar project in Shiga.
details: Vena Energy signed a corporate PPA with Mitsubishi Corporation Clean Energy for power from its 31.65 MW Maibara Solar project in Shiga Prefecture, under construction.
context: It could supply about 8,560 Japanese households. Vena Energy has 922 MW operating in Japan.

sources.title: Vena Energy and Mitsubishi partner on 31.65 MW Maibara Solar PPA

title: CPP Investments provides $135M financing to Enfinity Global for 1.2 GW of solar and wind in India
target: 1.2 GW India solar and wind portfolio
summary: Enfinity Global has signed a $135 million financing with Canada Pension Plan Investment Board for the development and construction of 1.2 GW of solar and wind projects in India. The capital comes through subsidiaries of CPPIB Credit Investments Inc.
details: The portfolio is spread across five Indian states, namely Maharashtra, Delhi, Karnataka, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The projects are described as being in advanced development, meaning permits and land work are largely progressed, and commissioning, the point when plants start operating, is expected between 2025 and 2026. The release does not split the capacity between solar and wind or describe the loan structure in detail. Enfinity projects the plants will produce 2.4 GWh of electricity a year once connected to the grid.
context: Enfinity presents the deal as evidence of its commitment to India and its ability to draw foreign capital into the market. The company already owns and operates 240 MW of solar in India with more than 1.5 GW under development, and plans to expand into storage, hybrid projects and green ammonia. CPP Investments says it views the financing as a source of long-term returns for its fund.

title: First Citizens Bank and Bank United arrange over $150 million for two Apex Clean Energy battery storage projects in Texas

sellers.role: owner of Great Kiskadee Storage (JV of Apex, SK Gas and SK Eternix)

target: Great Kiskadee Storage and Angelo Storage
summary: First Citizens Bank's Energy Finance unit led financings totaling more than $150 million for two Apex Clean Energy battery storage projects in Texas. The two projects add up to 200 MW of power and 400 MWh of storage.
details: Great Kiskadee Storage is a 100 MW/200 MWh battery system in Hidalgo County, owned by SA Grid Solutions, a joint venture of Apex, SK Gas and SK Eternix. Angelo Storage is a 100 MW/200 MWh system in Tom Green County. Both have two-hour storage duration, meaning they can discharge at full power for about two hours, and both are under construction. First Citizens acted as sole bookrunner, the bank that organizes and places the loans, and as co-lead arranger alongside Bank United. Both projects are expected to begin commercial operation by the third quarter of 2024.
context: Apex says battery storage helps make the grid more resilient and renewable power more reliable and cost-effective. The deal adds to the growing volume of bank lending for standalone storage in Texas, and First Citizens says it hopes to work with Apex on further deals.

title: Acciona Energía buys 80% of Philippines' Freya Renewables
summary: Acciona Energía bought 80% of Freya Renewables, adding 880 MW of development projects in the Philippines.
details: Acciona Energía bought 80% of Philippine developer Freya Renewables, adding 880 MW of projects in development. It will also develop a 150 MW solar plant in Daanbantayan, Cebu, the Philippines' first public–private partnership for solar.

title: Active Surfaces raises $5.6 million pre-seed round led by Safar Partners for flexible solar technology
summary: Active Surfaces, an MIT spinout based in Woburn, Massachusetts that develops lightweight flexible solar panels, raised $5.6 million in a pre-seed round. Deep tech venture fund Safar Partners led the round, joined by investors including QVT, Lendlease and Sabanci Climate Ventures.
details: A pre-seed round is a very early stage of startup funding, typically before a product is on the market. The company currently makes 4-by-4-inch solar cells in the lab and plans to use the money to scale up with roll-to-roll printing, a process that prints thin semiconductor layers onto continuous rolls of flexible material, much like a newspaper press. It says the funds will also go toward expanding research and development and production. The release describes the round as oversubscribed, meaning investor demand exceeded the amount sought.
context: The company claims its thin-film panels will offer higher efficiency, lower cost and more versatility than conventional rigid panels, and can be built into surfaces from consumer goods to commercial buildings. Participation by Lendlease, a construction and development group, signals interest in building-integrated solar. Active Surfaces also takes part in a Saint-Gobain accelerator program through Greentown Labs.

sources.title: Active Surfaces Secures $5.6M in Oversubscribed Pre-Seed Funding to Revolutionize Solar Technology

title: BrightNight and Cordelio Power close US$414 million construction financing for 300 MW Box Canyon solar project in Arizona

buyers.name: Zions Bancorporation
buyers.role: Administrative Agent and Coordinating Lead Arranger

sellers.name: BrightNight
sellers.role: Joint venture partner and lead developer

summary: BrightNight and its joint venture partner Cordelio Power reached financial close on a US$414 million construction credit facility for the 300 MW Box Canyon solar project in Pinal County, Arizona. Financial close means the loan agreements are signed and funds can be drawn. Zions Bancorporation led the bank group.
details: The project is owned by BOCA bn, LLC, a company in which BrightNight and Cordelio are co-members, with BrightNight leading development. Construction started in December 2023 and operation is expected in the first half of 2025. The financing is a construction credit facility, a loan used to pay for building the plant. Zions Bancorporation acted as administrative agent and coordinating lead arranger, with National Bank of Canada, Royal Bank of Canada, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as joint lead arrangers. The output is sold under a 20-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity, with the Southwest Public Power Agency signed in December 2022, and Blattner is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor.
context: Box Canyon is the first project to start construction in a 2 GW Arizona portfolio owned by BrightNight and Cordelio, which is wholly owned by Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. The release says it is the largest renewable energy purchase in the Southwest Public Power Agency's history. BrightNight presents the deal, alongside a recent US$375 million corporate credit facility, as a key step in funding its claimed 37 GW portfolio, and says the plant will supply power equivalent to about 77,000 Arizona homes and businesses.

sources.title: BrightNight and Cordelio Power Achieve Financial Close on $ 414M Project Financing for 300 MW Box Canyon Project in Arizona

summary: ISG Renewables, the Innova–Schroders Greencoat joint venture, acquired the 28.7 MWp Newbold Pacey solar farm in Warwickshire from Innova's pipeline.
details: ISG Renewables, a joint venture of Innova and Schroders Greencoat's Greencoat UK Solar, bought the 28.7 MWp Newbold Pacey solar farm (formerly Elms Farm) near Wellesbourne, Warwickshire, from Innova's pipeline. Innova manages construction; energisation was due later in 2024.
context: It is ISG's third deal after Carn Nicholas (10 MWp, Wales) and Bicker Fen (22.6 MWp, Lincolnshire). The farm could power about 10,600 homes.

sources.title: Innova and Schroders Greencoat JV acquires Newbold Pacey solar park

context: The deals involve 1,500 MW of solar and 688 MW of wind and take ReNew's contracted portfolio to 15.6 GW. Firm, dispatchable supply costs more because it needs storage.

context: Fortum, which entered India in 2012 and sold 56.25% in 2018–2019, is limiting its exposure in India to focus on the Nordics.

title: Matrix Renewables closes €300 million green corporate loan with Santander CIB

advisors.name: EY
advisors.role: valuation adviser and financial model auditor to Santander CIB

summary: Matrix Renewables, a renewable energy platform backed by TPG Rise, has closed a €300 million corporate debt financing with Santander CIB. The money will help fund construction of its advanced-stage projects in Spain, the US, Italy and Chile.
details: The loan is made to the company as a whole rather than to a single project, and it is labelled Green and Sustainability-Linked, meaning the funds go to green uses and terms are tied to sustainability targets under recognised loan principles. Matrix says its advanced development pipeline totals 2.5 GW out of a 14 GW portfolio of solar, storage and green hydrogen projects across Europe, the United States and Latin America. Clifford Chance in Madrid advised Matrix on legal matters, while Linklaters in Madrid advised Santander CIB on legal matters and EY acted as valuation adviser and financial model auditor.
context: Matrix says the facility supports its aim of long-term growth and making better use of the equity it has invested, and its executives claim it strengthens the company's standing in the sector. Santander CIB presents the deal as part of its push to finance renewable energy, and the bank has a stated goal of raising €220 billion in green financing between 2019 and 2030.

sources.title: MATRIX RENEWABLES SECURES €300 MILLION GREEN AND SUSTAINABLE CORPORATE FINANCING WITH SANTANDER CIB

title: Vesper Energy sells Deer Creek solar and storage project in California to unnamed Fortune 500 energy company
summary: Vesper Energy, a Texas-based renewable developer, has completed the sale of its Deer Creek Renewable Energy project in Tulare County, California. The buyer is described only as a Fortune 500 energy company. The project combines up to 50 MWac of solar with up to 50 MW of energy storage.
details: Deer Creek sits on 378 acres in Tulare County, California. It is planned to host up to 50 MWac of solar generation, meaning capacity measured on the alternating current side that feeds the grid, plus up to 50 MW of battery storage. The storage energy volume in MWh and its duration were not disclosed. The price, the buyer's name and the project's development stage were not stated, and no advisers were named.
context: Vesper says the sale reflects the strength of its development portfolio in California, where it reports a pipeline of about 1,750 MW of solar and storage projects. The company has two more projects in development in Tulare County and links its work there to California's target of 100% zero-carbon electricity planning by 2045. Selling developed projects to larger owners is a common way for developers to recycle capital into new projects.

sources.title: Vesper Energy Completes Sale of Deer Creek Renewable Energy Project

title: Canadian Solar wins 193 MW of battery storage contracts in Japan's first long-term decarbonization auction

buyers.name: Organization for Cross-regional Coordination of Transmission Operators (OCCTO)

target: Three battery storage projects in Aomori, Fukushima and Yamaguchi prefectures
summary: Canadian Solar won three battery energy storage projects totaling 193 MW in Japan's first Long-Term Decarbonization Power Source Auction. The company says this represents 13.3% of all storage capacity awarded in the auction, whose results were published on April 26, 2024.
details: The three projects are located in Aomori, Fukushima and Yamaguchi prefectures and are expected to begin commercial operation between 2027 and 2028. Canadian Solar will sign Capacity Reserve Agreements with OCCTO, Japan's grid coordination body, under which the projects make their capacity available for 20 years in exchange for fixed payments that help cover the storage systems' fixed costs. The projects will use the SolBank 3.0 battery system made by e-STORAGE, a subsidiary of CSI Solar. Individual project sizes, storage duration and contract value were not disclosed.
context: The auction is Japan's first long-term mechanism to support low-carbon capacity with multi-decade revenue contracts, giving storage developers predictable income. Canadian Solar claims the win confirms its strong position in Japan's storage market and says its Japanese pipeline stood at 1.376 GWh of storage and 213 MWp of solar as of January 31, 2024. The company expects further growth in Japan driven by the auction and corporate demand.

sources.title: Canadian Solar Secures 193 MW of BESS Projects in Japan's Inaugural Long-term Decarbonization Power Source Auction

context: FDRE projects combine solar, wind and batteries to give round-the-clock supply. The deal takes TPREL to 9,421 MW, including 4,906 MW under implementation.

title: Avaada Energy secures about US$143 million from SBI for 400 MWp Gujarat solar
summary: Avaada Energy secured INR 1,190 crore (about US$143 million) of green financing from the State Bank of India for a 400 MWp solar project in Surendranagar, Gujarat.

title: Eavor Erdwärme Geretsried signs loan for Bavarian geothermal project
summary: Eavor Erdwärme Geretsried, the project company of Chubu Electric and Eavor, signed a loan agreement for the Geretsried geothermal project in Bavaria.
details: Eavor Erdwärme Geretsried, the project company of Chubu Electric and Eavor, signed about €130 million of project loans from JBIC, the EIB, ING (Tokyo) and Mizuho for the Geretsried geothermal project in Bavaria, with Nippon Export and Investment Insurance covering the commercial banks. It also receives a €91.6 million EU Innovation Fund grant.

title: ADB signs US$121.55 million for 100 MW solar plant in Bangladesh

sources.title: ADB signs $121.55m financing deal for Bangladesh's 100 MW solar project

title: Morgan Stanley provides $82 million tax equity for Plus Power's 90 MW Superstition storage project in Arizona
summary: Plus Power closed an $82 million tax equity investment from Morgan Stanley for its 90 MW / 360 MWh Superstition Energy Storage facility in Gilbert, Arizona. Plus Power says it has raised about $2 billion for five Arizona and Texas storage facilities since October 2023.
details: Superstition is a standalone battery storage facility that stores 90 MW for four hours, giving 360 MWh. Tax equity is a form of investment where an investor funds a project in return for using its federal tax credits. The facility is due online in June 2024 alongside the related 250 MW / 1000 MWh Sierra Estrella project in Avondale, Arizona. Both will supply capacity and energy services to the Salt River Project grid near Phoenix.
context: The company expects the new funding to let it bring its Arizona and Texas facilities online by summer 2024, ahead of expected peak demand in the Southwest. Plus Power earlier raised nearly $100 million in tax equity from Greenprint Capital Management for its Ebony project in Texas. The company says it has 10 GW of battery storage in grid connection queues.

title: Captona makes preferred equity investment in UBS Asset Management's 728 MW Texas battery storage portfolio
target: Portfolio of four utility-scale battery storage projects in Texas

advisors.name: Kirkland & Ellis
advisors.role: legal counsel to Captona and its equity partner

advisors.name: Troutman Pepper
advisors.role: legal counsel to UBS Asset Management

summary: Captona has closed a preferred equity investment in a portfolio of four battery storage projects in Texas owned by UBS Asset Management's Real Estate & Private Markets business. The portfolio totals 728 MW of power capacity and 1.06 GWh of storage. The deal was structured as a joint venture between the two firms.
details: The four projects, previously acquired by UBS Asset Management, each range from 100 MW to 300 MW and are expected to begin operating in 2024. Captona's investment takes the form of preferred equity, meaning it receives priority returns ahead of common owners. According to the release, the structure lets UBS Asset Management capture the value of federal tax credits without forming a traditional tax equity partnership, a common arrangement where an investor funds a project in exchange for its tax benefits. Kirkland & Ellis advised Captona and its equity partner, and Troutman Pepper advised UBS Asset Management. No financial terms were disclosed.
context: The parties present the deal as an alternative way to monetise tax credits on storage projects. Captona says it wants to expand its energy transition portfolio, which includes solar, storage, fuel cell and clean fuels assets. UBS Asset Management describes the transaction as one of several approaches it uses to add value across its projects' lifecycle, and Captona argues battery storage supports grid reliability as demand rises.

sources.title: Captona and UBS Asset Management Close Joint Venture with Innovative Structure for 728MW/1.06GWh Battery Storage Portfolio

title: LiNova Energy raises $15.8 million Series A for polymer cathode battery development
summary: California-based battery developer LiNova Energy has raised $15.8 million in a Series A round, meaning its first major institutional funding round. Catalus Capital led the round, with participation from TotalEnergies subsidiary Saft, Chevron Technology Ventures and a group of other investors.
details: LiNova is developing a polymer cathode battery that is meant to avoid cobalt, nickel and other metal oxides in the cathode, the positive electrode of a battery cell. The company says it will use the money to expand research and development, scale up operations and move toward commercial sales. Alongside the raise, LiNova signed a joint development agreement with Saft to work on bringing the technology to market in Saft's key markets. Chevron's investment came from its $300 million Future Energy Fund II.
context: The company claims its technology can deliver higher energy density with a safer, lighter and cheaper battery that relies less on critical minerals. Backing from two oil and gas majors, through Saft and Chevron, gives the start-up access to industrial battery expertise and prototype production lines. LiNova targets electric vehicles, aerospace and stationary energy storage.

sources.title: LiNova Energy Secures $15.8 Million in Series A Financing to Accelerate High Energy Polymer Cathode Battery Development

context: Hyundai is buying the power to support its US manufacturing plants' sustainability goals.

sources.title: Matrix Renewables and Hyundai sign solar PPA

title: energyRe secures $155 million debt and $85 million tax equity for Lone Star solar-plus-storage project in South Carolina
summary: energyRe has raised $155 million in project financing arranged by Santander and an $85 million tax equity commitment from Bank of America for its Lone Star Solar project in South Carolina. The project pairs 108 MWdc of solar with a 198 MWh battery system.
details: The $155 million package combines a construction loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term debt repaid when the tax equity investor funds) and a letter of credit facility. Tax equity is an investment from a party, here Bank of America, that receives the project's federal tax benefits, in this case Investment Tax Credits under the Inflation Reduction Act. The project is under construction and is expected to start operating by fall 2024. It holds a 10-year power purchase agreement with Dominion Energy South Carolina, and Syensqo will buy all of its renewable energy certificates.
context: This is energyRe's first project financing and first tax equity deal in the US. The company says the battery will be the largest in South Carolina and on the Dominion Energy South Carolina network. energyRe reports more than 700 MW of contracted solar in the state and a regional development pipeline above 7 GW.

sources.title: energyRe Secures $155 Million in Project Financing and $85 Million Tax Equity Commitment for 108 MW Solar and 198MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) for the Lone Star Project

title: WEC Energy Group to buy 90% of Invenergy's 300 MW Delilah I solar project in Texas
summary: WEC Energy Group has agreed to acquire a 90% ownership interest in the 300 MW Delilah I Solar Energy Center in Texas, developed and built by Invenergy. The company expects its investment to total $459 million.
details: Delilah I sits about 140 miles northeast of Dallas and is expected to start commercial operation by the end of June 2024. Its output is sold under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to sell electricity at agreed terms, with an unnamed global automaker. The project is eligible for production tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act, which are federal tax benefits earned per unit of power generated. The deal still needs regulatory approvals.
context: Delilah I is one phase of the five-phase Samson & Delilah solar portfolio, which the release describes as one of the largest solar facilities under construction in the United States. WEC already holds a majority stake in the Samson I phase. The purchase adds to WEC's Infrastructure segment, which the company says has existing or planned investments in 11 solar and wind projects totaling over 2 GW, all with long-term offtake contracts.
