title: Enfinity Global secures $195 million long-term financing for 70 MW Aomori solar plant in Japan

buyers.name: Nomura Securities International
buyers.role: initial lead arranger and sole bookrunner

summary: Enfinity Global has closed $195 million (about ¥29.2 billion) of long-term debt for its 70 MW Aomori solar plant in northern Japan. Nomura Securities International and Aozora Bank arranged the financing.
details: The plant sits in Aomori Prefecture and was recently completed, so it is already producing power. The company expects it to generate more than 75 GWh a year, which it says could cover about 15,600 households and avoid roughly 35,000 tons of CO2 annually. It uses bifacial panels, which capture light on both sides and can benefit from sunlight reflected off snow. Nomura acted as initial lead arranger and sole bookrunner, meaning it structured and placed the loan, while Aozora Bank served as lead arranger and agent, administering the loan for lenders.
context: The project forms part of the 250 MW solar portfolio Enfinity Global owns in Japan. Refinancing an operating plant with long-term debt lets the owner recover capital for further investment. The company presents the deal as support for Japan's goal of carbon neutrality by 2050 and claims the plant shows bifacial panels can work well in one of the world's snowiest cities.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes $195 million of long-term financing for a 70 MW operational solar power plant in Japan

title: NT Solar makes four solar tax credit investments totaling 152.5 MWdc and launches Renewable Investing Fund
target: Four US solar projects and portfolios in Rhode Island, New Jersey, New York and California
summary: NT Solar, a tax credit syndicator owned by the National Trust Community Investment Corporation, completed four solar investment tax credit deals backing projects with a combined 152.5 MWdc. The projects are in Rhode Island, New Jersey, New York and California, with developers Dimension Energy, New Energy Equity and Revity Energy. The latest Dimension financing was the first deal from NT Solar's new Renewable Investing Fund.
details: The investments use the federal investment tax credit (ITC), a tax break that investors can claim in exchange for funding a project. The portfolio includes what the release calls the largest solar installation in Rhode Island to date, along with community solar projects, where local subscribers share output from a single array. NT Solar's work with Dimension Energy, begun in late 2022 and expanded in September and December 2023, now covers 10 projects of over 71 MWdc in New Jersey, New York and California. The Revity Energy deal was done via Nelnet, Inc., and offtakers include corporate and community subscribers plus municipal, university, school and hospital buyers. No deal values were disclosed.
context: NT Solar says the projects will produce nearly 250 million kWh a year and that the Dimension projects will save subscribers over US$1 million annually. The company presents the new fund, backed by an unnamed new investor partner, as a sign of its fund management record. Its newly appointed CEO said it is expanding fundraising to meet demand from its project pipeline.

sources.title: NT Solar Celebrates New Impact Investment Fund & Series of Successful Transactions

title: Globeleq buys 48.3% stake in 25 MWp Winnergy solar plant in Egypt
summary: Globeleq has completed the purchase of a 48.3% equity stake in the operating 25 MWp Winnergy solar plant in Egypt. The sellers were Enerray, Enerray Global Solar Opportunities and Desert Technologies. No price was disclosed.
details: The plant sits in the Benban Solar complex near Aswan, next to Globeleq's 66 MWp ARC solar plant, and has been running since 2019. It was built under the second round of Egypt's feed-in tariff program, a scheme that pays a fixed price for renewable power. It sells about 58 GWh a year to the state grid company EETC under a 25-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy its output. The project was financed by IFC, British International Investment, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and Europe Arab Bank. GILA Altawakol Electric stays on as co-shareholder and as the operations and maintenance contractor.
context: Globeleq, which is owned by British International Investment and Norfund, says the asset fits its existing Egyptian portfolio, where it has invested for 20 years. The company says it is pursuing further opportunities in Egypt in green hydrogen and ammonia, solar, wind and desalination. It is also leading a large green hydrogen and ammonia project in the country under a framework agreement signed at COP27.

sources.title: GLOBELEQ ACQUIRES THE 25 MWp WINNERGY SOLAR PV PLANT IN EGYPT

title: Eversource agrees to sell 50% of Sunrise Wind to Ørsted
summary: Eversource Energy signed definitive documents to sell its 50% stake in the 924 MW Sunrise Wind offshore project to Ørsted.
details: Eversource finalised the sale of its 50% stake in the 924 MW Sunrise Wind offshore project to Ørsted. Eversource will stay on under a construction management agreement to lead onshore construction, with no ownership or cost obligations.
context: Sunrise Wind will serve New York State, and its onshore transmission is to be built by local union labour. Eversource becomes a paid service provider only.

sources.title: Eversource Energy to sell Sunrise Wind stake to Ørsted

title: CC&L Infrastructure completes purchase of 80% stake in 300 MW Sharp Hills wind farm from EDPR Canada
summary: Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure has closed its acquisition of an 80% equity interest in the Sharp Hills wind farm in Alberta, Canada, from EDP Renewables Canada. The onshore project has about 300 MW of capacity. No price was disclosed.
details: Sharp Hills finished construction and began full operations in early 2024. Its output is sold under a 15-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract fixing who buys the electricity, with a counterparty the buyer describes as high quality. EDPR Canada keeps the remaining 20% and the two companies plan to own and operate the project together. The release says the farm produces power equivalent to the use of more than 160,000 Alberta homes.
context: The company says this is its first wind investment in Canada and lifts its renewable ownership to about 1.8 GW across Canada, the US and Chile, with roughly $6 billion in assets under management. It is the second deal between the two firms after a 560 MW US wind and solar portfolio purchase in 2020, bringing their joint holdings to more than 800 MW of operating projects.

sources.title: CONNOR, CLARK & LUNN INFRASTRUCTURE EXCEEDS 1.8 GW OF CLEAN ENERGY CAPACITY WITH CLOSING OF ALBERTA WIND FARM INVESTMENT

title: Sonnedix Japan refinances eight solar projects with ¥5.3 billion
summary: Sonnedix Japan refinanced eight high-voltage solar projects of about 19 MW with ¥5.3 billion (about US$34.4 million) from MUFG Bank and The Iyo Bank.
details: Sonnedix Japan refinanced eight solar projects of about 18–19 MW with ¥5.3 billion (about US$34.4 million) from MUFG Bank and Iyo Bank, its first portfolio financing in Japan.
context: Financing several plants together simplifies management. Sonnedix runs 25 projects in Japan with about 495 MW.

sources.title: Sonnedix secures $34.4m refinancing for Japanese solar projects

title: Origin Energy to buy 1.5 GW Yanco Delta Wind Farm from Vinya Energy
summary: Origin Energy agreed to buy the 1.5 GW Yanco Delta Wind Farm in New South Wales from Vinya Energy for A$80.3 million upfront, plus up to A$112.4 million more.
details: Origin Energy agreed to buy the 1.5 GW Yanco Delta Wind Farm, with an 800 MWh battery, in New South Wales from Virya Energy for A$125 million plus up to A$175 million tied to milestones. Key planning approvals are secured.
context: The site covers 33,000 ha in the South West Renewable Energy Zone, an area planned for new transmission. Origin is shifting its portfolio from coal to renewables and storage.

sources.title: Origin Energy expands RE portfolio with Yanco Delta Wind Farm acquisition

title: Nova Clean Energy buys HyFuels' 1 GW Texas wind and solar portfolio
summary: Nova Clean Energy acquired HyFuels, a portfolio of more than 1 GW of wind and solar projects and an early green ammonia project on the Texas Gulf Coast.
details: Nova Clean Energy bought HyFuels from BNB Renewable Energy: more than 1 GW of mid- to late-stage wind and solar development on about 25,000 acres on the Texas Gulf Coast, plus an earlier-stage green ammonia project. Phase one aims for notice to proceed in 2025 and operation in 2026.
context: The power is split evenly between wind and solar, whose output peaks at different times. BNB will keep providing development services.

sources.title: Nova Clean Energy acquires 1 GW wind and solar portfolio

title: Madison Energy Infrastructure acquires Sun Tribe's commercial and K-12 solar business
target: Sun Tribe Solar commercial projects, pipeline and development team
summary: Madison Energy Infrastructure has bought the commercial solar business of Virginia developer Sun Tribe, including its current projects, future pipeline and development team. The business is known for school solar installations in Virginia. Financial terms and portfolio capacity were not disclosed.
details: The asset purchase agreement covers Sun Tribe Solar's existing commercial projects, its pipeline of future projects, and the transfer of its commercial development staff. Sun Tribe Solar has helped 94 schools across 21 Virginia counties install solar over seven years. Rich Allevi, previously president of Sun Tribe Solar, will keep leading the team under Madison, which stays based in Charlottesville. The Solar Empowered Schools education program will continue under Madison's ownership.
context: Madison, which says it owns over half a gigawatt of clean energy assets in more than 25 states, had already been the preferred long-term owner of Sun Tribe's commercial projects and plans to extend the school solar model across its footprint. Bringing development in-house means the team no longer needs an outside buyer to own finished projects. Sun Tribe will narrow its focus to utility-scale and community solar in Appalachia, the Mid-Atlantic and the Southeast through its development, construction and asset management units.

sources.title: Madison Energy Infrastructure Acquires Commercial and K-12 Solar Portfolio from Longtime Partner Sun Tribe

title: Origis Energy closes $136 million MUFG financing for 75 MW Rice Creek Solar in Florida
summary: Origis Energy has closed a $136 million construction financing facility with MUFG for its Rice Creek Solar project in Putnam County, Florida. The 75 MW plant will sell its power to members of the Florida Municipal Power Agency.
details: Rice Creek Solar is a 75 MW photovoltaic plant that is under construction and described as nearing completion. The MUFG facility is a construction loan that converts into a term loan, meaning the money used to build the plant turns into longer-term debt once it is operating. The Florida Municipal Power Agency coordinates the contract on behalf of its member utilities, which will buy the plant's output, while Origis builds, owns and operates it. Latham & Watkins advised Origis with Akerman as local counsel, and Milbank advised MUFG with Greenberg Traurig as local counsel.
context: The project is part of what the release calls one of the largest municipal-backed solar programmes in the US, and the deal extends an existing lending relationship between Origis and MUFG. Origis expects the project to qualify for an energy community bonus on its investment tax credit, an extra federal incentive for projects near retired fossil plants, because it sits in the same census tract as a recently closed coal plant. The company says its Florida solar footprint is close to one gigawatt.

sources.title: Origis Energy and MUFG Close $136 Million Project Financing for Florida Municipal Solar Project

title: Recurrent Energy secures BRL 343 million BNB financing for 152 MWp Jaiba III solar project in Brazil

buyers.name: Banco do Nordeste do Brasil S.A. (BNB)

summary: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, has obtained 343 million Brazilian reais (about US$70 million) of project financing from Banco do Nordeste do Brasil for its 152 MWp Jaiba III solar project in Brazil. The plant is under construction and has a long-term power contract with steelmaker Usiminas.
details: The loan is non-recourse, meaning lenders are repaid from the project's own cash flows rather than from the parent company. It runs for 22 years, covering both construction and operation, and is indexed to Brazil's IPCA consumer price index, so repayments adjust with inflation. Power will be sold to Usiminas under a 15-year inflation-adjusted power purchase agreement won in a private auction. The project uses Canadian Solar BiHiKu modules, employs nearly 900 workers, and is expected to start operating in the fourth quarter of 2024.
context: The deal extends an existing lending relationship between Recurrent and BNB. Recurrent says it owns or operates about 2 GWp of solar in Latin America and has a regional pipeline of 5 GWp of solar and 2 GWh of storage. The company claims the plant will avoid roughly 150,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year and describes Brazil as the largest renewable energy market in Latin America.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Secures 343 Million Brazilian Reais Financing for 152 MW Solar Project in Brazil

title: Bitech Technologies agrees to acquire Bridgelink's Emergen Energy with 5.8 GW solar and storage pipeline
summary: Bitech Technologies signed a definitive agreement to buy all of Emergen Energy, a subsidiary of Texas developer Bridgelink Development. Emergen holds development rights to an estimated 1,965 MW of battery storage and 3,840 MW of solar projects in the United States. In exchange, Bridgelink will own about 31.3% of Bitech's common stock.
details: The projects are at the development stage, meaning they are planned but not yet built, and sit in states including Texas, Arizona and Louisiana. The deal is a share-based business combination under a membership interest purchase agreement, the contract used to buy ownership units in a limited liability company. Closing is expected by April 24, 2024 and depends on conditions including a project management services agreement with a Bridgelink affiliate, employment agreements for Benjamin Tran and Cole Johnson, and Bitech completing due diligence to its satisfaction. Tran remains chairman and interim CEO while Johnson becomes president leading the new storage and solar division.
context: The deal would turn Bitech, an over-the-counter listed technology company, into a holder of a large solar and storage pipeline. Bitech claims the projects could be worth up to about 325 million dollars once launched and says it believes it can secure financing, though no funding is yet committed. The combined company says it aims to raise capital and pursue a listing on NASDAQ.

sources.title: Bitech Technologies Executes Definitive Agreement with Bridgelink for a Business Combination to Acquire Battery Energy Storage Systems and Solar Projects with estimated capacity of up to 5.8 GW

title: Shell co-invests in Eco Wave Power's first US wave energy station
summary: Eco Wave Power agreed with Shell for Shell to participate in developing Eco Wave Power's first US onshore wave energy project.
details: Shell agreed to co-invest in the development of Eco Wave Power's first US onshore wave energy project, after a three-month feasibility study with Shell identified at least 77 potentially suitable US sites.
context: Eco Wave Power already runs a pilot station at the Port of Los Angeles. California's SB 605 directs the state Energy Commission to study wave and tidal energy along its coast.

sources.title: Shell and Eco Wave co-invest in first US onshore wave energy station

title: ANDRITZ invests NOK 82.7 million in electrolyser maker HydrogenPro via private placement
summary: Norwegian electrolyser company HydrogenPro has raised NOK 82.7 million in new equity by issuing new shares to Austrian technology group ANDRITZ. The deal was done as a private placement, meaning the shares were sold directly to one investor rather than offered to the public.
details: HydrogenPro, listed on the Oslo stock exchange, issued new shares to ANDRITZ, which is listed in Vienna and works on green hydrogen plants. The release does not give the number of shares, the price per share or the resulting ownership stake, and points to a separate stock exchange notice for those details. ANDRITZ brings EPC capability, short for engineering, procurement and construction, meaning it can design, source and build complete plants. HydrogenPro says the two firms have been cooperating for about nine months before this investment.
context: HydrogenPro says the investment fits a strategy launched in August 2023 under CEO Jarle Dragvik that focuses on growing in the United States and finding strategic partners and new funding sources. The company claims that combining its electrolysers with ANDRITZ construction capability will let the partners offer full-scope delivery for large-scale electrolysis projects, which many customers require. It has also recently set up a US sales organization.

sources.title: HydrogenPro ASA: Secures strategic NOK 82.7 million investment from ANDRITZ AG

title: PNE sells 240 MW Khauta solar project to NOA Group
summary: PNE sold the 240 MW Khauta solar project in South Africa's Free State to NOA Group.
details: PNE sold the 240 MW Khauta solar project in Free State province, South Africa, to NOA Group, with PNE's WKN Windcurrent continuing to support development. It was expected to be fully developed by mid-2024, and could be enlarged.
context: NOA, backed by African Infrastructure Investment Managers, is an aggregator that buys power from several plants and sells it to private customers; Khauta will be the first large solar plant in its portfolio.

sources.title: PNE sells 240 MW South African PV project

title: SUSI Asia Energy Transition Fund invests in Alba Renewables

buyers.name: SUSI Partners (SUSI Asia Energy Transition Fund)

summary: SUSI Partners' Asia Energy Transition Fund agreed to invest with developer Alba Renewables in utility-scale solar and onshore wind in the Philippines.
details: The SUSI Asia Energy Transition Fund signed an investment agreement with Alba Renewables to fund the construction of designated utility-scale solar and onshore wind projects in the Philippines over the next 24 months.
context: The deal helps Alba scale up across Southeast Asia; strong deal flow led SUSI to reopen the fund to investors until September 2024.

sources.title: SUSI Partners invests in buildout of utility scale renewables projects in the Philippines

title: Luxcara and BayernLB close financing for 315.7 MWp Danish solar portfolio
summary: Luxcara and Bayerische Landesbank reached financial close on a 315.7 MWp solar portfolio of three plants in Denmark.
details: Luxcara and BayernLB reached financial close on a 315.7 MWp Danish solar portfolio of three plants: Barmosen (137.3 MWp) and Faxe (111.6 MWp) in Zealand and Vildbjerg (66.7 MWp) in Jutland, energised in late 2022 and fully connected in 2023. The amount is confidential.
context: It is one of Northern Europe's largest solar portfolios. Financing operating plants lets Luxcara recycle equity into new projects.

sources.title: Luxcara achieves financial close for Danish PV portfolio

title: Solar Philippines and Medco joint venture signs PPAs with PLN for 50 MW

sellers.name: Solar Philippines and Medco Energi JV

summary: A Solar Philippines–Medco Energi joint venture signed 20-year PPAs with Indonesia's PLN for two solar projects totalling 50 MW.
details: A joint venture of Solar Philippines and Medco Energi signed 20-year PPAs with Indonesian state utility PLN for two 25 MW solar farms in east and west Bali, 50 MW in total, described as the largest ground-mounted solar projects in Indonesia to date.
context: Solar Philippines says the projects are not financially significant for it, but show it can form ventures and win PPAs abroad.

sources.title: Solar Philippines memulai PPA dengan PLN untuk proyek solar sebesar 50 MW

title: Natixis CIB and three banks close $176.6 million green loan for Solarpack's 300 MW San Martin solar plant in Peru

buyers.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: Joint Bookrunner, Joint Lead Arranger, Joint Green Loan Coordinator and Administrative Agent

summary: Natixis CIB and three other international commercial banks have closed a $176.6 million senior secured green loan for the roughly 300 MW San Martin solar plant in southern Peru. The project is sponsored by Spain-based independent power producer Solarpack.
details: The loan will fund construction, operation and maintenance of the San Martin solar photovoltaic plant in southern Peru. It is senior secured, meaning lenders are repaid first and hold claims on project assets, and it is labelled green, meaning proceeds go to environmentally beneficial use. Natixis CIB served as joint bookrunner, joint lead arranger, joint green loan coordinator and administrative agent, the bank that manages the loan on behalf of the lending group. The other three banks were not named in the release.
context: The parties say the plant will be the largest solar facility in Peru's history and claim it will supply power equivalent to the needs of about 440,000 homes a year. Natixis describes it as the largest solar financing in Peru, and it is Solarpack's largest project financing to date according to the bank.

sources.title: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking closes $176.6 million financing of a c. 300MW solar PV plant in Peru sponsored by Solarpack, acting as Joint Bookrunner, Joint Lead Arranger, Joint Green Loan Coordinator, and Administrative Agent

title: Raven SR raises $15 million led by Ascent Funds for waste-to-hydrogen technology
summary: Wyoming-based renewable fuels company Raven SR has secured $15 million in new investment. Venture fund Ascent Funds led the round, joined by existing backers Chevron New Energies, ITOCHU and Stellar J.
details: Raven SR uses a steam and carbon dioxide reforming process that turns waste into hydrogen and synthetic fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel, without burning the material or using a catalyst. The company says the money will help finalize production setup as it moves toward building an organic waste-to-hydrogen plant in Richmond, California. Stellar J, one of the investors, is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, meaning the firm that designs and builds the plant, for that project. Alongside the raise, former Fannie Mae CFO Stuart McFarland became board chairman, Ascent's Mark Gordon became vice chairman, and CFO Matt Scanlon was promoted to president.
context: The company presents the round as a sign of investor confidence in its technology, which it claims produces more hydrogen and aviation fuel per ton of waste than alternatives. The Richmond project is described as the first biomass-to-hydrogen facility in California permitted under the state's environmental quality law. Raven SR expects 2024 to be the year it begins commercializing the process.

sources.title: Renewable fuels company Raven SR bolsters leadership team, secures $15M investment

title: Ridgewood Infrastructure makes structured equity investment in US solar producer MN8 Energy
summary: US infrastructure investor Ridgewood Infrastructure has made a structured equity investment in MN8 Energy, a large independent US solar and storage power producer. The size of the investment and any stake acquired were not disclosed.
details: Structured equity is a form of investment that sits between ordinary shares and debt, often with preferred returns or special terms, though the release does not describe the specific terms. MN8 reports a solar fleet of more than 3.2 GW across over 875 projects in 28 states, plus over 270 MW of battery storage projects and EV charging services. The capital is meant to support continued growth of MN8's solar, storage and EV charging portfolio. Wells Fargo acted as Ridgewood's exclusive financial adviser and King & Spalding was its legal counsel.
context: Ridgewood presents the deal as part of its strategy of sustainability-focused investments in the US lower middle market. MN8 says the funding gives it capital to scale growth and develop new solutions for its enterprise customers. The parties also claim the investment will support green energy jobs and lower emissions.

sources.title: Ridgewood Infrastructure Announces Structured Equity Investment in MN8 Energy, One of America's Largest Privately Owned Solar Energy Companies

title: Commerz Real buys 45.6 MW Lumivaara wind farm in Finland
summary: Commerz Real bought the 45.6 MW, eight-turbine Lumivaara wind farm in Finland from Energiequelle for its Klimavest fund.
details: Commerz Real bought the 45.6 MW, eight-turbine Lumivaara wind farm in Hyrynsalmi, Kainuu, about 560 km north-east of Helsinki, for its Klimavest fund, handed over turnkey by Energiequelle. Nordex supplied the turbines.
context: It is Klimavest's fourth Finnish wind farm, taking it past 170 MW there; Finland allows subsidy-free wind farms to be built and run on market revenue.

sources.title: Commerz Real acquires Klimavest wind farm in Finland

title: Southwest Airlines takes full ownership of renewable ethanol developer SAFFiRE Renewables
summary: Southwest Airlines has acquired SAFFiRE Renewables through its subsidiary Southwest Airlines Renewable Ventures, moving from minority investor to sole owner. SAFFiRE is developing technology to turn corn stover into renewable ethanol that can be upgraded into sustainable aviation fuel in the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: SAFFiRE holds an exclusive license for technology developed at the US Department of Energy's National Renewable Energy Laboratory to convert corn stover, the leftover stalks and leaves from corn harvests, into ethanol. Southwest first invested during the first phase of the DOE-supported pilot project in 2022. With the acquisition, SAFFiRE plans a second-phase pilot plant at Conestoga's Arkalon Energy ethanol facility in Liberal, Kansas, initially designed to process 10 tons of corn stover per day. The ethanol is then planned to be converted into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), a jet fuel substitute made from non-fossil sources, by LanzaJet. The release does not name the sellers, the deal value or advisers.
context: Southwest describes SAF as a key part of its plan to reach net zero carbon emissions by 2050 and says the deal reflects confidence in SAFFiRE's technology. The acquisition follows Southwest's recent investment in LanzaJet, which the release says runs the world's first commercial ethanol-to-SAF plant. The company presents renewable ethanol as an important feedstock for making SAF affordable at large volumes, though the project remains at pilot stage.

sources.title: SOUTHWEST AIRLINES ACQUIRES SAFFiRE RENEWABLES AND STRENGTHENS FOCUS ON SUSTAINABILITY

title: Aster Renewable secures NT$8.25 billion from MUFG for Changhua floating solar and storage
summary: Aster Renewable Energy secured NT$8.25 billion (about US$257.7 million) of debt from MUFG Bank for floating solar and battery projects in Changbin Industrial Area, Taiwan.
details: Aster Renewable Energy secured NT$8.25 billion (about US$257.7 million) of debt led by MUFG for a 140.2 MWp floating solar project with 19.6 MW / 78.3 MWh of battery storage in the Changbin Industrial Area, Changhua, Taiwan. It was MUFG's first solar loan in Asia-Pacific.
context: The deal was 1.8 times oversubscribed. Taiwan targets 20 GW of solar by 2025 and 30 GW by 2030.

sources.title: Aster Renewable bags $257.7m loan from MUFG for RE project

title: Stonepeak buys 80% of TerraWind Renewables
summary: Stonepeak acquired 80% of TerraWind Renewables, an onshore wind platform for Japan and Asia Pacific; Shizen Energy keeps the rest.
details: Stonepeak bought 80% of TerraWind Renewables, an onshore wind platform from Shizen Energy, which keeps 20%. TerraWind has 30 MW in late-stage development in Japan and a pipeline of over 300 MW across Asia-Pacific.
context: Stonepeak cites TerraWind's secured long-term contracts. The deal funds expansion of Shizen's wind business.

sources.title: Stonepeak invests in APAC onshore energy wind platform

title: wpd and Bank SinoPac close financing for 25.2 MW Hsinyuan wind farm
summary: wpd's Hsinyuan Wind Power and Bank SinoPac closed financing for the 25.2 MW Hsinyuan onshore wind farm in Yunlin County, Taiwan.
details: wpd's subsidiary Hsinyuan Wind Power and Bank SinoPac closed financing on 18 March 2024 for the built and commissioned 25.2 MW Hsinyuan wind farm in Lunbei, Yunlin County, Taiwan: six Vestas V136 turbines of 4.2 MW.
context: With 112 m hub height they are Taiwan's largest onshore turbines. wpd has installed over 200 onshore turbines in Taiwan and has 275 MW of wind and 50 MWp of solar in its pipeline there.

sources.title: wpd and Bank SinoPac announce financial close Hsinyuan onshore wind project

title: Walmart signs 15-year PPA for 162 MW of new EDPR NA solar project in Texas
target: 162 MWac share of a new 180 MWac solar project in Texas
summary: EDP Renewables North America and Walmart have signed a 15-year power purchase agreement covering 162 MWac of a new 180 MWac solar project in Texas. A power purchase agreement is a long-term contract under which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project.
details: Walmart will take 162 MWac of output from the 180 MWac utility-scale solar project, which has not been named and is still in development. The companies say the project could supply the equivalent of more than 27,000 homes per year. EDPR NA estimates about 42 million dollars in payments to local governments over the project's life, plus around 300 construction jobs and three permanent operations jobs. No financial terms, construction timeline or advisers were disclosed.
context: The deal extends a partnership dating to 2018 that includes Walmart offtake from EDPR NA wind farms in Illinois and Indiana and 36 MWac of distributed solar across 66 sites. With this contract, utility-scale procurement between the two reaches 395 MW. Walmart says it aims to enable up to 10 GW of new clean energy projects by 2030, and EDPR NA describes Texas as a strategic market where it already has over 1.2 GW installed.

sources.title: EDP Renewables and Walmart Announce 15-Year Power Purchase Agreement in Texas

title: Swift Current Energy secures tax equity and NRG offtake for 260 MWdc Tres Bahias Solar in Texas

advisors.name: Vinson & Elkins LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Swift Current Energy

advisors.name: Husch Blackwell LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Swift Current Energy

advisors.name: Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Morgan Stanley Renewables

advisors.name: Jackson Walker LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Morgan Stanley Renewables

summary: Swift Current Energy announced tax equity financing from UnitedHealth Group and Morgan Stanley Renewables, along with a power purchase agreement with an NRG Energy affiliate, for its 260 MWdc Tres Bahias Solar project in Calhoun County, Texas. Part of the output is used to power City of Houston facilities.
details: Tres Bahias is an operating 260 MWdc solar plant on the Texas Gulf Coast. Tax equity, a form of investment where investors fund the project in exchange for its tax credits and other tax benefits, comes from UnitedHealth Group and Morgan Stanley Renewables. Construction was earlier financed by ING Capital with Siemens Financial Services and Associated Bank as additional lenders, and that construction loan has been fully repaid. Under the power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity, an NRG affiliate takes power and part of it supplies City of Houston facilities as part of the city's electricity supply arrangements. First Solar supplied modules, Array Technologies supplied trackers and IEA Constructors built the project.
context: The company says Tres Bahias is the largest operating solar project in Calhoun County and the third largest in the Texas Gulf Coast region. Swift Current, which remains owner and operator, presents the deal as part of growing its operating portfolio and supplying power to large cities, following a similar arrangement with Chicago through its Double Black Diamond project.

sources.title: SWIFT CURRENT ENERGY ANNOUNCES POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT AND TAX EQUITY FINANCING FOR 260 MW SOLAR PROJECT IN TEXAS

title: Natixis CIB leads US$1.27 billion construction financing for four Invenergy wind and solar projects in Kansas and Texas

buyers.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: Joint Lead Arranger, Co-Green Loan Coordinator, Joint Bookrunner, Documentation Agent and Administrative Agent

target: Diversion, Flat Ridge IV, Flat Ridge V and Pixley projects
summary: Natixis CIB has closed a series of construction loans totalling about US$1.27 billion for four Invenergy renewable projects. The wind and solar projects in Kansas and Texas add up to 677 MW and will be taken over by AEP utility subsidiaries once they start operating.
details: The portfolio includes the 200 MW Diversion wind project in Baylor and Wilbarger Counties, Texas, the 135 MW Flat Ridge IV and 153 MW Flat Ridge V wind projects in Harper and Kingsman Counties, Kansas, and the 189 MW Pixley solar project in Barber County, Kansas. All four are under construction. Construction financing is a loan that pays for building the plant before it earns revenue. Southwestern Electric Power Company will buy Diversion, expected online in Q4 2024, and Public Service Company of Oklahoma will buy the three Kansas projects, expected online in Q1 2025. Natixis CIB held several arranging roles, including green loan coordinator and administrative agent across all four financings.
context: The deal reflects a model where a developer builds projects and then hands them to a utility at commercial operation. According to the release, SWEPCO and PSO selected these facilities as the best economic option to meet customer capacity needs. Natixis presents the financings as part of its support for the energy transition and its long relationship with Invenergy.

sources.title: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking leads $1.27Bn construction financing of four renewable energy projects for Invenergy

title: RIC Energy sells seven New York solar plants to Radial Power
summary: RIC Energy sold seven solar plants in upstate New York, 34 MW in total, to Radial Power.
details: RIC Energy sold seven community solar plants of 34 MW in upstate New York to Radial Power, a total investment of more than US$85 million. They will supply more than 8,000 homes under utility community solar programmes.
context: RIC Energy has sold 13 New York plants of 70 MW in recent months and has over 600 MW of solar and storage upstate.

sources.title: Radial Power buys 7 solar projects from RIC Energy

title: Primergy signs PPA with San Diego Community Power for Purple Sage
summary: Primergy signed a long-term PPA with San Diego Community Power for the full 400 MWac and 1.6 GWh battery of its Purple Sage Energy Center.
details: Primergy signed a long-term PPA with San Diego Community Power, California's second-largest community choice aggregator, for the full 400 MWac and 1.6 GWh battery Purple Sage Energy Center in Nevada, between Las Vegas and the California border, from 2027.
context: A community choice aggregator buys power for local customers in place of the utility. Primergy is working with the Bureau of Land Management on siting standards.

sources.title: Primergy signs solar and storage PPA with San Diego Community Power

title: Ameren Missouri wins regulatory approval to acquire 300 MW Split Rail Solar from Invenergy and build two 50 MW projects

sellers.name: Invenergy
sellers.role: developer and seller of Split Rail Solar

target: Split Rail Solar (300 MW, Warren County, Missouri)
summary: The Missouri Public Service Commission approved Ameren Missouri's plan to build or acquire about 400 MW of solar in Missouri. The package includes buying the 300 MW Split Rail Solar project from Invenergy and building two 50 MW projects itself. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Split Rail Solar in Warren County is due to enter service in 2026 after Ameren Missouri acquires it from developer Invenergy. The utility will develop the 50 MW Vandalia Renewable Energy Center, targeted for 2025, and the 50 MW Bowling Green Renewable Energy Center, targeted for 2026. The order also sets conditions under which a fourth project, a 150 MW solar facility in Cass County, Illinois, could be approved if businesses fully subscribe to it through the utility's Renewable Solutions Program, a scheme where companies pay to source up to all of their power from renewables. Terms of all agreements are confidential.
context: Ameren Missouri describes this as its largest solar investment to date and says the projects could power roughly 73,000 homes. The company says federal tax credits will lower project costs and that those savings will pass to customers. It presents the projects as part of Ameren's goal of net-zero carbon emissions by 2045.

sources.title: Ameren Missouri receives approval for largest-ever solar investment

title: DPO's Cascade Digital Power acquires controlling stake in second US hydroelectric facility
summary: Digital Power Optimization, through its subsidiary Cascade Digital Power, has bought a controlling interest in a second hydroelectric plant in the United States. An affiliate of Aegon Asset Management Real Assets provided the funding. The price, seller, location and capacity of the plant were not disclosed.
details: The release does not name the facility or its location, but DPO says it can produce nearly twice as much power as the Hatfield, Wisconsin hydro plant that Cascade has managed since early 2022. DPO describes the new plant as in good condition with steady operations and cash flow. The purchase was financed by an affiliate of Aegon Asset Management Real Assets. No seller, advisers or deal value were named.
context: DPO builds data centers next to power plants so they can use the electricity directly, known as behind-the-meter, and says this approach significantly raised revenues at its Hatfield site. Cascade believes older rural hydro plants are undervalued and says it has invested over $20 million in the sector so far. DPO says it hopes to make further acquisitions with Aegon Asset Management Real Assets.

sources.title: DPO Acquires Controlling Interest in Second Hydroelectric Asset

title: Ocean Winds buys Shell's 50% stake in 2.4 GW SouthCoast Wind offshore project
summary: Shell New Energies US, a Shell plc subsidiary, has sold its 50% interest in SouthCoast Wind Energy to its joint venture partner Ocean Winds North America. SouthCoast Wind is developing an offshore wind farm of about 2,400 MW off the coast of Massachusetts. No price was disclosed.
details: The proposed wind farm sits in US federal waters roughly 30 miles south of Martha's Vineyard and 23 miles south of Nantucket, under federal lease OCS-A 0521 covering 127,388 acres. The joint venture was set up in 2018 under the name Mayflower Wind Energy and was previously owned equally by Shell and Ocean Winds. The deal was signed and closed at the same moment, so it took effect immediately. Ocean Winds is itself an equal joint venture of EDP Renewables and ENGIE.
context: Shell describes the sale as part of narrowing its renewable generation portfolio to markets where it believes it holds an advantage. The exit gives Ocean Winds full ownership of the Massachusetts project. Shell remains a 50% partner in Atlantic Shores Offshore Wind with EDF-RE, which is developing wind farms off New Jersey and New York, and says it plans to invest 10 to 15 billion dollars in low-carbon energy across 2023 to 2025.

sources.title: Shell sells interest in SouthCoast Wind to existing joint venture partner, Ocean Winds

title: Recurrent Energy acquires 420 MWp Rey solar portfolio in Andalusia, Spain
summary: Recurrent Energy, the development arm of Canadian Solar, has acquired a cluster of four solar projects in southern Spain with combined capacity of more than 420 MWp. The seller and price were not disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of the Rey I, II, III and IV projects in Carmona, in the province of Seville in Andalusia. The projects are already under construction and will use Canadian Solar's TOPCon bifacial modules, a panel type that captures light on both sides. MWp, or megawatt peak, measures the maximum output of the panels under standard test conditions. The company expects the portfolio to generate about 916,000 MWh per year, which it says is enough for more than 275,000 homes.
context: Recurrent Energy says the deal fits its aim of growing assets in Spain and globally, combining its own greenfield development with selective acquisitions. The company expects to start building more than 1 GW of solar projects in Spain during 2024.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Expands Solar Pipeline in Spain with the Acquisition of a Portfolio exceeding 420 MWp

title: Kyushu Electric completes purchase of 40% stake in Enfinity Global's 400 MW US solar portfolio
target: 400 MW US operating solar portfolio (28 plants)
summary: Enfinity Global has completed the sale of a 40% minority stake in its 400 MW portfolio of operating US solar plants to Japanese utility Kyushu Electric. Enfinity keeps the remaining 60% of the portfolio.
details: The portfolio consists of 28 solar PV power plants that are already in operation, located in California, North Carolina and Idaho. The two companies signed the definitive agreement in September 2023, and the deal has now closed. Enfinity Global will stay on as the long-term asset manager, meaning it will oversee day-to-day operation and performance of the plants. No price was disclosed.
context: The sale brings a large Japanese utility into the US solar market as a co-owner alongside Enfinity. Enfinity says it intends to build out an 11.6 GW US development pipeline over the next few years and to pursue more acquisitions and developer partnerships, and it recently announced buying 546 MW of solar projects under development from CS Energy in Colorado. Selling minority stakes in operating assets is a common way for developers to raise capital for new projects while keeping control.

sources.title: Enfinity Global completes a minority sale of its 400 MW operating portfolio in the United States to Kyushu Electric

title: ACEN Australia and SmartestEnergy sign PPA for New England Solar
summary: SmartestEnergy signed an eight-year PPA for 25% of the output of the 400 MW first stage of ACEN Australia's New England Solar project.
details: ACEN Australia and SmartestEnergy signed an eight-year PPA for 25% of the output of the 400 MW Stage 1 of ACEN's New England Solar project.
context: New England Solar is ACEN Australia's first operating project and will be one of Australia's largest solar plants at 720 MW when complete. SmartestEnergy resells renewable power to businesses.

sources.title: ACEN Australia inks PPA with SmartestEnergy for New England Solar

title: Standard Solar buys 18.5 MW Vermont solar portfolio from MHG Solar
summary: Standard Solar acquired six solar projects totalling 18.5 MW in Vermont from local developer MHG Solar.
details: Standard Solar bought an 18.5 MW portfolio of six Vermont solar projects from local developer MHG Solar, including Evergreen (2.9 MW, Fair Haven), Halladay (3.3 MW, Middlebury), Midway (3.3 MW, Berlin), Steinberg (3.3 MW, Brandon) and Stone Mill (2.8 MW, Castleton).
context: The projects sell to Vermont utilities under the state's Standard Offer Program, which sets long-term fixed prices for small renewable plants.

sources.title: Standard Solar acquires 18 MW solar portfolio

title: Longroad Energy reaches financial close on 220 MWdc Serrano solar-plus-storage project in Arizona

buyers.name: CIBC
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger, Administrative Agent, Collateral Agent, Green Loan Coordinator

buyers.name: U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance
buyers.role: Joint Lead Arranger and Depositary Bank

buyers.name: Athene Annuity and Life Insurance Company

advisors.name: Apterra Infrastructure Capital
advisors.role: adviser to tax equity investor Athene

summary: Longroad Energy has closed financing for Serrano, a 220 MWdc solar project paired with a 214 MWac / 855 MWh battery in Pinal and Pima Counties, Arizona. Debt was led by CIBC and Societe Generale, with Athene providing tax equity. The financing amount was not disclosed.
details: The project pairs 220 MWdc of solar using First Solar's US-made Series 7 thin-film panels with a battery of about four hours' duration supplied by Powin. Construction has started, with McCarthy as the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, and commercial operation is expected by mid-2025. Arizona Public Service will buy the output under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to buy electricity at agreed terms. Lenders include CIBC, Societe Generale, ANZ, PNC, Commerzbank and U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance, while Athene, an Apollo affiliate, is the tax equity investor, meaning it invests in exchange for the project's federal tax benefits. Apterra Infrastructure Capital advised Athene.
context: Longroad says the project lifts its operating or under-construction Arizona solar portfolio above 1.5 GW and is its first to use First Solar's Series 7 modules. The company expects Serrano to power about 61,000 homes and support grid reliability during hot summers. It also claims the project will contribute over $25 million to Arizona schools and communities over its life.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Closes Financing of Serrano, a 220 MWdc Solar and 214 MWac / 855 MWh Storage Project

title: Scout Clean Energy closes back-leverage financing for 130 MW Bitter Ridge wind farm in Indiana
summary: Scout Clean Energy has closed a back-leverage financing for its 130 MW Bitter Ridge Wind Farm in Jay County, Indiana. The lenders and loan amount were not disclosed.
details: Bitter Ridge is an operating wind farm that has been producing power since 2020. Back-leverage financing is a loan taken out at the owner level and secured by the owner's interest in the project, typically sitting behind any tax equity investors. The release does not name lenders, advisers or the loan size. The project also has a tax incentive agreement with Jay County that has led to 1.56 million US dollars in economic development payments, and the county is estimated to receive over 18 million US dollars in tax revenue over the project's life.
context: Scout describes the deal as the first step in a capital recycling strategy, meaning it borrows against operating assets to free up cash for new projects. The company says the money will help fund development across its roughly 19 GW US pipeline of wind, solar and storage projects, and expects more such financings to follow. Scout has been owned by Brookfield since early 2023.

sources.title: Scout Clean Energy Closes Financing for 130 MW Indiana Wind Farm

title: Sonnedix buys 49 MW solar portfolio in Portugal
summary: Sonnedix acquired a 49 MW portfolio of operating solar plants, its first operating assets in Portugal.
details: Sonnedix bought four operating solar plants of 49 MW in Évora, Setúbal and Faro, southern Portugal, from Cubico Sustainable Investments, its first operating assets in Portugal. They began operating in 2012–2014.
context: The plants earn a government feed-in tariff, giving long-term fixed revenue. Buying operating plants avoids permitting and construction risk.

sources.title: Sonnedix acquires 49 MW portfolio in Portugal

title: Pedal Steel Solar acquires two 800 MWh MISO storage projects from Valor Infrastructure Partners
target: Two standalone energy storage projects in Michigan and Kentucky
summary: Pedal Steel Solar, a subsidiary of Runway Group, has bought two standalone battery storage projects from developer Valor Infrastructure Partners. Each project is expected to store and dispatch up to 800 MWh of energy, and both sit in the MISO power market in the central United States.
details: One project is in Ostego County, Michigan and the other in Caldwell County, Kentucky. Both are still in development, meaning they are not yet built. Standalone storage means the batteries are not paired with a solar or wind plant on site. MISO is the regional grid operator covering much of the US Midwest and parts of the South. The price and power capacity in MW were not disclosed.
context: Pedal Steel, based in Bentonville, Arkansas, says the projects add to its pipeline aimed at meeting clean energy demand in the Heartland states. Valor, founded in 2022 and backed by investor Pelion Green Future, presents the sale as part of its strategy of developing and selling well-sited projects.

sources.title: Pedal Steel Solar acquires two 800 MWh Standalone Storage Projects Under Development in MISO from Valor Infrastructure Partners

title: Downing buys 46 MWp operating wind farm in Sweden
summary: Downing acquired an operating 46 MWp onshore wind farm of twenty Enercon turbines in northeast Sweden.
details: Downing completed the purchase of an operating 46 MWp onshore wind farm of twenty Enercon 2.3 MW turbines on a plateau in north-east Sweden, in the SE2 price region. It has run since 2012 and produces about 110 GWh a year; Enercon provides O&M.
context: Downing now has 44 renewable assets across Sweden, Finland, Norway and Iceland and about £850 million under management. KPMG advised.

sources.title: Downing acquires a 46 MWp wind farm in Sweden

title: Codelco signs 15-year round-the-clock solar-plus-storage PPA with Atlas Renewable Energy in Chile
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has signed a power purchase agreement with Chilean state copper miner Codelco to supply about 375 GWh of electricity per year for 15 years. The power will come from a new solar project with an integrated battery storage system that Atlas will develop, build and operate in Chile.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a generator at set terms. This one is described as 24/7, meaning the supply is meant to cover every hour of the day, which the batteries make possible by storing solar power for use at night. Atlas won the contract through a public tender run by Codelco. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in 2026 and run for 15 years. The release does not give the project's generation or storage capacity, its location within Chile, or the contract value.
context: Codelco is described as the world's largest copper producer, and the deal adds to Atlas's history of supplying mining companies, including the Javiera solar plant in Chile and the Lar do Sol plant serving Anglo American in Brazil. Atlas says the project marks its formal entry into battery storage technology. The company claims round-the-clock renewable supply of this kind will improve power reliability and help large industrial users raise their share of clean energy.

sources.title: ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY UND CODELCO UNTERZEICHNEN 24/7 PPA FÜR DIE REALISIERUNG EINES NEUEN SOLARPROJEKTS MIT BATTERIESPEICHERSYSTEM IN CHILE

title: Trinity Capital commits $50 million equipment financing to electrolyzer maker Electric Hydrogen
summary: Trinity Capital, a Nasdaq-listed lender to growth-stage companies, has committed $50 million in equipment financing to Electric Hydrogen. The US company builds electrolyzer systems that make green hydrogen from renewable electricity and water.
details: Equipment financing is a loan secured against the machinery it pays for, here supporting Electric Hydrogen's factory in Devens, Massachusetts. The release describes the facility as a key part of the financing for that plant, which is due to start production in the second quarter of 2024. Electric Hydrogen sells a complete 100 MW electrolyzer plant based on PEM (proton exchange membrane) technology, which it says produces nearly 50 tons of hydrogen a day. The company raised a $380 million Series C equity round in 2023 and has raised more than $600 million in total.
context: Electric Hydrogen says the financing will help it expand manufacturing quickly to meet what it describes as growing customer demand for green hydrogen. Trinity presents the deal as backing a US electrolyzer manufacturer that could lower hydrogen costs for industries such as fertilizer, steel and chemicals. The deal finances manufacturing capacity rather than a specific hydrogen production project.

sources.title: Trinity Capital Inc. Provides $50 Million in Equipment Financing to Electric Hydrogen

title: BayWa r.e. sells 109 MWp Lirios solar park to Encavis
summary: BayWa r.e. sold the 109 MWp Lirios solar park in Spain, due online in 2025, to Encavis.
details: BayWa r.e. sold the 109 MWp Lirios solar park, 35 km west of Seville, to Encavis, one of BayWa r.e.'s largest projects in Spain. It is due for commissioning in the second half of 2025 and should produce about 220 GWh a year.
context: It is the latest in a series of deals between BayWa r.e. and Encavis across Europe, followed later by the sale of the 95 MW Almodóvar farm.

sources.title: BayWa r.e. sells Spanish solar park to Encavis AG

title: RIC Energy sells 20 MW of New York solar to Luminace
summary: RIC Energy sold three New York solar plants totalling 20 MW to Brookfield-owned Luminace.
details: RIC Energy sold three community solar plants of 20 MW in upstate New York to Brookfield-owned Luminace: Hanover II and Pomfret II in Chautauqua County and Cortlandville in Cortland County, a total investment of more than US$50 million.
context: They are in the NYSEG and National Grid service areas and will supply more than 5,000 homes through community solar programmes.

sources.title: RIC sells 20 MW of New York solar projects to Luminace

title: StormFisher Hydrogen raises $30 million from ARC Financial for e-fuel projects
summary: StormFisher Hydrogen, a developer of low carbon fuel plants, has secured a $30 million investment from ARC Financial Corp. The money will fund development of its pipeline of e-fuel facilities in the United States and Canada.
details: StormFisher Hydrogen is developing several facilities that together could convert up to 300 MW of wind and solar electricity into e-fuels, meaning fuels made using renewable power. The plants would use electrolysis, which splits water into hydrogen with electricity, to make clean hydrogen, e-methane, e-methanol and green ammonia. The investment is the first made from ARC Energy Fund 10, which targets energy transition infrastructure and services. The release does not state the currency or the size of the stake acquired, and an ARC senior vice-president chairs StormFisher's board.
context: StormFisher recently sold its organic waste-to-energy business to focus on e-fuels, which it has worked on since 2018. The company says its pipeline could deploy several billion dollars of capital over the next five to ten years, aimed at hard-to-decarbonize users such as gas utilities, LNG, heavy industry and shipping. It has also rehired three former executives to lead its expansion.

sources.title: StormFisher Hydrogen Secures $30 Million from ARC Financial to Develop e-Fuel Production Facilities

title: Sosteneo to buy 49% of Enel Libra Flexsys battery company
summary: Enel agreed to sell 49% of Enel Libra Flexsys, its Italian battery storage company, to Sosteneo Fund 1.
details: Enel agreed to sell 49% of Enel Libra Flexsys to Sosteneo Fund 1 for about €1.1 billion. The company will build and run 23 batteries of 1.7 GW and renovate three open-cycle gas turbine plants of 900 MW in Italy, an enterprise value of about €2.5 billion when built.
context: The assets provide grid flexibility. Closing needs antitrust clearance and Italy's golden power review of strategic assets.

title: Innova buys 21.6 MWp Bedworth Solar from Industria Brand Energy
summary: Innova acquired the consented 21.6 MWp Bedworth Solar site from Industria Brand Energy and will take it through construction.
details: Innova bought the fully consented, ready-to-build 21.6 MWp Bedworth Solar site from Industria Brand Energy on 28 February 2024. It is near Innova's Tolldish Hall Farm project; Innova will build it for operation in 2025.
context: Innova has a 2 GW pipeline of projects connecting to regional distribution networks (DNOs) and sells many through joint ventures such as ISG Renewables.

summary: Masdar completed its acquisition of 49% of RWE's 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind project, part of a planned £11 billion joint investment.
details: Masdar completed buying 49% of the 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind project from RWE, a planned £11 billion joint investment over 100 km off north-east England, split into two 1.5 GW sites, DBS East and DBS West.
context: It builds on the £10 billion UAE-UK Sovereign Investment Partnership. The farm could power about three million UK homes.

title: Fervo Energy raises US$244 million led by Devon Energy
summary: Fervo Energy raised US$244 million in new funding led by Devon Energy to scale next-generation geothermal.
details: Fervo Energy raised US$244 million led by Devon Energy, joined by Galvanize, John Arnold, Liberty Mutual Investments, Marunouchi Innovation Partners, Mercuria, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and existing investors.
context: Fervo adapts oil and gas drilling to enhanced geothermal systems, which create fractures in hot rock to circulate water. Its first commercial project is online.

title: EDF Renewables signs 20-year PPA with SCPPA for Bonanza solar and storage
summary: EDF Renewables North America signed a 20-year PPA with the Southern California Public Power Authority for part of the 125 MWac Bonanza solar and 65 MW four-hour battery project.
details: EDF Renewables North America signed a 20-year PPA with the Southern California Public Power Authority for 125 MWac of solar and a 65 MW four-hour battery from the Bonanza project in Clark County, Nevada, for Pasadena Water & Power and Azusa Light & Water, with delivery by end-2028.
context: Bonanza will total 300 MWac of solar and a 195 MW four-hour battery on federal land, with about 500 peak construction jobs.

sources.title: EDF Renewables signs PPA for Californian solar and storage project

title: Exus acquires New Mexico Renewable Development solar portfolio from PNM Resources and AEP
summary: PNM Resources has completed the sale of its 50% interest in the New Mexico Renewable Development joint venture to Exus North America Holdings. Together with co-owner American Electric Power, the partners agreed to sell the full portfolio for $234 million after adjustments, with PNM Resources receiving $117 million.
details: The portfolio consists of nine operating solar projects with a combined 185 MW and six projects still in development with an estimated 440 MW of output. Closing required approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, New Mexico regulatory approvals tied to one of the projects, and clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust law, which reviews large deals for competition concerns. PNM Resources had previously reported its share of the venture's earnings in its Corporate and Other segment.
context: PNM Resources says its $117 million share of the proceeds will help fund investments in its regulated utility business, meaning assets whose returns are set by regulators. The sale marks the exit of both PNM Resources and AEP from the jointly owned solar platform and hands Exus a mix of operating and pipeline solar assets in New Mexico.

sources.title: PNM Resources Completes Sale of Renewable Joint Venture

title: AEP completes sale of 50% stake in New Mexico solar portfolio to Exus
target: New Mexico Renewable Development, LLC (50% interest)
summary: American Electric Power has closed the sale of its 50% interest in New Mexico Renewable Development, LLC to Exus North America Holdings. The portfolio holds nine operating solar plants totaling 185 MW in New Mexico. AEP says it nets about $104 million in cash after tax, fees and adjustments.
details: Besides the 185 MW of operating solar, the portfolio includes six projects still in development with an estimated 440 MW of output. AEP started the sale process in June 2023. Closing required approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, New Mexico regulatory approvals tied to one of the projects, and clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust law, a US review of larger deals for competition concerns. The headline purchase price was not disclosed, only AEP's net cash proceeds.
context: The sale lets AEP turn a minority-style stake in non-utility solar assets into cash as it pursues a stated $43 billion five-year investment plan focused on its grid. For Exus, the deal adds both operating solar capacity and a development pipeline in New Mexico.

sources.title: AEP Completes Sale of New Mexico Solar Assets

title: Recurrent Energy closes $51 million non-recourse financing for 119 MW Horus Solar project in Mexico
summary: Recurrent Energy, the development arm of Canadian Solar, has closed $51 million of non-recourse project financing for the 119 MW Horus Solar project in Aguascalientes, Mexico. The loans come from two South Korean lenders, Korea Eximbank and KEB Hana Bank.
details: The financing has two tranches, $43 million from Korea Eximbank, South Korea's official export credit agency, and $8 million from KEB Hana Bank. Non-recourse means the lenders are repaid from the project's own cash flows rather than from the owners' wider balance sheets. The project is owned 49% by Recurrent, 36% by Sprott and 15% by KEPCO. It won a contract in Mexico's third renewable energy auction to sell 75% of its output for 15 years and Clean Energy Certificates for 20 years, with the remaining 25% sold on the spot market, meaning at short-term market prices. The plant uses Canadian Solar bifacial modules and has been in commercial operation since March 2023.
context: The deal refinances an already operating plant with debt backed by Korean institutions, reflecting the involvement of Korean utility KEPCO as a co-owner. Recurrent says it remains committed to Mexico, which it describes as having strong fundamentals for solar development.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes Project Financing for 119 MW Solar Project in Mexico

title: Renewable Power Capital buys 57 MW ready-to-build UK battery project
summary: Renewable Power Capital acquired a 57 MW ready-to-build battery storage project, its first shovel-ready storage project in the UK.
details: Renewable Power Capital completed buying a 57 MW ready-to-build UK battery project, its first shovel-ready storage project in the UK. Construction was due to start immediately, with energisation in summer 2025 on the transmission network.
context: RPC's UK storage pipeline now exceeds 4.5 GW, including partnerships with Greenfield (500 MW) and Elmya Energy (4 GW).

sources.title: Renewable Power acquires 57 MW BESS project

title: MPC Energy Solutions starts building 65 MWp San Patricio solar plant in Guatemala backed by 16-year IMSA PPA
target: San Patricio Renovables solar PV plant
summary: MPC Energy Solutions has begun construction of its 65 MWp San Patricio Renovables solar plant in Guatemala. All of the plant's output will be sold to sugar producer Ingenio Magdalena (IMSA) under a 16-year fixed-price power purchase agreement. Total investment is put at around USD 42 million.
details: The company issued a limited notice to proceed, meaning an early go-ahead to its contractor, to the Enerland Group, which holds the turnkey engineering, procurement and construction contract. The plant is expected to produce about 141 GWh per year and construction is expected to finish by mid-2025. The power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity at a set price, was first announced in February 2023. The roughly USD 42 million cost includes financing costs and risk contingencies.
context: San Patricio is the company's largest project and, according to MPCES, will nearly double its installed capacity from around 79 MWp across five assets. The company expects the plant to earn more than USD 8 million a year at EBITDA margins above 80 percent and to lift group revenue above USD 20 million annually. IMSA is described as Guatemala's leading sugar producer and its largest private energy producer.

sources.title: MPC Energy Solutions commences construction of 65 MWp solar PV plant in Guatemala, 16-year PPA signed with IMSA Group

title: First Gen wins auction for 165 MW Casecnan hydropower plant
summary: First Gen's subsidiary Fresh River Lakes won the auction for the 165 MW Casecnan hydropower plant and its facilities.
details: First Gen's subsidiary Fresh River Lakes won the government auction for the 165 MW Casecnan hydropower plant with a US$526 million bid, including its switchyard, administration complex, guest house and roads. PSALM ran the sale as part of the privatisation programme.
context: First Gen says building a similar plant would cost more and take seven years or more. PSALM and the National Irrigation Administration keep the non-power parts; First Gen also runs Pantabangan-Masiway and is building the 120 MW Aya pumped storage plant.

sources.title: First Gen acquires 165 MW hydropower plant

title: Highfield Solar closes €65 million for 93 MWp Gaskinstown solar in Ireland
summary: Highfield Solar, a joint venture of ib vogt, Highfield Energy and Aura Power, closed a €65 million project debt facility with Rabobank for the 93 MWp Gaskinstown solar plant.
details: Highfield Solar, a joint venture of ib vogt, Highfield Energy and Aura Power, reached financial close on a €65 million debt facility from Rabobank for the 93 MWp Gaskinstown solar plant in Ireland, after Rabobank financed its 106 MWp Rathnaskilloge project in December 2023.
context: Gaskinstown won support in Ireland's RESS 2 auction in 2022, which gives 15 years of support and requires about €150,000 a year for local community funds. Ireland targets 80% renewable electricity by 2030.

sources.title: Highfield Solar secures €65m financing for Irish solar PV expansion

title: Nordic Solar buys 40 MWp Gotland solar project from Helios Nordic Energy
summary: Nordic Solar acquired a 40 MWp ready-to-build solar project on Gotland from Helios Nordic Energy, part of a 270 MWp joint pipeline.
details: Nordic Solar bought a 40 MWp ready-to-build solar project on 60 ha south of Visby, Gotland, from Helios Nordic Energy, the first large-scale solar project on the island, with all permits and a grid agreement with GEAB.
context: It is part of a 270 MWp Swedish pipeline developed with Helios, of which 150 MWp is now ready-to-build or under construction.

sources.title: Nordic Solar acquires Swedish solar project

title: FirstLight acquires Hydroméga's 10 hydropower stations
summary: FirstLight, owned by PSP Investments, acquired Hydromega Services, including interests in ten hydropower stations in Québec and the northeastern US.
details: FirstLight, owned by PSP Investments, completed buying Hydroméga Services, with interests in 10 hydropower stations, five in Québec and five in north-eastern Ontario, and a pipeline of over 2 GW of wind, solar, storage and hydro.
context: The deal doubles FirstLight's development pipeline to more than 4 GW in the US and Canada.

sources.title: FirstLight acquires Hydroméga

title: Stonepeak agrees to acquire 50% of Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind
summary: Stonepeak agreed with Dominion Energy to acquire a 50% interest in the Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project through a new offshore wind partnership.
details: Stonepeak agreed with Dominion Energy to buy 50% of the 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project, 27 miles off Virginia Beach, through a new offshore wind partnership. Offshore construction was to begin in spring 2024, finishing by end-2026.
context: CVOW is expected to be the largest offshore wind farm in the US and could serve 660,000 homes. Dominion began developing it in 2013.

sources.title: Stonepeak have acquired 50% interest in Dominion wind project

title: Matrix Renewables closes $283 million financing and PTC transfer deal for 260 MWdc Pleasant Valley Solar in Idaho

advisors.name: Allen & Overy
advisors.role: Counsel to Stonehenge Capital and tax credit buyer

summary: Matrix Renewables, backed by TPG Rise, closed $283 million of construction-to-term loan financing for its 260 MWdc Pleasant Valley Solar project in Ada County, Idaho. It also signed an agreement to sell the project's production tax credits to an unnamed insurance company.
details: The debt package, led by MUFG as coordinating lead arranger with HSBC, SMBC, National Bank of Canada, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Mizuho as mandated lead arrangers, combines a construction loan that converts into a long-term loan after the plant is built, plus letter of credit support. Matrix chose to sell its production tax credits, which are federal tax breaks earned per unit of power generated, and the buyer committed to purchase the full 10 years of credits, with Stonehenge Capital servicing the arrangement. Construction began in the third quarter of 2023 and power deliveries are expected from 2025 to Idaho Power and Meta under a 20-year power purchase agreement. Latham & Watkins advised the lenders and Allen & Overy advised Stonehenge and the tax credit buyer.
context: The deal uses tax credit transfer, a mechanism that lets developers sell clean energy tax credits for cash to companies with tax bills. Matrix says the project will supply power equal to about 14,500 homes and avoid about 211,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent a year. The company reports owning over 6.7 GW of US projects and more than 14 GW globally.

sources.title: Matrix Renewables closes Tax Credit Transfer Agreement and Construction to Term Loan Financing for 260MWdc solar project in Ada County, Idaho

title: Arevon closes over $1 billion in financing for Eland 2 solar-plus-storage project in California

buyers.name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC)
buyers.role: Administrative Agent, Coordinating Lead Arranger, Green Loan Coordinator, Bookrunner

buyers.name: J.P. Morgan
buyers.role: Joint Lead Arranger, Collateral and Depositary Agent

summary: Arevon Energy has reached financial close on more than $1 billion of financing for Eland 2, a 374 MWdc solar project with 150 MW/600 MWh of battery storage in Kern County, California. The package combines a $431 million tax equity commitment from Wells Fargo with $654 million of bank debt led by CIBC.
details: Eland 2 is in early construction and is expected to start operating in the first quarter of 2025. Its four-hour battery system uses Tesla Megapack 2 XL units, and SOLV Energy is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor. Tax equity means an investor funds part of the project in exchange for its federal tax credits, while the debt includes a construction-to-term loan (a construction loan that converts into long-term debt), a tax equity bridge loan that covers the gap until tax equity funds arrive, and letter of credit facilities. CIBC led the lender group with BNP Paribas, CoBank, Commerzbank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and National Bank of Canada, and J.P. Morgan as joint lead arranger. The project will sell 200 MWac to Southern California Public Power Authority under a long-term power purchase agreement.
context: Eland 2 is the second phase after Eland 1, which closed its financing in 2022, and together they would total 751 MWdc of solar and 300 MW/1,200 MWh of storage. Arevon says the combined site will be one of the largest solar-plus-storage plants in the US. The company claims hybrid plants give more predictable output during peak demand and support steady returns across its portfolio.

sources.title: Arevon Secures $1.1 Billion Financial Close for Eland 2 Solar-plus-Storage Project

title: DEWA and Masdar reach financial close on 1,800 MW sixth phase of Mohammed bin Rashid Solar Park
summary: DEWA and Masdar reached financial close on the 1,800 MW sixth phase of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park in Dubai.
details: DEWA and Masdar reached financial close on the 1,800 MW sixth phase of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park in Dubai, costing about AED5.5 billion (US$1.5 billion) over 20 km², at the park's lowest levelised cost of 1.6215 US cents/kWh.
context: It is the world's largest single-site solar park and should exceed 5,000 MW by 2030, with total investment of AED50 billion.

sources.title: Dubai, Masdar reaches financial close for 1,800 MW solar project

title: Strata Clean Energy closes US$559 million for Scatter Wash battery in Arizona
summary: Strata Clean Energy closed US$559 million of financing to build and own the 255 MW / 1,020 MWh Scatter Wash battery complex in Arizona.
details: Strata Clean Energy closed US$559 million to build and own the 255 MW / 1,020 MWh Scatter Wash battery complex in Arizona, which broke ground on 18 January 2024 and should operate by April 2025. J.P. Morgan and Nomura led, with U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance also the main tax equity investor.
context: CoBank, Korea Development Bank, NORD/LB, Siemens and Regions also lent. Tax equity investors fund part of the project in return for its tax credits.

sources.title: Strata Clean Energy Secures financing for 1GWh BESS project in Arizona

title: PLT Energia and GGS Energy form joint venture to develop over 1 GW of Texas renewables

buyers.name: PLT Energy US Corp
buyers.role: 80% joint venture partner (subsidiary of PLT Energia)

buyers.name: GGS Energy LLC
buyers.role: 20% joint venture partner (subsidiary of Glacier Global Partners)

summary: Italian renewables group PLT Energia, through its US subsidiary PLT Energy US Corp, has formed a joint venture with GGS Energy LLC to develop more than 1 GW of renewable energy projects in Texas. The new company, PLT US Solar 1 LLC, is owned 80% by PLT and 20% by GGS Energy.
details: The first project is Indigo Project Phase I in West Texas, totaling 330 MW, made up of 150 MW of solar photovoltaic capacity and 180 MW of battery storage. Storage energy capacity in MWh and storage duration were not disclosed. Construction is expected to begin in June 2024. No deal value, financing or advisers were disclosed.
context: PLT describes the joint venture as its entry platform into the US market and part of a strategy of spreading its business across more countries. For GGS Energy, a developer formed in 2020 with an initial focus on utility-scale solar, the company says the partnership supports its growth plans.

sources.title: PLT Energia and GGS Energy LLC announce joint venture to realize renewable energy projects in Texas

title: Vestas sells 12.5% of Lake Turkana Wind Power to BlackRock's Climate Finance Partnership
summary: Vestas completed the sale of its 12.5% stake in Lake Turkana Wind Power in Kenya to the BlackRock-managed Climate Finance Partnership.
details: Vestas completed the sale of its 12.5% of Lake Turkana Wind Power in Kenya to the Climate Finance Partnership managed by BlackRock, for an undisclosed price, in a process run with Finnfund and IFU.
context: At 310 MW with 365 Vestas turbines, LTWP is Africa's largest wind farm, connected in 2018, and meets about 14% of Kenya's electricity demand. Vestas keeps servicing the turbines.

sources.title: Vestas sells shares in Lake Turkana Wind Power

title: RWE signs seven PPAs with German industry for Kaskasi offshore wind
summary: RWE signed PPAs with seven German industrial customers, including DHL, Ensinger, Evonik, Infraserv Höchst, thyssenkrupp Steel and Vodafone, for power from its Kaskasi offshore wind farm from 2026.
details: RWE Supply & Trading signed PPAs with DHL Group, Ensinger, Evonik, Infraserv Höchst, thyssenkrupp Steel Europe and Vodafone for power from the 342 MW Kaskasi offshore wind farm, 35 km off Heligoland, after a first deal with the Schwarz Group. Most run ten years, starting from 2026–2028.
context: The contracts use as-produced, scheduled-profile or baseload delivery. Three of Kaskasi's 38 turbines have the world's first recyclable rotor blades.

sources.title: RWE signs seven wind PPAs from Kaskasi wind farm

title: Greenprint Capital Management provides about $98 million tax equity for Plus Power's 200 MW Ebony storage project in Texas
summary: Plus Power has completed a tax equity investment of about $98 million from Greenprint Capital Management for its Ebony Energy Storage facility in Comal County, Texas. The standalone battery project has 200 MW of power and 400 MWh of storage and will serve the ERCOT grid.
details: Tax equity is a form of financing where an investor puts money into a project in exchange for the right to use its federal tax credits. Ebony sits on roughly 13 acres near San Antonio, uses 176 Sungrow battery containers and offers about two hours of storage at full output. Construction began in March 2023 and the plant is expected to start operating in spring 2024. It will run as a merchant project, meaning it earns revenue by selling energy and grid support services in the ERCOT market rather than under a long-term fixed contract. Ebony was also part of a $1.8 billion financing Plus Power announced in 2023 covering five projects in Arizona and Texas.
context: Plus Power says the project will help ERCOT cope with high summer and winter peak demand and integrate more renewable power. The company expects to have four operating storage plants in ERCOT totaling 800 MW and 1,575 MWh by summer 2024, and it describes the investment as a sign of investor confidence in its standalone storage projects.

sources.title: Plus Power Secures Nearly $100 Million Tax Equity Financing for Merchant Battery Storage Project in ERCOT

title: GoldenPeaks Capital buys Polish solar assets from R.Power
summary: GoldenPeaks Capital's Oicles Renewable Energy finalised the purchase of solar assets from R.Power in Poland.
details: Oicles Renewable Energy, a GoldenPeaks Capital subsidiary, completed buying 100% of the companies holding R.Power's 69 MWp portfolio of ready-to-build ground-mounted solar farms in various parts of Poland.
context: Once built the farms should produce about 75 GWh a year. Ready-to-build means permits and grid connections are in place.

sources.title: GoldenPeaks Capital to acquire photovoltaic assets from R.Power

title: CC&L Infrastructure agrees to buy 80% of 297 MW Sharp Hills wind farm in Alberta from EDP Renewables Canada
summary: Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure has agreed to acquire an 80% stake in the 297 MW Sharp Hills wind farm in southeastern Alberta from EDP Renewables Canada. The deal values the stake at an estimated enterprise value of about C$0.6 billion, including investment tax credits.
details: Sharp Hills is a newly built onshore wind farm that has recently begun operating, with the remaining construction work expected to finish by the second quarter of 2024. Its output is fully sold under a 15-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity at agreed terms, with an unnamed counterparty. EDPR will keep a minority stake and continue to operate and manage the project.
