The enterprise value figure covers the company's total value including debt and counts investment tax credits, which are government tax incentives for clean energy investment. Closing is subject to customary conditions and is expected within weeks.
context: This is the second deal between the two firms, following CC&L Infrastructure's earlier purchase of a 560 MW US wind and solar portfolio from EDPR. The buyer says the acquisition will lift its wind holdings above 600 MW and its total renewable portfolio above 1.8 GW across Canada, the United States and Chile. For EDPR, selling a majority stake while keeping operations fits a pattern of recycling capital from completed projects.

sources.title: CONNOR, CLARK & LUNN INFRASTRUCTURE TO EXPAND RENEWABLE ENERGY PORTFOLIO WITH INVESTMENT IN 297 MEGAWATT ALBERTA WIND FARM

title: Ardian takes final investment decision on 38.5 MW Mertaniemi battery in Finland
summary: Ardian and its platform eNordic took a final investment decision to build the 38.5 MW one-hour Mertaniemi battery in Finland.
details: Ardian, with its eNordic platform, took a final investment decision to build the 38.5 MW one-hour Mertaniemi battery in Finland, the first battery investment by its Ardian Clean Energy Evergreen Fund.
context: The fund aggregates Finnish wind and solar and adds batteries to use grid connections better; it bought two wind farms of over 27 MW in 2023. BNEF expects European storage to grow from 11 GWh to 75 GWh by 2030.

sources.title: Ardian invests in 38.5 MW Finnish BESS project

title: Arevon closes $350 million financing with Blackstone for 200 MW Condor battery project in California

advisors.name: The Bank of New York Mellon

summary: Arevon Energy and Blackstone Credit & Insurance reached financial close on a $350 million package for the Condor Energy Storage Project in Grand Terrace, California. The 200 MW / 800 MWh battery project combines preferred equity, a sale of tax credits and bank debt.
details: Condor is under construction, uses Tesla Megapack 2 XL batteries, and is expected to begin operating in the second quarter of 2024, with Rosendin Electric as the construction contractor and Tesla handling operations and maintenance. Its output is sold under a 15-year contract with Southern California Edison. Blackstone provided preferred equity, an investment that ranks ahead of common equity, while Stifel committed to buy the project's investment tax credits, a federal incentive that can be sold to other companies for cash. A $164 million debt facility was arranged by CoBank, Helaba and SMBC with BNY Mellon as agent, and HASI financed the project land. Financial close means all funding agreements are signed and money can flow.
context: The parties say the structure lets the project turn its tax credits into cash without traditional tax equity, where an outside investor takes an ownership stake to use the credits. Arevon plans to own and run the project long term, and the release presents the deal as an example of combining several funding sources for storage. Helaba said it expects the project to support California's grid decarbonization.

sources.title: Arevon and Blackstone Credit & Insurance Close $350 Million Preferred Equity, Debt, and ITC Transfer Financing for Condor Energy Storage Project

title: Standard Solar buys 84 MW Illinois community solar portfolio
summary: Standard Solar acquired a portfolio of 14 community solar projects totalling 84 MW in Illinois.
details: Standard Solar bought an 84 MW Illinois community solar portfolio of 14 projects from New Leaf Energy, in three groups of about 47 MW, 12 MW and 25 MW. Construction starts in 2024, with most finished by year-end and the rest in 2025.
context: The projects support Illinois' goal of 100% clean energy by 2050. Community solar lets households subscribe to a share of a local solar farm.

sources.title: Standard Solar acquires 84 MW solar portfolio in Illinois

title: Air Products signs 10-year solar power purchase agreement with Eneco in the Netherlands
summary: Industrial gases company Air Products has signed a 10-year power purchase agreement with Dutch energy company Eneco. The electricity will come from the Vlagtwedde solar farm in the northeast of the Netherlands. Capacity and price were not disclosed.
details: A power purchase agreement is a long-term contract to buy electricity from a specific source at agreed terms. Under this 10-year contract, Air Products plans to cover most of the current energy use of its merchant business in the Netherlands, meaning gases sold to many customers rather than under dedicated supply deals, specifically its liquid nitrogen and oxygen production. The power will be generated at the Vlagtwedde solar PV farm. The release does not state the farm's capacity, the contract volume or financial terms.
context: Air Products says the deal will cut emissions by an amount equal to the carbon footprint of about 45,000 households over the contract term. The company presents it as part of a wider Dutch decarbonisation effort that includes a planned blue hydrogen plant and renewable energy import terminal in the Port of Rotterdam and a green hydrogen truck refuelling station. Eneco frames the agreement as an example of industrial customers moving to greener power.

sources.title: Air Products and Eneco Sign Power Purchase Agreement for Solar Electricity in The Netherlands

title: Avangrid signs wind PPA with Amazon for Leaning Juniper in Oregon
summary: Avangrid signed a PPA with Amazon for power from its Leaning Juniper wind farm in Gilliam County, Oregon.
details: Avangrid signed a PPA with Amazon for the 98.4 MW, 40-turbine Leaning Juniper IIA wind farm in Gilliam County, Oregon, Amazon's first utility-scale renewable project in the state. It is a repowering project that will extend the life of the existing farm.
context: Repowering replaces old turbines with newer, more efficient ones on the same site. Amazon has enabled 2 GW of renewables on the western US grid.

sources.title: Avangrid and Amazon expand US partnership with wind PPA

title: TagEnergy signs PPA with Equinix for Golden Plains Wind Farm
summary: TagEnergy signed a PPA with Equinix for 20% of the energy and green certificates from the first stage of Golden Plains Wind Farm in Victoria.
details: TagEnergy signed a PPA with Equinix for 20% of the energy and green certificates from Stage 1 of the Golden Plains Wind Farm in Victoria, the project's second PPA after Snowy Hydro took 40%.
context: It is Equinix's first long-term PPA in Asia-Pacific and will help supply its 17 data centres in Australia with renewable power.

sources.title: TagEnergy inks 2nd PPA for Golden Plains Wind Farm

title: Spearmint Energy closes US$47.5 million loan from Manulife for battery project
summary: Spearmint Energy closed a US$47.5 million project finance term loan from Manulife for its Revolution battery storage project.
details: Spearmint Energy closed a US$47.5 million project finance term loan from Manulife for Revolution, its operating 150 MW / 300 MWh battery in West Texas's ERCOT market, after a competitive bidding process.
context: It is one of Manulife's first investments in standalone battery storage. Batteries in ERCOT earn money from price swings and grid services.

sources.title: Spearmint Energy secures US$47.5 million loan from Manulife for BESS project

title: SMT Energy sells about 400 MW of Texas battery storage projects to UBS Asset Management
target: Portfolio of about 400 MW of battery energy storage projects in Texas
summary: Battery storage developer SMT Energy has sold a portfolio of roughly 400 MW of battery energy storage projects in Texas to UBS Asset Management. The financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The battery projects are located in Texas and connect to the ERCOT grid, the network run by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas that serves most of the state. The projects are expected to begin commercial operations, meaning start selling services to the grid, in 2024 and 2025. The release does not give the storage duration or energy capacity in MWh. Law firm Stoel Rives advised SMT Energy on the sale.
context: SMT Energy says battery storage is becoming more important for keeping the fast-growing ERCOT system stable and reliable while lowering costs for customers. The company, founded in 2019, claims to have developed more than US$1.5 billion of battery storage assets. The deal adds operating-stage storage assets to the portfolio of UBS Asset Management, a global investment manager.

sources.title: SMT ENERGY SELLS 400 MEGAWATTS OF BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE FACILITIES TO UBS ASSET MANAGEMENT

title: Recurrent Energy closes $160 million financing for 127 MWdc Bayou Galion Solar in Louisiana, signs Microsoft as offtaker
summary: Recurrent Energy, a unit of Canadian Solar, has closed $160 million in project financing for its 127 MWdc Bayou Galion Solar project in Morehouse Parish, Louisiana. Microsoft will buy all of the project's power and renewable energy credits.
details: The solar plant began development in 2018 and started construction in December 2023, with operation expected by fall 2024. MUFG served as coordinating lead arranger, meaning it led the organisation of the bank loans. Microsoft signed a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity, covering 100 percent of output plus the renewable energy credits, which are certificates proving the power came from a clean source. The contract length was not disclosed. Primoris Renewables Energy is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, and Recurrent plans to own and operate the plant once built.
context: The release notes Louisiana had only 145 MW of operating wind, solar and storage at the end of September 2023, so this project would substantially add to the state's clean capacity. Microsoft is buying the output toward its goal of becoming carbon negative by 2030. Recurrent describes the deal as a step in entering new markets and holding more projects in its own portfolio rather than selling them.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes $160 Million in Project Financing, Secures Microsoft as Customer for 127 MW Solar Project in Louisiana

title: Octopus Renewables Infrastructure Trust buys 199 MW of Irish solar from Statkraft
summary: Octopus Renewables Infrastructure Trust acquired four newly built solar farms near Dublin totalling 199 MW from Statkraft Ireland.
details: Octopus Renewables Infrastructure Trust completed buying four newly built solar farms near Dublin, 199 MW in total, from Statkraft Ireland for €160 million, partly financed with an €80.6 million loan from Allied Irish Banks and La Banque Postale.
context: The farms began operating in late December 2023 and sell their output to Microsoft under a 15-year PPA signed in 2022. ORIT's operating capacity is now 735 MW.

sources.title: Octopus Renewables Infrastructure Trust acquires Irish solar farms

title: MYTILINEOS closes financing for Chilean solar portfolio
summary: MYTILINEOS closed financing for a Chilean solar portfolio with BNP Paribas, Intesa Sanpaolo, SMBC, Rabobank and Santander Chile, with DNV as market adviser.
details: MYTILINEOS closed financing with BNP Paribas, Intesa Sanpaolo, SMBC, Rabobank and Santander Chile for four Chilean solar farms of 588 MWp: the operating Willka, Doña Antonia (energising February 2024), and Tocopilla and Tamarico under construction. DNV advised on the market.
context: Enel Chile will buy most of the power under 10-year PPAs, and the plants can also earn capacity payments from Chile's grid operator. They should produce about 1.6 TWh a year.

sources.title: DNV supports MYTILINEOS S.A. in securing financing for Chilean solar farms

title: AdventHealth signs virtual PPA for 90 MW of Scout Clean Energy's Heart of Texas Wind Farm
target: 90 MW portion of Heart of Texas Wind Farm
summary: Scout Clean Energy has signed a virtual power purchase agreement with health system AdventHealth covering 90 MW of its Heart of Texas Wind Farm in McCulloch County, Texas. The contracted share is expected to produce about 380,000 MWh of electricity per year.
details: Heart of Texas is an operating 180 MW wind farm with 64 turbines connected to the ERCOT grid, Texas's main power network. AdventHealth's contract covers half of the plant's capacity. A virtual power purchase agreement is a financial contract in which the buyer agrees a fixed price for power and receives the renewable energy credits, while the electricity itself is sold into the wholesale market rather than delivered directly. The contract length and price were not disclosed. The wind farm is owned and operated by Scout, a portfolio company managed by Brookfield Asset Management.
context: The release says the contracted output would match roughly 40 percent of AdventHealth's current system-wide electricity use, supporting its stated goal of 100 percent renewable electricity by 2026. AdventHealth says the deal is among the largest of its kind signed by a US health system. Scout reports about 1,000 MW of operating and under-construction wind assets and a pipeline of over 19,000 MW across 22 states.

sources.title: Scout Signs Virtual Power Purchase Agreement with AdventHealth for Texas Wind Farm

title: Vesper Energy closes $590 million debt financing for 600 MWac Hornet Solar project in Texas

advisors.name: CCA Capital
advisors.role: adviser to Vesper Energy on PTC transfer sourcing and structuring

summary: Vesper Energy has closed a $590 million debt financing package for its Hornet Solar project in Swisher County, Texas. The 600 MWac project is backed by a bank group led by MUFG, Nord/LB and Santander, and draws on a commitment to buy more than $500 million of production tax credits.
details: Hornet Solar covers more than six square miles and has a capacity of 600 MWac and 745 MWdc, using bifacial panels that capture light on both sides mounted on single-axis trackers that follow the sun. The financing combines a construction-to-term loan, which funds building and then converts into a long-term loan, with a letter of credit facility. MUFG, Nord/LB and Santander are coordinating lead arrangers, BayernLB is joint lead arranger and Associated Bank is a lender. Under Inflation Reduction Act rules allowing tax credits to be sold, Advantage Capital arranged a purchase commitment for more than $500 million of production tax credits over 10 years, and CCA Capital advised Vesper on that structure. Blattner Energy is building the project, which connects to Oncor's transmission system in the ERCOT grid and sells its power to four buyers under separate power purchase agreements.
context: The company says Hornet will be one of the largest single-phase solar projects in the United States and it is Vesper's largest solar project to date according to MUFG. The deal illustrates how tax credit transfers created by the Inflation Reduction Act can be used to support project loans. Vesper presents the close as evidence of its financial strength as it pursues a pipeline it puts at 17 GW.

sources.title: Vesper Energy Closes $590 Million in Financing for its Hornet Solar Project

title: EDPR enters Australia by buying ITP Development and 1.5 GW pipeline
summary: EDP Renewables entered Australia by acquiring ITP Development and about 1.5 GW of renewable projects.
details: EDP Renewables entered Australia by buying local developer ITP Development and its 1.5 GW pipeline of wind and solar projects in New South Wales and Queensland, with options to add batteries, including 480 MWp of solar and 200 MW of storage at an advanced stage in Queensland.
context: The advanced projects could come online by 2026. EDPR has installed 1.3 GW of solar in Asia-Pacific since 2022.

sources.title: EDPR enters Australia, acquires 1.5 GW renewable assets

title: SKF signs 12-year REC deal with Clearway for Texas solar farm
target: Portion of RECs from 452 MW Kent County, Texas solar farm
summary: Swedish bearing maker SKF has signed two renewable energy certificate (REC) purchase agreements in North America. The larger one is a 12-year deal with Clearway Energy Group for part of the certificates from a 452 MW solar farm being built in Kent County, Texas. The second covers Green-e certified wind certificates through 2025.
details: A REC is a certificate showing that one megawatt-hour of electricity came from a renewable source, and buying it lets a company claim that renewable power without taking physical delivery. The Clearway agreement starts in 2026 and runs for 12 years, covering a portion of the output certificates from the Texas solar project, which is under construction. The wind certificate agreement runs through 2025 and the counterparty is not named. Schneider Electric helped SKF select and negotiate both deals, and the Clearway certificates will be listed with the Center for Resource Solutions to meet the Green-e standard.
context: SKF says the agreements will let it match all of the annual electricity use of its U.S. and Canadian facilities with renewable power. The company describes the Clearway contract as its first large long-term REC purchase in the U.S. and links it to its goals of decarbonizing operations by 2030 and reaching net zero across its value chain by 2050.

sources.title: SKF secures 100% renewable electricity in the U.S. and Canada

title: AlphaReal buys 40.36 MW Bubney solar site in Shropshire
summary: AlphaReal acquired Bubney Energy Centre, a newly commissioned 40.36 MW solar site in Shropshire.
details: AlphaReal completed buying Bubney Energy Centre, a newly commissioned 40.36 MW solar site on 150 acres in Shropshire, from a global renewables developer. It is the largest ground-mounted solar site in AlphaReal's portfolio.
context: AlphaReal says the site mixed greenfield and brownfield land. Its survey found 90% of UK pension funds and insurers plan to increase renewable allocations.

sources.title: AlphaReal acquires UK solar site

title: Downing Renewables & Infrastructure Trust buys five Swedish hydropower plants
summary: Downing Renewables & Infrastructure Trust acquired five Swedish hydropower plants producing about 9 GWh a year for around £6 million.
details: Downing Renewables & Infrastructure Trust bought five Swedish hydropower plants in the SE2 and SE3 price regions, producing about 9 GWh a year, for around £6 million (€6.7 million), funded by Downing Hydro's long-term debt facility. One is on the Säveån river in south-west Sweden.
context: All have reservoirs that let output be timed. Downing now has 34 hydro assets and is upgrading plants to sell frequency containment services to the Swedish grid operator.

sources.title: Downing Renewables acquires five Swedish hydropower plants

title: ADB lends up to US$147 million for SAEL's 400 MW solar plant in India
summary: The Asian Development Bank signed a loan of up to US$147 million with SAEL Industries' unit SAEL Solar P4 for a 400 MW greenfield solar plant.
details: ADB signed a loan of up to US$147 million with SAEL Solar P4 to build a 400 MW greenfield solar plant in the Khavda Ultra Mega Solar Park, Gujarat, selling to GUVNL for 25 years. Tata Capital underwrote a parallel loan of up to about US$73.5 million.
context: ADB lends in local currency, which avoids exchange-rate risk for the developer. The plant should produce about 953 GWh a year.

sources.title: ADB approves $147m loan for 400 MW solar project development in India

title: Lhyfe and EDP Renewables sign 15-year corporate PPA
summary: Green hydrogen producer Lhyfe signed a 15-year corporate PPA with EDP Renewables for renewable electricity.
details: Lhyfe signed a 15-year corporate PPA with EDP Renewables to buy the output of a 39 MWac (55 MWp) solar project in Germany, developed by Kronos Solar EDPR and due to connect in 2025, its largest PPA to date.
context: The power will feed Lhyfe's green hydrogen plants in Baden-Württemberg and Lower Saxony, up to 8 tonnes a day. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable electricity.

sources.title: Lhyfe and EDP renewables sign corporate PPA

title: S2G Ventures makes growth equity investment in 38 Degrees North, which agrees to buy 62 MW New York community solar portfolio
summary: Investment firm S2G Ventures has closed a growth equity investment in 38 Degrees North, a California-based community solar and distributed renewables platform. Alongside the investment, 38 Degrees North agreed to buy 10 community solar projects totaling 62 MW in New York state from Community Power Group. The size of the investment was not disclosed.
details: Growth equity is money invested in an established company in exchange for an ownership share so it can expand. The acquired portfolio consists of 10 community solar projects in New York, which are local solar farms whose power is shared by subscribing households and businesses. This is the first acquisition funded together with S2G, and 38 Degrees North plans to raise tax equity (investment from parties that use the projects' tax credits) and debt in 2024. Two S2G representatives, Priyanka Duvvuru and Francis O'Sullivan, will join the company's board. Norton Rose Fulbright advised S2G and Vinson & Elkins advised 38 Degrees North.
context: 38 Degrees North says it has aggregated, financed, built and managed more than 400 MW across over 100 projects since 2015. The company says the new capital will let it back developers at all project stages and expand into new markets and technologies. The New York acquisition is described as giving the platform a scaled base ahead of its 2024 financing efforts.

sources.title: 38 Degrees North Announces Growth Equity Investment from S2G Ventures and 62 MWs of Community Solar Project Acquisitions

title: ACEN's UPC Power Solutions buys 38 MW Chestnut Flats wind from EDF Renewables
summary: UPC Power Solutions, a joint venture of ACEN, PivotGen and UPC Solar & Wind, bought the 38 MW Chestnut Flats wind project from EDF Renewables North America.
details: UPC Power Solutions, a joint venture of ACEN, PivotGen and UPC Solar & Wind Investments, completed buying the 38 MW Chestnut Flats wind project near Altoona, Pennsylvania, from EDF Renewables North America, including the lessee interest.
context: EDF Renewables keeps asset management and O&M. UPC Power Solutions now has over 170 MW of operating US renewables.

sources.title: ACEN JV buys 38 MW wind project from EDF Renewables North America

title: European Energy signs PPA with Rio Tinto for Upper Calliope Solar Farm
summary: European Energy signed a PPA with Rio Tinto for all output of the planned Upper Calliope Solar Farm in Queensland, set to be Australia's largest.
details: European Energy signed a 25-year PPA with Rio Tinto for all the output of the planned 1.3 GWp (1.1 GWac) Upper Calliope Solar Farm, about 50 km south-west of Gladstone, Queensland, Australia's largest solar corporate PPA. The two will develop, build and run it.
context: The 2,700 ha project needs development and grid approvals, with construction targeted for 2025–26. It is planned as Australia's largest solar farm.

sources.title: European Energy signs Australian solar PPA

title: Field buys 100 MW Holmston and Drum Farm battery sites from RES
summary: Field acquired the Holmston and Drum Farm battery projects in Scotland, 100 MW / 200 MWh combined, from RES.
details: Field bought the Holmston (Ayr, South Ayrshire) and Drum Farm (Keith, Moray) battery projects from RES, 100 MW / 200 MWh combined, adding to 210 MWh of Field batteries planned to come online in the next few years.
context: Scotland produces more renewable power than the grid can always carry south; batteries store the surplus instead of wasting it, and balance supply and demand.

sources.title: Field acquires 100 MW Holmston and Drum Farm battery sites in Scotland

title: Deriva Energy acquires 140 MW Spanish Peaks Solar project in Colorado from JUWI
summary: Deriva Energy, a Brookfield portfolio company based in Charlotte, has completed its purchase of the 140 MW Spanish Peaks Solar project in Las Animas County, Colorado, from developer JUWI. The price was not disclosed. The plant will sell its power to Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association.
details: Spanish Peaks is a 140 MW solar plant that has started construction and is expected to begin operating in the fourth quarter of 2024. JUWI will handle engineering, procurement and construction, meaning it designs and builds the plant, while Deriva will buy the solar modules itself. Output is contracted to Tri-State under a 19-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity at agreed terms. Deriva will own the plant and split operations and maintenance work with JUWI. The project sits in the service area of San Isabel Electric Association, a Tri-State member.
context: The deal lifts Deriva's owned and operated capacity in Colorado to 388 MW and represents repeat business between Deriva, JUWI and Tri-State. Tri-State says it is adding 595 MW of solar in 2024 and 2025 and that half of its members' energy will come from clean sources in 2025. The companies say the project will create about 250 jobs at peak construction.

sources.title: Deriva Energy marks milestone with successful closure of Spanish Peaks Solar acquisition in Colorado

title: Votorantim Cimentos signs 15-year, 100 MW solar PPA with Atlas Renewable Energy in Brazil
summary: Building materials group Votorantim Cimentos has signed a power purchase agreement with Atlas Renewable Energy to buy 100 MW of solar power for 15 years. The electricity will come from Atlas's planned Luiz Carlos solar project in Paracatu, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific power plant at agreed terms. The Luiz Carlos project is planned with 787 MWp of installed capacity (MWp measures peak panel output), of which 470 MWp is earmarked for Votorantim Cimentos. The power will supply the company's production units and distribution centres in the south, southeast and centre-west of Brazil. The contract is structured as a self-production arrangement, and closing still depends on customary conditions including approval from Brazil's competition authority CADE.
context: Votorantim Cimentos says the deal will cover about a third of its Brazilian electricity use and lift the renewable share of its consumption in Brazil to 75%, supporting its goal of 45% renewable energy globally by 2030. The company already owns hydro assets and signed a 220 MW wind deal with Auren in 2022. For Atlas, which reports about 5.2 GW developed and built, the contract adds another large industrial customer in Latin America.

sources.title: ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY UND VOTORANTIM CIMENTOS UNTERZEICHNEN STROMABNAHMEVERTRAG (PPA) FÜR EIN SOLARPARK IN BRASILIEN

title: Genesis Energy and FRV Australia reach financial close on 63 MW Lauriston solar farm
summary: Genesis Energy and FRV Australia reached financial close on their 63 MW solar farm in New Zealand, with a construction cost of about NZ$104 million.
details: Genesis Energy and FRV Australia reached financial close on the 63 MW Lauriston solar farm on 93 ha of the Canterbury Plains, costing about NZ$104 million, with debt from Bank of New Zealand and MUFG. BOEN will build it; Genesis takes all output under a 10-year PPA.
context: Genesis and FRV formed a joint venture in late 2021 to build up to 500 MW of solar in five years. Generation was expected by Q2 of FY25.

sources.title: Genesis, FRV Australia reaches financial close for 63 MW solar farm

title: OX2 sells 45 MW of Spanish solar projects to Greening
summary: OX2 sold late-stage rights to 45 MW of solar projects in Andalucía to Greening.
details: OX2 sold late-stage project rights to 45 MW of solar in Andalusia, Spain, to Greening, its second Spanish solar sale. The plants should produce about 84 GWh a year once operating.
context: OX2 had more than 6.4 GW of solar projects by end-Q3 2023; selling late-stage rights is its main business model.

sources.title: OX2 sells 45 MW solar projects in Spain

title: Bitech Technologies signs binding letter to combine with Bridgelink's 5.8 GW US solar and storage pipeline
target: New entity holding Bridgelink Development's BESS and solar development projects
summary: OTC-listed Bitech Technologies has signed a binding letter of agreement to combine with Fort Worth developer Bridgelink Development. Bridgelink will move its development projects, about 3.84 GW of solar and 1.965 GW of battery storage in Texas, Arizona and Louisiana, into a new entity that Bitech will acquire for about $50 million worth of its own shares.
details: Under the deal, the owners of the new entity will swap all of its units for Bitech common stock equal to $50 million, which would represent about 31.8% of Bitech's shares after issuance, making the entity a wholly owned subsidiary. The agreement also calls for at least $50 million of fresh capital to be injected into the combined company at closing. The companies say they are finalizing a share subscription agreement of up to $250 million, hold a committed letter of intent for up to $100 million for a late-stage battery project near Houston, and plan to sell the projects' investment tax credits, a federal incentive that can be transferred to other taxpayers for cash. The combined company would have a division developing the solar and storage projects and a division pursuing clean technology and acquisitions. No closing date was given.
context: The deal would turn Bitech, a small technology company, into the owner of a large early-stage US solar and storage pipeline. The companies also mention a joint venture with an undisclosed larger infrastructure group. They claim the combination will speed project development toward commercial operation, though the deal is still at the letter-of-agreement stage and the financing pieces are not yet finalized.

sources.title: Bitech Technologies Executes a Binding LOA with Bridgelink for a Business Combination to Develop 5.8 GW of Utility Power for BESS and Solar Projects including Pre-Negotiated Financing and Key Resources Procurement

title: EDF Renewables and KOWEPO reach financial close on 500 MW Manah 1 solar in Oman
summary: A consortium of EDF Renewables and Korea Western Power reached financial close on Manah 1, a 500 MW solar plant in Oman.
details: EDF Renewables and Korea Western Power (KOWEPO) reached financial close on the 500 MW Manah 1 solar plant in Al Dakhiliyah Governorate, south of Muscat, Oman, with French and Korean lenders. It has a 20-year PPA with Oman Power and Water Procurement signed on 23 March 2023.
context: It will use over a million bifacial panels and should start operating in Q1 2025. Oman targets 35–39% renewable generation by 2040.

sources.title: EDF Renewables and KOWEPO reach financial close for 500 MW Oman solar project

title: ReNew sells 300 MW Rajasthan solar project to India Grid Trust
summary: ReNew agreed to sell a 300 MW operating solar project in Rajasthan to India Grid Trust for about US$199 million, plus a possible earn-out of about US$8 million.
details: ReNew agreed to sell a 300 MW Rajasthan solar project, operating since December 2021 with a 25-year SECI PPA, to India Grid Trust for about US$199 million, plus about US$8 million expected as change-in-law earn-out. ReNew expects net cash of about US$82 million after the buyer takes on the debt.
context: Change-in-law payments compensate developers for cost increases from new taxes or rules after bidding. ReNew is recycling capital from stable assets.

sources.title: ReNew sells 300 MW solar project in India

title: Cactos raises more than €26 million for its battery fleet
summary: Cactos raised more than €26 million of equity in Cactos Fleet Finland, led by OP Finland Infrastructure, to grow its battery storage portfolio.
details: Cactos raised more than €26 million of equity for its Cactos Fleet Finland LP, led by OP Finland Infrastructure and the Finnish Climate Fund, to fund behind-the-meter battery units it leases to clients. The partnership aims for €70 million, half equity and half debt.
context: Behind-the-meter batteries sit on a customer's site, cutting their bills and also selling flexibility to the grid.

sources.title: Cactos raises over €26 million to increase BESS portfolio

title: Emeren acquires 10.76 MWh storage portfolio in Zhejiang, China from Kunneng Group

sellers.name: Kunneng Smart Energy Service Group Co. LTD

target: 10.76 MWh portfolio of six energy storage power stations in Zhejiang Province
summary: Emeren Group, a US-listed solar developer and operator, has completed the purchase of a 10.76 MWh battery storage portfolio from Kunneng Smart Energy Service Group. The portfolio consists of six storage stations in Zhejiang Province, China. No price was disclosed.
details: The six storage stations run under Energy Management Services agreements, in which customers benefit from energy arbitrage, meaning power is stored when it is cheap and used or sold when it is expensive. Emeren says most of its return will come from this arbitrage, with extra income from virtual power plant services. A virtual power plant links many small energy assets through software so they can be dispatched together like one larger plant. All six stations are already connected to a virtual power plant platform owned and run by Huaneng Power International.
context: Emeren presents the deal as its entry into China's virtual power plant market and as support for its wider storage expansion plans. The company says it has a solar pipeline and assets of over 3 GW and a storage pipeline of over 10 GWh across Europe, North America and Asia. The portfolio is small relative to that pipeline, so the deal mainly marks a strategic move into a new revenue model.

sources.title: Emeren Group Successfully Acquired 10.76 MWh Energy Storage Portfolio in China, Entering Virtual Power Plant Market

title: Nexif Ratch buys 30 MW Minh Luong hydropower plant in Vietnam
summary: Nexif Ratch Energy acquired the 30 MW Minh Luong run-of-river hydropower plant in Lao Cai, Vietnam, which has a 20-year PPA with an EVN subsidiary.
details: Nexif Ratch Energy completed buying the 30 MW Minh Luong run-of-river hydro plant in Lào Cai province, Vietnam, from developer Nam Tien Group. It has run since April 2018 and sells to an EVN subsidiary under a 20-year PPA.
context: It adds to Nexif Ratch's two Song Giang hydro projects; run-of-river plants use river flow without a large reservoir.

sources.title: Nexif Ratch acquires 30 MW Vietnam hydropower plant

title: Recurrent Energy sells 100 MW/200 MWh Mannum battery project in South Australia to Epic Energy
summary: Recurrent Energy, the development arm of Canadian Solar, has completed the sale of its 100 MW/200 MWh Mannum battery storage project in South Australia to Epic Energy. The price was not disclosed.
details: The standalone battery can deliver 100 MW for about two hours and sits in Mannum next to two solar farms, Mannum Stage One (7 MW) and Stage Two (39 MW), that Epic Energy already owns and that Recurrent Energy also developed. e-STORAGE was chosen to supply its SolBank battery system. Construction is expected to begin in the first half of 2024, with commercial operation, meaning the start of regular power delivery, targeted for 2025.
context: This is the third project Recurrent Energy has sold to Epic Energy, a South Australian infrastructure owner, and it completes Epic's holdings at the Mannum site. Epic says the battery will help feed surplus renewable power to the grid at peak times and support grid stability. Recurrent Energy says it plans to keep advancing its pipeline of storage and solar projects in Australia.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Completes Sale of 100 MW/200 MWh Battery Energy Storage Project in South Australia to Epic Energy

title: TotalEnergies sells 25.5% of Seagreen offshore wind to PTTEP
summary: TotalEnergies agreed to sell 25.5% of the 1,075 MW Seagreen offshore wind farm to PTTEP for £522 million (about US$689 million).
details: TotalEnergies agreed to sell half its stake, 25.5% of the 1,075 MW Seagreen offshore wind farm off Scotland, to Thailand's PTTEP for £522 million (US$689 million), an enterprise value of US$4.3 billion. TotalEnergies keeps 25.5% and SSE Renewables 49%.
context: Seagreen is the world's deepest fixed-bottom wind farm. The price is about 13 times expected average EBITDA over five years.

sources.title: TotalEnergies sells 25.5% of Seagreen Offshore Wind Farm to PTTEP

title: HASI invests in 605 MW AES renewables portfolio
summary: HASI invested in a 605 MW portfolio of renewable assets developed, owned and operated by AES.
details: HASI made a structured equity investment, closed on 22 December 2023, in a roughly 605 MW AES portfolio of more than 200 operating solar and solar-plus-storage projects across 11 US states, mostly community and commercial solar; over a third is paired with batteries.
context: Contracts have a weighted average of 16 years left, mostly with investment-grade buyers. AES keeps ownership and operation; structured equity gives the investor priority returns.

sources.title: HASI invests in 605 MW renewables portfolio owned and operated by AES

title: Digital Power Optimization signs behind-the-meter wind PPA for up to 100 MW of Texas data centers
summary: Digital Power Optimization (DPO), a developer of green data centers, has signed a binding power purchase agreement with an unnamed multinational renewable energy producer. The deal is expected to support data center deployments totaling 100 MW across up to six of the seller's wind farms in Texas.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract to buy electricity from a generator. Here the data centers will sit on site at the wind farms and draw power behind the meter, meaning directly from the turbines rather than through the public grid. The seller operates several wind farms of 150 MW or more in Texas. DPO says funding for the first phase at the initial site is secured, with operations expected to start in 2024 and the other sites following over the next 12 to 18 months. Contract length and financial terms were not disclosed.
context: DPO contrasts its approach with data centers that buy clean power through virtual PPAs or offsets, which are financial contracts not tied to physical delivery. The company says the structure gives the seller extra revenue at no cost by using power that is otherwise undervalued, and it follows a pilot DPO ran at the seller's site for over a year. DPO targets power-hungry computing such as cryptocurrency mining and AI training.

sources.title: DPO Signs Behind-the-Meter Wind PPA to Directly Power 100MW Green Data Center Project

title: Statkraft signs PPA with Gresham House and CPPA with Workspace for Beavor Grange solar
summary: Statkraft signed a PPA with Gresham House and a corporate PPA with Workspace for the 20 MW Beavor Grange solar farm in Devon.
details: Statkraft signed a PPA with Gresham House and a corporate PPA with Workspace for the 20 MW Beavor Grange solar farm in Devon. From February 2024 for ten years, Workspace receives as-generated power and REGOs, about two-thirds of its demand.
context: Statkraft's firming service turns variable solar output into a steady baseload supply by buying power when the farm is not producing and selling surplus when it is.

sources.title: Statkraft signs PPA and CPPA for UK solar farm

title: CIP buys Soltec's early-stage Danish solar portfolio

buyers.name: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (Energy Transition Fund I)

summary: CIP's Energy Transition Fund I is taking full ownership of Soltec's early-stage Danish solar portfolio to supply its Power-to-X projects.
details: CIP's Energy Transition Fund I agreed to buy 100% of Soltec's early-stage Danish solar portfolio of about 850 MWdc, mostly in Jutland, to supply its Danish Power-to-X projects such as Fjord eSAF and Høst green ammonia.
context: Power-to-X uses renewable electricity to make fuels such as hydrogen, ammonia or sustainable aviation fuel. It is CIP's first Danish solar purchase.

sources.title: CIP acquire Danish solar PV portfolio

title: Vestas sells 656 MW Italian wind portfolio to PLT Energia
summary: Vestas sold a 656 MW portfolio of wind projects it developed in Italy to PLT Energia.
details: Vestas sold a 656 MW portfolio of Italian wind projects it developed to PLT Energia, a long-standing customer that will continue developing them with Vestas turbines. Rothschild & Co advised Vestas.
context: Developing and selling projects helps Vestas create demand for its turbines in markets like Italy.

sources.title: Vestas sells Italian 656 MW portfolio to PLT Energia

title: Adani Green completes 1,050 MW joint venture with TotalEnergies
summary: Adani Green Energy completed a 1,050 MW joint venture with TotalEnergies, which invested US$300 million for a 50% stake.
details: Adani Green Energy completed a 1,050 MW joint venture with TotalEnergies, which invested US$300 million for 50%. The portfolio mixes 300 MW operating, 500 MW under construction and 250 MW in development, solar and wind.
context: The deal supports AGEL's target of 45 GW by 2030. Bringing in an equity partner funds growth without new shares.

sources.title: Adani Green finalises 1,050 MW joint venture with TotalEnergies

title: Vattenfall to sell Norfolk Offshore Wind Zone to RWE
summary: Vattenfall agreed to sell the Norfolk Offshore Wind Zone to RWE at an enterprise value of £963 million.
details: Vattenfall agreed to sell the Norfolk Offshore Wind Zone to RWE at an enterprise value of £963 million. The zone has three fully consented wind farms off the east coast of England, Norfolk Boreas, Norfolk Vanguard West and Norfolk Vanguard East, 4.2 GW in total.
context: It is one of the world's largest offshore wind developments. The sale lets Vattenfall reverse earlier impairments and focus on projects that fit its risk appetite, such as the 1.5 GW Nordlicht cluster off Germany with BASF.

sources.title: Vattenfall to divest Norfolk Offshore Wind Zone to RWE

title: Globeleq completes purchase of 75% of 41 MW Mocuba solar plant in Mozambique from Scatec and KLP Norfund
summary: Globeleq has completed the purchase of a combined 75% stake in the 41 MW Central Solar de Mocuba solar plant in Mozambique. It bought 52.5% from Scatec ASA and 22.5% from KLP Norfund, while state utility Electricidade de Moçambique keeps the remaining 25%. No price was disclosed.
details: The Mocuba plant sits on 126 hectares about 13 km from the city of Mocuba in Zambezia province in central Mozambique. It reached financial close, the point when funding is fully committed, in March 2018 and finished construction in August 2019. Electricidade de Moçambique buys the output under a 25-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity, and the power feeds the national grid. The International Finance Corporation and the Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund are lenders to the project.
context: The deal expands Globeleq's presence in Mozambique shortly after it started operating a 19 MW solar and 7 MWh storage project at Cuamba. The company says its African solar portfolio now nears 400 MW across South Africa, Egypt, Kenya and Mozambique. Globeleq, owned by British International Investment and Norfund, is also building a 450 MW gas-to-power plant at Temane and expects its 120 MW Namaacha wind project, described as the country's first, to reach financial close in 2024.

sources.title: GLOBELEQ COMPLETES ITS ACQUISITION OF THE MOCUBA SOLAR PV PLANT IN MOZAMBIQUE

title: Globeleq reaches financial close on US$117 million 35 MW Menengai geothermal project in Kenya

buyers.name: African Development Bank
buyers.role: mandated lead arranger and senior lender

summary: Globeleq and state-owned Geothermal Development Company have reached financial close on the US$117 million, 35 MW Menengai geothermal power project in Nakuru County, Kenya. Financial close means the funding agreements are signed and money can flow so building can begin. The senior lenders are the African Development Bank, Finnfund and TDB.
details: The plant will use steam from the Menengai steam field, supplied by GDC under a 25-year project implementation and steam supply agreement. Electricity will be sold to national distributor Kenya Power under a 25-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract fixing the buyer for the output. Toyota Tsusho Corporation and its subsidiary CFAO Kenya Limited are the engineering, procurement and construction contractor and are due to start work in the coming weeks. Commercial operations are expected in 2025, after which Globeleq will operate and maintain the plant. The African Development Bank acted as mandated lead arranger, meaning it led the organisation of the loans.
context: Menengai will be Globeleq's first geothermal plant and adds to its Kenyan business, which includes the 52 MWp Malindi Solar plant that it plans to expand with 40 MWac of solar and 40 MW/40 MWh of batteries. The project provides baseload power, meaning steady round-the-clock output, and lets GDC earn revenue from its steam resource. TDB linked the deal to Kenya's aim of meeting all its electricity needs with clean energy by 2030.

sources.title: GLOBELEQ'S 35MW MENENGAI GEOTHERMAL POWER PROJECT IN KENYA REACHES FINANCIAL CLOSE

title: PNM Resources and AEP agree to sell NMRD solar joint venture to Exus North America
summary: PNM Resources and American Electric Power, which each own half of the joint venture New Mexico Renewable Development (NMRD), have agreed to sell the whole portfolio to Exus North America Holdings for about $230 million. The portfolio holds 185 MW of operating solar plus a development pipeline in the US.
details: NMRD owns nine operating solar projects totaling 185 MW and six projects in development with an estimated 440 MW. The price of roughly $230 million is subject to true-up adjustments, meaning final corrections to the price at closing, and PNM Resources' share is about $115 million. The deal needs approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and New Mexico regulators for one project, while the US antitrust waiting period has already expired. Closing is expected in February 2024. KeyBanc Capital Markets is financial adviser and Foley & Lardner is legal counsel to both sellers.
context: PNM Resources says it will use its share of the proceeds to fund investment in its regulated utility business. The sale comes while PNM Resources is itself the subject of a pending acquisition by Avangrid.

sources.title: PNM Resources Announces Sale of Renewable Joint Venture

title: Emeren sells 53.6 MWp Hungarian solar portfolio to Kronospan / Douglas Renewables
target: 53.6 MWp solar project portfolio in Hungary
summary: Emeren Group, a US-listed solar developer and operator, has sold a portfolio of six solar projects in eastern Hungary totalling 53.6 MWp to Kronospan / Douglas Renewables. The deal closed by the end of November 2023 after final government approval. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio has six projects in the municipalities of Törökszentmiklós, Békésszentandrás, Mezőtúr and Szolnok. Four plants are already running, one is due to start operating at the end of Q4 2023 and the last is expected online by mid 2024. MWp (megawatt peak) is the maximum output of the solar panels under ideal conditions. Emeren says the plants together can supply about 9,500 households. Pontes Budapest acted as Emeren's legal counsel.
context: The sale fits Emeren's model of developing solar projects and selling them to long-term owners. The buyer is described as a major manufacturer of wood-based panels, an example of an industrial company acquiring its own renewable generation. Emeren presents the projects as a meaningful addition to Hungary's growing solar capacity.

sources.title: Emeren Group Sells a 53.6 MWp Solar Portfolio in Hungary

title: First Citizens Bank provides $65.2 million construction financing for Jupiter Power's 200 MW Houston battery project
target: 200 MW / 400 MWh battery energy storage system in Houston, Texas
summary: First Citizens Bank's Energy Finance unit and Jupiter Power have closed $65.2 million in financing to build a standalone battery storage system in Houston, Texas. The project has 200 MW of power capacity and 400 MWh of energy storage.
details: The money will fund construction of a battery system that can deliver 200 MW for about two hours, based on its 400 MWh capacity. It is a standalone project, meaning it is not paired with a solar or wind plant, and it sits in the ERCOT grid that serves most of Texas. First Citizens led the financing. The bank previously acted as coordinating lead arranger, the bank organizing the loan, on a $70.4 million construction and term loan for two other Jupiter Power battery projects in Texas totaling 160 MW / 320 MWh.
context: Jupiter Power says the project responds to calls from Texas lawmakers for more dispatchable power, meaning electricity that can be supplied on demand, near large population centers in ERCOT. The developer reports 775 MWh of operating storage, 620 MWh under construction and more than 11,000 MW in development across the US. The deal marks a repeat lending relationship between the two companies.

sources.title: First Citizens Bank Provides $65.2 Million to Jupiter Power for Standalone Battery Energy Storage Project Financing

title: Renewa closes land sale-leaseback with Leeward Renewable Energy for White Wing Ranch Solar in Arizona

sellers.name: Leeward Renewable Energy
sellers.role: land seller and lessee, project developer

target: Land for the White Wing Ranch Solar project
summary: Renewa, a land and infrastructure investor backed by QIC, has closed a sale-leaseback deal with Leeward Renewable Energy covering the site of the White Wing Ranch Solar project in Maricopa County, Arizona. Financial terms and project size were not disclosed.
details: In a sale-leaseback, the owner of an asset sells it to an investor and then rents it back, freeing up cash while keeping use of the asset. Here the arrangement concerns the land under the White Wing Ranch Solar project, allowing Leeward to keep long-term control of the site for building and running the plant. The release does not state the price, capacity, construction timeline or any advisers.
context: Renewa says the deal helps fund growth in Leeward's project pipeline and is one of several sale-leasebacks it closed over the past year despite tighter capital markets. The company describes itself as a land financing partner to renewable developers and claims a presence in more than 30 GW of projects across over 30,000 acres in 26 US states.

sources.title: Renewa Secures Sale-Leaseback Transaction with Leeward Renewable Energy for the White Wing Ranch Solar Project

title: Castleton Commodities International takes majority stake in UK battery storage developer L48 Energy
summary: A subsidiary of Castleton Commodities International (CCI) has bought a majority stake in Lower 48 Energy BESS, a UK company that develops, builds, owns and operates grid-scale battery storage. The price, the exact stake size and the capacity of the portfolio were not disclosed.
details: L48 Energy describes itself as an independent battery storage business that handles projects from origination, meaning finding and securing sites, through to operation. It plans to build and own large batteries at important points on the UK grid and may later expand into other European markets. The release does not name the sellers, advisers or any project capacities. L48 Energy is led by chief executive Hugh Mainwaring, and CCI's principal investments team led the deal.
context: CCI, a global energy commodity merchant, meaning a firm that trades and markets energy commodities, calls the UK a strategic market and says it aims to grow L48 Energy into one of the country's largest storage platforms. The company states it sees energy storage as a key enabler of decarbonization. L48 Energy says the investment validates its work to date and will support its next stage of growth.

sources.title: CCI Acquires Majority Stake in UK Battery Storage Company L48 Energy BESS Ltd.

title: Shell agrees to sell stakes in 182 MW Texas wind farm and 180 MW Ohio solar project to InfraRed Capital Partners
target: 60% of Brazos Wind Holdings, LLC and 50% of Madison Fields Class B Member, LLC
summary: Two Shell subsidiaries have agreed to sell partial stakes in two US renewable projects to InfraRed Capital Partners. InfraRed will take 60% of the 182 MW Brazos onshore wind farm in Texas and 50% of the 180 MW Madison Fields solar project in Ohio. No price was disclosed.
details: Brazos, in Fluvanna, Texas, is being repowered, meaning older equipment is replaced to restore or boost output, and is expected to reach 182 MW in early 2024. Madison Fields, in Madison County, Ohio, is under development and expected to be finished by the end of 2023. Shell will keep buying all power from Brazos through Shell Energy North America, while Madison Fields keeps an existing corporate power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity, with an unnamed third party. Shell will remain asset manager for both projects, which are expected to use Inflation Reduction Act tax credits. Completion is expected by early 2024 with an effective date in December 2023.
context: Shell says the sale follows its stated plan to reduce ownership in power assets while keeping access to renewable electricity through selected offtake deals. The company describes a disciplined approach to its renewables portfolio focused on partnering and integrating projects with its trading business. The deal gives InfraRed exposure to US wind and solar assets backed by federal tax credits.

sources.title: Shell agrees to sell partial ownership stake in two U.S.-based renewable energy projects to InfraRed Capital Partners

title: Masdar and Taaleri Energia acquire 1 GW hybrid solar-wind portfolio in Poland from Domrel
target: Eight hybrid solar PV and onshore wind development projects in Poland
summary: Masdar and Finnish developer and fund manager Taaleri Energia have bought eight hybrid solar and onshore wind projects in Poland from local developer Domrel. The portfolio is expected to total more than 1 GW once built. No price was disclosed.
details: The eight projects sit on separate sites across Poland and combine solar panels and onshore wind turbines at each location. They are at the development stage and are expected to start operating between 2026 and 2030. Domrel will keep working with the buyers to move the projects through the remaining permitting and development steps. The companies say the portfolio could supply about 223,000 households and avoid about 1.8 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year.
context: The projects rely on cable pooling, a Polish rule in force since October 2023 that lets different renewable sources share a single grid connection, which helps make better use of limited grid capacity since wind and sun rarely peak together. For Masdar the deal adds to its 51.4 MW of operating wind farms in Poland, and for Taaleri it brings its SolarWind III Fund to 61 development projects with a potential 7.6 GW. Poland aims for 11 GW of wind and 10 to 16 GW of solar by 2040.

sources.title: Masdar Expands European presence with Acquisition of 1GW Renewable Portfolio in Poland

title: Masdar and Taaleri Energia acquire 1 GW hybrid solar-wind development portfolio in Poland from Domrel
target: Eight hybrid solar PV and onshore wind projects in Poland
summary: Masdar and Finnish developer and fund manager Taaleri Energia have bought eight hybrid solar and onshore wind projects in Poland from local developer Domrel. The portfolio is expected to exceed 1 GW of combined capacity once built. No price was disclosed.
details: The eight projects are at the development stage, meaning they are not yet built, and are expected to start operating between 2026 and 2030. Each site will combine solar panels and onshore wind turbines behind a single grid connection, using a Polish rule called cable pooling that took effect in October 2023 and allows different renewable sources to share one connection. Domrel will keep working with the buyers to move the projects through the remaining development steps. For Taaleri Energia, the projects join its SolarWind III Fund. The agreement was signed at COP28 in Dubai.
context: The deal adds to Masdar's existing Polish assets, the Mlawa and Grajewo wind farms totalling 51.4 MW, and expands its European portfolio. Masdar says the projects could supply about 223,000 households and help Poland meet its wind and solar targets for 2040. Taaleri says the deal brings its SolarWind III Fund to 61 development projects with about 7.6 GW of potential capacity. The release frames the purchase as an early use of Poland's cable pooling rules, which are expected to enable around 25 GW of new renewable capacity.

sources.title: Masdar Expands European presence with Acquisition of 1GW Renewable Portfolio in Poland

title: Enfinity Global closes €118 million financing for 101 MW of solar projects in Lazio, Italy
target: Four utility-scale solar plants in Lazio, Italy (101 MW)
summary: Enfinity Global has closed €118 million in financing to build four utility-scale solar plants totalling 101 MW in the Lazio region of Italy. UniCredit, BayernLB and Siemens Bank led the lending.
details: The four plants are under construction and are expected to start operating in 2024, producing an estimated 172 GWh of electricity per year. The package includes €77 million of non-recourse senior debt, meaning lenders are repaid from the projects' cash flows rather than from the parent company, plus €41 million of VAT financing, a short-term loan covering value-added tax paid during construction. It also includes letter of credit facilities, which are bank guarantees, supporting power purchase agreements and solar module purchases. The three banks acted as mandated lead arrangers in a club deal, where a small group of banks lends together on each project.
context: Enfinity says these projects are an initial set within its 4 GW Italian portfolio, and it is separately building four other projects totalling 134 MW in Viterbo that were financed earlier with €165 million. The company says it expects to invest €3 billion in Italy over the next three years through development, partnerships and acquisitions. BayernLB noted this is its second transaction with Enfinity in Italy.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes €118 million financing for 101 MW in four solar power plants in Italy

title: Enfinity Global closes €118 million financing for 101 MW of solar plants in Lazio, Italy
target: Four utility-scale solar plants in Lazio, Italy
summary: Enfinity Global has closed €118 million of financing to build four utility-scale solar plants totaling 101 MW in the Lazio region of Italy. UniCredit, BayernLB and Siemens Bank led the lending as mandated lead arrangers.
details: The money splits into €77 million of non-recourse senior debt, meaning lenders are repaid from project cash flows rather than by the parent company, and €41 million of VAT financing, which covers value-added tax paid during construction until it is refunded. Letter of credit facilities, which are bank guarantees, were also provided to back power purchase agreements and solar module purchases. The three banks lent to each project together as a club deal. The plants are expected to start operating in 2024 and to generate about 172 GWh of electricity per year.
context: Enfinity Global says the projects are an initial part of a 4 GW portfolio it is building in Italy, where it is already constructing another four projects totaling 134 MW in Viterbo backed by €165 million in earlier financing. The company says it expects to invest €3 billion in Italy over the next three years through its own development, partnerships and acquisitions. BayernLB noted this is its second deal with Enfinity in Italy.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes €118 million financing for 101 MW in four solar power plants in Italy

title: Masdar to acquire 49% stake in RWE's 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects
target: Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects (49% stake)
summary: Masdar agreed to buy a 49% stake in RWE's 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects off northeast England. The deal was signed at COP28 in Dubai and is described as part of an £11 billion joint investment in UK renewables. The price paid for the stake was not disclosed.
details: Dogger Bank South sits more than 100 km off England's northeast coast and is split into two sites, the East Array and the West Array, each planned at 1.5 GW over about 500 square km. RWE keeps 51% and will lead development, construction and operation over the life of the projects. Closing, meaning the point when ownership actually transfers, depends on customary approvals and is expected in the first quarter of 2024. Construction could begin as early as late 2025, with the first 800 MW planned for 2029 and full commissioning targeted by end of 2031.
context: The companies say the projects could power up to 3 million UK homes and create about 2,000 construction jobs and over 1,000 operational jobs. For Masdar, the deal fits a stated strategy of entering offshore wind projects at early stages and its target of 100 GW of global capacity by 2030. RWE describes Dogger Bank South as its largest UK offshore wind development, and the release links the investment to the £10 billion UAE-UK Sovereign Investment Partnership.

sources.title: Masdar Joins Forces with RWE in £11 billion Investment to Co-develop Massive 3GW Offshore Wind Projects in UK

title: Masdar agrees to buy 49% of RWE's 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects
target: Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects (49% stake)
summary: Masdar has signed a deal to acquire a 49% stake in RWE's 3 GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind projects off northeast England. The release describes the partnership as part of an £11 billion investment in UK renewables, but no price for the stake is given.
details: Dogger Bank South sits more than 100 km off England's northeast coast and is split into two sites, the East Array and West Array, each planned at 1.5 GW and covering about 500 square kilometres. The projects are at an early development stage. RWE keeps 51% and will lead development, construction and operation over the projects' life. Construction could begin as early as late 2025, with the first 800 MW expected online in 2029 and full commissioning by end of 2031. Closing depends on customary approvals and is expected in the first quarter of 2024.
context: The agreement was signed at the COP28 climate conference in Dubai, and Masdar links it to the £10 billion UAE-UK Sovereign Investment Partnership. RWE says the projects are its largest offshore wind development in the UK, and the companies claim they could power up to 3 million homes and create around 3,000 jobs. Masdar presents the deal as part of a strategy of entering offshore wind projects early and reaching 100 GW of global capacity by 2030.

sources.title: Masdar Joins Forces with RWE in £11 billion Investment to Co-develop Massive 3GW Offshore Wind Projects in UK

title: SB Energy closes $2.4 billion in tax equity and debt for 1.3 GW US solar portfolio
target: Orion I, Eiffel, Orion II and Orion III solar projects
summary: SB Energy raised a combined $2.4 billion to fund four utility-scale solar projects totaling 1.3 GW in the United States. The package includes about $800 million in tax equity from four banks plus $450 million in term debt and $1.2 billion in construction debt from seven lenders.
details: The portfolio consists of the Orion I, Eiffel, Orion II and Orion III solar projects, all sited in so-called energy communities, areas hit by coal or fossil plant closures. Tax equity, meaning investment from parties that receive the projects' tax credits in return, came from J.P. Morgan, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley Renewables and Truist Bank, one per project. MUFG and Mizuho Americas each lead the lending on two projects, joined by ING, SMBC, CIBC, Fifth Third Bank and Société Générale. Construction debt funds building the plants, while term debt is longer-term financing once they operate. Google will buy roughly 75 percent of the output to supply its Texas data centers.
context: SB Energy says three of the projects are the first US utility-scale projects to reach financial close, the point when all funding is committed, using the Inflation Reduction Act's domestic content bonus, a tax credit boost for US-made equipment. The projects use First Solar modules made in Ohio, Nextracker trackers and US steel. The company claims the projects will support more than 3,600 direct and supply chain jobs and presents the deals as a model for similar financings.

sources.title: SB ENERGY SECURES $2.4 BILLION FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS, CREATING BLUEPRINT FOR PROJECT FINANCINGS AROUND DOMESTIC CONTENT AND ENERGY COMMUNITIES

title: BNDES lends US$447.8 million to Atlas Renewable Energy for 902 MWp Vista Alegre solar plant in Brazil
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has secured a US$447.8 million loan (about 2.18 billion reais) from Brazil's state development bank BNDES to build the Vista Alegre solar plant in Brazil. The plant has 902 MWp of panel capacity, equal to 768 MW of grid-side (AC) capacity.
details: Vista Alegre is described as the largest solar project in Brazil to be built in a single phase, and is expected to produce around 2 TWh of electricity a year. Its output is sold to aluminium producer Albras under a 21-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the plant's electricity, which is priced in US dollars. Construction began in 2023 and the plant is expected to start supplying Albras in 2025. This is the second BNDES financing for Atlas, following the 438 MWp Boa Sorte solar project, another joint venture with Albras.
context: According to the release, the loan is the largest US dollar loan BNDES has granted for renewable energy to date. Atlas says the deal strengthens its position in dollar-denominated power contracts for large energy users in Brazil. The company expects the project to create more than 2,500 construction jobs.

sources.title: ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY RECIBE MAYOR PRÉSTAMO EN USD PARA ENERGÍAS RENOVABLES DE BNDES PARA EL MAYOR PPA SOLAR DE AMÉRICA LATINA

title: BNDES lends US$447.8 million to Atlas Renewable Energy for 768 MWac Vista Alegre solar plant in Brazil
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has secured a US$447.8 million loan from Brazil's national development bank BNDES to build the Vista Alegre solar plant in Brazil. The plant has a capacity of 902 MWp, or 768 MW in alternating current terms. BNDES describes the loan as its largest US dollar loan for renewable energy to date.
details: Vista Alegre is described as the largest solar project in Brazil to be built in a single phase, and it is expected to produce about 2 TWh of electricity a year. Its output will be sold to aluminum producer Albras for 21 years under a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity at agreed terms, with prices set in US dollars. Construction started in 2023 and supply to Albras is planned to begin by 2025. The loan is equivalent to about R$2.18 billion.
context: This is the second BNDES financing for Atlas, following the loan for the 438 MWp Boa Sorte solar plant, which also supplies Albras. Atlas says the deal strengthens its position in dollar-denominated power contracts for large industrial buyers in Brazil. The company also says construction will create more than 2,500 jobs and include local training programs.

title: Longroad Energy closes $600 million corporate credit facility led by Apterra, Barclays and HSBC
summary: US renewable developer and owner Longroad Energy has closed a $600 million corporate debt facility to fund growth of its wind, solar and battery portfolio. The syndicated loan was led by Apollo platform Apterra Infrastructure Capital, with Barclays and HSBC as joint lead arrangers.
details: The $600 million package is split into a $275 million term loan (borrowed money repaid over a set schedule), a $175 million revolving credit facility (a credit line that can be drawn and repaid repeatedly) and a $150 million letter of credit facility (bank guarantees often used to secure project obligations such as grid connection or offtake contracts). It is a corporate-level facility shared among several lenders rather than debt tied to a single project. Longroad says it currently owns more than 3.1 GW of wind, solar and storage assets in the US and operates 5.0 GW for itself and third parties.
context: The financing follows a $500 million equity investment in August 2022 by Infratil, New Zealand Superfund and MEAG, which marked Longroad's shift toward mainly owning projects rather than selling them after development. The company says the new capital will help grow its owned operating fleet to more than 9 GW by 2027 and support a development pipeline it puts at 30 GW.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Secures $600 Million in Debt Financing to Power Expansion of its Renewable Energy Portfolio

title: Mainstream Renewable Power reaches financial close on 97.5 MW South African solar farm backed by Sasol and Air Liquide PPAs
target: 97.5 MW solar PV farm in Free State province
summary: Mainstream Renewable Power, majority-owned by Aker Horizons, has reached financial close on a 97.5 MW solar PV farm in South Africa's Free State province. The project sells its output to Sasol and Air Liquide under 20-year power purchase agreements.
details: Financial close is the point when all funding and contracts are signed so construction can begin. Construction is set to start in 2023, with full operation targeted for 2025. Power will be carried over the national grid to Sasol and Air Liquide sites in Secunda, Mpumalanga province, under 20-year power purchase agreements, which are long-term contracts to buy electricity at agreed terms. The release does not name lenders, the financing amount or advisers.
context: Sasol and Air Liquide are using the contracts as part of a joint effort to cut emissions at their operations. Mainstream claims private offtake deals like this can ease South Africa's power shortages and rolling blackouts, known as loadshedding, quickly and at low cost. The company says it has brought 850 MW of wind and solar into operation in South Africa and holds a local pipeline of over 10 GW.

sources.title: Mainstream Renewable Power reaches financial close on 97.5 MW solar PV farm with corporate PPAs in South Africa

title: CM Energy raises its shareholding in Xiamen electrolyzer maker CM Xiageng

sellers.name: CM Xiageng Hydrogen Energy Technology (Xiamen) Co., Ltd.
IKKEM Technology and Industry Development (Xiamen) Co., Ltd.

target: CM Xiageng Hydrogen Energy Technology (Xiamen) Co., Ltd.
summary: Hong Kong-listed CM Energy signed a capital increase agreement on November 17, 2023 that will raise its shareholding in CM Xiageng, a Xiamen-based maker of alkaline hydrogen electrolyzers. The size of the investment and the resulting stake were not disclosed.
details: CM Xiageng is a joint venture between CM Energy and the Tan Kah Kee Innovation Laboratory, linked to Xiamen University, and it designs and builds alkaline (ALK) electrolyzers, which split water into hydrogen using electricity, along with membranes and electrodes. A capital increase means new money is put into the company in exchange for more shares. The agreement was signed in Xiamen with TKK Lab, IKKEM Tech and CM Xiageng. The company says its first-generation 1000 Nm3 per hour electrolyzer is in place and expects trial production of a new 2-meter-wide composite membrane and mass production of next-generation cells in 2024.
context: CM Energy says the larger stake will let it combine TKK Lab research with its own manufacturing and global sales network to meet rising demand for green hydrogen equipment. The company claims CM Xiageng's electrolyzers lead the industry on energy use, cold start time, size and weight. Partners at TKK Lab expect the new money to strengthen research and help scale up production.

sources.title: CM Energy Accelerates Its Green Energy Transition by Increasing Its Stake in A Leading Hydrogen Electrolyzer Company

title: TSUN raises over RMB 150 million in IDG Capital-led Series B round
summary: Suzhou-based TSUN, which makes solar microinverters and energy storage products, has raised more than RMB 150 million in a Series B funding round led by IDG Capital. It is the company's second funding round of 2023, after an earlier investment from Hidden Hill Capital in February.
details: A Series B round is a mid-stage venture investment in which outside investors buy shares in a growing company. TSUN says the money will go toward automated production lines, more manufacturing capacity, product development, supply chain work and wider sales channels at home and abroad. Microinverters are small devices fitted to individual solar panels that convert their direct current into household alternating current. The company plans to start building a 50,000 square meter factory in Suzhou this year, with support from Suzhou High-Speed Rail New City, and expects it to be running by 2025. TSUN says the new plant will raise its production capacity by 500 percent. The stated figure of RMB 150 million is a minimum, as the release says the round exceeded that amount.
context: Founded in 2019, TSUN sells microinverters ranging from 300W to 3000W and a plug-in balcony solar kit, and distributes in Europe, South America and Asia-Pacific. The company claims its TITAN series, launched in 2020, was the first high-power single-phase microinverter. TSUN says it intends to develop higher-power microinverters by 2024 to expand into commercial and industrial uses.

sources.title: TSUN Secures Over RMB 150 Million in Series B Funding, Accelerating Innovation in Photovoltaic Technology and Sustainable Energy Solutions

title: First Citizens Bank and MUFG arrange $250 million financing for Middle River Power's 327 MW California battery portfolio
target: Portfolio of three battery storage projects in Kings County and Fresno County, California
summary: First Citizens Bank and MUFG acted as co-lead arrangers on a $250 million financing for three battery storage projects developed by Middle River Power in California. The portfolio totals 327 MW of one-hour batteries. Morgan Stanley Renewables provided the tax equity commitment.
details: The three battery projects have one-hour duration and will sit alongside existing gas-fired peaking plants in Kings County and Fresno County, forming hybrid facilities. The financing includes a construction loan that converts into a longer-term loan once the projects are built, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term debt repaid when tax equity investors fund), and letter of credit facilities for the projects. Tax equity is investment from a party that receives the projects' tax credits in return for capital, here committed by Morgan Stanley Renewables Inc.
context: The batteries are meant to absorb surplus daytime solar power and discharge it during evening demand peaks, so the gas turbines should run less often while remaining available in extreme conditions. Middle River Power describes the pairing as a first of its kind and calls this the first tranche of a larger development pipeline it plans to bring to market in coming years. First Citizens notes it has worked with the developer before.

sources.title: First Citizens Bank Serves as Lead Arranger on $250 Million Financing for Innovative Hybrid Thermal and Battery Energy Storage Projects in California

title: Fujifilm and Bristol Myers Squibb sign PPAs for National Grid Renewables' 270 MW Blevins Solar Project in Texas

advisors.name: Edison Energy, LLC
advisors.role: independent advisor to Bristol Myers Squibb

summary: National Grid Renewables has signed two power purchase agreements covering the full output of its 270 MW Blevins Solar Project in Falls County, Texas. Fujifilm has contracted 125 MW and Bristol Myers Squibb has contracted 145 MW.
details: A power purchase agreement is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project. Blevins is a solar project under development in the ERCOT market, the grid that serves most of Texas, and is expected to start construction in 2024 and begin operating in 2025. The release does not state the contract lengths or prices. Edison Energy advised Bristol Myers Squibb on the deal, and World Kinect Energy Services helped Fujifilm identify the project.
context: The company says Blevins brings its ERCOT investment to nearly 1 GW and is its second project in Falls County, with an estimated direct economic impact of about 35 million US dollars over 30 years. Both buyers say the contracts support goals of sourcing all of their purchased electricity from renewables, with Fujifilm targeting its operations in the United States and Canada.

details: A power purchase agreement is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project. title: Enbridge takes 50% stake in EDF Renewables' Fox Squirrel solar project in Ohio
summary: Enbridge has signed a definitive agreement to take a 50% interest in a joint venture with EDF Renewables that will build and run the Fox Squirrel solar project in Madison County, Ohio. Enbridge will put US$149 million into the first phase of the project, which is planned to reach up to 577 MW across three phases.
details: Fox Squirrel is a ground-mounted solar plant now under construction. Its first phase of about 150 MW is expected to start operating by the end of 2023, and the full build-out of up to 577 MW is targeted for the end of 2024. Enbridge's US$149 million covers only the first phase, and the company plans to make final investment decisions, meaning a firm commitment to fund construction, on the later phases during 2024 if certain conditions are met. All of the project's output is sold under 20-year fixed-price power purchase agreements, which are long-term contracts to sell electricity at a set price, with a counterparty the release describes as strongly investment grade.
context: The deal extends an existing relationship between Enbridge, a company best known for oil and gas pipelines, and EDF Renewables. Enbridge says the project should immediately raise its distributable cash flow per share and supports its energy transition strategy. The company also claims the finished project will power about 118,000 Ohio homes and bring local jobs and tax revenue.
