title: First Citizens Bank leads $170 million refinancing for esVolta's 370 MWh California storage portfolio
summary: First Citizens Bank's Energy Finance unit acted as lead agent on a $170 million credit facility for battery storage developer esVolta. The loan refinances and enlarges financing for esVolta's esFaraday portfolio of 370 MWh of storage projects in California.
details: The esFaraday portfolio has four battery storage projects in California, two already operating and two under construction. The new facility upsizes an earlier credit line from February 2020 that was arranged by CIT, which later merged into First Citizens in January 2022. Refinancing means replacing an existing loan with a new one, here on larger terms, to help finish building the projects. Morgan Lewis & Bockius advised esVolta and Winston & Strawn advised the lenders.
context: esVolta, owned by Generate Capital, says its operating and contracted projects total more than 1,600 MWh of storage. The deal extends an existing lending relationship between the developer and the bank and supports the completion of the company's California storage build-out.

sources.title: First Citizens Bank Leads $170 Million Refinancing for California Battery Energy Storage Project Portfolio

title: Emeren and Eiffel joint venture agrees to sell 29 MWp Spanish solar portfolio to Rubis Photosol
target: 29 MWp portfolio of three solar PV projects in Algorfa, Alicante, Spain
summary: A joint venture between solar developer Emeren Group and French asset manager Eiffel Investment Group has signed a share purchase agreement to sell a 29 MWp solar portfolio in Spain to Rubis Photosol. The portfolio consists of three projects in Alicante province. No price was disclosed.
details: The three late-stage projects are in the municipality of Algorfa, Alicante, and are close to receiving the Administrative Authorisation for Construction, the Spanish permit needed before building can start. They will use solar trackers, which tilt panels to follow the sun, and are projected to produce about 57,000 MWh a year, which the company says could supply around 20,000 households. Operation is expected in the second half of 2025. The deal was signed as a share purchase agreement (SPA), a contract to buy the companies holding the projects. Finergreen gave financial advice, Squire Patton Boggs legal advice and Everoze technical support to the sellers, while Watson Farley Williams advised Photosol.
context: The joint venture was set up in early 2021 to combine Emeren's European development experience with Eiffel's capital, and this sale shows it moving projects through to buyers. Emeren says the deal supports its expansion in Spain and across Europe. For Rubis Photosol, a French solar producer owned by the Rubis Group since 2022, the purchase adds to its growing international portfolio.

sources.title: Emeren Group and Eiffel Investment Group's Joint Venture Signs an Agreement to Sell 29 MWp Solar Portfolio in Spain

title: Emeren sells 410 MW Italian battery storage portfolio to Matrix Renewables
target: Portfolio of five standalone battery energy storage projects in Apulia, Italy
summary: Emeren Group has sold a portfolio of five standalone battery storage projects in Italy to Matrix Renewables. The projects total 410 MW of power and 3,787 MWh of storage capacity and are located in the southern region of Apulia.
details: The five projects are standalone battery systems, meaning they are not paired with a solar or wind plant. They are still in development and are expected to reach ready-to-build status, meaning all permits and grid rights are secured so construction can start, by late 2024. The sale falls under a development service agreement the two companies signed in June covering a planned 1.5 GW battery storage portfolio. No price or advisers were disclosed.
context: This is the second deal between Emeren and Matrix, and Emeren says it strengthens its position in European storage development, particularly in Italy. Matrix, a platform backed by TPG and its TPG Rise impact fund, says the purchase supports its expansion in the Italian market and grid resilience. Matrix reports a portfolio of 11.7 GW across Europe and the Americas.

sources.title: Emeren Group Sells a 410 MW Battery Energy Storage Portfolio in Italy

title: Aypa Power closes $550 million debt and tax equity financing for Cald and Borden County battery projects
target: Cald and Borden County battery storage projects
summary: Aypa Power, a Blackstone-owned storage developer, has closed a $550 million portfolio financing combining bank debt and tax equity. The money supports two battery projects totalling 250 MW and 700 MWh in California and Texas.
details: The Cald project in urban Los Angeles is a 100 MW / 400 MWh standalone battery, meaning about four hours of storage, and has a long-term tolling agreement with San Diego Gas & Electric, a contract where the utility pays for the right to use the battery. The Borden County project in Texas is 150 MW / 300 MWh, about two hours of storage. First Citizens Bank, Nomura, National Bank of Canada and MUFG are the lenders, with MUFG acting as administrative agent, the bank that manages the loan for the group. U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance is the tax equity investor, an investor that funds the projects in return for their federal tax benefits. Both projects are under construction and expected to start commercial operation in 2024.
context: Aypa says the batteries will support grid reliability and help integrate renewable power in California and Texas. The company states it has more than 22 GW of projects in development across North America and plans to bring more standalone and hybrid storage systems online as demand grows.

sources.title: AYPA POWER SECURES $550 MILLION PORTFOLIO FINANCING FOR BORDEN COUNTY AND CALD BATTERY STORAGE PROJECTS

title: Arevon closes $529 million financing for Vikings solar-plus-storage project in California
summary: Arevon Energy has closed a $529 million financing package for its Vikings solar-plus-storage project in Imperial County, California. The package pairs a $338 million bank debt facility with a commitment from J.P. Morgan to buy $191 million of federal tax credits generated by the project.
details: Vikings combines 157 MW DC of solar panels with a 150 MW / 600 MWh battery system, which works out to about four hours of storage. J.P. Morgan agreed to purchase both investment and production tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act's transferability rule, which lets a project owner sell its tax credits for cash to another taxpayer. MUFG, BNP Paribas, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and First Citizens Bank led the debt as coordinating lead arrangers, with National Bank of Canada also lending. The project is contracted to supply renewable energy and resource adequacy, meaning guaranteed available capacity, to San Diego Community Power, and is under construction by SOLV Energy with commercial operation planned for the third quarter of 2024. Equipment comes from First Solar, Nextracker and Tesla.
context: Arevon describes Vikings as one of the first utility-scale solar peaker plants in the US, using batteries to shift solar output to times of peak demand. The company says the deal is among the first solar-plus-storage financings to close using tax credit transfers since the Inflation Reduction Act passed in 2022, following Treasury guidance on the mechanism issued in June 2023.

sources.title: Arevon Completes Financing on Nation's First Utility-Scale Solar Peaker Project Using the IRA's Transferability Provision

title: EQT Infrastructure VI agrees to buy UK battery storage developer Statera from InfraRed
summary: The EQT Infrastructure VI fund has agreed to acquire London-based Statera Energy from InfraRed Capital Partners. Statera develops and operates battery storage and flexible generation in the UK, with 1 GW in operation or under construction. No price was disclosed.
details: Statera, founded in 2015, has about 1 GW of flexible capacity operating or being built and a project pipeline of more than 16 GW, which it says includes batteries, pumped hydro and green hydrogen. Flexible generation here means assets that can supply or absorb power on demand to balance the grid. The company aims to deliver 7.5 GW of such assets by 2030. The deal needs customary conditions and approvals and is expected to close around the end of 2023. DC Advisory acted as financial adviser and Simpson Thacher & Bartlett as legal adviser to EQT.
context: EQT argues that demand for grid balancing services from batteries will grow quickly as intermittent wind and solar expand and fossil plants close. EQT says it will provide growth capital to speed up Statera's project rollout. With this deal, EQT expects its sixth infrastructure fund to be 20 to 25 percent invested relative to its target size.

sources.title: EQT Infrastructure to acquire Statera, a leading battery storage and flexible generation platform supporting the UK's renewable energy transition

title: Talus Renewables raises $22 million Series A for modular green ammonia systems
summary: New York based Talus Renewables has raised $22 million in a Series A funding round, meaning an early round of venture capital, to scale up its modular green ammonia systems. The round was co-led by Material Impact and Xora Innovation, the early-stage deep tech platform of Temasek, with Cavallo Ventures and Rice Investment Group also taking part.
details: Talus builds containerized units that make ammonia from water, air and renewable electricity, an approach usually called green ammonia because it avoids fossil fuels. Its talusOne unit produces up to 1.4 tonnes of ammonia per day and its talusTen unit up to 20 tonnes per day. The company plans to deliver multiple units in US and European markets starting later in 2023. Its first talusOne was installed with the Kenya Nut Company in the Kenya Highlands. Cavallo Ventures is the venture capital arm of Wilbur-Ellis.
context: Ammonia is a key fertilizer ingredient and is normally made in large fossil-fuel plants and shipped long distances. Talus claims its systems can produce cheaper, carbon-free ammonia at or near where it is used, cutting supply chains for farming, mining and industry. One investor said Talus stands out because it is already delivering systems while many green ammonia rivals are still in development.

sources.title: Talus Renewables Announces $22 Million Raised in Series A Financing

summary: Longroad Energy has closed financing and started building Sun Streams 4, a 377 MWdc solar and 300 MWac / 1,200 MWh battery project in Maricopa County, Arizona. Debt was led by CIBC with a group of eight other banks, and U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance provided tax equity. Arizona Public Service will buy the full output.
details: The project pairs 377 MWdc of solar panels with a four-hour battery system of 300 MWac and 1,200 MWh, and is the third project in Longroad's Sun Streams complex acquired from First Solar in 2021. Financial close means the funding agreements are signed and money is available to build. U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance supplied tax equity, an investment that earns returns largely from federal tax credits, as well as debt. Arizona Public Service signed a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to buy the electricity, with its length not stated. McCarthy is the EPC contractor, First Solar supplies modules, Powin supplies the batteries, and commercial operation is expected by mid-2025.
context: Longroad says Sun Streams 4 is its largest project by both capacity and investment and one of its first to use Inflation Reduction Act provisions. The utility expects the project to support reliability during Arizona's peak summer demand. CIBC described the deal as Longroad's largest financing to date.

title: Subterra Renewables affiliates acquire Earth Drilling and Harris Exploration
target: Earth Drilling Co. Ltd. and Harris Exploration
summary: Affiliates of Toronto-based geothermal heating and cooling provider Subterra Renewables have acquired Alberta-based Earth Drilling Co. and, as part of the same transaction, Nevada-based Harris Exploration. The purchase extends Subterra's geothermal drilling operations into Western Canada and the southwestern United States. No price was disclosed.
details: Earth Drilling is a privately held geotechnical and environmental drilling firm with close to 50 years of history, and Harris Exploration provides drilling and installation services in Nevada, California and Arizona. The companies will drill boreholes for geo-exchange systems, which move heat between buildings and the ground to provide heating and cooling. Subterra says the combined group now runs 68 drilling rigs and plans to grow the fleet to more than 100 within 12 months. Subterra also opened a Calgary office led by its President Matthew Tokarik.
context: Subterra describes itself as a vertically integrated geothermal utility, meaning it designs, installs, owns and operates its systems, and it says the deal gives it coast-to-coast drilling reach. The company claims the combined fleet is the largest geothermal drilling fleet in North America. It points to rising clean energy investment in Alberta and Arizona as reasons for basing western drilling fleets there.

sources.title: Subterra Renewables expands into Western Canada and U.S. following affiliate acquisition of Alberta's Earth Drilling Co. to meet North American geothermal demands

title: A2A signs PPA with Enfinity Global for 97 MW of solar projects in Lazio, Italy
target: Three Enfinity Global photovoltaic projects in Lazio, Italy
summary: Italian utility A2A has agreed to buy power from three Enfinity Global solar projects in the Lazio region of Italy under a power purchase agreement. The projects total 97 MW, and A2A is set to take about 160 GWh of electricity per year.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific power plant, often over many years. The agreement covers three photovoltaic projects developed by Enfinity Global in Lazio and is scheduled to take effect in July 2025. The companies say the roughly 160 GWh per year matches the annual consumption of about 64,000 Italian households and offsets more than 60,000 tonnes of CO2. Price and contract length were not disclosed.
context: Enfinity Global says the deal brings its contracted capacity in Italy under long-term power sales agreements to 232 MW, making it, by its own account, the largest such provider in the country. The company also reports 500 MW of fully permitted solar, 1.8 GW of solar in advanced permitting and 2 GW of storage projects in Italy. A2A presents the agreement as part of its effort to supply customers with more renewable power, alongside a planned 11 billion euro investment in energy transition infrastructure by 2030.

title: Ultra Capital makes $10 million equity investment in US solar and storage developer Palladium Energy
summary: Palladium Energy, a Jacksonville, Florida based developer of utility-scale solar and storage projects, has closed a $10 million corporate equity investment from Philadelphia investment firm Ultra Capital. The money is meant to grow the company's team and project pipeline in the US.
details: The investment is at the corporate level, meaning Ultra Capital is buying into the development company itself rather than funding a single project. Palladium says it will use the funds to originate, acquire and develop solar and storage projects. As part of the deal, Palladium formed a Board of Directors made up of its three co-founders, Mark Mirabito, Nobel Chang and Danny Weidlich, plus Ultra Capital Managing Director Mike Reynolds. No stake size, project capacities or advisers were disclosed.
context: Palladium, founded in 2019, says its team has previously developed 6.9 GW of projects and financed $2.8 billion worth. The company presents the investment as validation of its team and asset base. Ultra Capital, which provides growth equity and asset capital to energy transition companies, frames the deal as a bet on the ongoing decarbonization of the US power grid.

title: TransAlta completes buyout of minority shares in TransAlta Renewables
summary: TransAlta Corporation has closed its acquisition of all TransAlta Renewables shares it did not already own, making the Calgary-based renewables company a wholly owned subsidiary. Before the deal TransAlta and its affiliates held about 60.1% of the shares. Minority holders received a mix of up to about C$800 million in cash and roughly 46.4 million TransAlta shares.
details: The deal was carried out as a court-approved plan of arrangement, a Canadian legal process for corporate takeovers, approved by shareholders on September 26, 2023 and by the Court of King's Bench of Alberta on October 4, 2023. Each holder could choose 1.0337 TransAlta shares or C$13.00 in cash per share, with pro-rationing, meaning payouts were adjusted so total cash and shares stayed within set limits. Holders of about 36.8 million shares chose cash and those of about 69.7 million chose shares. TransAlta Renewables shares will be delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange and the company will apply to stop being a reporting issuer. Eligible shareholders can make a joint tax election with TransAlta by January 3, 2024.
context: TransAlta says merging the two companies simplifies its corporate structure and should make its cash flow more predictable while supporting future growth. The company describes itself as one of Canada's largest wind power producers and Alberta's largest hydro producer, with assets in Canada, the United States and Australia.

title: ArcLight completes acquisition of Duke Energy's commercial distributed generation portfolio including REC Solar
target: Duke Energy commercial distributed generation portfolio, including REC Solar
summary: Duke Energy has completed the sale of its commercial distributed generation business, which includes REC Solar, to an investment fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners. The deal was first announced in July 2023. No price or capacity figure was disclosed.
details: The portfolio covers REC Solar's operating solar assets, its pipeline of projects still in development, and its operations and maintenance (O&M) service business, meaning the work of running and repairing plants. It also includes distributed fuel cell projects managed by Bloom Energy. Distributed generation refers to smaller power systems located at or near the customers who use the electricity, such as on commercial sites. Staff of the business are moving to ArcLight. BofA Securities and Mayer Brown advised Duke Energy, while Scotia and Kirkland & Ellis advised ArcLight.
context: Duke Energy says it will use the proceeds, along with those from the pending sale of its utility-scale renewables platform expected by the end of 2023, to strengthen its balance sheet and avoid issuing more holding company debt. The company says the exits let it focus on its regulated utilities, including plans to add over 30,000 MW of regulated renewables by 2035. For ArcLight, the release describes the purchase as extending its strategy of building standalone renewable platforms.

sources.title: Duke Energy completes sale of commercial distributed generation portfolio, including REC Solar, to ArcLight

title: TDK Ventures invests in US sodium-ion storage startup Peak Energy
summary: TDK Ventures, the venture capital arm of Japan's TDK Corporation, has made an undisclosed investment in Peak Energy, a US startup developing sodium-ion batteries for grid-scale energy storage. The size of the investment and the stake acquired were not stated.
details: Peak Energy was founded in 2023 by former executives from Tesla, Northvolt and Enovix, and is led by CEO Landon Mossburg. It is working on sodium-ion battery systems for utility-scale storage, meaning large batteries connected to the power grid. The company plans to build domestic supply chains and gigafactory-scale manufacturing in the United States. Venture firm Eclipse is also involved with the company, according to a partner quoted in the release.
context: The release cites an estimate that the US will need about 600 GWh of energy storage by 2030. Peak Energy claims sodium-ion batteries can be cheaper and safer than lithium-ion and less exposed to lithium price swings and foreign supply chains, since sodium is abundant in the US. TDK says the investment fits its focus on societal impact and financial return in energy technology.

sources.title: TDK Ventures invests in Peak Energy to advance sodium-ion energy storage solutions

title: Sabanci Renewables acquires 232 MWdc Oriana Solar plus storage project in Texas from Advanced Power
summary: Advanced Power has completed the sale of its full interest in Oriana Solar LLC to Sabanci Renewables, a unit of Turkey's Sabanci Holdings. The project in Victoria County, Texas combines 232 MWdc of solar with a 60 MW/120 MWh battery. No price was disclosed.
details: Oriana Solar is a photovoltaic plant on a 1,100-acre site about 10 miles north of Victoria, Texas, with a co-located battery able to deliver 60 MW for about two hours. The project is still in late development, with construction expected to start in the first quarter of 2024 and commercial operation planned for 2025. It will sell power and renewable energy credits into the ERCOT wholesale market rather than under a disclosed long-term contract, which is often called merchant sales. Marathon Capital led the sale process.
context: This is the second deal between the two companies, following Sabanci's earlier purchase of Advanced Power's Cutlass Solar projects. Advanced Power says the sale brings its closed Texas solar and solar-plus-storage projects to four, totaling more than 800 MWdc and 240 MWh of storage, and that it has an 8 GW US renewables pipeline. Sabanci says the purchase reflects its aim to build a sizable international clean energy portfolio.

sources.title: Advanced Power Closes Sale of Oriana Solar to Sabanci Renewables

title: Greenprint Capital and AB CarVal form joint venture to fund up to $2.5 billion tax equity pipeline

buyers.name: AB CarVal
buyers.role: funds managed by AB CarVal provide capital

sellers.name: Greenprint Capital Management
sellers.role: joint venture partner and tax equity platform

summary: Greenprint Capital Management signed an agreement with funds managed by AB CarVal to form a joint venture called Greenprint Value Investors. The venture is meant to give US renewable energy developers access to up to $2.5 billion in tax equity capital for projects due in 2024 and 2025.
details: Tax equity is investment from parties who put money into clean energy projects in exchange for the federal tax credits those projects generate. AB CarVal funds will finance Greenprint's tax equity pipeline and its tax credit warehouse, which is a facility that holds tax credit investments before they are passed to final buyers. Greenprint's existing portfolio spans 37 funds across 16 states, focused mainly on utility-scale solar and energy storage. The venture plans to source and manage tax credit and tax equity investments in sustainable infrastructure across the United States.
context: Greenprint says the new liquidity lets it do more deals with existing corporate clients and bring in new buyers looking to reduce their tax bills by acquiring renewable energy tax credits. AB CarVal describes the venture as a source of late-stage working capital for developers and of due diligence support for tax credit buyers. AB CarVal, part of AllianceBernstein, reports investing over $4 billion in clean energy since 2017.

sources.title: Greenprint Capital Management and AB CarVal finalize joint venture to support a $2.5 billion tax equity investment pipeline of 2024-2025 renewable energy and storage projects

title: Generate Capital makes $10 million corporate equity investment in Cultivate Power
summary: Chicago-based distributed solar and storage developer Cultivate Power has raised $10 million in corporate equity from Generate Capital. The money is meant to fund the developer's growth in US community solar markets.
details: The deal is a corporate equity investment, meaning Generate Capital is buying into the company itself rather than financing a single project. Cultivate Power develops solar and storage projects on sites of roughly 10 to 50 acres, mostly on farmland and infill land, and has development teams across the Midwest and California. The company says it will use the funds to expand project development, hire staff and back local programs such as scholarships and workforce training. No stake size, capacity figures or advisers were disclosed.
context: Community solar lets nearby households and businesses subscribe to a share of a local solar farm's output. Generate Capital says it has known the Cultivate founders for years and sees their portfolio as a fit with its infrastructure strategy. Cultivate Power claims its locally focused approach brings rural communities benefits such as cheaper power and added tax revenue.

sources.title: CULTIVATE POWER SECURES $10 MILLION EQUITY INVESTMENT FROM GENERATE CAPITAL TO DEVELOP AND BUILD CLEAN ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE IN EMERGING COMMUNITY SOLAR MARKETS

title: Canadian Solar's Recurrent Energy sells 17.5 MWp Hiroshima Suzuhari solar plant to private Japanese fund
summary: Canadian Solar, through its Recurrent Energy development arm, has completed the sale of the 17.5 MWp Hiroshima Suzuhari solar plant in Hiroshima prefecture, Japan, to an unnamed private Japanese fund. The price was not disclosed.
details: The plant began commercial operation in the second quarter of 2022 and uses more than 42,500 Canadian Solar HiKu modules. It had been held since 2021 by the Japan Green Infrastructure Fund and financed with an investment-grade Green Project Bond rated Green 1 under Japanese green bond guidelines. Its output is bought by Chugoku Electric Power Transmission & Distribution at JPY17.97 per kWh under Japan's feed-in tariff, a government-set fixed price, for the remaining 17.5 years. Recurrent Energy's local subsidiary will keep providing operations and maintenance after the sale, and Canadian Solar expects to book the revenue in the third quarter of 2023.
context: The project was Recurrent Energy's first to win a tariff in Japan's inaugural solar auction in late 2017. With this sale, all projects bought by the Japan Green Infrastructure Fund have been sold in line with its business plan, according to the company. Recurrent Energy says it intends to build more solar and storage projects across Japan.

sources.title: Canadian Solar's Recurrent Energy Executes Sale of 17.5 MWp Solar Power Plant in Japan

title: Southern Power acquires 150 MW South Cheyenne Solar Facility in Wyoming from Qcells USA
summary: Southern Power, the wholesale generation arm of Southern Company, has acquired the 150 MW South Cheyenne Solar Facility in Wyoming from developer Qcells USA. It is Southern Power's 30th solar project and its first solar plant in Wyoming. No price was disclosed.
details: The project is under construction and is expected to begin commercial operation, meaning start selling power on a regular basis, in the first quarter of 2024. Qcells USA developed the project and is also handling engineering, procurement and construction (the full design and build work) and supplying the solar modules. The electricity and renewable energy credits, which are certificates proving power came from a renewable source, will be sold under a 20-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell the output at agreed terms. The buyer of the power was not named. About 180 jobs are expected at peak construction.
context: Southern Power says the deal fits its strategy of owning generating assets backed by long-term contracts with creditworthy buyers. With this addition, the company reports more than 2,740 MW of solar within a 5,280 MW renewable fleet of 30 solar and 15 wind facilities operating or under construction. The project extends its footprint into a new state.

sources.title: Southern Power acquires South Cheyenne Solar Facility

title: Enfinity Global acquires 546 MW Colorado solar development portfolio from CS Energy
target: Portfolio of three solar projects under development in Colorado (546 MW)
summary: Enfinity Global, a renewable power producer based in Miami, has bought three solar projects in development in Colorado totalling 546 MW. The seller is CS Energy, an engineering and construction firm owned by private equity group American Securities. The price was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio is made up of three solar projects still in development in Colorado, part of the western US grid region known as WECC. Construction is expected to begin within the next two years, and once running the projects are expected to generate about 1,054 GWh of electricity a year. Enfinity says the portfolio should bring in roughly $59 million a year in EBITDA, a measure of operating earnings, from sales to investment grade customers. The projects will be folded into Enfinity's in-house development team.
context: The deal adds to Enfinity's US pipeline, which the company says includes about 6 GW of solar and storage projects in development alongside 400 MW in operation in California, Idaho and North Carolina. Enfinity presents the purchase as part of a strategy of buying portfolios from developers who value its access to capital and supply chains. Colorado was chosen partly because the state requires 100% renewable electricity by 2050.

sources.title: Enfinity Global acquires 546 MW of solar assets in Colorado (United States)

title: Southern Power acquires 200 MW Millers Branch solar project in Texas from EDF Renewables
summary: Southern Power, the wholesale generation arm of Southern Company, has bought the Millers Branch Solar Facility from EDF Renewables. The 200 MW project is in Haskell County, Texas, and could be expanded to as much as 500 MW.
details: The project is at an early development stage, and Southern Power will take over its further development and construction. Commercial operation, meaning the start of regular power sales, is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2025. The output and renewable energy credits from the 200 MW facility will be sold to Thermo Fisher Scientific under a 20-year virtual power purchase agreement, a financial contract where the buyer pays a fixed price for the power and receives the green certificates without taking physical delivery. No purchase price or advisers were disclosed.
context: Southern Power says this is its 29th solar project and brings its solar portfolio to more than 2,590 MW within a 5,130 MW renewable fleet. The company describes the deal as fitting its strategy of buying and building plants backed by long-term contracts with creditworthy customers. Thermo Fisher plans to use the certificates toward its net zero by 2050 goal.

sources.title: Southern Power acquires Millers Branch Solar Facility

title: DSD Renewables acquires 15 MW Minnesota community solar portfolio from New Energy Equity
target: Nine-project, 15 MW community solar portfolio in Minnesota
summary: DSD Renewables has bought a portfolio of nine community solar projects totalling 15 MW in Minnesota from developer New Energy Equity. The projects are expected to produce more than 20,000 MWh a year for about 900 subscribers. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The ground-mounted projects are located in Belle Plaine, Clear Lake, Howard Lake, Mankato, Mazeppa, Saint Cloud, Sauk Rapids and Winsted. The Winsted site is agrivoltaic, meaning solar panels share the land with farming. Community solar lets households subscribe to a share of a local solar farm and receive credits on their power bills, and this portfolio is sold entirely to residential subscribers. Construction has begun on four projects, the other five are due to start by the end of 2023, and the full portfolio is expected to be finished in 2024. Arcadia Power will manage customer sign-ups and subscriptions.
context: The deal expands DSD's presence in Minnesota after it bought an 11.3 MW community solar portfolio there the year before. DSD says the acquisition supports the state's goal of 100% clean energy by 2040. New Energy Equity, a unit of ALLETE, points to the state's recently extended community solar program as a benefit for communities and developers.

sources.title: DSD Acquires 15 MW Community Solar Portfolio from New Energy Equity in Minnesota

title: Ellevio acquires Markbygden Net grid serving Markbygden 1101 wind cluster from Svevind and Enercon
summary: Swedish grid company Ellevio has bought Markbygden Net AB, the transmission network that links parts of the Markbygden 1101 wind farm cluster near Piteå in northern Sweden to the power system. The network was owned 75% by Svevind and 25% by turbine maker Enercon. No price was disclosed.
details: The acquired grid has about 1,700 MW of distribution capacity and carries roughly 5 to 6 TWh of wind power a year from parts of the cluster. The full Markbygden 1101 cluster is estimated at about 3,400 MW and up to 12 TWh a year, which the release puts at around 7% of Sweden's electricity output. Ellevio took ownership on 20 September 2023 and will serve five customers, all wind farm operators. Ellevio itself is owned by pension investors OMERS Infrastructure, AP3, Folksam and AMF.
context: The deal marks Ellevio's first entry into Sweden's northern electricity region, where large power producers and energy-intensive industry are concentrated. Ellevio says the move supports electrification of industry and Sweden's goal of net-zero emissions by 2045. Svevind, which developed the network, describes the transfer to a major distribution company as a fitting next step for the infrastructure.

sources.title: Ellevio expands to northern Sweden - acquires power grid for Europe's largest wind farm

title: Shanghai Electric Energy Storage Technology raises RMB400 million in Series A round
summary: Shanghai Electric Energy Storage Technology, the energy storage unit of Chinese group Shanghai Electric, has raised RMB400 million in a Series A round, meaning its first major outside equity funding. The company says its valuation after the investment will be above RMB2.2 billion.
details: The business makes vanadium redox flow batteries, a type of battery that stores energy in liquid electrolyte tanks and suits long-duration storage. It has developed battery stacks of 5 kW to 65 kW and says it has delivered over 50 flow battery storage projects. The new money is meant for research and development, expanding production lines, building larger stacks for megawatt-scale container systems, and pursuing 100 MW projects. The release does not name the investors or any advisers.
context: The raise supports Shanghai Electric's stated strategy of combining wind, solar, hydrogen and storage. The company plans a Series B round in 2024 and expects to begin a listing process on Shanghai's Science and Technology Innovation Board in 2026. It presents itself as a leader in long-duration electrochemical storage, a claim made by the company.

sources.title: Shanghai Electric Subsidiary, Shanghai Electric Energy Storage Technology, Receives RMB400 Million in Series A Financing, Accelerating Development of Its Energy Storage Business

title: BXP signs PPA with Enel for 21 MW of Texas Estonian solar project
target: Estonian solar + storage project (21 MW portion)
summary: Enel North America has agreed to sell power from a 21 MW share of its Estonian solar project in Delta County, Texas, to office real estate company BXP under a power purchase agreement. The project is under construction and is expected to start operating in late 2024.
details: A power purchase agreement is a contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project, often over many years. The Estonian project combines a 202 MW (AC) solar plant, about 262 MW in DC terms, with a 104 MW battery system, and Enel expects it to produce about 499 GWh per year. The plant connects to ERCOT, the main Texas power grid. The release does not state the contract length or price. Edison Energy advised BXP on the deal.
context: The deal extends an existing relationship in which Enel already provides BXP with demand response and utility bill management services. BXP says it wants to buy power from new projects so that its purchases add renewable generation to the grid. Enel describes itself as one of the largest renewable operators in Texas, with 1.8 GW of solar under construction in the state, and the company expects the project to bring over $23 million in local tax revenue over its life.

sources.title: ENEL AND BXP EXECUTE POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT FOR NEW TEXAS SOLAR PROJECT

title: Recurrent Energy closes $200 million debt and tax equity package for 134 MW Liberty Solar in Texas

buyers.name: Rabobank
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger and Joint Lead Arranger

advisors.name: Foley & Lardner
advisors.role: Legal counsel to U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance

summary: Recurrent Energy, the development arm of Canadian Solar, has closed $120 million of debt and $80 million of tax equity for its 134 MW Liberty Solar project in Liberty County, Texas. Rabobank, Nord LB and U.S. Bank provided the loans and U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance provided the tax equity.
details: Liberty Solar is rated 134 MW on the panel side and 100 MW on the grid side (MWac), sits about 50 miles northeast of Houston, is under construction and is expected to start operating in 2024. The $120 million debt package includes a construction loan, a letter of credit facility and a longer term loan. The $80 million tax equity comes from U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance, meaning the investor funds part of the project in exchange for using its federal tax credits. All of the output is sold under an aggregated virtual power purchase agreement, a financial contract where buyers pay a set price for power without taking physical delivery. CohnReznick Capital and Latham & Watkins advised Recurrent, Milbank represented the lenders and Foley & Lardner represented U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance.
context: Recurrent says this is its second North American project financing closed this summer and reflects its strategy of keeping more ownership of projects in chosen markets. The project adds solar to the MISO grid region, where the release says solar is only about 1% of the resource mix.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes $120 Million in Project Financing and $80 Million in Tax Equity for 134 MW MISO South Project

title: Colgate-Palmolive signs virtual PPA for Scout Clean Energy's 209 MW Markum Solar Farm in Texas

advisors.name: Stoel Rives LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Scout Clean Energy

summary: Scout Clean Energy, a Brookfield Renewable portfolio company, has signed a power purchase agreement with Colgate-Palmolive for its 209 MWdc Markum Solar Farm near Waco, Texas. The project is Scout's first greenfield solar build.
details: Markum sits in McLennan and Bosque Counties and will feed the ERCOT grid, the network serving most of Texas. Colgate-Palmolive described the contract as a virtual PPA, a financial arrangement where the buyer pays a fixed price for the project's output and receives the renewable attributes without taking physical delivery of the power. Scout planned to start construction in fall 2023, manage the build itself, and finish by the end of 2024. Contract length and price were not disclosed. Stoel Rives advised Scout and Morgan, Lewis & Bockius advised Colgate-Palmolive.
context: Scout says the signed PPA and construction contracts give it the certainty needed to build its first solar project, and that more Scout-owned projects are set to start construction over the following year. Colgate-Palmolive says such agreements support its targets of 100% renewable electricity by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2040. Brookfield Renewable acquired Scout at the start of 2023.

sources.title: Scout Signs Power Purchase Agreement with Colgate-Palmolive for 209 MW Solar Farm

title: Dimension Renewable Energy closes $237 million financing for 120 MWdc US community solar portfolio
target: 120 MWdc portfolio of 28 community solar projects

advisors.name: Milbank
advisors.role: legal counsel to SVB and lenders

summary: Dimension Renewable Energy has closed a $237 million financing to build a 120 MWdc portfolio of 28 community solar projects. The projects are in New York, New Jersey, Virginia and California. Silicon Valley Bank led the debt, while NT Solar and Advantage Capital arranged tax equity.
details: The 28 projects are community solar sites, meaning local households and small businesses subscribe to a share of a nearby solar farm and receive credits on their power bills instead of installing panels at home. The portfolio is expected to serve more than 12,000 residential and commercial customers, with over half of it set aside for low and moderate income households. Silicon Valley Bank, a division of First Citizens Bank, led and syndicated the construction debt, meaning it organised the loan and shared it among other lenders. NT Solar and Advantage Capital arranged tax equity, which is investment from parties that receive the projects' federal tax credits in return for funding. The financing supports construction of the portfolio.
context: The bank described this as Dimension's first project financing. Dimension, owned by Partners Group, says the funding supports its aim of becoming a leading community solar independent power producer in the US. The deal reflects growing lender and tax equity interest in community solar aimed at lower income customers.

sources.title: Updated: Dimension Renewable Energy Announces Closing of $237 Million Financing to Support Construction of 120 MWdc Distributed Generation Portfolio

title: BlueWave closes $91 million debt and tax equity financing for five Massachusetts agrivoltaic solar projects
target: Five agrivoltaic solar projects in Massachusetts
summary: BlueWave, a Boston-based solar developer and owner, has closed a $91 million financing for five dual-use solar projects in Massachusetts. The package combines $64 million of debt from KeyBank with $27 million of tax equity from U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance and covers the first 20 MW of its pipeline.
details: The five projects are agrivoltaic, meaning solar panels share land with farming. Four allow crops or farming to continue beneath the arrays and the fifth will create new grazing pasture. The money funds both construction and long-term financing. Tax equity is investment from a party that receives the project's tax credits in return for capital. KeyBanc Capital Markets acted as coordinating lead arranger on the debt, and CohnReznick Capital and Foley Hoag advised BlueWave. The projects are expected to start commercial operation later in 2023.
context: This is described as BlueWave's first major financing round and lets it hold projects long term rather than sell them, with backing from its parent company Axium Infrastructure. The projects will join the state's SMART solar incentive program and the company says they will deliver bill credit savings to about 770 low-income households. BlueWave reports a pipeline of more than 2 GW and says the projects aim to show solar can coexist with farming.

sources.title: BlueWave Closes First Major Financing Round to Support Agrivoltaic Solar Development and Long-Term Project Ownership

title: Vertimass EMEA agrees to buy Polish renewable fuel producer Ekobenz
summary: Vertimass EMEA has signed a purchase agreement to acquire all shares of Ekobenz, a Polish company that produces renewable gasoline, LPG and other fuels. No price was disclosed.
details: Ekobenz, founded in 2006, runs a plant in Poland that began operating in 2018 with a designed yearly output of about 8 million gallons (22,500 tons) of fuel. The site covers more than 5.5 hectares and includes a warehouse, laboratory and support building. The company is a certified producer of bio-gasoline and bio-LPG in Europe and says its fuel cuts CO2 emissions by about 80% on average. The final sale and purchase agreement is scheduled to be signed on December 31, 2023.
context: Vertimass plans to use the plant as a commercial-scale base for its CADO process, a technology that turns alcohols such as ethanol into hydrocarbon fuels, with sustainable aviation fuel as a main focus. The company says the deal will let it produce fuel commercially right away, prove its technology at scale and expand into markets outside the United States.

sources.title: Vertimass EMEA Signs Agreement to Acquire European Renewable Fuel Company Ekobenz

title: Igneo Infrastructure Partners agrees to buy majority stake in US solar and storage producer Soltage
summary: Igneo Infrastructure Partners, an infrastructure investment manager with about US$18 billion under management, has agreed to acquire a majority equity interest in Soltage, a New Jersey based solar and storage company active in 18 US states. The stake is being bought from investors including Prudential Private Capital and some management members. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Soltage, founded in 2005, develops, owns and operates solar and battery storage assets and has developed more than 500 MW of solar across roughly 125 projects for utility, business and municipal customers. It has a 1.9 GW identified pipeline of solar and storage projects and is building its first standalone battery storage project in New York. CEO Jesse Grossman, CFO Sripradha Ilango and other managers will keep ownership stakes. Mayer Brown and Macquarie Capital advised Igneo, while Foley Hoag and Citi advised Soltage. The deal is expected to close later in 2023.
context: With Igneo's backing, Soltage plans to become a full independent power producer, meaning a company that owns its plants and sells the electricity rather than mainly developing projects for others. The deal would be Igneo's fifth North American asset and its first in US distributed generation, which refers to smaller power plants located near where the electricity is used. Igneo says it expects Soltage to expand into new regions and electrification technologies.

sources.title: Igneo Infrastructure Partners to Acquire Majority Equity Interest in U.S. Renewable Power Producer Soltage

title: AB CarVal funds commit up to $250 million equity to solar land financier SolaREIT
summary: Funds managed by AB CarVal, an alternative investment manager within AllianceBernstein, have closed an equity investment in SolaREIT, a Virginia-based solar real estate investment fund. The investment starts at $100 million and can grow to as much as $250 million, and it is meant to expand SolaREIT's land, lease and loan financing for US solar and battery storage projects.
details: SolaREIT, founded in late 2020, buys land and existing land leases under solar farms and battery storage sites and also offers mortgage loans. This lets developers and landowners turn the value of the land or lease into cash up front, or lower ongoing lease costs. The release describes the deal as an initial $100 million with up to $250 million available, but it does not give a timeline for drawing the further capital. No stake size or advisers are disclosed.
context: SolaREIT says it has helped support hundreds of megawatts of renewable projects across the US since it was founded, and its leaders argue that developers need more flexible capital in the current financial environment. AB CarVal states it has invested over $4 billion in clean energy since 2017, including solar loans and solar asset-backed securities, and it presents this deal as a way to scale solar and storage growth.

sources.title: SolaREIT and AB CarVal Announce up to $250 million Investment to Turbocharge Solar and Battery Storage Development Growth

title: Recurrent Energy closes $112 million financing for 160 MW North Fork Solar in Oklahoma, signs OMPA as offtaker

buyers.name: NordLB
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger and Joint Lead Arranger

summary: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, has secured $112 million in project financing for its 160 MW North Fork Solar project in Oklahoma. NordLB and Rabobank arranged the debt, and the Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority will buy all of the plant's output.
details: North Fork Solar is rated 160 MW on the panel side and 120 MW on the grid connection side, and sits about 100 miles southwest of Oklahoma City. NordLB served as coordinating lead arranger and joint lead arranger, with Rabobank as joint lead arranger, meaning the banks organised and provided the loan. OMPA, which serves 42 municipally owned electric systems, signed a 15-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy all the electricity produced. Blattner Energy is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, and the project is expected to start operating in 2024. Development began in 2018, and Recurrent plans to own and operate the plant after construction.
context: The project is Recurrent Energy's first in Oklahoma and its first in the Southwest Power Pool, a grid and wholesale market covering 15 central US states where solar is under 1 percent of the resource mix. It is also OMPA's first solar purchase, adding to a supply that already includes 151 MW of Oklahoma wind. Recurrent says the deal fits its push to hold more projects in its own operating portfolio.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Closes $112 Million in Project Financing, Announces Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority as Customer for 160 MW Oklahoma Solar Project

title: Peregrine Energy Solutions secures over $700 million from AB CarVal funds for 7 GW pipeline
summary: Peregrine Energy Solutions, a Boulder, Colorado clean energy platform focused on utility-scale battery storage, has signed an agreement with funds managed by AB CarVal to raise more than $700 million. The mix of credit, equity and debt is meant to fund Peregrine's pipeline of over 7 GW of storage, solar and wind projects in North America.
details: The pipeline includes standalone battery storage, solar and wind projects spread across 10 states and five independent system operators, which are the organizations that run regional power grids. The money is intended to carry projects through to commercial operation date, meaning the point when a plant starts selling power. Peregrine also says the capital will let it pursue market arbitrage, which here means storing power when it is cheap and selling it when prices are higher, and expand into new regions. The release does not break down the split between credit, equity and debt or name any advisers.
context: Peregrine was set up in 2022 and the deal gives it substantial new liquidity to advance a large development pipeline. AB CarVal, part of AllianceBernstein's private alternatives business, says it expects strong growth in demand for renewables and storage in North America and states it has deployed over $4 billion in clean energy since 2017.

sources.title: Peregrine Energy Solutions and AB CarVal finalize $700 million financing agreement to support a pipeline of renewable energy and storage projects

title: BayWa r.e. Solar Trade agrees to acquire Brazilian solar distributor Ribeiro Solar
summary: BayWa r.e. Solar Trade, the solar component distribution arm of BayWa r.e., has signed an agreement to buy Ribeiro Solar, a solar equipment distributor that operates only in Brazil. The deal marks BayWa r.e. Solar Trade's entry into the Brazilian market. No price was disclosed.
details: Ribeiro Solar is based in the Curitiba area of Paraná state and runs warehouse hubs in Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul and Pernambuco that supply solar products to installers across Brazil. The solar unit was set up in 2015 within the Ribeiro business, which marks 50 years in 2024, and is led by CEO Liciany Ribeiro. The parties said they would finalize the acquisition in the weeks following the August 2023 signing. The deal concerns a distribution business, meaning a company that buys and resells solar panels and related parts, rather than power generating assets.
context: BayWa r.e. says the purchase gives it a foothold in Brazil and adds to its existing solar distribution operations in the United States, Canada and Mexico. The company describes itself as one of the largest solar component distributors globally, active in more than 30 countries and serving over 17,000 solar contractor customers. It expects Ribeiro Solar's installer network and local knowledge, combined with its own global supply chain, to help grow solar adoption in Brazil.

sources.title: BayWa r.e. Solar Trade Marks Brazilian Market Entry with Acquisition of Ribeiro Solar

title: Fiera Infrastructure Private Debt and Foundation Credit provide credit facility for three Pine Creek RNG projects
target: Three renewable natural gas projects in the western U.S.
summary: Fiera Infrastructure Private Debt has closed a senior secured credit facility for Pine Creek Renewables, a US developer of renewable natural gas projects. Foundation Credit also lent into the facility, which will fund three projects in the western United States. The size of the facility was not disclosed.
details: The loan is senior secured, meaning it is repaid first and backed by the project assets. The money will go toward building and running three renewable natural gas (RNG) projects, two at landfills and one at an anaerobic digester, which is a sealed tank where organic waste breaks down. The projects capture methane released by decomposing waste and upgrade it to gas clean enough to inject into pipelines. All three projects already have offtake contracts, which are agreements with buyers for their output, and they will also produce environmental attributes, tradable credits tied to the low-carbon fuel.
context: The financing backs Pine Creek's expanding RNG portfolio, which turns methane, a potent greenhouse gas, into usable fuel. For Fiera, which reported about US$570 million in infrastructure debt assets under management, the deal fits its focus on mid-market infrastructure lending. Foundation Credit participated through its infrastructure debt strategy.

sources.title: Fiera Infrastructure Private Debt Closes Project Financing Agreement with Pine Creek Renewables

title: Leyline Renewable Capital provides up to $15 million debt facility to BESS Power for 2.4 GW US storage pipeline
target: BESS Power Corporation energy storage development pipeline
summary: BESS Power Corporation, a US developer of utility-scale battery storage, has set up a project debt facility of up to $15 million with Leyline Renewable Capital. The money will fund development of a targeted 2.4 GW of standalone storage projects across the US over the next four years.
details: The loan is described as non-dilutive, meaning BESS Power borrows the money rather than giving up ownership shares. It will support the flagship Lund Storage Center in Travis County, Texas, which has a confirmed power capacity of 407.55 MW and would serve the ERCOT grid, along with projects in Arizona, Tennessee, New Mexico and other states. BESS Power plans to spend the funds on project-related development costs for greenfield sites, meaning projects built from scratch on new land. The company says the portfolio would be operational by 2026.
context: BESS Power is a joint venture of Italian-listed Redelfi and Altea Green Power with US-based Elio Energy Group. Leyline specializes in early-stage development capital that lets developers advance projects before construction financing. The company claims Lund will be one of the largest standalone storage projects in Texas.

sources.title: BESS Power Corporation Secures Financing from Leyline Renewable Capital to Accelerate 2.4 GW of Energy Storage Pipeline in the U.S.

title: AEP completes $1.5bn sale of 1,365 MW contracted renewables portfolio to Invenergy-led IRG
summary: American Electric Power has finished selling its 1,365 MW portfolio of unregulated, contracted wind and solar projects in the US to IRG Acquisition Holdings, a partnership of Invenergy, CDPQ and Blackstone Infrastructure funds. The deal values the portfolio at $1.5 billion including project debt, and AEP says it receives about $1.2 billion in cash after taxes, fees and adjustments.
details: The portfolio has 14 projects totalling 1,200 MW of wind and 165 MW of solar spread across 11 US states. Unregulated means the assets sit outside AEP's rate-regulated utility business, and their power is sold under long-term contracts to other utilities, companies and municipalities. The sale agreement was signed in February 2023 and closed after approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, clearance by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States and antitrust approvals. J.P. Morgan was lead financial adviser and Citigroup Global Markets was financial adviser to AEP, with Hunton Andrews Kurth as its legal counsel.
context: AEP describes the sale as part of a plan to simplify and lower the risk of its business by concentrating on regulated operations. The company says it will use the proceeds to modernize its grid, rebalance its generation mix and strengthen its balance sheet, alongside planned investment of nearly $40 billion over five years in its regulated businesses.

sources.title: AEP COMPLETES SALE OF UNREGULATED RENEWABLES ASSETS

title: TDB Group provides securitization facility of up to $125M to d.light for off-grid solar in Tanzania

buyers.name: Eastern and Southern African Trade and Development Bank Group (TDB Group)

summary: Off-grid solar products company d.light secured a $30 million securitization facility from the TDB Group, a regional development bank, that can purchase up to $125 million of customer receivables in Tanzania. The money will expand d.light's pay-as-you-go financing for solar household products in the country.
details: Securitization here means d.light pools the expected payments from existing and future pay-as-you-go customers and uses them as the basis for raising funding. The facility, anchored by TDB, will run through a new vehicle called Brighter Life Tanzania 1 Limited, set up with lending partner African Frontier Capital. AFC describes the structure as off-balance sheet, meaning the financing sits outside d.light's own accounts, and says it finances receivables in local currency. Pay-Go customers buy solar lanterns and home systems in small installments over time.
context: d.light says it has now raised $490 million in securitized financing since 2020 and has used the model in Kenya for several years before bringing it to Tanzania. The company states it expects to extend the facility to other sub-Saharan African markets during 2023. The release cites World Bank figures that only about 40 percent of Tanzanians have electricity access.

sources.title: d.light closes USD$125M funding through a securitization facility to meet growing demand for off-grid solar products in Tanzania

title: Greater Commercial Lending arranges second $25 million USDA-guaranteed loan for Aemetis dairy biogas project in California
target: Aemetis Biogas Central Dairy Digester Project
summary: Greater Commercial Lending has completed a second $25 million loan, guaranteed by the USDA, for the Aemetis dairy biogas project in California. The money will pay for building biogas digesters at eight dairies in Stanislaus and Merced counties, bringing GCL's total financing for the project to $50 million.
details: Digesters are sealed tanks that capture methane from cow manure, and the gas is piped to a central plant that turns it into renewable natural gas used as a vehicle fuel. This second phase expands the network from seven operating dairy digesters to 15 dairies, which the company estimates will supply about 400,000 MMBtu of gas per year. The loan is guaranteed through the USDA Rural Energy for America Program, meaning the government backs repayment if the borrower defaults. Magnolia Bank of Elizabethtown, Kentucky provided the main funding, and the borrower is Aemetis Biogas 2, LLC, a wholly owned Aemetis subsidiary. The first $25 million loan, closed in October 2022, funded the initial phase including a 40-mile biogas pipeline.
context: Aemetis says the full project will eventually link digesters at more than 65 dairies and produce over 1,650,000 MMBtu of renewable natural gas a year. The company claims this will cut greenhouse gas emissions by about 6.8 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent over ten years. Both GCL and Aemetis say government-guaranteed loans were essential because such projects struggle to get conventional financing.

sources.title: Greater Commercial Lending Completes Additional $25 Million in USDA-Guaranteed Financing for Aemetis Dairy Digesters to Produce Renewable Natural Gas

title: Swift Current Energy closes $779 million financing for 800 MWdc Double Black Diamond Solar in Illinois

buyers.name: MUFG
buyers.role: coordinating lead arranger and joint bookrunner

buyers.name: Societe Generale
buyers.role: coordinating lead arranger and joint bookrunner

summary: Swift Current Energy has closed $779 million of project financing for its Double Black Diamond Solar project near Springfield, Illinois. The 800 MWdc (593 MWac) plant is under construction, with MUFG, Societe Generale and Truist leading the bank group.
details: The package combines $695 million of construction loans and tax equity bridge loans, which are short-term loans repaid once tax equity investors (who invest in exchange for tax credits) fund the project, plus an $84 million letter of credit facility. ING structured the debt as a green loan and Wilmington Trust serves as collateral and depositary agent. McCarthy Building Companies is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, and the project uses First Solar modules and Nextracker trackers. Constellation will buy part of the output and renewable energy certificates to serve customers including the City of Chicago, Cook County, CVS Health, Loyola University of Chicago, PPG, State Farm and TransUnion. Energization is scheduled for 2024.
context: Swift Current says the project will be the second largest single-phase solar project in the US and the largest in the MISO grid region, and calls the financing one of the largest ever for a US solar project. The company expects about $100 million in local tax revenue over the project life. Swift Current is majority owned by BAES Infrastructure, with IFM Net Zero Infrastructure Fund and Lookout Ridge Energy Partners as other owners.

sources.title: Swift Current Energy Secures $779 Million in Project Financing for American-Made Double Black Diamond Solar Project

title: Greenprint Capital provides tax equity for SMT Energy and SUSI Partners' 100 MW Texas battery portfolio

sellers.name: SUSI Partners
sellers.role: co-owner on behalf of SUSI Energy Transition Fund

target: 100 MW South Texas battery storage portfolio
summary: SMT Energy and its joint venture partner SUSI Partners, acting for the SUSI Energy Transition Fund, signed a tax equity financing deal with Greenprint Capital. The investment covers a co-owned portfolio of ten battery storage projects totalling 100 MW in South Texas. The size of the investment was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio is made up of ten utility-scale standalone battery projects, including a 10 MW facility in Mercedes, Texas, which sell into the ERCOT power market. SMT Energy developed the projects, managed construction and will oversee operations as minority owner. Tax equity means an investor puts money into a project in exchange for using its federal tax credits. Battery storage became eligible for the investment tax credit under the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act, and most of these projects qualify for a higher rate because they sit in so-called Energy Communities that historically relied on fossil fuels. All projects are expected to begin commercial operation in the coming months.
context: The companies say the investment shows confidence in the assets' ability to operate in ERCOT, where SMT Energy focuses on batteries with full merchant exposure, meaning revenue comes from market prices rather than fixed contracts. The deal illustrates how the Inflation Reduction Act has opened tax credit financing to standalone storage. SUSI Partners is a Swiss fund manager with EUR 1.9 billion in commitments, and Greenprint says it has deployed over USD 300 million since 2020.

sources.title: SMT Energy & SUSI Partners Secure Tax Equity Investment For Texas Battery Storage Portfolio

title: Matrix Renewables takes controlling stake in 200 MWac Pleasant Valley solar project in Idaho from rPlus Energies
summary: Matrix Renewables, a platform backed by TPG Rise, has bought a controlling interest in the Pleasant Valley Solar Project from developer rPlus Energies. The project in Idaho is sized at 200 MWac (261 MWdc). The price and exact stake were not disclosed.
details: The solar plant will feed power into the Idaho Power grid, the same network that serves Meta's new data center in Kuna, Idaho. Its output is covered by a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity, negotiated with Meta and Idaho Power under a special Energy Services Agreement that lets Meta access renewable power locally. Construction is scheduled to start in the third quarter of 2023. Matrix says it plans to finalize project financing in the coming months. The release gives the capacity both in AC terms (what reaches the grid) and DC terms (the panels' rated output).
context: The deal adds to Matrix's US portfolio, which the company says exceeds 6 GW across four regional power markets, within a global portfolio of about 13 GW. The project is linked to Meta's stated goal of supporting all its operations with renewable energy. rPlus, which says it has developed over 40 projects totaling more than 14 GW, will remain a partner in the project.

sources.title: Matrix Renewables announces acquisition of a controlling interest in 200 MWac / 261 MWdc Pleasant Valley Solar Project from rPlus Energies

title: Natixis CIB leads $1.5 billion sustainability-linked revolving credit facility for Invenergy Renewables Operating I

buyers.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: Mandated Lead Arranger and Sustainability Coordinator

buyers.name: Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A., New York Branch
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, New York Branch
Banco Santander, S.A., New York Branch

summary: Natixis CIB has closed a $1.5 billion sustainability-linked revolving credit facility for Invenergy Renewables Operating I LLC. The facility refinances and enlarges an existing $600 million working capital line to support Invenergy's project development pipeline.
details: A revolving credit facility is a corporate loan line the borrower can draw, repay and redraw as needed. The new facility replaces a $600 million working capital facility and was syndicated among existing and new banks, with Natixis CIB, Rabobank, Export Development Canada and Desjardins as mandated lead arrangers. Being sustainability-linked means the loan terms are tied to performance targets, here two indicators: growth in greenhouse gas emissions avoided by IROI's assets and a health and safety metric. Natixis CIB acted as sustainability coordinator, helping design these features.
context: Invenergy says the financing strengthens its ability to execute a large project portfolio during a period of rapid growth. Natixis CIB described the deal as part of a long relationship with Invenergy and its investors Blackstone and CDPQ, and said it should speed Invenergy's goal of expanding clean power in the US. Invenergy reports more than 30,000 MW of projects developed across wind, solar, storage, transmission and gas.

sources.title: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking leads financing for $1.5 billion sustainability-linked revolving credit facility for Invenergy Renewables Operating I LLC

title: MET Group buys 11.5 MWp ready-to-build Kentzlin solar project in Germany from Emeren

advisors.name: Capcora
advisors.role: exclusive sell-side M&A advisor to Emeren

summary: Emeren Group has sold an 11.5 MWp solar project in Kentzlin, Germany, to Swiss energy company MET Group. The project was sold at the ready-to-build stage, and MET Group will build and operate it. No price was disclosed.
details: The ground-mounted solar plant will sit in Kentzlin in the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Ready-to-build means the project has its permits and approvals in place so construction can begin. MET Group will handle construction and operation, with commercial operation expected in the second half of 2024. Capcora, a Frankfurt-based advisory firm, was Emeren's exclusive sell-side M&A adviser. The capacity is stated in MWp, meaning peak output of the solar panels.
context: This is the first project that Emeren's Berlin-based subsidiary has taken to ready-to-build stage since entering Germany in early 2021. For MET Group, the company says the deal supports its plan to enter the German renewables market and grow its renewables portfolio in Western Europe. Both parties said they expect to work together on further projects.

sources.title: Emeren Group Announces Sale of First RTB Solar Power Project in Germany

title: First Citizens Bank arranges $211 million financing for SunEnergy1's 200 MW Oak Solar project in North Carolina
summary: First Citizens Bank's Energy Finance group, part of its CIT division, acted as sole lead arranger on a $211 million financing for the 200 MW Oak Solar plant in Gaston, North Carolina. The project is being developed by SunEnergy1, based in Mooresville, North Carolina.
details: SunEnergy1 plans to build the solar plant in two phases. All of its electricity will be sold to McDonald's Corporation under a 17-year power purchase agreement, which is a long-term contract fixing who buys the power and on what terms. The financing combines a term loan (a loan repaid over a set period), a letter of credit (a bank guarantee of payment obligations) and a bridge loan (short-term funding until longer-term money is in place). As sole lead arranger, the bank organized the financing package.
context: SunEnergy1 presents the project as a further addition to North Carolina's clean energy infrastructure and says it will avoid carbon emissions and diversify the state's power supply. The deal also shows a large corporate buyer, McDonald's, securing renewable power through a long-term contract with a utility-scale solar developer.

sources.title: First Citizens Bank Serves as Lead Arranger on $211 Million Financing for North Carolina Solar Power Development

title: Corre Energy agrees to acquire 280 MW / 4.2 GWh compressed air storage project in West Texas from Contour Energy

buyers.name: Corre Energy US Development Company LLC

target: 280 MW / 4.2 GWh compressed air energy storage project in West Texas
summary: Corre Energy, through its US subsidiary, has signed an exclusive agreement to buy a 280 MW / 4.2 GWh compressed air energy storage project in West Texas from developer Contour Energy. It is the company's first project acquisition in the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: The project sits in the West Texas part of ERCOT, the main Texas grid, and is designed to deliver 280 MW for up to 15 hours. It uses compressed air energy storage, which stores power by pumping air into underground salt caverns when electricity is cheap and releasing it through turbines when demand is high. The project is at an early development stage and is targeted to reach final investment decision, the point when owners commit to build it, in 2025. The deal depends on confirmatory due diligence and is expected to close before the end of 2023. Funding is to be arranged alongside the company's wider fundraising.
context: Corre Energy says the deal supports its goal of having 1.3 GW of storage projects in construction by 2026 and follows an option agreement in Germany that it says doubled its European portfolio. The company points to the US Inflation Reduction Act as creating opportunities for growth and claims that reusing existing salt caverns will cut costs and construction time. It describes Texas as an attractive market for large-scale storage.

sources.title: Corre Energy to Acquire 280MW Energy Storage Project in West Texas

title: RockCreek invests in renewable hydrogen and SAF producer Raven SR

buyers.name: RockCreek
buyers.role: investor via Smart Aviation Futures fund

summary: Investment firm RockCreek has closed an investment of undisclosed size in Raven SR, a Wyoming-based company that turns biomass and waste into renewable hydrogen and sustainable aviation fuel. The money will help Raven SR move its fuels toward commercial production.
details: Raven SR uses a patented steam and carbon dioxide reforming process, which heats waste without burning it to make a hydrogen-rich gas that can be turned into hydrogen or synthetic liquid fuels. Its Richmond, California project was recently permitted as what the company calls the first biomass-to-renewable hydrogen project in the state. Hydrogen from that project is expected to be sold in the Bay Area from 2024 under agreements with Chevron New Energies and Hyzon Motors. The company plans to adapt the same technology to produce sustainable aviation fuel, a lower-carbon jet fuel, in 2025. The investment came from RockCreek's Smart Aviation Futures fund, which works with a major US airline.
context: RockCreek says the fund targets companies helping decarbonize aviation, supported by policies such as the US Inflation Reduction Act. Raven SR claims its process needs no fresh water and uses less than half the energy of electrolysis, and that its fuels can have low to negative carbon intensity. The company says the funding will support expansion of its global business model.

sources.title: RockCreek Invests in Raven SR, Producer of Renewable Transportation Fuels

title: Seraya-backed Cyan Renewables acquires Belgian offshore wind service vessel Groenewind
summary: Cyan Renewables, an offshore wind vessel services company owned by Singapore infrastructure manager Seraya Partners, has bought full ownership of Groenewind, a service operations vessel working for offshore wind farms in Belgium. The price and seller were not disclosed. It is Cyan's first acquisition in Europe.
details: Groenewind is a two-year-old service operations vessel, a ship that houses and transfers technicians who maintain offshore wind turbines. Built in 2021, it is described as the first twin-hulled vessel of its type with DP2 dynamic positioning, a system that keeps the ship in place in rough seas. It carries a motion-compensated gangway, a walkway that stays steady so crew can step onto turbines, and has room for 24 crew and technicians. The vessel works under a 17-year contract servicing Belgian offshore wind farms.
context: Cyan was created by Seraya in 2022 to serve growing demand for offshore wind vessels in Asia, and it plans to buy or build several vessel types over five years. Cyan says it aims to operate a fleet worth about US$1 billion in Asia and Europe within three years. Seraya says long-term contracted vessels, often with inflation pass-through terms, suit infrastructure investors. Cyan is Seraya's third energy transition and digital infrastructure platform.

sources.title: Seraya Partners' Offshore Wind Services Platform Acquires State-of-Art Service Operations Vessel in Belgium

title: Cyan Renewables acquires Groenewind offshore wind service vessel in Belgium
summary: Cyan Renewables, an offshore wind vessel services company owned by Singapore infrastructure manager Seraya Partners, has bought full ownership of Groenewind, a service operations vessel working at offshore wind farms in Belgium. The price and seller were not disclosed.
details: Groenewind is a service operations vessel, a ship that houses and transfers technicians who maintain offshore wind turbines. It was completed in 2021 and is described as the first twin-hulled vessel of its type with DP2 dynamic positioning, a system that keeps the ship steady in place using thrusters. It carries a motion-compensated gangway for walking onto turbines, a smaller daughter craft, and room for 24 crew and technicians. The vessel works under a 17-year contract servicing Belgian offshore wind farms.
context: The deal is Cyan's first acquisition anywhere and its first in Europe, under a plan to build or buy service, cable-lay, turbine installation and foundation installation vessels over five years. Cyan says it aims to run a US$1 billion fleet across Asia and Europe within three years. Seraya argues that long-term vessel contracts, often with inflation protection, make these ships attractive core infrastructure for its investors. Cyan was set up by Seraya in 2022 and is its third energy transition and digital infrastructure platform.

sources.title: Seraya Partners' Offshore Wind Services Platform Acquires State-of-Art Service Operations Vessel in Belgium

title: Fortescue Future Industries to acquire Nikola's Phoenix Hydrogen Hub project in Arizona
summary: Fortescue Future Industries (FFI) has agreed to buy the Phoenix Hydrogen Hub project from truck maker Nikola. The project is a planned green hydrogen production plant using electrolysis in Buckeye, Arizona. No price or capacity was disclosed.
details: The hub is designed to make green hydrogen by splitting water with electricity (electrolysis) and is planned to be built in phases as demand grows. It is in the final stages of permitting, and orders for equipment with long delivery times are underway. FFI is expected to provide the capital needed to fully develop it, and the parties say first hydrogen production is targeted for around the middle of the decade. The two companies are also negotiating a hydrogen supply agreement to fuel Nikola's heavy-duty fuel cell trucks.
context: The deal is the first project to come out of a January 2023 memorandum of understanding between the two companies to jointly evaluate large US green hydrogen plants. Nikola describes the sale as part of a capital-light strategy that relies on partners to build hydrogen supply. The companies expect the project to benefit from the federal hydrogen production tax credit under the Inflation Reduction Act and from state incentives such as California's Low Carbon Fuel Standard.

sources.title: NIKOLA AND FORTESCUE FUTURE INDUSTRIES COMMIT TO CREATING AMERICAN GREEN ENERGY JOBS WITH ACQUISITION OF NIKOLA'S PHOENIX HYDROGEN HUB

title: Globeleq agrees to buy 75% of 41 MW Mocuba solar plant in Mozambique from Scatec and KLP Norfund
summary: Globeleq has agreed to acquire Scatec's 52.5% stake and KLP Norfund Investments' 22.5% stake in the 41 MW Mocuba solar plant in central Mozambique. After completion Globeleq will own 75% and manage the plant, with national utility EDM keeping 25%. No price was disclosed.
details: The plant sits on 126 hectares about 13 km from Mocuba city in Zambezia province. It reached financial close, the point when funding is fully committed, in March 2018 and finished construction in August 2019. EDM buys the output under a 25-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity, and supplies it to the national grid. The International Finance Corporation and the Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund are the project's lenders. The deal needs regulatory and lender approval and is expected to close in the first half of 2024.
