context: The purchase adds an operating asset to Globeleq's Mozambique business, where it is commissioning a 19 MW solar and 7 MWh storage project at Cuamba, building a 450 MW gas plant at Temane and developing a 120 MW wind project at Namaacha. The company says its African solar portfolio will approach 400 MW across four countries once this deal and Cuamba are complete. Globeleq is owned by British International Investment and Norfund.

sources.title: GLOBELEQ TO ACQUIRE THE MOZAMBICAN MOCUBA SOLAR PV PLANT FROM SCATEC

title: First Citizens Bank leads $70.4 million loan for two Jupiter Power battery storage projects in Texas
target: Two standalone battery storage projects in Texas
summary: Jupiter Power has closed a $70.4 million construction and term loan facility for two standalone battery storage projects in Texas. The projects total 160 MW of power and 320 MWh of storage. First Citizens Bank's Energy Finance group led the financing.
details: The two projects are standalone batteries, meaning they are not paired with a solar or wind plant, and together offer about two hours of storage at full output. The facility combines a construction loan, which funds building the projects, with a term loan, which carries the debt after they begin operating. First Citizens Bank, through the Energy Finance group of its CIT division, acted as coordinating lead arranger, while BankUnited and Siemens Financial Services joined as joint lead arrangers. The release does not give construction or operation dates.
context: Jupiter Power, based in Austin and Chicago, says it has 655 MWh of storage operating, 740 MWh under construction and more than 11,000 MW in development across the US. Its CEO described storage as increasingly important for grid reliability as demand for firm power grows. The deal adds to First Citizens' activity in lending to battery storage projects.

sources.title: From Jupiter Power:  First Citizens Bank Serves as Lead Arranger on $70.4 Million in Financing for Two Texas Battery Storage Projects

title: Ryse Energy acquires US micro wind turbine maker Primus Wind Power
summary: Ryse Energy, a maker of small wind turbines and hybrid renewable systems, has bought Primus Wind Power, a US manufacturer of micro wind turbines. The price and the seller of the company were not disclosed.
details: Primus Wind Power makes the AIR line of micro wind turbines, which the release says has sold more than 180,000 units worldwide since 1995. The turbines carry CSA certification to UL and CSA standards and are used in marine, telecoms, military and residential settings. Ryse Energy plans to use the deal to set up manufacturing in the United States. No financial terms, advisers or seller details were given.
context: Ryse Energy says the purchase makes it the most diverse small wind turbine technology company globally and speeds up its growth in North America. The company expects the AIR turbines to broaden its hybrid offerings, which combine wind with solar and batteries for off-grid users such as telecoms and oil and gas sites. This is a manufacturing company acquisition rather than a power project deal.

sources.title: Ryse Energy Acquires US-based Micro Wind Turbine Manufacturer Primus Wind Power

title: DESRI closes construction financing for 200 MWac San Juan 1 solar and storage project in New Mexico
summary: D. E. Shaw Renewable Investments (DESRI) reached financial close on construction loans for its San Juan 1 project in San Juan County, New Mexico, and began building it. The project pairs 200 MWac of solar with 100 MWac of battery storage. A lender group led by Société Générale provided the financing, with no amount disclosed.
details: San Juan 1 sits next to the former San Juan Generating Station, a coal plant retired in 2022, and will reuse that plant's grid connection. It is the first phase of a larger development that DESRI expects to reach 400 MWac. Financial close means the loan agreements are signed and money can be drawn. The output is sold to Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM) under a 20-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy the electricity. SOLV Energy is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor for the solar and battery parts and will handle operations and maintenance, while EPC Services Company builds the transmission tie-line and substation, with operations expected to start in mid-2024.
context: The project is intended to replace capacity lost when the San Juan coal plant closed, and PNM says it supports its goal of emissions-free generation by 2040. It is DESRI's third project in New Mexico. Photosol USA originally developed the project and sold it to DESRI in 2022. DESRI says the facility should supply power equal to about 52,400 homes a year.

sources.title: D. E. Shaw Renewable Investments Announces Close of Financing and Start of Construction for 200MWac San Juan Solar and Storage Project in New Mexico

title: TransAlta agrees to buy out minority shareholders of TransAlta Renewables

sellers.name: Public shareholders of TransAlta Renewables Inc.

advisors.name: National Bank Financial Inc.
advisors.role: financial advisor and formal valuator to RNW Special Committee

advisors.name: TD Securities Inc.
advisors.role: financial advisor to RNW Special Committee

advisors.name: Stikeman Elliott LLP
advisors.role: legal advisor to RNW Special Committee

summary: TransAlta Corporation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire the roughly 39.9% of TransAlta Renewables (RNW) it does not already own. The consideration is valued at about C$1.38 billion, of which C$800 million is cash, and adds economic interest in 1,187 MW of generating capacity across Canada, the US and Australia.
details: RNW shareholders can choose either 1.0337 TransAlta shares or C$13.00 in cash per share, subject to pro-rationing capped at 46,441,779 new TransAlta shares and C$800 million of cash. The price is an 18.3% premium to RNW's closing price on July 10, 2023. RNW holds interests in 2,965 MW, including 26 wind farms, 11 hydro plants, two solar facilities, one battery storage project, eight natural gas plants and a gas pipeline. The deal is a court-approved plan of arrangement under Canadian corporate law and needs two-thirds approval of RNW votes plus a majority of votes from shareholders not linked to TransAlta. TransAlta would receive a C$95.4 million break fee in certain termination cases, the RNW shareholder meeting is expected around September 26, 2023, and closing is targeted for early in the fourth quarter of 2023.
context: The companies say merging into one listed entity will simplify governance, increase trading liquidity and let all growth be funded through a single company. RNW's chair said the deal addresses risks to RNW's dividend from expiring contracts and rising cash taxes. TransAlta claims the deal will add to free cash flow and have a neutral effect on its credit rating, and that it raises the share of its earnings from contracted rather than merchant (market-price) sales.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation to Acquire TransAlta Renewables Inc. to Simplify Structure and Enhance Strategic Position

title: Energix closes $520 million debt and tax equity financing for six US solar projects

buyers.name: Santander Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: sole underwriter, structuring bank and lead lender

target: Six utility-scale solar projects in Virginia and Pennsylvania
summary: Energix Renewables has closed two financing transactions totaling $520 million for six utility-scale solar projects in Virginia and Pennsylvania. Santander CIB arranged $260 million of construction and term debt, and Morgan Stanley Renewables committed $260 million of tax equity. The portfolio totals 416 MWdc.
details: The debt package from a lender group led by Santander CIB covers construction and a longer-term loan, and includes a tax equity bridge loan, which is short-term funding repaid once the tax equity investor pays in. Tax equity means an investor funds part of the project in return for the federal tax benefits it generates. Morgan Stanley's commitment is $260 million but could rise depending on how much investment tax credit the projects qualify for. The portfolio includes the Adams Solar project, which the company says will supply 22 percent of the City of Philadelphia's municipal electricity use. The projects use First Solar panels.
context: This is Energix's third tax equity deal with Morgan Stanley, after earlier deals in 2020 and 2021 covering eight Virginia projects of about 200 MWdc, and its first US financing with Santander CIB, which already works with it in Poland. Energix says the deal brings its US investment close to $1 billion. The company owns nine facilities totaling 224 MWdc and expects to reach 640 MWdc of operating projects by the end of 2023.

sources.title: Energix Closes $520 Million Financing and Tax Equity Deal to Fund New Solar Projects

title: Matrix Renewables acquires 284 MWdc Stillhouse solar project in Texas from OCI Solar Power
summary: Matrix Renewables, a renewable energy platform backed by TPG Rise, has bought the Stillhouse Solar Project from developer OCI Solar Power. The project is a late-stage 284 MWdc solar development in Bell County, Texas. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Stillhouse is located in the northern part of the ERCOT grid, the system that serves most of Texas. Its capacity is given in MWdc, meaning the direct-current rating of the solar panels. OCI says land acquisition, environmental review and grid connection studies are all finished after more than two years of development work. Matrix plans to arrange a power sales contract, equipment purchasing and financing in the coming months. Construction is scheduled for 2024, with commercial operation expected in 2025.
context: The purchase comes shortly after Matrix brought its Gaskell West solar and storage project in California into commercial operation. Matrix says it owns close to 6 GW of projects at various stages across four US power regions and more than 12 GW globally, including Spain, Italy and Chile. The company presents the deal as part of its plan to grow into a major clean energy platform in the US.

sources.title: MATRIX RENEWABLES ANNOUNCES ACQUISITION OF STILLHOUSE SOLAR PROJECT FROM OCI SOLAR POWER

title: Leyline Renewable Capital provides development loan to RAI Energy for western US solar and storage pipeline
target: RAI Energy utility-scale solar and solar-plus-storage development portfolio

advisors.name: Holland & Knight
advisors.role: legal adviser to Leyline Renewable Capital

summary: Leyline Renewable Capital has extended a project development loan to RAI Energy, a developer focused on the western United States. The money will support several large utility-scale solar and solar-plus-storage projects in the WECC grid region over the next four years. The loan amount was not disclosed.
details: A development loan funds the early, pre-construction work on projects, such as permitting, land and grid studies, before conventional construction financing is available. The projects sit in the Western Electricity Coordinating Council area, which covers the grid in the western US. Holland & Knight advised Leyline, while Orrick provided legal advice and KeyBanc Capital Markets acted as financial adviser to RAI Energy. No loan size, project capacities or timing of individual projects were given.
context: RAI Energy says it has developed more than 750 MW of solar and storage, including a 150 MW / 600 MWh hybrid solar and battery plant under construction, and aims to build a 4 GW portfolio by 2027. The developer says the financing will help it grow its team and portfolio. Leyline argues that utility-scale projects are becoming harder to complete, and its model lets developers scale without giving up ownership.

sources.title: Leyline Renewable Capital Provides Financing to RAI Energy to Develop Large Scale Renewable Energy Project Portfolio

title: SKF signs 15-year virtual PPA with Enel for Spanish solar project
summary: Swedish bearing maker SKF has signed a 15-year virtual power purchase agreement with Enel tied to an upcoming Enel solar plant in Spain. The volume is said to match the electricity used by about one third of SKF's European operations in 2022.
details: A virtual power purchase agreement is a financial contract in which a buyer supports a renewable project and receives its green attributes without taking physical delivery of the power. Under this deal SKF will buy guarantees of origin, which are certificates proving electricity came from renewable sources, for 15 years. The Spanish solar plant is expected to generate more than 260 GWh per year and to be connected to the grid by August 2024. Installed capacity and financial terms were not disclosed.
context: SKF says the deal advances its goal of using 100% renewable electricity by 2030 under its RE100 membership. The company also has science-based targets to cut scope 1 and 2 emissions by 95% by 2030 from 2019 levels and reach net zero by 2050. It claims the agreement helps add new renewable capacity in Europe.

sources.title: SKF signs Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA) to support renewable energy in Europe

title: Idemitsu Renewables signs PPA with Sonoma Clean Power for Azalea solar-plus-storage project
target: Azalea solar and battery storage project
summary: Idemitsu Renewables has signed a long-term power purchase agreement with Sonoma Clean Power, a community electricity provider in California. The deal covers power, storage capacity and related attributes from the Azalea project in Kern County, which pairs 84 MWp of solar with a 38 MW / 152 MWh battery.
details: A power purchase agreement is a contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project over many years. Azalea combines an 84 MWp solar plant, where MWp refers to peak panel output, with a 38 MW battery that can store 152 MWh, meaning roughly four hours of discharge at full power. The project is located in Kern County, California and is expected to start commercial operation in 2025. The release does not give the contract length, price or financing details.
context: Sonoma Clean Power is a Community Choice Aggregator, a local public body that buys power on behalf of residents in Sonoma and Mendocino counties. It says the project will help it keep its supply more than 50% renewable at competitive prices and add reliability through battery storage. Idemitsu Renewables, the US subsidiary of Japan's Idemitsu Kosan, describes the contract as a significant addition to its portfolio.

sources.title: Idemitsu Renewables Executes Power Purchase Agreement with Sonoma Clean Power

title: New Energy Capital provides $40 million growth equity to battery storage developer Granite Source Power
summary: New Energy Capital has closed an equity partnership with Granite Source Power, a New Hampshire-based developer of utility-scale renewable and battery storage projects. The headline puts the strategic growth capital at $40 million, to fund further development in the developer's core markets.
details: Granite Source Power was founded in 2022 and develops greenfield projects, meaning new projects built from scratch rather than acquired. The company says it has built a development pipeline of about 3 GW so far. It is also marketing a 2 GW portfolio of stand-alone battery storage projects for sale with the help of Marathon Capital. The release does not disclose the size of the stake New Energy Capital receives or other deal terms.
context: The deal gives an early-stage developer capital to advance its pipeline, while New Energy Capital, an alternative asset manager owned within Victory Capital, adds a development platform to a portfolio it says exceeds $1.5 billion across more than 40 investments. The developer's founders previously worked at a large global independent power producer and claim experience with more than 10 GW of projects and over $10 billion of financings.

sources.title: NH-Based Battery Storage Developer Granite Source Power Secures $40M In Strategic Growth Capital from New Energy Capital

title: Nexus Renewables closes four financings totaling over US$40 million for California battery project and pipeline
target: 10MW/40MWh battery energy storage system in Fairfield, California
summary: Toronto-based developer Nexus Renewables closed four financings at the same time, which it says total more than US$40 million. The money will build a 10 MW / 40 MWh battery storage project in Fairfield, California and fund development of the rest of its portfolio.
details: The package includes a US$13.3 million senior secured loan led by Aiga Capital Partners, a US$14.5 million project-level loan led by Synovus Bank, a CAD5.0 million commitment for privately placed preferred shares, and a US$10.8 million tax equity commitment led by Greenprint Capital. The Synovus loan covers construction and then converts to a longer-term loan, and it also bridges the tax equity, meaning it fronts cash until the tax investor pays in. Tax equity is investment from a party that receives the project's tax credits, here investment tax credits available under the Inflation Reduction Act. The four-hour battery in Fairfield, Solano County, is headed into construction, and the wider portfolio includes a 300 MW / 600 MWh battery project near Houston, Texas. Aiga says its facility can grow as the value of Nexus' collateral rises.
context: Nexus describes the deal as marking its shift from a pure developer to an independent power producer, a company that owns and operates its plants and sells their power. The company says the financings show it can raise project money under its own name and give a repeatable model for future projects. The tax equity piece reflects how the Inflation Reduction Act made standalone storage eligible for investment tax credits.

sources.title: Nexus Renewables closes multiple financings totaling over USD40 Million

title: Fiera Infrastructure and Palisade complete acquisition of Amp US community solar and storage platform from Amp Energy
target: Amp US Primary Holdings Inc. (renamed PureSky Energy Inc.)
summary: A consortium of funds managed by Fiera Infrastructure and Palisade Infrastructure Group has completed the purchase of all equity in Amp US from Canada-based Amp Energy. Amp US, a Denver-based community solar and storage business with about 200 MW DC across 39 projects, will now operate as PureSky Energy. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio comprises 39 community solar and storage projects that are either operating or under construction, totalling roughly 200 MW of DC capacity (measured at the solar panels, before conversion to grid power). Community solar means projects whose output is shared by many local subscribers, such as households, rather than serving a single site. The business also has a development pipeline, including a recently acquired 22 MW DC portfolio in New York. Macquarie Capital and DLA Piper advised the buyers, while KeyBanc Capital Markets and Milbank advised Amp Energy.
context: The buyers say they plan to back PureSky in expanding beyond its current markets and serving low-to-moderate income households and housing authorities. The sale marks an exit for Amp Energy from its US platform, which it built since 2016 with backing from Carlyle. The companies expect the existing portfolio to avoid about 171,000 tonnes of CO2 per year by 2024.

sources.title: Fiera Infrastructure and Palisade Infrastructure Group complete the acquisition of Amp US, a Leading Renewable Energy and Battery Storage Platform

title: Emeren agrees to sell 29 MW Henan rooftop solar portfolio to CNNP Rich Energy
target: Portfolio of 6 rooftop distributed generation solar projects in Henan province
summary: Emeren Group, a solar developer listed in New York, has signed an agreement to sell six rooftop solar projects in Henan province, China, to CNNP Rich Energy. The portfolio totals 29 MW. No price was disclosed.
details: The assets are rooftop distributed generation projects, meaning solar panels installed on buildings that supply power close to where it is used rather than from a large central plant. All six projects are located in Henan province. The release describes the deal as an agreement to sell and does not give a price, a closing date or the names of any advisers. The buyer is the clean energy development, construction and operation arm of China National Nuclear Power Company.
context: Emeren says the sale fits a new China strategy that concentrates on five coastal provinces it views as having attractive power prices and strong economies. The company also says the proceeds will strengthen its balance sheet. For CNNP Rich Energy, the purchase adds to its portfolio of non-nuclear clean energy assets.

sources.title: Emeren Group Announces Sale of 29 MW of China Rooftop DG Projects

title: AES acquires 2 GW Bellefield solar-plus-storage project in California from Avantus
summary: AES has acquired the Bellefield project in Kern County, California, from developer Avantus. The 2 GW late-stage solar-plus-storage project is described by AES as the largest permitted project of its kind in the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: Bellefield is split into two phases, each combining 500 MW of solar panels with up to 500 MW of batteries that can discharge for four hours. Phase one already has a 15-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to sell electricity, with an existing AES corporate customer to supply hourly carbon-free power. AES expects to sign contracts for phase two, up to another 1 GW, by the end of 2023. The phases are expected to start operating in 2025 and 2026. The project is in late-stage development, meaning permits are in place but construction has not been completed.
context: AES says the deal strengthens its business of supplying renewable power to corporate buyers under long-term contracts and grows its signed contract backlog to more than 12 GW. The company also links the project to California's goal of 100% carbon-free electricity by 2045. Canadian investor AIMCo holds a 25% stake in the growth projects of AES's US clean energy business.

sources.title: AES Acquires Largest Permitted Solar-Plus-Storage Project in the United States

title: Oort Energy closes £5M seed round led by Energy Revolution Ventures for PEM electrolysers
summary: UK electrolyser developer Oort Energy has closed a £5 million seed funding round led by venture investor Energy Revolution Ventures. TRIREC, an Asia-based decarbonisation fund, and an unnamed corporate strategic investor also took part.
details: An electrolyser is a machine that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity, and Oort builds the PEM type, which uses a polymer membrane. The round was raised in two equal tranches, the first used to build the team and launch a stack manufacturing facility, the second bringing in a strategic investor to help with supply chain and large-scale manufacturing. The funding adds to about £800,000 in non-dilutive grants, meaning money that does not require giving up ownership, from UK and EU public bodies. The company has designed a 250 kW stack platform and plans to commission its first containerised demonstrator at a customer site in Q3 2023.
context: The company says its redesigned stack lowers the cost of producing green hydrogen, which could help decarbonise sectors such as fertiliser, steel and shipping. Oort plans to launch 250 kW and 1 MW commercial systems in 2023, and describes the round as oversubscribed.

sources.title: Oort Energy Secures £5M Seed Funding to Decarbonise Industry with Green Hydrogen

title: Oort Energy closes £5M seed round led by Energy Revolution Ventures
summary: UK electrolyser developer Oort Energy has closed a £5 million seed funding round led by venture investor Energy Revolution Ventures. Asian decarbonisation fund TRIREC and an unnamed corporate strategic investor also took part.
details: The round was raised in two equal tranches. The first paid for team building and the launch of a manufacturing facility, and the second brought in a strategic investor expected to help with supply chains and large-scale production. The money will fund an electrolyser stack factory and a first demonstrator unit, which uses renewable electricity to split water into hydrogen. Oort says it has designed a 250 kW stack platform and plans commissioning at a customer site in Q3 2023. The equity adds to about £800,000 in grants from UK and EU public bodies, which do not dilute existing shareholders.
context: Oort claims its PEM (polymer electrolyte membrane) electrolyser design lowers the cost of producing green hydrogen. The company plans to launch 250 kW and 1 MW commercial systems in 2023, and its lead investor says the technology could help decarbonise sectors such as fertiliser, steel and shipping.

sources.title: Oort Energy Secures £5M Seed Funding to Decarbonise Industry with Green Hydrogen

title: DSI acquires solar and commercial fencing contractor Fortress Fencing

sellers.name: Jason Truesdale
sellers.role: founder and president of Fortress Fencing

summary: North Carolina renewable energy contractor DSI has bought Fortress Fencing, a company that builds security fencing for utility-scale solar farms and commercial sites. Fortress becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of DSI. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Fortress Fencing, founded in 2001 and based in Carrboro, North Carolina, has built solar farm fencing in 32 states and says it will pass four million linear feet of fence built in 2023. It will keep its current leadership, including founder Jason Truesdale, and operate as a subsidiary owned entirely by DSI. DSI, headquartered in Hope Mills with offices in Wilmington, provides construction, operations and maintenance services for utility-scale solar and electrical work. DSI is backed by investment firm Rising Point Capital. No price or advisers were named.
context: DSI says the purchase adds perimeter security to its turn-key offering, meaning it aims to deliver complete services for solar projects from a single provider. Rising Point Capital describes the deal as part of its plan to spread DSI across more steps of the utility-scale solar value chain. Fortress says DSI's resources will help it scale to meet growing national demand.

sources.title: DSI, a prominent national renewable energy solutions provider acquires Fortress Fencing, the leader in utility-scale solar & commercial fencing

title: Cordelio Power closes construction loan and tax equity for 171 MW Moraine Sands wind project in Illinois
summary: Cordelio Power has closed a $301 million construction loan and a $157 million tax equity commitment for its 171 MW Moraine Sands wind project in Mason County, Illinois. Microsoft will buy all of the project's power under a long-term contract.
details: The construction loan comes from affiliates of MUFG, National Bank of Canada, Bank of Montreal and Export Development Canada, and part of it will convert into a longer-term loan once the wind farm starts commercial operation. JPMorgan Chase is providing the tax equity, meaning it invests in exchange for the project's US tax benefits, and its money will be paid in when the project begins operating. The offtake is a long-term agreement with Microsoft covering 100% of output, though its exact length is not stated. Cordelio expects to finish construction later in 2023.
context: The project is Cordelio's second in Mason County. Cordelio, which is wholly owned by Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, says it operates more than 1,200 MW of renewable assets in Canada and the US and has a pipeline of over 18,000 MW of US wind, solar and storage projects. The deal marks a new relationship with JPMorgan, according to the company.

sources.title: Cordelio Power Completes Financing for Moraine Sands Wind Project

title: PSEG sells 25% stake in 1,100 MW Ocean Wind 1 offshore wind project to Ørsted North America
summary: Public Service Enterprise Group has completed the sale of its 25% equity interest in the 1,100 MW Ocean Wind 1 offshore wind project to Ørsted North America. Ørsted now owns the entire project, which is New Jersey's first offshore wind farm.
details: Under the agreement, Ørsted North America repaid PSEG for all the money PSEG had spent on the project to date. The release does not state a separate purchase price. PSEG has also signed a limited transition services agreement, meaning it will keep supplying certain support for a period, covering construction management and environmental permitting for the onshore substations and the installation of transmission cables.
context: The sale leaves Ørsted as sole owner of Ocean Wind 1 and ends PSEG's equity role in the project. PSEG describes itself as a mainly regulated infrastructure company, and the deal lets it recover its investment while still contributing services to the onshore part of the build.

sources.title: PSEG Completes Sale of its 25% Equity Interest in Ocean Wind 1 to Ørsted N.A.

title: Canadian Solar sells 100 MWp Azuma Kofuji solar plant in Japan to Mizuho-arranged investors

buyers.name: Mizuho Fund (Japanese investors arranged by Mizuho Securities)

summary: Canadian Solar, through its development arm Recurrent Energy, has completed the sale of the 100 MWp Azuma Kofuji solar plant in Fukushima prefecture, Japan. The buyers are Japanese investors brought together by Mizuho Securities. No price was disclosed.
details: The plant began commercial operation in the third quarter of 2022 and uses Canadian Solar HiKu modules. Its output is bought by Tohoku Electric Power Company at JPY36 per kWh under Japan's feed-in tariff, a government scheme that guarantees a fixed price for renewable power, for the remaining 18 years of the contract. A local Recurrent Energy subsidiary will keep running operations and maintenance for the plant after the sale. Canadian Solar expects to book the revenue from the deal in the second quarter of 2023.
context: The project is described by the company as its largest in Japan and the largest operating solar plant in Fukushima prefecture, built on former abandoned farmland and under development since 2014. Canadian Solar says the sale lets it turn the asset into cash while keeping long-term service income, and it states it plans to grow this operations business. The company says the plant produces nearly 110 GWh a year.

sources.title: Canadian Solar's Recurrent Energy Executes Sale of 100 MWp Solar Power Plant in Japan

title: SOLEK closes US$379 million debt package for Chilean solar portfolio

buyers.name: BCI
buyers.role: agent and lender on local facilities

buyers.name: Scotiabank Chile
buyers.role: agent and lender on local facilities

summary: Czech solar group SOLEK has closed a US$379 million financing for its portfolio of solar plants in central Chile. The portfolio, which SOLEK says totals about 284 MWdc, includes both utility-scale plants and PMGD plants, a Chilean category of small distributed generators.
details: The package is made up of a US$178 million senior private placement of 20-year amortizing bonds (repaid gradually over the life of the debt) sold in the US private placement market, a US$75 million mezzanine loan (debt ranking below senior debt), a US$55 million PMGD bridge loan, a US$37 million utility-scale bridge loan, a US$19 million letter of credit facility and a US$15 million line to cover value added tax. BNP Paribas and Natixis New York Branch acted as placement agents, arrangers and lenders, while BCI and Scotiabank Chile were agents and lenders on the local facilities. White & Case and Guerrero Olivos advised SOLEK as international and local legal counsel. Bond proceeds are to be used mainly for expansion and to refinance existing debt.
context: The deal marks SOLEK's first issuance in the US private placement market, a large bond market whose investors include major funds and insurers, and the company says demand from investors was strong. SOLEK reports more than 38 Chilean projects to be built in 2023 and 2024 and targets 400 MW installed worldwide by end of 2023 and 2 GW by end of 2027.

sources.title: SOLEK closes a USD379 million financing for its portfolio of PV projects in Chile

title: Leyline Renewable Capital provides development loans to Westbridge Renewable for Alberta solar pipeline
target: Alberta solar project portfolio (Georgetown, Sunnynook, Dolcy, Eastervale and Red Willow)
summary: Westbridge Renewable Energy has signed two loan agreements with lending entities set up by Leyline Renewable Capital. One loan of up to the US dollar equivalent of CAD 30.45 million covers grid connection security payments for five Alberta solar projects, and a second loan of up to US$4.9 million funds further development.
details: The larger loan, made to a wholly owned Westbridge holding subsidiary, can be used to post Generating Unit Owners Contribution security, a deposit the Alberta grid operator AESO requires from projects seeking a grid connection. It is backed by a first priority claim on the projects, meaning the lender is repaid first if the borrower defaults. The separate development loan of up to US$4.9 million has second ranking security and supports advancing the five projects and originating new solar and battery storage projects. Both loans were signed on May 30, 2023 and mature 18 months later. The projects are Georgetown, Sunnynook, Dolcy, Eastervale and Red Willow, held by Westbridge subsidiaries.
context: The deal extends an existing relationship between Westbridge and Leyline, which specialises in lending to renewable projects at early development stages. Westbridge says the funding strengthens its financial position for its Alberta portfolio. Leyline describes its model as helping developers grow without issuing new shares that would dilute owners.

sources.title: Westbridge Renewable Secures Financing to Complete its Interconnection Deposits for its Alberta Portfolio and Project Development
