buyers.role: agent and lender on local facilities

buyers.name: Scotiabank Chile
buyers.role: agent and lender on local facilities

target: SOLEK solar PV portfolio in Chile (utility-scale and PMGD plants)
summary: Czech solar group SOLEK has closed a US$379 million financing package for its Chilean solar portfolio. The portfolio includes utility-scale and small distributed (PMGD) plants in Chile's Central Region, with SOLEK owning about 284 MWdc in the country.
details: The package combines a US$178 million senior private placement, a US$75 million mezzanine loan (debt ranking below senior debt), a US$55 million PMGD bridge loan, a US$37 million utility-scale bridge loan, a US$19 million letter of credit facility and a US$15 million VAT line, which covers value-added tax paid during construction. The private placement is a 20-year amortizing bond, meaning it is repaid gradually, sold in the US Private Placement market where large funds and insurers buy debt directly. BNP Paribas and Natixis New York Branch acted as placement agents, arrangers and lenders, while BCI and Scotiabank Chile were agents and lenders on local facilities. White & Case and Guerrero Olivos advised SOLEK as international and local legal counsel. Proceeds will mainly fund expansion and refinance existing debt.
context: The deal marks SOLEK's first entry into the US private bond market, which the company says saw strong investor demand and gives it more flexible access to future funding. SOLEK says it has over 38 projects to build in Chile in 2023 and 2024 and targets 400 MW installed worldwide by end of 2023 and 2 GW by end of 2027.

sources.title: SOLEK closes a USD379 million financing for its portfolio of PV projects in Chile

title: Emeren sells 58 MW Polish solar portfolio to GoldenPeaks Capital's Spectris Energy
target: 58 MW solar portfolio in Pomorskie Voivodeship, Poland
summary: Emeren Group has completed the sale of a 58 MW portfolio of solar projects in Poland to Spectris Energy, a wholly owned subsidiary of GoldenPeaks Capital. The price was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of several solar farms in the Pomorskie region of northern Poland. The projects were sold at the ready-to-build stage, meaning permits and development work are done and construction can begin. Spectris Energy plans to build the farms and keep them as long-term owned assets. No financial terms or advisers were disclosed.
context: Emeren, a NYSE-listed solar developer with a pipeline it puts at about 3 GW, says the deal extends its track record of selling projects in Europe and strengthens its position in Poland. Spectris Energy says the acquisition fits its strategy of developing and operating renewable projects across Europe. GoldenPeaks Capital says it has completed over 6,000 MW of capacity through its subsidiaries.

sources.title: Emeren Group Completed Sale of 58 MW of Solar Projects in Poland

title: Natixis CIB arranges US$364 million financing for Solek's 284 MWdc Chile solar portfolio

buyers.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: lead arranger, structuring advisor and placement agent

buyers.name: BNP Paribas
buyers.role: co-global coordinator placement agent for private placement

target: Solek Chile solar PV portfolio (PMGD and utility-scale)
summary: Natixis CIB has closed a US$364 million financing package for a portfolio of solar plants in Chile owned and operated by Solek Holding SE. The portfolio totals about 284 MWdc of capacity.
details: The portfolio includes 190 MWdc of small distributed solar projects under Chile's PMGD regime, which lets them sell power at a regulated stabilized price, plus one 94 MWdc utility-scale solar plant. The package combines a US$75 million mezzanine facility (debt ranking below senior loans), a US$55 million PMGD bridge loan (short-term financing until permanent funding is in place), a US$19 million letter of credit facility, and a US$178 million US private placement of green notes sold directly to institutional investors. A separate US$37 million bridge loan was also provided. The private placement allows delayed funding of up to 18 months, giving Solek committed long-term refinancing as the projects move into operation. BNP Paribas acted alongside Natixis as global coordinator on the private placement.
context: Natixis says this is its fourteenth PMGD financing in four years and the first to combine senior bank debt, a US private placement and mezzanine debt, with about US$1.8 billion financed or arranged for PMGD projects in Chile overall. Solek says the financing will help it consolidate its Chilean portfolio and broaden its investor base. The release states the plants are expected to produce more than 750,000 MWh per year once all are operating, supporting Chile's shift away from coal.

sources.title: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking leads financing for US$364 million portfolio of PV projects in Chile

title: TotalEnergies forms biogas joint venture with Ductor and takes 20% stake in the company

buyers.name: TotalEnergies
buyers.role: JV partner, 20% shareholder and offtaker of renewable natural gas

target: Ductor (20% stake) and joint venture for 15-20 anaerobic digestion plants
summary: TotalEnergies and Ductor, a Finnish-Swiss circular biotechnology firm, agreed to set up a joint venture to develop and invest in 15 to 20 anaerobic digestion plants that turn farm waste into renewable natural gas and organic fertiliser. TotalEnergies also acquired a 20% stake in Ductor. The priority regions for the projects are the United States and Europe.
details: Anaerobic digestion is a process where microbes break down organic waste without oxygen, producing biogas that can be upgraded to renewable natural gas. The plants will use Ductor's proprietary pre-treatment technology, already running at its sites in Germany and Mexico, to process nitrogen-rich waste from poultry and aquaculture. Ductor will screen sites, secure land, feedstock and permits and carry out feasibility studies, while TotalEnergies will take part in development, construction and operation. TotalEnergies will buy all the renewable gas and related environmental attributes, and Ductor will buy and market the specialty fertilisers, such as liquid nitrogen fertiliser. TotalEnergies' biogas vice president Olivier Guerrini will join Ductor's board. No financial terms were disclosed.
context: TotalEnergies says the deal supports its aim of producing 20 TWh of biogas a year by 2030, up from a stated 1.1 TWh of capacity in Europe today. Ductor says the partnership will help it move its project pipeline forward and build its first integrated fertiliser and biogas project. The company claims strong growth ahead in the markets for organic fertiliser and biogas.

sources.title: Ductor und TotalEnergies gründen Joint Venture zur Entwicklung, zum Bau und Betrieb einer Reihe von Biogas- und organischen Düngemittelprojekten

title: Toyota signs 100 MW virtual PPA with Savion for solar project on former Kentucky coal mine
summary: Toyota Motor North America has agreed to take 100 MW of the output of Savion's Martin County Solar Project in Kentucky through a virtual power purchase agreement. The project is being built on the former Martiki coal mine, a reclaimed brownfield site near the West Virginia border.
details: The solar photovoltaic plant sits on a mountaintop coal mine that closed in the 1990s and can use existing transmission lines. A virtual power purchase agreement is a financial contract in which the buyer agrees a price for power fed into the grid and receives the renewable attributes, without the electricity being physically delivered to its sites. Savion is developing the project with local partner Edelen Renewables. Construction is expected to begin in mid-2023, with commercial operation planned for 2024. The release does not state the total project size, contract length or price.
context: Toyota says the deal supports its target of sourcing at least 45 percent of purchased electricity from renewables by 2025 and making its North American operations carbon neutral by 2035. Kentucky hosts Toyota's largest vehicle plant worldwide. The companies present the project as an example of reusing former coal sites and their grid connections for clean energy, and expect it to be among the largest solar facilities in the state.

sources.title: Reclaimed Kentucky Coal Mine Sees the Sun Shining on New Solar Power Purchase Agreement with Toyota

title: Green Bridge Energy to fund RISE's 257 kW solar and storage system at Massachusetts college through a PPA

buyers.name: Unnamed non-profit private college in Falmouth, Massachusetts

target: 257 kW / 319 kWh solar and storage system at a private college in Falmouth, Massachusetts
summary: Northeast US commercial solar developer RISE Engineering has lined up financing from Green Bridge Energy for a 257 kW solar system with 319 kWh of storage at a non-profit private college in Falmouth, Massachusetts. The financing takes the form of a power purchase agreement (PPA) quoted through Energy Toolbase's ETB Developer software.
details: The system will be built at a co-ed non-profit college and is meant to help it stabilise electricity costs and meet its environmental, social and governance goals. Under a PPA, a financier pays for and owns the system, and the customer buys the power it produces at an agreed rate, so the college avoids upfront costs. The release says the PPA quote is indicative, meaning a preliminary price rather than a final contract, and that it covers the full cost of the system. RISE won the work in a competitive bid for turnkey solar funded by a PPA. No contract length, price or construction dates are given.
context: The release is largely a showcase for the link between Green Bridge's financing and the ETB Developer platform, which lets developers generate PPA quotes for commercial and non-profit projects without switching tools. Energy Toolbase claims this helps developers sell projects faster, and Green Bridge says it plans to add EV charging financing to the platform in 2023. The deal itself is small and illustrates financing for mid-market distributed solar.

sources.title: Renewable Developer Taps Green Bridge Energy and Energy Toolbase for Solar PPA Financing at Non-Profit, Private College

title: Evergy acquires 199 MW Persimmon Creek Wind Farm in Oklahoma from Scout Clean Energy and Elawan

advisors.name: McDermott Will & Emery LLP
advisors.role: legal advisor to Scout Clean Energy

summary: Scout Clean Energy and its joint venture partner Elawan Energy have completed the sale of the 199 MW Persimmon Creek Wind Farm in western Oklahoma to US utility Evergy. The price was not disclosed.
details: The wind farm has been operating since 2018 and uses 80 General Electric turbines spread across about 17,000 acres in Dewey, Ellis and Woodward counties. Power from the project will serve customers in Evergy's service area in Kansas and Missouri. Under an existing operations agreement, Scout will keep servicing the project until the end of 2023. McDermott Will & Emery advised Scout and Morgan, Lewis & Bockius advised Evergy.
context: Scout, which became a Brookfield Renewable portfolio company about six months earlier, says it will put the sale proceeds into new development projects. The company says the deal delivers a significant return on its invested capital. Scout reports a pipeline of about 16.5 GW of wind, solar and battery projects across 22 states, including the 200 MW Sweetland Wind Farm under construction in South Dakota and the 209 MW Markum Solar project in Texas for which it is raising financing.

sources.title: Scout Clean Energy Closes on Persimmon Creek Wind Farm Sale to Evergy

title: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company reaches financial close on US$8.4 billion green hydrogen plant in Saudi Arabia

buyers.name: 23 local, regional and international banks and financial institutions

target: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company plant at Oxagon, NEOM
summary: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company, owned equally by ACWA Power, Air Products and NEOM, has reached financial close on a green hydrogen plant at Oxagon in Saudi Arabia with a total investment value of US$8.4 billion. The project is backed by US$6.1 billion of non-recourse debt from 23 banks and financial institutions.
details: The plant will use up to 4 GW of solar and wind power to make up to 600 tonnes per day of hydrogen, delivered as green ammonia, with production targeted for the end of 2026. Financial close means all funding agreements are signed so construction money can flow. The loans are non-recourse, meaning lenders are repaid only from the project's own revenues rather than the owners' wider balance sheets, and include a tranche covered by Euler Hermes. Air Products holds a US$6.7 billion engineering, procurement and construction contract and an exclusive 30-year agreement to buy all the ammonia produced. S&P Global, acting as second party opinion provider, certified the financing as meeting green loan principles.
context: The company describes the facility as the world's largest green hydrogen plant and says the financing is among the largest arranged under a green loan framework. Air Products claims the output will avoid about five million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The project follows the first industrial operating licence awarded to the company by Saudi Arabia's industry ministry in January 2023 and is presented as supporting the country's Vision 2030 goals.

sources.title: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company completes financial close at a total investment value of USD 8.4 billion in the world's largest carbon-free green hydrogen plant

title: BlackRock GRP III acquires 97 MWp distributed solar portfolio in Chile from RRG Capital Management
target: 97 MWp portfolio of distributed solar (PMGD) projects in Chile

advisors.name: Honorato Delaveau
advisors.role: legal adviser to Aediles and BlackRock GRP III

summary: BlackRock's Global Renewable Power III fund has closed its purchase of a 97 MWp portfolio of small distributed solar projects in Chile. The projects were developed by RRG Capital Management with local partners, and Aediles Capital supported the buyer.
details: The portfolio consists of distributed solar plants under Chile's PMGD scheme, which covers small generators connected to local distribution networks rather than the high-voltage grid. Capacity is given as 97 MWp, meaning peak output of the solar panels in direct current. Aediles, through its Chilean asset manager Aediles Talinay, will manage the assets and says it plans to originate more capacity for the platform. No price or financing terms were disclosed. Honorato Delaveau advised Aediles and BlackRock, while Carey Abogados and JV Legal advised RRG.
context: RRG describes the portfolio as one of the largest clean energy portfolios in Chile and says the deal could lead to more work with BlackRock in Chile and elsewhere. For Aediles, the deal sets up an ongoing platform it intends to grow with further projects.

sources.title: AEDILES CONGRATULATES BLACKROCK GRP III IN THE ACQUISITION OF A MAJOR DISTRIBUTED SOLAR ENERGY SOLAR PORTFOLIO (PMGD)

title: Leyline Renewable Capital provides US$30 million development financing to Accelergen Energy
summary: Leyline Renewable Capital has provided US$30 million in financing to Accelergen Energy, a solar and storage developer based in Austin, Texas. Accelergen plans to use the money to build a multi-gigawatt pipeline of utility-scale solar and storage projects across several US markets over the next four years.
details: The funding comes through Leyline Growth Capital and is development finance, meaning money lent at the early stage of projects before they are built, when risk is highest. Accelergen, founded in late 2020, works on greenfield projects, which are new sites developed from scratch, covering standalone solar, solar paired with batteries, and standalone storage. No specific project sizes, sites or loan terms were disclosed. Accelergen is led by CEO Thomas Houle, formerly of Macquarie's Green Investment Group, and Josh Skogen, formerly of sPower.
context: Leyline says it backs experienced teams and that its lending lets developers grow without giving up ownership to equity investors. Accelergen says the capital will strengthen its balance sheet and help it expand its team as it launches. The deal reflects continued demand for early-stage capital for US utility-scale solar and storage developers.

sources.title: Leyline Renewable Capital Provides Financing to Accelergen Energy to Develop Solar and Storage Pipeline

title: ArcLight's Sequitur Renewables acquires operating wind farm in California's Altamont Pass
target: Operating wind farm in the Altamont Pass region of California
summary: Sequitur Renewables, a portfolio company of infrastructure investor ArcLight Capital Partners, has bought an operating wind farm in the Altamont Pass area of California. The seller, price and capacity were not disclosed.
details: The asset is a wind farm that is already running and producing power, located in the Altamont Pass region east of the San Francisco Bay Area. The release says the acquisition has closed. Milbank acted as legal counsel to ArcLight on the deal. No financial terms, capacity figures or seller identity were given.
context: ArcLight set up Sequitur in 2022 by buying operating wind farms in Pennsylvania and West Virginia, and the platform focuses on buying mature wind projects and improving their operations, commercial arrangements and financing. Sequitur says it is looking at further acquisitions across the US to grow the platform. ArcLight describes the deal as supporting carbon-free power from existing wind resources.

sources.title: ArcLight's Sequitur Platform to Acquire Operating California Wind Farm

title: Matrix Renewables closes tax equity and debt financing for Gaskell West 2 and 3 solar-plus-storage projects in California

advisors.name: CohnReznick Capital
advisors.role: exclusive financial advisor to Matrix Renewables

summary: Matrix Renewables, a renewable energy platform backed by TPG Rise, finished building its Gaskell West 2 and 3 solar-plus-storage projects in Kern County, California, and closed the financing. Bank of America provided $106 million of tax equity, and a bank group provided $99 million of permanent debt plus a $25 million letter of credit facility.
details: The projects combine 143 MWdc of solar panels with an 80 MWh battery storage system. Construction started on April 27, 2022, and the projects began commercial operation on May 5, 2023. Tax equity, meaning investment from a party that receives the projects' federal tax benefits in return, came from Bank of America. The $99 million long-term loan and the $25 million letter of credit facility, a bank guarantee used to back project obligations, were provided by MUFG, HSBC, National Bank of Canada and Commonwealth Bank of Australia. Output is sold under five long-term power purchase agreements with California utilities and cities.
context: Matrix Renewables says this is the first project it has completed in the United States. The company reports a US pipeline of more than 7 GW and a global pipeline of 11.7 GW across North America, Europe and Latin America, and says it aims to become a leading renewable platform in those regions.

sources.title: Matrix Renewables Completes Construction and Closes on Debt and Tax Equity Financing for the Gaskell West Projects

title: Pattern Energy signs PPAs with Shell Energy and University of California for SunZia Wind output

buyers.name: Regents of the University of California

summary: Pattern Energy has signed long-term power purchase agreements with Shell Energy North America and the Regents of the University of California for part of the output of its SunZia Wind project in New Mexico. The project is described as having more than 3,500 MW of new wind capacity.
details: A power purchase agreement is a contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a project over many years. SunZia Wind will be built in Torrance, Lincoln and San Miguel Counties in New Mexico, and the contracts cover only a portion of its power. Its output will travel over SunZia Transmission, a planned 550-mile high-voltage direct current line from central New Mexico to south-central Arizona able to carry 3,000 MW. Construction is expected to begin later in 2023, subject to remaining federal and local approvals including from the Bureau of Land Management, with completion and first deliveries expected in 2026. Contract lengths and prices were not disclosed.
context: Pattern Energy calls SunZia the largest wind project in U.S. history and the Western Hemisphere, and says its evening generation peak complements daytime solar for customers in Arizona and California. The company cites an independent study estimating 20.5 billion dollars in total economic benefit, including over 8 billion dollars of direct capital investment. For the University of California, the deal marks its first wind contract after earlier utility-scale solar deals. Pattern says it is still in talks with other potential buyers in the western region.

sources.title: Pattern Energy Signs Power Purchase Agreements for Largest Wind Project in U.S. History

title: Pivot Energy closes about $203 million financing for 100 MWdc US distributed solar portfolio

buyers.name: Silicon Valley Bank
buyers.role: Coordinating lead arranger, sole bookrunner and administrative agent

buyers.name: National Bank of Canada
buyers.role: Lender and letter of credit provider

target: 100 MWdc portfolio of 35 community solar and C&I projects

advisors.name: CohnReznick Capital
advisors.role: Exclusive financial advisor to Pivot Energy

summary: Pivot Energy has closed a financing package of roughly $203 million for 35 distributed solar projects totaling 100 MWdc across seven US states. Silicon Valley Bank led the debt and Foss & Company provided the initial tax equity.
details: The portfolio mixes community solar projects, where local subscribers buy shares of a solar farm's output, and commercial and industrial (C&I) projects in Colorado, Minnesota, Illinois, New York, Hawaii, Maryland and California. The projects are scheduled to start commercial operation between the second quarter of 2023 and the second quarter of 2024. The debt includes a construction loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term money until the tax equity investor pays in) and a term loan, with National Bank of Canada also providing a letter of credit facility. Tax equity means an investor funds part of the project in exchange for its federal tax credits. Subscribers include municipalities, healthcare and retail businesses, residential customers and about 8,000 low-to-moderate income households.
context: This is the second portfolio Pivot will build, own and operate since ECP acquired it in June 2021, and the release says it is the largest low-to-moderate income community solar portfolio developed to date. It is described as the first syndicated loan SVB has led since First Citizens Bank acquired it, and as J.P. Morgan's first debt financing in community solar. SVB and Foss also led financing for Pivot's first portfolio in 2022.

sources.title: Pivot Energy Closes $200 Million Financing Facility for a 100 MW Multi-State Portfolio of Distributed Solar Projects

title: EE North America acquires majority stake in 700 MW of Colorado solar projects from Horus Energy
target: Majority stake in Sandy Hill Solar and Sand Dune Solar
summary: EE North America, the US arm of Denmark's European Energy, has bought a majority stake in two Colorado solar projects, Sandy Hill Solar and Sand Dune Solar, totalling 700 MW. The projects will be held in a joint venture with developer Horus Energy. No price was disclosed.
details: The two projects are early-stage developments that will connect to the grid of Public Service of Colorado, the local utility network. Construction is expected to begin in 2025. Horus Energy, which originated the projects from undeveloped land (greenfield development), remains a minority partner in the joint venture. The exact stake size and deal terms were not stated.
context: The deal marks EE North America's first entry into Colorado and lifts its US solar development pipeline to 2.5 GW across Texas, Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado. The company says it aims to develop 10 GW of renewable capacity in the US by 2026. Horus Energy describes the partnership as validation of its development model.

sources.title: EE North America Expands U.S. Renewable Energy Footprint, Adding 700MW Through Acquisition of Colorado Solar Projects

title: Swift Current Energy closes financing for 266 MWdc Tres Bahias Solar project in Texas

buyers.name: ING Capital, LLC
buyers.role: sole lead arranger, bookrunner and green loan structuring agent

advisors.name: Vinson & Elkins
advisors.role: legal counsel to Swift Current Energy

advisors.name: Husch Blackwell
advisors.role: legal counsel to Swift Current Energy

advisors.name: Jackson Walker
advisors.role: legal counsel to ING and Morgan Stanley

summary: Swift Current Energy has closed project financing led by ING Capital and secured a tax equity commitment from Morgan Stanley Renewables for its Tres Bahias Solar project in Calhoun County, Texas. The project is rated at 266 MWdc, or 195 MWac. No financing amount was disclosed.
details: The solar plant is under construction and is expected to start operating by the end of 2023. ING served as the sole lead arranger and bookrunner and structured the debt as a green loan, meaning a loan tied to environmentally beneficial use of proceeds. Morgan Stanley committed tax equity, which is investment from a party that receives the project's federal tax credits in exchange for funding. First Solar is supplying the panels and IEA Constructors is handling engineering, procurement and construction. The deal was structured to follow new guidance under the US Inflation Reduction Act.
context: Swift Current, the developer, will keep long-term ownership and operation of the project. The company says it has more than 1 GW of wind and solar under construction, including the 800 MW Double Black Diamond Solar project in Illinois, and plans to expand work with both financiers across its US pipeline.

sources.title: SWIFT CURRENT ENERGY CLOSES PROJECT FINANCING ON 266 MW TRES BAHIAS SOLAR PROJECT IN SOUTHEAST TEXAS

title: Atlas Renewable Energy signs 21-year dollar-denominated solar PPA with Albras in Brazil
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has signed a 21-year power purchase agreement with Albras, Brazil's largest primary aluminium producer. Power will come from the 902 MWp Vista Alegre solar project in Minas Gerais. Atlas describes it as the largest private PPA signed in Latin America.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a generator at set terms. This contract runs for 21 years and is priced in US dollars, which Atlas says is unprecedented in the sector. The Vista Alegre plant in Minas Gerais has 902 MWp of panel capacity, equal to 768 MWac of grid output capacity, and is expected to produce about 2 TWh per year. Operations are planned to begin in 2025. No contract value or financing details were disclosed.
context: This is the second supply contract between Atlas and Albras, and Atlas says it shows its ability to give corporate clients predictable energy costs while meeting sustainability goals. Atlas estimates the plant will offset about 154,000 tonnes of CO2 a year. The company also plans a training program for local women aiming for more than 15% female representation in the construction workforce. Atlas reports more than 4 GW of contracted projects, of which 2.2 GW are operating.

sources.title: ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY ASSINA MAIOR PPA PRIVADO DE ENERGIA SOLAR DA AMÉRICA LATINA

title: Atlas Renewable Energy signs 21-year solar PPA with Albras for 902 MWp Vista Alegre project in Brazil
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has signed a 21-year power purchase agreement to sell solar electricity to Albras, Brazil's largest primary aluminum producer. The power will come from the planned 902 MWp Vista Alegre solar plant in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a generator at set terms. This contract is priced in US dollars and runs for 21 years. The Vista Alegre plant will have an installed capacity of 902 MWp (peak output of its solar panels) and is expected to generate about 2 TWh of electricity per year. Operations are expected to begin in 2025. Atlas also plans a social program during construction aimed at training local women and reaching more than 15% female representation in the workforce.
context: This is the second PPA between Atlas and Albras. Atlas claims it is the longest-term corporate renewable PPA ever signed in Latin America and describes it as the region's largest private solar PPA. The company says the deal reflects its strategy of supplying clean power to large corporate energy users, and it reports over 4 GW of contracted projects, 2.2 GW of them operating.

sources.title: ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY SIGNS LARGEST PRIVATE SOLAR PPA IN LATAM

title: Montana Renewables closes $75 million bridge loan from I Squared Capital
target: Montana Renewables renewable fuels plant, Great Falls, Montana
summary: Montana Renewables, a subsidiary of Calumet Specialty Products Partners, closed a $75 million bridge loan with I Squared Capital on April 19, 2023. The borrower runs a renewable fuels plant in Great Falls, Montana, producing sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel and renewable hydrogen.
details: The bridge loan, meaning short-term debt meant to cover a gap until longer-term funding is arranged, carries a floating interest rate of SOFR plus 6.0 to 7.3% a year. SOFR is a benchmark US lending rate. Montana Renewables can prepay half of the principal from free cash flow by the end of 2024. The plant is permitted to process 15,000 barrels per stream day of renewable feedstocks and began operating in late 2022, and its sustainable aviation fuel and feedstock pretreatment units have now completed startup. A ribbon cutting with the fuel's offtaker, the buyer of the output, was planned for May 10, 2023.
context: The financing came as Calumet announced the plant was fully operating, which the company says makes it the largest sustainable aviation fuel producer in North America. Management said its capital markets strategy is unchanged and that the loan gives it strategic flexibility. The company reconfirmed expected EBITDA of $1.25 to $1.45 per gallon based on locally sourced feedstocks.

sources.title: Calumet Reaches Milestone of Largest Sustainable Aviation Fuel Producer in North America; Enters Full Operations at Montana Renewables; Arranges Bridge Financing

title: Mitsui acquires 110 MW Three W Solar project in Texas from OCI Solar Power
summary: OCI Solar Power has sold its 110 MW Three W Solar photovoltaic project in Hill County, Texas, to Japanese trading house Mitsui & Co., Ltd. The project is construction-ready, and Mitsui will take it through to completion. No price was disclosed.
details: Three W Solar covers 875 acres near Hillsboro, south of Dallas. Construction-ready means permits, environmental studies and grid connection requirements have been dealt with so building can start. OCI says it spent nearly two years developing the site, working with landowners and the local school district. Construction is planned for 2024, with the plant expected to begin operating in 2025.
context: The sale comes less than two months after OCI Solar Power and Mitsui's US arm signed an agreement to collaborate on solar projects in Texas. OCI Solar Power, a subsidiary of South Korea's OCI Company, says it has originated more than 3 GW of solar and storage projects across the US. The deal gives Mitsui a project ready to build in the Texas market.

sources.title: OCI Solar Power sells 110 MWac project to Mitsui

title: Energy Capital Partners makes US$300 million preferred equity investment in Braya Renewable Fuels
summary: Energy Capital Partners has invested US$300 million in preferred equity in Braya Renewable Fuels, which owns the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. The money completes funding to convert the former oil refinery into a plant making renewable fuels.
details: Preferred equity is an ownership stake that is paid out before ordinary shareholders but usually carries fewer control rights. Once running, the converted refinery is expected to produce 18,000 barrels per day of renewable fuel, mainly renewable diesel, with plans to expand output and add more sustainable aviation fuel. Braya says it expects to begin producing and selling fuel later in 2023. Lazard was Braya's financial adviser, with Kirkland & Ellis, Norton Rose Fulbright Canada, McInnes Cooper and Sidley Austin as its lawyers, while Latham & Watkins and Blake, Cassels & Graydon advised ECP.
context: ECP joins existing owners Cresta Fund Management, the controlling shareholder since 2021, and North Atlantic Refining Corp., managed by Silverpeak. The deal follows Braya's agreement with ABO Wind to jointly develop green hydrogen and green ammonia production at the site. Cresta claims the investment positions Braya to become one of the largest independently owned renewable fuel producers globally.

sources.title: Braya Renewable Fuels receives a $300 Million investment from Energy Capital Partners.

title: SolaREIT closes second solar land loan with Norbut Solar Farms for New York projects
target: Seven solar leases covering more than 250 acres in New York
summary: Solar land investment fund SolaREIT has closed a second solar land loan with New York developer Norbut Solar Farms. The financing covers seven solar leases on more than 250 acres and supports over 50 MW DC of solar capacity in New York state.
details: The deal is secured on the land leases where solar farms will be built, rather than on the panels themselves. The seven leases together span more than 250 acres in New York and are linked to more than 50 MW of solar measured in DC, meaning the rated output of the panels before conversion to grid power. SolaREIT says its land financing lets developers free up cash and lower lease costs. The loan amount and terms were not disclosed.
context: This is the second land financing between the two companies, and Norbut says the deal closed faster than earlier ones. SolaREIT, launched in late 2020, argues that solar development needs large amounts of land and capital, and that its land-focused financing gives developers an alternative funding source. The companies claim the projects will offset about 34,810 metric tons of CO2 each year.

sources.title: SolaREIT Closes On Second Solar Land Loan with Norbut Solar Farms

title: Lowe's partners with DSD Renewables, Greenskies Clean Focus and Infiniti Energy on rooftop solar at 174 US sites
target: Rooftop solar portfolio at 174 Lowe's stores and distribution centers
summary: Home improvement retailer Lowe's announced a rooftop solar program covering 174 stores and distribution centers in California, Illinois and New Jersey. The installations are being delivered with three solar partners, DSD Renewables, Greenskies Clean Focus and Infiniti Energy, and 20 sites are already running.
details: Infiniti Energy has 20 New Jersey stores in operation and six more in development for later in 2023. DSD Renewables is working on 55 California stores plus 36 stores and three distribution centers in Illinois, with construction expected to start at all of them by the end of 2023. Greenskies Clean Focus is handling 52 California stores and two distribution centers, with construction planned to begin later this year. The release does not state total capacity, deal value or the contract structure, so it is unclear whether Lowe's owns the panels or buys the power from the partners. Lowe's says each completed site should meet about 90% of its own energy use.
context: Lowe's presents the program as part of its goals of powering operations with 50% renewable energy by 2030 and reaching net-zero emissions by 2050. The company says the investment should also lower operating costs. It notes it already hit its 2025 target of cutting scope 1 and scope 2 emissions by 40% versus 2016 levels, which it says it reached four years early. Scope 1 and 2 emissions are those from a company's own operations and the energy it buys.

sources.title: LOWE'S INVESTS IN RENEWABLE ENERGY WITH ROOFTOP SOLAR PANEL INSTALLATIONS AT 174 LOCATIONS AS PART OF NET-ZERO TARGET

title: HASI makes follow-on equity investment in ForeFront Power's 48.5 MW-DC California distributed solar-plus-storage portfolio
target: Portfolio of distributed commercial and industrial solar and solar-plus-storage projects in California
summary: HASI has made a follow-on equity investment alongside ForeFront Power in a portfolio of distributed commercial and industrial solar projects across California. The portfolio totals 48.5 MW-DC of solar, with several projects paired with 3.7 MW of battery storage. The deal reached financial close, meaning the funding agreements were signed and money began to flow, on March 30, 2023.
details: The projects are ground-mounted, carport and rooftop solar systems serving commercial and industrial customers, mostly behind-the-meter, meaning the power is used on site rather than sold to the grid. About 36 MW of the assets were mechanically complete and funded at financial close, while the rest will be funded as they are completed through the end of 2023. HASI acts as a co-sponsor, an equity partner sharing ownership with the developer. ForeFront Power will keep managing customer relationships and provide ongoing asset management services. No deal value or advisers were disclosed.
context: The investment builds on a first co-sponsor equity deal the two companies made in 2022 for a separate U.S. distributed solar portfolio. ForeFront Power, a subsidiary of Mitsui & Co., says the new capital supports its continued growth in behind-the-meter solar and storage. HASI says ForeFront has shown it can deliver projects that perform in line with financial projections.

sources.title: ForeFront Power and HASI Expand Equity Investment with New Distributed Solar-Plus-Storage Portfolio Across California

title: Greenwood Sustainable Infrastructure acquires Saturn Power's 1.4 GW solar and storage development portfolio
target: Saturn Power solar and battery development portfolios and team
summary: Greenwood Sustainable Infrastructure, the North American renewables arm of Libra Group, has bought the solar and battery development portfolios of Saturn Power along with its development team. The roughly 1.4 GW pipeline covers early to late stage projects in five U.S. states and two Canadian provinces. No price was disclosed.
details: The acquired pipeline consists of 72 solar projects, about 90% of which are community solar, plus six battery storage projects. Community solar lets households and businesses that cannot install their own panels subscribe to a share of a shared solar farm. The deal expands GSI's footprint from seven to 12 U.S. states and adds Alberta and Saskatchewan in Canada, bringing its headcount to more than 50. GSI plans to direct US$200 million of capital investment into its North American operations, including building out the acquired projects in the coming years.
context: GSI says the deal strengthens its development capabilities and is a step toward its goal of a 5 GW clean power pipeline by 2029. Libra Group says the acquisition lifts its overall renewable portfolio to 3 GW of projects owned, developed or pending development across eight countries. The company frames community solar as a growth opportunity supported by U.S. federal infrastructure policy.

sources.title: Greenwood Sustainable Infrastructure (GSI) Enhances Renewable Energy Platform with Strategic Acquisition of Saturn Power

title: Ameren Missouri wins regulatory approval to acquire 150 MW White County solar facility in Illinois
target: 150 MW solar facility in White County, Illinois
summary: Ameren Missouri, a subsidiary of Ameren Corporation, received approval from the Missouri Public Service Commission to buy a 150 MW solar facility in White County, Illinois once it is built. The facility will also support a new Renewable Solutions program in which local organizations help pay for it.
details: The utility will take ownership of the solar plant upon completion, and the purchase remains subject to customary closing conditions. The company expects the facility to start producing power late in 2024 and says it should cover the yearly electricity use of nearly 27,500 homes. Under the Renewable Solutions program, ten Missouri organizations, including Bi-State Development, bioMérieux, Emerson, General Motors, Mastercard, SSM Health and Walmart, contribute part of the plant's cost. In return they receive renewable energy credits, which are certificates proving a unit of clean power was generated, while the plant's output serves all Ameren Missouri customers. The developer and purchase price were not disclosed.
context: The company says this is its tenth solar facility announced or placed in service since 2019, and it plans to add 2,800 MW of new renewable generation by 2030. Earlier in the year it also received approval to acquire the 200 MW Huck Finn solar project in central Missouri, which is not part of the program. The arrangement lets corporate customers pursue their own clean energy targets through the utility.

sources.title: Ameren Missouri receives approval to acquire new solar facility to supply local organizations with up to 100% renewable energy

title: Dominion Energy to acquire Longroad Energy's 108 MWdc Foxhound Solar project in Virginia
summary: Longroad Energy has agreed to sell its Foxhound Solar project in Halifax County, Virginia, to Dominion Energy. The project is rated at 108 MW of direct current panel output, or 83 MW on the alternating current grid side, and is now under construction.
details: Foxhound has reached full notice to proceed, meaning construction is fully authorized, after six years of development. The acquisition is expected to close financially once the plant reaches mechanical completion, when the main equipment is installed, which is anticipated in January 2024. The project has long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts to sell its electricity over many years. KeyBank N.A. and HSBC acted as lenders, and Balch & Bingham was Longroad's legal counsel. First Solar supplies the modules, Nextracker the trackers and TMEIC the inverters, with grid connection near the Clover Power Station.
context: The project is Longroad's first solar plant in Virginia and its first greenfield project, meaning built from scratch, in the PJM grid region. Longroad says Dominion's purchase will help meet customer sustainability goals and targets under the Virginia Clean Economy Act. The release states Foxhound is the first utility-scale project certified under Virginia's Pollinator-Smart biodiversity program.

sources.title: Longroad Energy's 108 MWdc Foxhound Solar Project to be Acquired by Dominion Energy

title: NJR Clean Energy Ventures acquires 2.8 MWdc Old Bridge landfill community solar project from AC Power
target: Old Bridge solar project (Global Sanitary Landfill)
summary: AC Power has sold the Old Bridge solar project in Old Bridge Township, New Jersey, together with its 25-year site lease, to NJR Clean Energy Ventures. The 2.8 MWdc community solar project sits on a former landfill designated as a federal Superfund site. No price was disclosed.
details: The project is planned on the Global Sanitary Landfill, a former municipal and non-hazardous industrial waste site that has been inactive since 1984. It won capacity in October 2021 under the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities Community Solar Pilot Program, which lets local subscribers buy power from a nearby solar plant to cut their bills. An AC Power affiliate, Superfun LLC, took title to the land in February 2023 and leases it to the project for 25 years. CS Energy, acting as the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, is set to start building in June 2023, and VHB designed an ecological recovery plan including pollinator habitat.
context: The release says this will be the first New Jersey community solar project owned by NJR Clean Energy Ventures, the renewables arm of New Jersey Resources, which reports more than 430 MW of installed solar. For AC Power it is the first Superfund site in its ownership structure. The companies say the project, expected to supply power for about 400 homes, shows how contaminated or unused land can be reused for clean energy.

sources.title: AC POWER ANNOUNCES SALE OF OLD BRIDGE SOLAR PROJECT  TO NJR CLEAN ENERGY VENTURES

title: Cowboy Clean Fuels closes $7.5 million Series A led by Machan Investments
summary: Denver-based start-up Cowboy Clean Fuels has closed a $7.5 million Series A funding round led by Houston investment firm Machan Investments. The money will support work toward a first commercial-scale renewable natural gas project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin.
details: Series A refers to a company's first significant round of outside equity funding. Cowboy Clean Fuels says the proceeds will go toward meeting regulatory requirements, early engineering design and preparation for its first commercial project in the Powder River Basin of Wyoming. Its process injects agricultural waste into idle coal bed methane wells, where microbes in the deep coal seams turn it into methane, a process the company compares to anaerobic digestion. The technology was developed by co-founder Dr. Michael Urynowicz and is exclusively licensed from the University of Wyoming's Center for Biogenic Natural Gas Research. Syren Capital advised on the round.
context: Renewable natural gas is methane made from organic waste that can replace fossil gas in existing pipelines. The company claims its method removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere rather than only cutting emissions, and Machan argues that reusing existing gas infrastructure lowers project costs compared with other RNG and carbon capture approaches. The round marks the company's first funding as it moves from research toward commercial operation.

sources.title: Cowboy Clean Fuels Completes Series A Financing to Advance Renewable Natural Gas Commercialization Plan

title: Birch Creek Energy acquires US solar developer Foundation Solar Partners from Hull Street Energy

advisors.name: Lazard Frères & Co. LLC
advisors.role: exclusive financial advisor to Hull Street Energy

advisors.name: Foley & Lardner LLP
advisors.role: legal counsel to Hull Street Energy

advisors.name: Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough LLP
advisors.role: legal counsel to Birch Creek Energy

summary: Private equity firm Hull Street Energy has sold Foundation Solar Partners, a US developer of utility-scale solar projects, to Birch Creek Energy. Financial terms and the size of the acquired pipeline were not disclosed.
details: Foundation Solar was founded in 2019 and develops large, grid-connected solar projects in selected US markets. Its team has previously developed, acquired or managed more than 6 GW of renewable capacity over about twenty years. The buyer, St. Louis-based Birch Creek, says it has developed 872 MW of solar since 2019 and holds a pipeline of over 8 GW of solar and storage projects across the MISO, PJM, Texas and Southeast power markets. Lazard advised Hull Street Energy on the financial side and Foley & Lardner acted as its lawyers, while Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough represented Birch Creek.
context: The sale marks an exit for Hull Street Energy, which describes its investment in Foundation Solar as part of building the clean power infrastructure needed to decarbonize North America. For Birch Creek, the deal adds a development team and projects to its existing utility-scale solar and storage platform.

sources.title: Hull Street Energy Sells Foundation Solar Partners

title: Birch Creek Energy acquires solar developer Foundation Solar Partners from Hull Street Energy
summary: St. Louis based Birch Creek Energy has bought Foundation Solar Partners, a Washington DC solar and storage developer, from Hull Street Energy. The deal closed on March 24, 2023 and gives the combined company a development pipeline of about 13.5 GW across the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: Foundation Solar focuses on greenfield origination, meaning it finds and starts new projects from scratch, mainly in the MISO and PJM regional power markets. It reports having developed and sold over 800 MW of solar and holding a pipeline of nearly 5 GW of solar and storage projects, with seven employees. Combined, the two firms say they have developed over 1.7 GW since 2019, have 7.5 GW of pipeline in PJM and MISO, and will have 30 staff based in St. Louis. Lazard Frères & Co. was exclusive financial adviser to Hull Street Energy, Foley & Lardner was its legal counsel, and Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough advised Birch Creek.
context: Birch Creek says the deal adds early-stage project origination skills to its existing strengths in mid to late stage development, project finance and ownership. The company claims the acquisition materially enlarges its portfolio in PJM and MISO and will help it grow faster. Foundation Solar's leadership says joining Birch Creek gives its projects more paths to completion.

sources.title: Birch Creek Energy Acquires Foundation Solar Partners

title: Twenty20 Energy acquires owner of Traunstein geothermal project in Bavaria
target: Petra Energy Holding Sarl (owner of the Traunstein Geothermal Energy Project)
summary: Singapore-based Twenty20 Energy has bought Petra Energy Holding Sarl, the company that owns the Traunstein Geothermal Energy Project in Bavaria, Germany. The deal closed on December 30, 2022, and its financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Early modeling puts the project at an estimated 13 MW of electricity generation and 20 MW of thermal output for district heating, which means piped heat supplied to local buildings. The design calls for two production wells that draw hot underground fluid and two reinjection wells that return it to the reservoir. The project is still in development, and the operating subsidiary Petra Energy GmbH will be renamed Bayern Renewables GmbH and will finish building it. The seller and the deal value were not named.
context: Twenty20 Energy says geothermal fits its strategy of adding cleaner energy sources to its portfolio. The company presents the project as a way to help ease Germany's energy shortages, which it notes have led to some coal plants being restarted. It also plans to base a Bayern Renewables headquarters at the site, which it expects to serve as a hub for expansion elsewhere in Germany and Europe.

title: Genie Renewables acquires site rights for 6.25 MW community solar project in Upstate New York
target: Site rights for a proposed 6.25 MW community solar project in Upstate New York
summary: Genie Renewables, a division of Genie Energy, has acquired the rights to a site in Upstate New York for a planned community solar project. The company expects the project to reach about 6.25 MW of generating capacity once built. The seller and price were not disclosed.
details: The project is at an early development stage, with only site rights secured so far. Community solar lets multiple local customers subscribe to a shared solar farm and receive credits on their bills. Separately, Genie said it received a favorable interconnection review (CESIR, a utility study of how a project connects to the grid and what that costs) from Con Edison for a 3 MW community solar project in Downstate New York. The company expects to get a notice to proceed and start building that project in the coming months, subject to a land lease and local permits.
context: The deal adds to the solar pipeline of Genie's renewables division, which develops and invests in commercial, community and utility-scale solar. Genie's chief executive claims improved economics are driving strong demand for solar projects in its existing markets and pushing expansion into new ones.

title: Nestlé becomes sole tax equity investor in Enel's 208 MWdc Ganado solar-plus-storage project in Texas

buyers.name: Nestlé
buyers.role: tax equity investor and buyer of renewable energy attributes

summary: Enel North America has secured Nestlé as the only tax equity investor in its Ganado solar-plus-storage project in Jackson County, Texas. The project has 208 MWdc of solar capacity. Nestlé will also buy all of the renewable energy attributes the solar plant produces.
details: Tax equity is a US financing method in which an investor puts money into a project in exchange for the federal tax credits and other tax benefits it generates. Besides its investment, Nestlé agreed to purchase 100% of the project's renewable electricity attributes, which are certificates showing that clean power was produced. Output is estimated at an average of 333,000 MWh a year over a 15-year term. The storage capacity was not disclosed, and the investment amount was not stated. Marathon Capital advised Nestlé and CCA Capital LLC advised Enel, and the project is expected to start operating in the second quarter of 2023.
context: Enel says corporate customers increasingly want clean energy through varied arrangements such as power purchase agreements, retail supply and upfront tax equity investments. Nestlé says the deal supports its goal of sourcing 100% renewable electricity at its sites by 2025 and reaching net zero by 2050. Nestlé expects the attributes to cut about 126,294 tonnes of CO2 emissions per year across its US facilities. The deal follows the 12 power purchase agreements Enel signed with commercial and industrial customers in 2022.

sources.title: ENEL PARTNERS WITH NESTLÉ FOR INVESTMENT IN GANADO SOLAR PROJECT

title: Infinity Power completes acquisition of Lekela Power's 1 GW African wind platform
summary: Infinity Power, a joint venture between Egypt's Infinity and the UAE's Masdar, has completed its purchase of all shares in Lekela Power. Lekela runs about 1 GW of wind farms in South Africa, Egypt and Senegal. The sellers were Actis and a consortium led by Mainstream Renewable Power.
details: Lekela's operating wind portfolio totals roughly 1 GW across three countries, alongside a 1.8 GW pipeline of projects at different development stages. Before the sale, Actis owned 60% of Lekela and a Mainstream-led consortium held the remaining 40%. The purchase was paid for with equity from Infinity Power's shareholders plus acquisition loans arranged by Absa CIB and Mauritian Commercial Bank as mandated lead arrangers, meaning the banks that organised and led the lending. No price was disclosed. Infinity Power was advised by Cantor Fitzgerald, Absa CIB, Norton Rose Fulbright, Al Kamel Law, Ernst & Young and AFRY.
context: The release describes the deal as Africa's biggest renewable energy transaction and says it makes Infinity Power the continent's largest pure-play renewable power company, with 1.3 GW in operation and a 13.8 GW pipeline. Infinity Power says it aims to install and operate 2 GW of new greenfield projects by 2025. For Actis the sale marks an exit from a platform it founded in 2015.

title: ACEN joint venture agrees to buy 136 MW Texas wind portfolio from GlidePath
target: Portfolio of eight operating wind projects in northern Texas
summary: UPC Power Solutions, a joint venture of Philippine energy company ACEN with PivotGen and UPC Solar & Wind Investments, signed a purchase and sale agreement to buy eight operating wind projects in northern Texas from GlidePath. The portfolio totals 136 MW. No price was disclosed.
details: The eight projects are already operating and are located in northern Texas. The companies estimate the portfolio produces about 360 GWh of electricity a year, which they say is enough for around 24,000 households. The partners plan to extend the life of the wind farms through preventative maintenance and repowering, meaning replacing older turbines or components with newer equipment. The sale still needs regulatory approvals, including from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, the US agency that oversees interstate electricity transmission.
context: The deal marks ACEN's first move into the US renewables market, expanding beyond its Asia Pacific base. It follows a partnership formed in April 2022 to acquire and repower operating US wind projects. ACEN says it aims to reach 20 GW of renewables capacity by 2030.

title: Peregrine Energy Solutions and investment manager partner acquire 80 MW Old Gold wind asset in Iowa

buyers.name: Unnamed global alternative investment manager
buyers.role: financial partner on behalf of managed funds

target: Old Gold Energy Center, LLC (formerly Top of Iowa I)
summary: Peregrine Energy Solutions, partnering with an unnamed global alternative investment manager, has acquired the Old Gold Energy Center, an 80 MW operating wind farm in northern Iowa. Peregrine will run the site and plans to redevelop and expand it. Price and seller were not disclosed.
details: The wind farm, formerly called Top of Iowa I, sits in Worth County and has been producing power since 2001. Peregrine intends to keep it running while working on a redevelopment, often called repowering, meaning replacing older turbines with fewer, more productive ones, and adding battery storage. Early company projections suggest the site could grow to as much as 230 MW of wind with an 80 MW battery system, though the final size is still under study. Peregrine expects redevelopment to be finished around the end of 2027.
context: The deal adds an operating asset to Peregrine, a Boulder-based platform formed in 2022 that mainly focuses on utility-scale battery storage. The company claims the site has one of the strongest wind resources in North America and favorable pricing at its grid delivery point. It follows Peregrine's earlier storage acquisitions in the Texas ERCOT market and a joint venture with an Asian investment firm to develop new battery projects.

sources.title: Peregrine Energy Solutions and Global Investment Manager Partner to Acquire, Operate, Redevelop and Expand 80 MW Operating Wind Asset in Northern Iowa

title: TAQA and Reykjavik Geothermal form joint venture to develop geothermal energy in Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi energy services firm TAQA and Icelandic developer Reykjavik Geothermal signed a joint venture agreement to create TAQA Geothermal Energy LLC, based in Riyadh. The new company will explore and develop geothermal resources in Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East and North Africa region.
details: The agreement was signed at the Public Investment Fund private sector forum in Riyadh on 15 March 2023. TAQA's CEO said the venture aims to explore and develop the equivalent of 1 GW of geothermal energy from resources in the Kingdom. Reykjavik Geothermal said the venture also intends to pursue large-scale direct use of geothermal heat for cooling and desalination, drawing on low and medium temperature resources. Ownership shares, investment amounts and project timelines were not disclosed.
context: TAQA, which is 54% owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, presents the venture as supporting the country's decarbonisation goals and Vision 2030 plan to diversify its energy mix. The deal builds on TAQA's geothermal centre of excellence set up in Turkey in 2021 and on Reykjavik Geothermal's exploration in the Kingdom since 2009. The partners describe geothermal as a clean and stable baseload source, meaning it can supply power around the clock.

title: LyondellBasell signs five 15-year solar PPAs with Grenergy for La Cereal project in Spain
summary: Chemical company LyondellBasell has signed five 15-year power purchase agreements with Spanish renewable producer Grenergy. The contracts cover about 329,000 MWh of solar electricity per year from the 259 MW La Cereal solar project in Spain.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project at set terms. The five contracts each run for 15 years and will be supplied by La Cereal, which is expected to start operating at the end of 2025. La Cereal is part of Grenergy's larger Clara Campoamor solar complex, located between the Madrid and Castilla La Mancha regions, which is planned to reach about 575 MW in total. No financial terms were disclosed.
context: LyondellBasell says the deals bring it to 70% of its goal of sourcing at least half its electricity from renewables by 2030, supporting its target to cut scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% by 2030. Grenergy says the contracts will help finance its largest Spanish project to date and support its plan to raise Europe's share of its portfolio from 25% to 45% by 2025.

title: Pow.re secures 100 MW fixed-rate hydropower allocation in Paraguay for computing site
summary: Pow.re Holdings, a Montreal-based high-density computing and fintech company, signed a binding agreement with an unnamed local partner to secure a 100 MW power allocation in Paraguay. The power comes from utility ANDE's new Yguazu substation, which is fed by the Itaipu hydroelectric dam, at a fixed rate for five years.
details: The power allocation is fixed-price for five years and is delivered through ANDE's newly built Yguazu substation. Pow.re has begun building power transformation and computing infrastructure on an 8.5 hectare site next to the substation. ANDE energized the first of three 500 kV transmission lines linking the Itaipu dam to Yguazu on February 26, 2023. The company estimates the site could add about 4.5 exahash per second of computing power, a measure of crypto mining output, once fully running. The price and the name of the local partner were not disclosed.
context: Paraguay has historically sold most of its half share of Itaipu's 14 GW output to Brazil, and new transmission lines let it use more domestically. Pow.re claims the deal gives it access to large amounts of renewable power at a competitive price and presents it as evidence that surplus clean power can be paired with data centers. The company also named two advisors, Andres Romero and Matthew Carson, alongside the announcement.

sources.title: Pow.re secures 100 MW of renewable power in Paraguay and welcomes two industry veterans to the advisory board.

title: Aypa Power buys 268 MW of Indiana battery storage projects from Blue Steel Power
target: Williams Power and Fletcher Power battery storage projects
summary: Aypa Power, a Blackstone portfolio company, has closed its purchase of two standalone battery storage projects in Indiana totaling 268 MW. The seller was Blue Steel Power, a joint venture of Open Road Renewables and Eolian. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The Williams Power project in Jefferson County has a capacity of 150 MW and the Fletcher Power project in Decatur County has 118 MW. Both are late-stage development projects, meaning much of the permitting work is done but construction has not started. They received conditional use permits in late 2022 after development began in 2018. Aypa will handle the remaining development to bring the batteries into operation on the grid run by MISO, the regional grid operator covering much of the US Midwest. Storage energy capacity in MWh and expected operation dates were not stated.
context: Aypa says it expects capacity shortfalls in the MISO region and presents the projects as a way to improve grid reliability. The company said the deals materially expand its Indiana portfolio, and it reports more than 15 GW of projects in development across North America. For the sellers, the sale reflects a develop-and-sell model in which early-stage teams build up projects and hand them to long-term owners.

title: OYA Renewables secures US$216M in debt and tax equity for 15 New York community solar projects

buyers.name: CIT, a division of First Citizens Bank & Trust Company

target: 15 New York State community solar projects (2023 slate)
summary: Toronto-based OYA Renewables has closed US$216 million of financing to build 15 community solar projects across New York State. The package combines a US$145 million construction-to-term loan led by CIT with a US$71 million tax equity commitment from Monarch Private Capital.
details: The loan is a construction-to-term facility, meaning it funds building the projects and then converts into a longer-term loan once they operate. CIT Power and Energy led a bank syndicate that included Amalgamated Bank, Siemens Financial Services, Comerica Bank and Cadence Bank. Monarch Private Capital is providing tax equity, an investment where backers fund projects in return for federal tax credits and a share of cash flow, through its ESG-focused impact funds. Some projects in low-income communities may qualify for extra credits, lifting the potential credit from 30% to as much as 50%. The release says the projects are expected to total almost 100 MWdc once complete.
context: OYA says the financing grows its asset base and supports its shift from pure developer to independent power producer, a company that owns and runs plants and sells their power. Community solar lets households and businesses subscribe to part of a shared solar farm and receive bill credits. OYA says its 2024 projects are in preconstruction or late-stage permitting.

title: Masdar takes strategic stake in Indonesia's Pertamina Geothermal Energy
summary: Abu Dhabi clean energy company Masdar has made a strategic investment in Pertamina Geothermal Energy (PGE), an Indonesian geothermal operator with more than 1.87 GW of capacity. The size of the stake and the amount invested were not disclosed. The deal is Masdar's first move into geothermal power.
details: PGE has run geothermal plants in Indonesia for about 40 years, and its portfolio exceeds 1.87 GW. Geothermal plants use heat from inside the Earth to make electricity around the clock, unlike solar or wind which depend on weather. PGE says it aims to add 600 MW of installed capacity over the next five years. The release does not give the stake percentage, price, deal structure or advisers.
context: Masdar says the investment expands its presence in Asia-Pacific and gives it access to Indonesia, which it describes as the world's second-largest geothermal market. Indonesia plans to raise geothermal capacity from 2.8 GW in 2022 to 6.2 GW by 2030. Masdar is already building the 145 MW Cirata floating solar plant in Indonesia and is targeting 100 GW of renewable capacity by 2030.

title: ArcLight completes roughly $2 billion sale of Great River Hydro to Hydro-Québec
summary: ArcLight Capital Partners has completed the sale of Great River Hydro to affiliates of Hydro-Québec for about $2 billion. Great River Hydro owns 13 hydroelectric stations in New England with a combined capacity of 589 MW. The sale closed on February 10, 2023.
details: The hydro stations sit along the Connecticut and Deerfield rivers in New England, and the company also holds co-located battery storage and solar development projects, meaning projects planned at the same sites as existing plants. Part of the power output is sold to utilities and municipalities under long-term supply agreements signed in 2021 and 2022. During ArcLight's ownership, upgrades added 29 GWh per year of generation and 8 MW of qualified capacity, and a pipeline of solar, storage and hydro efficiency projects totaling more than 230 MW of qualified capacity was developed. TD Securities acted as exclusive financial adviser to ArcLight and Latham & Watkins as its legal adviser.
context: ArcLight describes Great River Hydro as the largest conventional hydroelectric portfolio in New England. The sale ends an ownership period of more than five years that began with ArcLight's 2017 investment. ArcLight says it expects the company to keep playing a leading role in the regional energy transition under its new owner.

title: Fiera Infrastructure and Palisade Infrastructure agree to buy Amp US community solar and storage platform from Amp Energy
summary: A consortium of funds managed by Fiera Infrastructure and Palisade Infrastructure Group has agreed to buy all of the equity in Amp US from Canada-based Amp Energy. Amp US develops, owns and operates community solar and battery storage projects in the United States, with about 200 MW DC across 39 operating or under-construction projects.
details: Amp US is based in Denver, Colorado and has been active in the US since 2016. Community solar means mid-sized solar projects whose output is shared by local subscribers such as households and housing authorities. Besides the 39 projects, the company has a pipeline of further solar and storage projects. Palisade is investing through funds of Palisade Americas Management LLC and its Australian affiliate Palisade Impact. Closing is expected in March 2023, subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals. No price was disclosed.
context: The buyers link the deal to the Inflation Reduction Act of August 2022, which they say gives long-term policy support to state community solar programs. Palisade says the deal lifts its renewables capacity under management above 1.8 GW and is its third North American investment. Fiera says it diversifies its clean energy holdings in wind, utility-scale solar, waste-to-energy and hydro.

title: TransAlta to acquire 50% of Montem's 320 MW Tent Mountain pumped hydro storage project in Alberta

buyers.name: TransAlta Corporation
buyers.role: acquirer of 50% interest and project developer

summary: TransAlta has signed a definitive agreement to buy a 50% stake in the Tent Mountain Renewable Energy Complex, an early-stage 320 MW pumped hydro storage project in southwest Alberta, from Montem Resources. The price is about C$8 million at closing plus up to C$17 million in milestone payments, for a total of roughly C$25 million.
details: Pumped hydro stores energy by pumping water to an upper reservoir and releasing it through turbines when power is needed. The project would reuse legacy water reservoirs from past mining at the site and is designed to offer about 15 hours of storage. The deal covers land rights, fixed assets and intellectual property, including rights tied to a planned 100 MW offsite green hydrogen electrolyser and a 100 MW offsite wind project. The two companies will form a partnership with TransAlta as developer, construction could begin as early as 2026, and commercial operation is targeted between 2028 and 2030. Closing depends on conditions including Montem shareholder approval and is expected in March 2023.
context: TransAlta says long-duration storage like this is needed to keep the Alberta grid reliable as wind and solar grow, and it claims the site's existing upper reservoir makes the project cost competitive. The project has no offtake contract yet, meaning no buyer has agreed to purchase its output, and TransAlta plans to seek one during development. TransAlta states it takes on no liability for Montem's historical mining reclamation or environmental issues at the site.

sources.title: TransAlta Announces Acquisition of 50% Interest in Early-Stage Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Development Project

title: Eolian closes tax equity financing with Churchill Stateside fund for 200 MW Texas battery storage projects
target: Madero and Ignacio battery storage projects

advisors.name: Husch Blackwell LLP
advisors.role: legal adviser to Churchill Stateside Group

summary: Eolian, backed by Global Infrastructure Partners, has closed a tax equity investment from a fund managed by Churchill Stateside Group in two standalone battery storage projects in Mission, Texas. The Madero and Ignacio projects have a combined capacity of 200 MW. The financing amount was not disclosed.
details: The two projects share a single site in the Rio Grande Valley and are designed to store several hours of energy. They will operate on a merchant basis, meaning they earn revenue by trading in the ERCOT wholesale market rather than under a long-term fixed-price contract. Tax equity is a form of investment where an investor provides capital in exchange for the tax credits a project generates, here the Investment Tax Credit. Full commercial operation is expected later in 2023. Norton Rose Fulbright advised Eolian and Husch Blackwell advised Churchill Stateside.
context: Eolian says this is the first use of the Investment Tax Credit by a standalone utility-scale battery project, made possible by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, which extended the credit to storage without paired solar. The company claims the site will be the largest fully merchant battery project built worldwide by deliverable energy. It presents the projects as a way to support the strained Texas grid during hours of high demand or low renewable output.

title: Longroad Energy closes financing for 202 MWdc Umbriel Solar project in Texas

buyers.name: Zions Capital Markets
buyers.role: Coordinating Lead Arranger and Administrative Agent

summary: Longroad Energy reached financial close on Umbriel Solar, a 202 MWdc (150 MWac) solar project in Polk County, Texas, and started construction. Debt came from Zions Capital Markets, Silicon Valley Bank and Rabobank, and Longroad arranged tax equity separately.
details: Umbriel is a greenfield photovoltaic project that has been in development since 2017 and is expected to begin commercial operation by the end of 2023. Financial close means the funding agreements are signed and money can be drawn to build the project. The debt was led by Zions Capital Markets as coordinating lead arranger and administrative agent, with Silicon Valley Bank as coordinating lead arranger and Rabobank as joint lead arranger. Longroad also secured tax equity, a type of investment where investors fund part of the project in return for its US tax credits, without naming the investor. Entergy Texas will buy all output under a long-term power purchase agreement, McCarthy Building Companies will build the plant, and First Solar, Power Electronics and Nextracker supply modules, inverters and trackers.
context: The project is Longroad's sixth greenfield project in Texas to reach financial close and its first in the part of Texas served by the MISO grid operator. Longroad says the deal brings its Texas wind and solar projects to more than 1.7 GW. Entergy Texas says Umbriel will be its first solar resource to come online, helping diversify its supply.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Completes Financing and Commences Construction of 202 MWdc Umbriel Solar Project

title: WEC Energy Group agrees to buy 80% of Invenergy's 250 MW Samson I solar project in Texas
summary: WEC Energy Group has agreed to acquire an 80% ownership interest in the 250 MW Samson I Solar Energy Center in northeast Texas. The company expects its investment to total about $250 million. The project was developed and built by Invenergy.
details: Samson I sits about 140 miles northeast of Dallas and began commercial operation in May 2022. It sells its output to AT&T under a long-term power purchase agreement, which is a contract to buy electricity at agreed terms over many years. The project is the first phase of the five-phase Samson solar portfolio, which is planned to reach 1,300 MW across 18,000 acres. The deal still needs regulatory approvals before it can close.
context: This is the second solar investment in WEC's Infrastructure segment, which also holds or plans stakes in eight large wind farms, together totaling nearly 2 GW. WEC says the project qualifies for production tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act, a federal incentive paid per unit of power generated. The release describes Samson as the largest solar project under construction in the United States.

sources.title: WEC Energy Group to acquire 80% ownership of Samson I Solar Energy Center

title: Gardant Investor SGR agrees to buy 30% of preferred units in Canadian Solar's 124.2 MWp Italian solar fund
target: CSFS Fund I (30% of preferred units)
summary: Canadian Solar has signed an agreement to sell 30% of the preferred units in CSFS Fund I, its first Italian alternative investment fund, to Gardant Investor SGR. The fund holds seven solar projects totalling 124.2 MWp in Sicily, Sardinia and Lazio. No price was disclosed.
details: The seven projects are under construction and are expected to start commercial operation between March and December 2023. Canadian Solar developed them and will run operations and maintenance once built. Gardant has also committed to fund 30% of the construction capital spending. CSFS Fund I is a closed-ended real-estate reserved alternative investment fund, meaning a fund with a fixed pool of capital open only to professional investors, and it is managed by Finint Investments SGR, which helped structure the deal. Canadian Solar aims to sell a further 30% of preferred units to another financial investor and keep 40% non-preferred units over the long term.
context: Canadian Solar says the fund carries out its long-term asset ownership strategy in Italy, where it reports a solar pipeline above 1.8 GWp and a storage pipeline above 2 GWh. The company presents the deal as part of its shift from pure project development toward becoming an independent power producer, a company that owns and sells power from its own plants. For Gardant, an asset manager mainly focused on credit and impaired loans, the investment marks an entry into renewable energy, which it says fits its ESG goals.

sources.title: CANADIAN SOLAR PARTNERS WITH GARDANT SGR ON ITS FIRST ITALIAN ALTERNATIVE INVESTMENT FUND

title: Pacolet Milliken forms joint venture with Evensol to own two North Carolina landfill RNG projects
target: Upper Piedmont Renewables and Foothills Renewables RNG projects
summary: Greenville-based investment firm Pacolet Milliken closed a joint venture investment with biogas developer Evensol on January 18, 2023. The venture will own and operate two renewable natural gas projects at landfills in North Carolina, working in partnership with Duke Energy. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The two projects, Upper Piedmont Renewables and Foothills Renewables, capture gas released by decomposing landfill waste and clean it into renewable natural gas (RNG), a pipeline-quality fuel that can be injected into regional gas networks. Evensol began developing the projects several years ago and started construction in the fourth quarter of 2021. Once finished, the projects are expected to produce about 500,000 dekatherms of RNG per year combined. Kirkland & Ellis acted as legal adviser to Pacolet Milliken.
context: Pacolet already owns landfill gas projects that generate electricity, and it describes this deal as its first move into RNG. The firm says it intends to pursue further RNG investments with Evensol. The release links growing RNG demand to federal and state incentive programs such as the Renewable Fuel Standard and California's Low Carbon Fuel Standard.

sources.title: Pacolet Milliken Completes First Renewable Natural Gas Investment

title: Foss & Company closes first tranche of tax equity for Nautilus Solar's 44 MWdc US community solar portfolio
target: 44 MWdc community solar portfolio in Maine, Minnesota and Maryland
