summary: Foss & Company closed the first tranche of a tax equity partnership with Nautilus Solar Energy, investing about US$42 million. The money backs more than 44 MWdc of community solar projects in Maine, Minnesota and Maryland.
details: Tax equity is an arrangement where an investor puts money into a project in exchange for the right to use its federal tax credits and other tax benefits. The portfolio consists of community solar farms, which sell shares of their output to local subscribers such as households and small businesses. Nautilus US Power Holdco, an affiliate of Nautilus, will be the long-term owner, while Nautilus oversees construction, operations and subscriber management. The projects are expected to be fully operational in 2023. This is described as the first tranche, meaning further investment rounds may follow.
context: Nautilus says the partnership lets it bring community solar into more US markets and capture more of the projects' value. Foss says the sites aim to give low-income families and small businesses access to cheaper clean power once running. Nautilus is owned by Power Sustainable, part of Power Corporation of Canada, and Foss reports having deployed over US$8 billion in tax equity.

sources.title: Foss & Company Announces Tax Equity Partnership with Nautilus Solar Energy, LLC

title: Thornton Tomasetti invests in rooftop wind technology firm Aeromine Technologies
summary: Engineering firm Thornton Tomasetti, through its investment vehicle TTWiiN IP, has taken part in a funding round for Aeromine Technologies, a developer of bladeless rooftop wind systems. The investment comes as the AEC Angels investor group, of which Thornton Tomasetti is a member, endorsed Aeromine. The size of the round and the amount invested were not disclosed.
details: Aeromine makes a stationary wind unit with no external moving parts that mounts on the edge of flat commercial rooftops and uses airfoil-style aerodynamics to capture building airflow. Typical systems use 20 to 40 units and installations are usually 50 kW or larger. The company says the units need about 10 percent of the roof space solar panels require and can work alongside existing rooftop solar and building electrical systems. BASF Corporation is piloting the system at its manufacturing plant in Wyandotte, Michigan. AEC Angels is a seed through Series B investment platform whose members also include STO Building Group, Syska Hennessy and SHoP Architects.
context: The deal is an early-stage venture investment rather than a project transaction, aimed at bringing wind generation to the distributed rooftop market that has largely been served by solar. Aeromine claims its technology can be up to 50 percent more productive than other renewable options and, combined with solar, could meet up to all of a building's onsite energy needs. AEC Angels says its members will also lend industry expertise to help the company grow.

sources.title: AEC Angels Endorses Aeromine, Thornton Tomasetti Invests in their Breakthrough Wind Energy Solution

title: Ørsted to buy PSEG's 25% stake in Ocean Wind 1 offshore wind project
summary: PSEG has agreed to sell its 25% equity stake in the Ocean Wind 1 offshore wind project off New Jersey to Ørsted. The deal would give Ørsted full ownership of the project. No price or capacity was disclosed in the release.
details: Ocean Wind 1 is an offshore wind project under development serving New Jersey. After the sale Ørsted will lead development, while PSEG will help build onshore infrastructure. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2023, subject to customary closing conditions. First power is scheduled for the end of 2024, with full commissioning expected in 2025.
context: PSEG said it is stepping aside so that an investor better able to use the project's tax benefits can join, allowing a more efficient tax structure. A tax investor is a party that funds a project partly in exchange for the right to use its tax credits. Ørsted says it remains confident the project will start commercial operations as planned, and PSEG says it will keep supporting offshore wind in the state through transmission and port work.

sources.title: PSEG to Sell its 25% Equity Stake in Ocean Wind 1 to Ørsted

title: Longroad Energy reaches financial close on Sun Streams 3 solar-plus-storage project in Arizona

buyers.name: CIBC
buyers.role: lead lender and coordinating lead arranger

summary: Longroad Energy has closed debt and tax equity financing for Sun Streams 3, a solar and battery project in Maricopa County, Arizona, and started construction. The project pairs 285 MWdc of solar panels with a 215 MWac / 860 MWh battery system. Loans were led by CIBC and KeyBank, with U.S. Bank as tax equity investor.
details: The project combines 285 MWdc of solar with a four-hour battery system of 215 MW and 860 MWh, connecting to the grid at the Hassayampa switchyard. Debt was led by CIBC and KeyBank, joined by ANZ, Commerzbank, PNC and Silicon Valley Bank, while U.S. Bank provides tax equity, meaning it invests in exchange for the project's federal tax credits. Arizona Public Service will buy all the output under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to purchase electricity at agreed terms. McCarthy is the construction contractor, First Solar supplies modules and Powin delivers the batteries. Commercial operation is expected in 2024.
context: Longroad says Sun Streams 3 will be the largest solar and storage project in its operating fleet and part of a 4 GW portfolio it holds in Arizona. The company bought the project from First Solar in early 2021. Longroad expects the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act to support further development in the state, and APS says the power will help its goal of a carbon-free mix by 2050.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Completes Financing of Sun Streams 3, a 285 MWdc Solar and 215 MWac / 860 MWh Storage Project

title: NaaS and HyperStrong form energy storage joint venture NewLink Hyper in China
summary: Chinese EV charging services company NaaS Technology, through its subsidiary Nengcang Technology, and storage system integrator HyperStrong agreed to set up a joint venture called NewLink Hyper. The venture will develop energy storage business in China.
details: NewLink Hyper is intended to offer storage solutions across many uses, which the partners call all-scenario, drawing on NaaS's customer base and use cases and HyperStrong's products and technology. HyperStrong develops energy management, battery management and battery evaluation systems used on the grid side, generation side and customer side. The release does not give ownership splits, investment amounts, capacity targets or timelines.
context: NaaS says growing solar, wind and EV use is making power supply and demand less balanced, which raises the need for storage. HyperStrong cites Chinese national targets for new energy storage installations to exceed 30 GW by 2025. The deal moves NaaS, mainly a charging services firm, into the storage market.

sources.title: NaaS and HyperStrong Establish Joint Venture to Develop All-Scenario Energy Storage Solutions

title: Southern Current signs PPA with Dominion Energy South Carolina for Lone Star Solar and storage project
summary: Southern Current, a developer owned by energyRe, has signed a power purchase agreement with Dominion Energy South Carolina for the Lone Star Solar project in Calhoun County, South Carolina. The project pairs 107.8 MWdc of solar capacity with a 198 MWh battery system.
details: A power purchase agreement is a long-term contract under which a buyer, here the utility, agrees to purchase the electricity a project produces. Lone Star Solar will sit on a 572-acre site and is expected to begin commercial operation in 2024. The release puts the investment at about $200 million and says construction will create roughly 185 jobs. The agreement still needs acceptance for filing by the Public Service Commission of South Carolina and other regulatory approvals. The length of the contract and pricing were not disclosed.
context: The company says the battery will be one of the largest in the Carolinas and the largest on the Dominion Energy South Carolina network. energyRe bought Southern Current in the third quarter of 2022, gaining a development pipeline of more than 9 GW, and this contract is presented as part of building out its national renewable portfolio. The company also claims the project will generate over $10 million in local property taxes over its life.

sources.title: Southern Current, an energyRe Company, Secures Power Purchase Agreement with Dominion Energy South Carolina for 108 MWdc Solar and 198 MWh Storage Project

title: ENGIE acquires 1,250 MW Arizona solar and storage development projects from Revolve
target: Bouse Solar and Storage Project and Parker Solar and Storage Project (Revolve Renewable AZ LLC and Revolve Parker Solar LLC)
summary: ENGIE, through its US subsidiary ENGIE IR Holdings, has bought two early-stage solar and battery storage projects totalling 1,250 MW in La Paz County, Arizona, from Canadian developer Revolve Renewable Power. The deal closed with an upfront payment of US$2 million, with further payments tied to development milestones.
details: The portfolio comprises the 1,000 MW Bouse project on about 6,155 acres and the 250 MW Parker project on about 1,530 acres, both on federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management. ENGIE took 100% of the two project companies free of cash and debt and will fund all further development. The remaining payments depend on completing further grid connection studies, ENGIE issuing a notice to proceed (the formal go-ahead for construction) to its building contractor, and each project reaching commercial operation. A put option lets ENGIE sell the projects back to Revolve, with costs refunded, for a limited time after the next interconnection study results, expected in 2023. Agentis Capital was Revolve's financial adviser, with Baker Botts and Miller Thomson as legal counsel.
context: Revolve says this is the first sale of utility-scale projects from its US development pipeline and that the total price falls within its earlier guidance. The company states the proceeds will help it advance its remaining roughly 2,450 MW portfolio and look for new early-stage projects. The deal shows a common model in which small developers sell projects at an early stage to large utilities, with much of the price deferred until risks are reduced.

sources.title: Revolve Announces Sale of 1,250MW of Utility Scale Solar and Storage Projects

title: Enfinity Global completes acquisition of 400 MW US operating solar portfolio from Capital Dynamics
target: 400 MW portfolio of 28 operating solar plants in California, North Carolina and Idaho
summary: Enfinity Global has closed its purchase of a 400 MW portfolio of 28 operating utility-scale solar plants from Capital Dynamics. The assets are located in California, North Carolina and Idaho. The purchase price was not disclosed.
details: The 28 solar plants all began commercial operation (COD, the date a plant starts selling power) within the past five years and sell their output under long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts to sell electricity at agreed terms, with investment-grade utilities. The portfolio generates about 1,175 GWh a year and, according to the release, roughly $45 million in annual EBITDA, a measure of operating earnings. The definitive agreement was signed in September 2022. Funds managed by AB CarVal and Nomura acted as co-financing partners, with additional lending at closing from Bayerische Landesbank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Fifth Third Bank and Zions Bancorporation. CCA Capital and McDermott Will & Emery advised Enfinity Global.
context: The deal significantly expands Enfinity Global's operating footprint in the United States. The company says it has a global portfolio of more than 7 GW across operation, construction and development, and plans further US growth through its 1.6 GW in-house pipeline and additional acquisitions and developer partnerships.

sources.title: Enfinity Global solidifies its US presence with the acquisition of 400 MW of operating solar projects

title: Seminole Financial Services and Blackstone Credit close $104 million construction loan for Revity Energy's 55 MW Rhode Island solar project
target: 55+ MW solar project in Rhode Island
summary: Seminole Financial Services, working with Blackstone Credit, closed a $104 million debt facility for Revity Energy. The money funds construction of a solar project of more than 55 MW in Rhode Island.
details: The facility is a construction loan, meaning debt used to pay for building the plant before it starts operating. The project is described as larger than 55 MW and is located in Rhode Island. The release does not name the project site, the offtaker or the expected completion date. No legal or financial advisers are named.
context: This is the 16th project Seminole has financed for Revity and its affiliates. Seminole says it has committed about $2.2 billion in debt and tax credit equity, a form of investment where investors get tax benefits from a project, to more than 325 solar and wind installations since 2009. Revity reports nearly 100 MW in operation in Rhode Island and Massachusetts, with 62 MW under construction and 95 MW in development.

sources.title: Seminole Financial Services and Blackstone Credit Provide Financing for Revity Energy's 55 MW Solar Project in Rhode Island

title: Castleton Commodities International acquires majority stake in Dutch storage developer S4 Energy
summary: A subsidiary of Castleton Commodities International (CCI) has bought a majority stake in S4 Energy, a Netherlands-based company that develops, owns and runs large battery storage systems. S4 Energy operates 25 MW of storage in the Netherlands. The price and exact stake size were not disclosed.
details: S4 Energy builds hybrid storage plants that pair grid-scale lithium-ion batteries with its own KINEXT flywheel technology, a spinning mass that stores energy mechanically. Its operating portfolio totals 25 MW in the Netherlands, and it has further projects at various stages of development and construction. The company aims to build more than 300 MW of long-duration storage across Western Europe over the next three years. The sellers, deal value and advisers were not named in the release.
context: CCI, a global energy commodity trader that also owns infrastructure, says it wants to grow S4 Energy into a large pan-European storage platform and views storage as key to decarbonisation and grid stability. S4 Energy's management says CCI's network and access to capital should let it speed up project deployment and promote its flywheel technology in other uses.

sources.title: CCI Acquires Majority Stake in European Battery Storage Company S4 Energy BV

title: PACE Loan Group closes $8 million C-PACE loan for carport solar at 1000 Omega in Pittsburgh
target: Carport solar PV system at 1000 Omega Corporate Center, Pittsburgh
summary: PACE Loan Group closed an $8 million C-PACE loan to fund a carport solar system at the 1000 Omega corporate office in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The system is rated 3.538 MW on the panel side and 2.874 MW on the grid side, and the lender says it is the largest C-PACE deal in Allegheny County and Western Pennsylvania.
details: The solar panels will be mounted on carports in the property's parking lot, supplying power to the building and selling surplus electricity to the local grid. C-PACE, short for Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy, is a type of loan for building energy upgrades that the owner repays through property tax assessments over 20 to 30 years. The loan received consent from a national life insurance company, which typically means an existing mortgage lender on the property agreed to it. Sustainable Energy Fund, a nonprofit, administers the Allegheny County C-PACE program. The project is expected to save about $378,407 per year.
context: PACE Loan Group says it is seeing more solar projects financed this way because of tax incentives in the Inflation Reduction Act. The deal is presented as a sign of growing C-PACE use in Western Pennsylvania, where the program administrator expects more projects to follow.

sources.title: PACE Loan Group Invests In Solar at 1000 Omega Corporate Center

title: Suburban Propane acquires two RNG facilities from Equilibrium Capital and forms RNG development venture
target: Two operating renewable natural gas and biogas facilities in Stanfield, Arizona and Columbus, Ohio

advisors.name: Evercore
advisors.role: financial advisor to Equilibrium Capital Group

summary: Suburban Propane, through its subsidiary Suburban Renewable Energy, bought two operating renewable natural gas (RNG) and biogas facilities in the US from Equilibrium Capital Group for $190 million. The two companies also set up a development company to build further RNG projects, which Suburban will own about 70% of.
details: The assets are a large RNG plant in Stanfield, Arizona with seven anaerobic digesters (tanks where bacteria break down manure into gas) using manure from about 55,000 dairy cows and connected to an interstate pipeline, and a food waste facility in Columbus, Ohio that earns tipping fees (charges for accepting waste) and has a project underway to upgrade its biogas into RNG for transport fuel. Suburban also gets option rights to a third RNG facility in the Midwest being developed by Equilibrium. The purchase is funded with about $120 million drawn on Suburban's revolving credit facility and the assumption of about $80 million of existing green bonds. The new development company is meant to invest about $155 million in future RNG projects, split roughly 70% Suburban and 30% Equilibrium once fully funded. Signing and closing happened at the same time after regulatory approvals were cleared.
context: The deal gives Suburban, mainly a propane distributor, immediate scale in renewable fuels alongside its own RNG project at Adirondack Farms in New York and its investments in rDME and hydrogen. Suburban expects the acquisition to add to its distributable cash flow in fiscal 2024 and says RNG will benefit from state low carbon fuel standards and the Inflation Reduction Act.

sources.title: Suburban Propane Partners, L.P. to Acquire Renewable Natural Gas ("RNG") Production Assets from Equilibrium Capital Group and Establishes Partnership for the Development of Additional RNG Projects

title: EQT Infrastructure VI agrees to buy US distributed solar platform Madison Energy Investments from Stonepeak
summary: EQT's Infrastructure VI fund has agreed to acquire Madison Energy Investments (MEI), a US developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and storage projects, from affiliates of Stonepeak. MEI has built a portfolio of more than 386 MW across the US. No price was disclosed.
details: MEI, founded in 2019 and based in Vienna, Virginia, builds solar and storage projects located on or near customer sites, known as distributed generation, for commercial and industrial users and for community solar programs, where multiple local customers share output from one project. Its management team says it has deployed over 800 MW across about 500 projects over their careers. The deal requires customary conditions and approvals and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2023. Barclays acted as financial adviser and Simpson Thacher & Bartlett as legal adviser to EQT.
context: This is the first deal signed by EQT Infrastructure VI, a fund targeting EUR 20 billion, which activates the fund and its management fees. EQT says it plans to give MEI growth capital, digital expertise and a wider customer base to speed up deployment. The companies point to customer demand and supportive federal and state policy as drivers of growth in distributed renewables.

sources.title: EQT Infrastructure to acquire Madison Energy Investments, a leading integrated US solar distributed generation platform

title: EQT Infrastructure VI agrees to acquire US distributed solar platform Madison Energy Investments from Stonepeak
summary: EQT's Infrastructure VI fund has agreed to buy Madison Energy Investments (MEI), a US developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and storage projects, from affiliates of Stonepeak. MEI has built a portfolio of more than 386 MW across the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: MEI, founded in 2019 and based in Vienna, Virginia, builds distributed generation, meaning smaller solar and storage projects located on or near the customer's site rather than large grid-scale plants. Its customers are commercial and industrial businesses and community solar subscribers, where many local users share the output of one project. EQT says it will provide growth capital, digital expertise and access to more customers. The deal requires customary conditions and approvals and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2023. Barclays acted as financial adviser and Simpson Thacher & Bartlett as legal adviser to EQT.
context: This is the first deal signed by EQT Infrastructure VI, a fund targeting EUR 20 billion, which activates the fund and starts its management fees. EQT says the purchase fits its thematic strategy in renewables and its prior solar experience. MEI's management describes the move as the start of a new growth phase, citing policy support and customer demand for cost savings and energy resilience.

sources.title: EQT Infrastructure to acquire Madison Energy Investments, a leading integrated US solar distributed generation platform

title: Basin Electric signs 25-year PPA for 200 MW from ENGIE's North Bend Wind project in South Dakota
summary: Basin Electric Power Cooperative has agreed to buy the output of ENGIE North America's 200 MW North Bend Wind project in South Dakota under a 25-year power purchase agreement. The project sits in Hughes and Hyde counties.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific plant at agreed terms, here for 25 years. North Bend Wind will have 71 turbines spread over about 47,000 acres near Harold, South Dakota, inside Basin Electric's service area. ENGIE will develop, build and operate the project, which is expected to begin operating in late 2023. ENGIE estimates more than 250 construction jobs and 8 to 10 longer-term local operating roles.
context: The contract adds wind power to Basin Electric's generation portfolio of more than 7,000 MW, which serves 131 member cooperatives across nine states. ENGIE claims the project will produce enough power for about 73,000 average US homes and cut emissions by up to 620,000 tonnes of CO2e a year. ENGIE says it operates or is building nearly 5 GW of wind, solar and storage in the US and Canada and added 12 GW to its pipeline in 2022.

sources.title: Basin Electric Power Cooperative and ENGIE announce 200 MW power purchase agreement for new South Dakota wind project

title: Globeleq signs US$72 million debt financing for 35 MW Menengai geothermal project in Kenya

buyers.name: African Development Bank
buyers.role: mandated lead arranger and senior lender

buyers.name: Eastern and Southern African Trade & Development Bank

summary: Globeleq has signed agreements with the African Development Bank, Finnfund and TDB for US$72 million of debt to fund the 35 MW Menengai geothermal project in Nakuru County, Kenya. The headline puts the total project at US$108 million, with Globeleq providing the equity.
details: Menengai is a new-build geothermal plant in the first phase of the wider Menengai complex, Kenya's second large geothermal field after Olkaria. The state-owned Geothermal Development Company will supply steam under a 25-year agreement, and Kenya Power will buy the electricity under a power purchase agreement of the same length. AfDB says it is providing US$29.5 million in senior debt, meaning loans repaid first, mobilised US$22.4 million of co-financing, arranged US$20 million of low-cost Clean Technology Fund money to help keep the tariff affordable, and will offer a US$4 million partial risk guarantee that covers lenders against certain government-related risks. Construction is expected to start in the first quarter of 2023 after financial close, the point when funds become available, with commercial operation targeted for 2025 and Globeleq operating the plant.
context: This is Globeleq's first geothermal project, and the company is owned 70% by British International Investment and 30% by Norfund. The project was among green investments the Kenyan and UK governments pledged to fast-track at COP27. The parties say it will supply low-cost baseload power, meaning steady round-the-clock output, and let GDC earn revenue from its steam resources.

sources.title: Globeleq Signs Financing Agreement with Senior Lenders on US$108 million Menengai Geothermal Project in Kenya

title: Element Energy closes first $28 million of Series B round for second-life battery storage

buyers.name: Unnamed large clean energy generation company

summary: Element Energy, a Menlo Park, California battery management technology company, closed the first $28 million of its Series B funding round. The round was co-led by Cohort Ventures and an unnamed large clean energy generator, with existing backers also taking part.
details: Series B is a later-stage venture funding round used to grow a company after early product development. Element says the money will fund assets, logistics and infrastructure for utility-scale deployments of second-life EV batteries, meaning used electric vehicle batteries repurposed for grid storage. The company has secured over 2.5 GWh of used EV batteries and received a $7.9 million US Department of Energy award for a planned 50 MWh battery project next to a wind farm in Texas. It plans gigawatt-hour scale grid-connected deployments in 2023 and 2024. Marvell Technology CEO Matt Murphy also joined the company's board.
context: The company says its battery management system improves safety, energy throughput and lifespan of large battery systems, and that the Texas project is believed to be the largest second-life EV battery installation on the US grid. The release cites McKinsey estimates of more than 200 GWh of second-life batteries available globally by 2030, framing reuse as a way to cut emissions and raw material needs.

sources.title: ELEMENT ENERGY, A PIONEER IN BATTERY STORAGE TECHNOLOGY, SECURES $28M SERIES B GROWTH CAPITAL

title: Keystone Development + Investment signs 18-month renewable power supply deal with ENGIE Resources for Philadelphia complex
summary: Commercial real estate firm Keystone Development + Investment agreed to buy power from ENGIE Resources, a unit of ENGIE North America, under an 18-month contract. The supply comes from the Cambria wind farm in Pennsylvania plus renewable energy credits, and is meant to cover all forecast electricity use at The Washington, a three-building complex in Philadelphia.
details: The agreement combines energy from the Cambria wind farm in Cambria County, Pennsylvania with renewable energy credits (RECs) from unrelated sources. A REC is a certificate representing the environmental benefit of one megawatt-hour of renewable power, which gives developers an extra income stream. The release says the RECs bought over the contract term will cut CO2 emissions by 11,875 metric tons, based on an EPA calculator. Industrial Energy of Wayne, Pennsylvania advised on the deal. No price or wind farm capacity was disclosed.
context: Keystone describes the deal as the first step in moving its property portfolio to renewable energy, and says tenants increasingly want carbon-neutral buildings. The firm holds about 10 million square feet of office and mixed-use space along the US East Coast. Its adviser says interest is growing among end users in supporting renewables through such purchases.

sources.title: Keystone Development + Investment Teams with ENGIE for Renewable Energy

title: Enhanced Capital and Crossroads fund Solar Landscape's 50.5 MWdc New Jersey community solar portfolio
target: 50.5 MWdc community solar portfolio of 46 rooftop systems in New Jersey
summary: Impact investor Enhanced Capital, together with Crossroads Impact Corp, has provided development capital to New Jersey developer Solar Landscape. The funding backs a 50.5 MWdc community solar portfolio of 46 rooftop systems in New Jersey. The amount invested was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of 46 solar installations on commercial warehouse rooftops across New Jersey and is expected to generate over 50 million kWh a year. It is part of New Jersey's community solar program, in which residents who cannot install panels themselves subscribe to a shared solar project and receive bill credits, here aimed at low- and moderate-income households. Development capital is money provided to fund projects before or during construction. Enhanced Capital says its investments combine flexible lending with state and federal tax credits. Under an advisory agreement, Enhanced Capital sources and manages such assets on behalf of Crossroads.
context: Solar Landscape describes the portfolio as the largest community solar portfolio in New Jersey to date. Enhanced Capital claims the projects will lower participating households' utility costs by 20% on average. Enhanced Capital has invested in several Solar Landscape transactions since 2020, and Solar Landscape says it plans to expand community solar nationwide.

sources.title: Impact Investor Enhanced Capital Invests in Solar Landscape Community Solar Projects in New Jersey

title: SunVest Solar closes $154 million debt and tax equity financing for 56 MW US solar portfolio

buyers.name: Guardian Life Insurance Company of America
buyers.role: tax equity partner of Rockwood Group

target: 56 MW solar portfolio in Illinois, Maine, Minnesota and Wisconsin
summary: SunVest Solar has closed $154 million of financing for a 56 MW portfolio of solar projects across four US states. The package combines a $113 million debt facility led by Silicon Valley Bank with $41 million of tax equity from Rockwood Group, working with Guardian Life.
details: The portfolio spans Illinois, Maine, Minnesota and Wisconsin, with construction at 10 projects already underway and the rest to be built in stages through 2023. The debt facility includes a construction loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term funding repaid when tax equity investors pay in) and a permanent loan. Tax equity is investment from parties that receive the projects' tax credits in return for funding. Power will be sold to a regulated utility under a long-term power purchase agreement and to commercial and residential customers through community solar subscriptions, where local users subscribe to a share of a shared solar farm. SunVest will own and operate the portfolio through a subsidiary.
context: SunVest says this is the largest portfolio it has developed and built since it was founded in 2009. The company describes the mix of states and revenue sources as giving the portfolio broad diversification. SunVest also reports a development pipeline of nearly 2 GW and expects its assets under management to reach 250 MW in 2023.

sources.title: SunVest Solar Closes $154 Million of Debt and Tax Equity Financing for 56 MW Solar Portfolio

title: Leyline Renewable Capital provides bridge loan to Westbridge for 278 MW Georgetown Solar in Alberta
summary: Leyline Renewable Capital, a US lender to renewable developers, closed a loan to Westbridge Renewable Energy Corp. for the 278 MW Georgetown Solar project in southern Alberta, Canada. The project may borrow up to the US dollar equivalent of C$4.83 million. It is Leyline's first loan outside the United States.
details: Georgetown Solar sits on 710 acres of privately owned, non-agricultural land in Vulcan County, Alberta. Westbridge will use the money to pay a security deposit required by the Alberta Electricity System Operator, known as the Generating Unit Owner's Contribution, which is a payment a generator makes toward grid connection costs. The loan is a bridge facility, meaning short-term funding that covers the gap between early development and construction. The project has recently received power plant and substation approval from the Alberta Utilities Commission.
context: Leyline describes the deal as its entry into new markets and says it wants to back developers in regions like Alberta that have relied heavily on fossil fuels. Westbridge says the loan lets it advance its flagship project without issuing new shares, which would dilute existing shareholders. Westbridge is a listed developer of solar and battery storage projects in Canada, the US and the UK.

sources.title: Leyline Closes Its First International Loan with Westbridge Renewable Energy Corporation

title: Modern Niagara makes equity investment in biogas upgrading firm Hydron Energy
summary: Canadian building contractor Modern Niagara has agreed to make an undisclosed equity investment in Hydron Energy and form a strategic partnership with it. Hydron, based in North Vancouver, is developing a system that upgrades biogas into renewable natural gas (RNG), a pipeline-quality fuel made from organic waste.
details: The partnership covers supplying waste-to-RNG plants, working together on products, and an equity stake in Hydron, meaning Modern Niagara buys part ownership in the company. The money is meant for commercializing Hydron's INTRUPTor upgrading system and building manufacturing capacity for its modules at Hydron's North Vancouver facility. Modern Niagara's vice president of energy solutions, Kevin Spencer, will join Hydron's board. The size of the investment and the stake were not disclosed. Hydron has also received non-dilutive funding, meaning grants that do not give away ownership, from the B.C. Centre for Innovation and Clean Energy.
context: Hydron claims its technology can cut the capital and operating costs of turning biogas into RNG by up to 50% and makes small plants matched to local waste supplies practical. The companies say the deal targets small and medium RNG producers they view as under-served. They expect the partnership to speed up the sale of Hydron's first plant in Canada.

sources.title: Hydron Energy and Modern Niagara Announce Strategic Partnership and Investment to Accelerate First Product Launch to Market

title: CVE North America completes purchase of 41 MW New York community solar portfolio from Saturn Power
target: Portfolio of seven community solar projects in upstate New York (41 MW)
summary: CVE North America, a New York City based solar producer, has completed its acquisition of seven community solar projects totaling 41 MW in upstate New York from Canadian developer Saturn Power. No price was disclosed.
details: The seven projects sit in National Grid's utility territory and were developed by Saturn Power to Notice to Proceed status, meaning they are cleared to start construction. CVE plans to begin building by the end of 2022 and will own and operate the assets, using outside contractors for construction and for signing up community solar subscribers. Community solar lets households and businesses subscribe to a share of a local solar farm and receive bill credits for their share of the output. The projects will take part in New York's Value of Distributed Energy Resources (VDER) program, which compensates power from small local generators.
context: CVE says the deal expands its presence in New York, which it describes as the largest US community solar market. The projects form part of a 13-project, 73 MW New York portfolio expected to be under construction through early 2023, alongside 37 MW operating in Massachusetts and a pipeline of over 250 MW. The company claims the portfolio will power about 8,500 homes and help low and moderate income subscribers lower their bills, and it targets over 450 MW in the US by 2026.

sources.title: CVE North America Announces the completion of a 41-megawatt New York Solar Portfolio acquisition from Saturn Power

title: Invenergy wins US$145.3 million offshore wind lease off central California

sellers.name: U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management

target: Offshore wind lease OCS-P 0565 (80,418 acres off central California)
summary: Invenergy, through its subsidiary Invenergy California Offshore LLC, was named provisional winner of a seabed lease covering 80,418 acres off the central California coast. Its winning bid of US$145.3 million secured lease OCS-P 0565 in the federal government's first West Coast offshore wind lease sale.
details: The lease was awarded by the U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM), the federal agency that manages offshore energy development. Invenergy is a provisional winner, meaning the award still has to be finalized. The site is intended for floating offshore wind, where turbines sit on anchored floating platforms instead of fixed foundations, which suits deep Pacific waters. No project capacity or timeline was given in the release.
context: Invenergy says the lease doubles its offshore wind portfolio and is its first floating offshore wind lease, adding to the Leading Light Wind lease it and partners secured in the New York Bight earlier in 2022. The company says it is the only American-owned provisional winner in the California sale and claims this positions it to build domestic offshore wind know-how.

sources.title: INVENERGY SECURES OFFSHORE WIND LEASE OFF CENTRAL CALIFORNIA COAST

title: Air Products and AES plan US$4 billion green hydrogen joint venture in Wilbarger County, Texas

buyers.name: Air Products
buyers.role: 50% joint venture partner and exclusive offtaker

buyers.name: The AES Corporation
buyers.role: 50% joint venture partner and renewable developer

summary: Air Products and AES announced plans to invest about US$4 billion in a green hydrogen production facility in Wilbarger County, Texas. The project pairs roughly 1.4 GW of wind and solar generation with electrolyzers able to produce more than 200 metric tons of hydrogen per day.
details: The two companies will jointly and equally own the wind, solar and electrolyzer assets. Electrolyzers split water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity, and the hydrogen counts as green because the power comes from renewables. Air Products will be the sole buyer and marketer of the hydrogen under a 30-year offtake contract. Commercial operations are targeted for 2027, and the project still depends on local permits and on local, state and federal incentives. The release notes that AIMCo holds 25% of the growth projects in AES's US clean energy business.
context: The companies say the plant would be the largest green hydrogen facility in the United States and aim it at mobility and industrial customers. They claim it could avoid more than 1.6 million metric tons of CO2 a year if the hydrogen displaced diesel in heavy trucks. They also expect over 1,300 construction jobs, 115 permanent jobs and about US$500 million in state tax benefits over the project's life.

sources.title: Air Products and AES Announce Plans to Invest Approximately $4 Billion to Build First Mega-scale Green Hydrogen Production Facility in Texas

title: Air Products and AES form joint venture to build roughly $4 billion green hydrogen facility in Texas

buyers.name: Air Products
buyers.role: 50% joint venture partner and exclusive offtaker

target: Green hydrogen production facility with about 1.4 GW of wind and solar in Wilbarger County, Texas
summary: Air Products and AES plan to invest about $4 billion in a green hydrogen plant in Wilbarger County, Texas. The project pairs roughly 1.4 GW of wind and solar power with electrolyzers able to make more than 200 metric tons of hydrogen per day.
details: The two companies will each own half of the renewable generation and the electrolyzers, which are machines that split water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity. Air Products will be the sole buyer and seller of the hydrogen under a 30-year offtake contract, meaning a long-term agreement to purchase the output. Commercial operation is targeted for 2027. The project still depends on local permits and on local, state and federal incentives. AIMCo holds a 25 percent stake in the growth projects of AES's US clean energy business.
context: The companies say it will be the largest green hydrogen facility in the United States, aimed at heavy trucking and industrial customers. They claim it could cut more than 1.6 million metric tons of CO2 a year if all output replaced diesel in heavy trucks, and expect about 1,300 construction jobs and around $500 million in state tax benefits over its life.

sources.title: Air Products and AES Announce Plans to Invest Approximately $4 Billion to Build First Mega-scale Green Hydrogen Production Facility in Texas

title: Ocean Winds and CPP Investments joint venture Golden State Wind wins 2 GW Morro Bay offshore wind lease

sellers.name: U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management

target: Offshore wind lease area OCS-P 0564, Morro Bay, California
summary: Golden State Wind, a new 50/50 joint venture between Ocean Winds and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, won an 80,418-acre offshore wind lease off central California with a bid of US$150.3 million. The Morro Bay site could host about 2 GW of floating offshore wind.
details: The lease area, OCS-P 0564, was one of five sites offered by the U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management in an auction off the California coast. Floating offshore wind means turbines sit on anchored floating platforms rather than fixed foundations, which suits deep waters. Each partner holds half of the project. As part of the bid, the partners committed US$30 million to workforce development and supply chain programs, and they say the fully built site could supply the equivalent of about 900,000 homes.
context: The auction was the first floating offshore wind lease sale in the U.S. and the first offshore wind lease sale of any kind on the West Coast. California targets 5 GW of floating offshore wind by 2030 and the U.S. 15 GW by 2035. Ocean Winds, owned by EDP Renewables and ENGIE, cites its floating wind track record including Windfloat Atlantic in Portugal, while CPP Investments says the deal fits its emissions reduction and return goals.

sources.title: Golden State Wind, a Joint Venture of Ocean Winds and CPP Investments, Wins 2 GW California Wind Energy Lease

title: Leyline Renewable Capital lends up to CAD$4.83 million to Westbridge for Georgetown solar and storage project
summary: Westbridge Renewable Energy's subsidiary Georgetown Solar Inc. signed a loan of up to the US dollar equivalent of CAD$4.83 million with a lending entity set up by Leyline Renewable Capital. The money will fund a grid connection payment required by Alberta's grid operator for the Georgetown solar and battery storage project in Canada.
details: The loan agreement is dated December 5, 2022 and lets Georgetown borrow up to the stated maximum. It carries 12% annual interest, matures 12 months after signing, and is backed by a first priority claim on Georgetown's assets, meaning the lender is paid first if the borrower defaults. The funds cover the Generating Unit Owner's Contribution, a security payment that the Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO) requires from projects seeking grid connection. The project had earlier received power plant and substation approval from the Alberta Utilities Commission. Capacity figures were not given in the release.
context: Westbridge says the loan bridges the gap between development and construction for its flagship project and lets it grow without issuing new shares, which would dilute existing shareholders. The company presents itself as one of few listed pure-play Canadian solar developers, with projects in Canada, the US and the UK.

sources.title: Westbridge Secures CAD$4,830,000 Financing for Georgetown Solar PV and Battery Energy Storage Project

title: Hover Energy acquires solar developer Shine Development Partners
summary: Dallas-based Hover Energy, which makes rooftop wind-powered microgrids, has acquired Shine Development Partners, a Texas developer of commercial solar and battery storage projects. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: Shine develops, finances and manages commercial solar, energy storage and distributed wind projects, with offices in Houston and Dallas. It says it has completed more than 100 solar projects across 10 US states and abroad since 2013, and has 50 MW of projects under contract for future deployment. Shine's development-stage assets and staff move to Hover as part of the deal, and Shine CEO Rajiv Pandya becomes Hover's chief operating officer. A microgrid is a small local power system, here combining rooftop wind turbines, solar panels and optional batteries to supply a building.
context: Hover says the acquisition brings solar capability in-house as it moves from research and product development toward large-scale production and global rollout of its patented wind-powered microgrid. The company presents the combined business as able to offer commercial and industrial customers lower power costs and greater energy security.

sources.title: Hover Energy acquires premier solar company, Shine Development Partners

title: Longroad Energy acquires 98 MWdc Titan Solar project in California from Sunpin
summary: Longroad Energy has closed its purchase of the operating 98 MWdc Titan Solar project in Imperial County, California, from Sunpin Holdings. Great Bay Renewables made a royalty investment in the project at closing to help fund the acquisition. No price was disclosed.
details: Titan has been in commercial operation since December 2020 and sits in the Imperial Irrigation District service area. It sells its power into the California grid market run by CAISO using firm transmission rights from the district, and the release says it supplies enough energy for more than 30,000 customers. Great Bay Renewables financed the deal through a royalty investment, meaning it provides money in exchange for a share of the project's future revenue. Morgan Stanley is the project's tax equity investor, an investor that funds the project partly in return for its tax credits. Allen & Overy acted as legal counsel to Longroad.
context: Longroad says this is its first acquisition since it closed a $500 million equity investment and that it reflects a goal of quickly growing its operating portfolio. The company says the deal expands its presence in the CAISO market and brings its operating solar capacity in California to about 340 MWdc. It is also a repeat partnership with Great Bay Renewables.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Acquires 98 MWdc Titan Solar Project from Sunpin

title: United Airlines Ventures makes strategic equity investment in sodium-ion battery maker Natron Energy
summary: United Airlines, through its venture arm United Airlines Ventures, has made a strategic equity investment in Natron Energy, a US maker of sodium-ion batteries. The size of the investment and the stake acquired were not disclosed.
details: Natron builds sodium-ion batteries using a Prussian blue electrode chemistry at a factory in Holland, Michigan. The company plans to use the new money to speed up production there and begin mass production of its UL-listed batteries in 2023. United says the batteries could be used to charge electric ground equipment such as pushback tractors, to charge possible future electric air taxis, to help airports manage power demand, and to improve resilience in bad weather. A strategic equity investment means United bought an ownership share in Natron partly for business reasons beyond financial return.
context: United says it is the first major airline to invest in a battery manufacturer, based on publicly announced deals, and that this is its first venture investment aimed at cutting emissions from ground operations rather than aircraft. The airline has more than 12,000 pieces of motorized ground equipment, about a third of which are electric. Natron claims its batteries offer better power density, faster recharging, longer life and lower fire risk than lithium-ion, and rely on more abundant materials.

sources.title: United Airlines Invests in Battery-Maker Natron Energy With Eye Toward Further Electrifying Ground Operations

title: Shell agrees to acquire Danish biomethane producer Nature Energy for nearly US$2 billion

advisors.name: J.P. Morgan Securities plc
advisors.role: sole financial advisor to the sellers

summary: Shell Petroleum NV, part of Shell plc, has signed a definitive agreement to buy all of Denmark-based Nature Energy Biogas at an enterprise value of nearly US$2 billion (about EUR 1.9 billion). The sellers are a group of institutional investors known as the NGF Partnership.
details: Nature Energy owns and runs 14 large biomethane plants, which turn organic waste into a renewable substitute for natural gas, producing about 180 million cubic metres a year. It has one plant under construction in France and a development pipeline of about 30 projects across Europe and North America. The company designs, builds, owns and operates its plants and employs more than 400 people. Enterprise value means the price for the whole business including its debt. The deal needs regulatory approvals and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2023, with J.P. Morgan Securities plc as sole financial adviser to the sellers.
context: Shell says the purchase gives it a European production platform and growth pipeline to add to its renewable natural gas projects in the United States, and that it aims to build a global renewable gas value chain. The company expects demand for low carbon fuels to grow strongly. Nature Energy points to the EU REPowerEU plan as signalling longer-term potential for biomethane.

sources.title: Leading Biomethane Producer Nature Energy Biogas to be Acquired By Shell

title: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions acquires 100 MW Wildflower Solar in Mississippi from Clearway Energy Group
summary: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions, the non-regulated commercial arm of Duke Energy, is buying the 100 MW Wildflower Solar project in Desoto County, Mississippi, from developer Clearway Energy Group. Toyota North America has agreed to buy up to 80 MW of the project's output under a 15-year contract. The price was not disclosed.
details: Wildflower Solar is a pre-construction project expected to start full construction in late 2022 and begin commercial operation in late 2023. Toyota signed a 15-year virtual power purchase agreement, a financial contract in which the buyer pays a set price for power without taking physical delivery, settled against the project's real-time output as it is generated. Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions will own and operate the plant, which is expected to employ about 300 people at peak construction. No advisers or financing terms were named.
context: The deal is the first renewable energy project in Mississippi for Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions. The site is near Toyota's Mississippi manufacturing plant, and Toyota says the purchase could cut its North American carbon footprint by up to 8 percent as it pursues carbon neutrality in its operations by 2035.

sources.title: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions enters Mississippi with acquisition of 100-MW Wildflower Solar from Clearway Energy Group

title: NextEra Energy Partners to buy about 1,080 MW net renewables interest from NextEra Energy Resources, backed by $805 million Ontario Teachers' financing
target: 49% of Emerald Breeze portfolio (about 1.5 GW) and about 100% of a 345 MW operating wind portfolio
summary: NextEra Energy Partners agreed to buy a 49% stake in a roughly 1.5 GW wind, solar and storage portfolio and nearly all of a roughly 345 MW operating wind portfolio from affiliates of NextEra Energy Resources, for about $805 million plus its share of about $1.5 billion of tax equity. The net interest is about 1,080 MW across several US states. Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board will invest $805 million in a new portfolio holding these assets and six existing NEP wind farms.
details: The 49% stake is in Emerald Breeze, which owns Great Prairie Wind (about 1,029 MW in Texas and Oklahoma), Appaloosa Run Wind (172 MW, Texas), Eight Point Wind (111 MW, New York) and Yellow Pine Solar (125 MW solar plus 65 MW storage, Nevada). The fully owned assets are Elk City Wind II (107 MW, Oklahoma), Sac County Wind (80 MW, Iowa) and Sholes Wind (160 MW, Nebraska). Tax equity is investment from parties who receive tax credits in return for funding projects, and NEP will assume its share of that obligation. Ontario Teachers' will fund about $645 million at closing and about $160 million once the three unfinished projects start operating, expected by the end of the third quarter of 2023, earning an effective coupon of about 2.8% over 10 years, with NEP able to buy out the stake at a fixed 7.0% return between years 5 and 10, payable in NEP units. Closing is expected later in 2022, and NEP can require the seller to buy back any project not operating by November 30, 2023.
context: The assets carry long-term contracts with about 15 years of remaining life and highly rated customers, and NEP expects them to add about $210 million to $230 million of annual adjusted EBITDA. The company presents the convertible financing as low-cost capital that lets it keep upside from any unit price rise. NEP says the deals support its target of 12% to 15% annual distribution growth through at least 2025.

sources.title: NextEra Energy Partners, LP announces agreement to acquire an approximately 1,080-megawatt net interest in a portfolio of long-term contracted renewables projects and enters into new convertible equity portfolio financing

title: Clearway Energy Group acquired 152 MW Cedar Creek Wind project in Idaho from rPlus Energies
summary: rPlus Energies disclosed that it sold its interest in the roughly 152 MW Cedar Creek Wind project in Bingham County, Idaho, to Clearway Energy Group in late 2021. Clearway has since signed a long-term power purchase agreement with utility PacifiCorp and started construction.
details: rPlus acquired the development rights in early 2019 and spent about 18 months re-developing the project, securing new land agreements, environmental studies, permits, a grid connection and an updated design. The project was shortlisted and awarded in PacifiCorp's 2020 All-Source Request for Proposals, a competitive tender for new power supply. After buying it, Clearway completed development, engineering and equipment purchasing and signed the power purchase agreement, a long-term contract under which PacifiCorp will buy the electricity. Construction began in September 2022 and completion is expected in 2024. The purchase price was not disclosed.
context: The announcement came after Clearway publicized its PPA with PacifiCorp, which rPlus describes as a major step for the project. The companies say the project represents a 250 million dollar investment in Idaho and will create more than 175 construction jobs. The deal illustrates a common model in which a developer advances a project through early stages and then sells it to a larger owner-operator to build.

sources.title: rPlus Energies Announces 152 MW Wind Project Has Been Acquired by Clearway Energy Group

title: Neste agrees to buy Crimson Renewable Energy's US used cooking oil collection business
target: Used cooking oil collection and aggregation business of Crimson Renewable Energy, including SeQuential Environmental Services, LLC, Pure, LLC and a processing plant in Salem, Oregon
summary: Finnish renewable fuels producer Neste has agreed to acquire the US used cooking oil collection and aggregation business of Crimson Renewable Energy Holdings. The business operates on the US West Coast. No price was disclosed.
details: The deal covers shares in SeQuential Environmental Services and Pure, plus a used cooking oil processing plant in Salem, Oregon. The business collects, transports and stores used cooking oil in California, Oregon and Washington. Used cooking oil is a waste feedstock that can be refined into renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel. Completion depends on customary closing conditions and regulatory approval.
context: Neste says the purchase extends its raw material sourcing to the US West Coast, near its planned Martinez Renewables renewable diesel joint operation with Marathon Petroleum in California. Combined with its earlier acquisition of Mahoney Environmental, the company says it will have a nationwide US used cooking oil collection network. The deal follows other feedstock acquisitions by Neste in the US, the Netherlands and Ireland as it expands renewable fuel output, which it expects to reach 5.5 million tons a year by end of 2023.

sources.title: Neste to acquire used cooking oil collection and aggregation business from Crimson Renewable Energy in the United States to strengthen Neste's renewable raw materials sourcing platform

title: LS Power agrees to buy 334 MW US run-of-river hydro portfolio from Hull Street Energy
summary: LS Power has agreed to acquire 42 run-of-river hydroelectric plants with a combined 334 MW from Hull Street Energy. The facilities are spread across 11 US states. No price was disclosed.
details: Run-of-river plants generate power from the natural flow of a river with little or no water storage behind a dam. Most of the capacity sits in three regional grid markets, with 152 MW in New England (ISO-NE), 86 MW in the PJM mid-Atlantic market and 48 MW in New York (NYISO). The rest is located in the CAISO, SERC and WECC regions. The deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2023, once closing conditions and regulatory approvals are met. Milbank acted as legal counsel to LS Power, while BMO Capital Markets and Scotiabank were its financial advisers.
context: LS Power presents the purchase as part of its energy transition strategy, which pairs renewables, storage, transmission and EV charging with a large gas fleet. The company says the plants are in states with supportive rules, noting that New York and Massachusetts already let small hydro count toward renewable portfolio standards, which are state targets for clean power. It expects more states to adopt similar policies and describes hydro as a long-lived carbon-free asset.

sources.title: LS Power to Acquire U.S. Portfolio of Hydro Facilities

title: Dandelion Energy raises US$70 million Series B1 for residential geothermal heating and cooling
summary: New York-based Dandelion Energy, which installs geothermal heat pump systems in homes, closed a US$70 million Series B1 venture funding round. The round was co-led by LEN X, the venture arm of homebuilder Lennar, and NGP ETP, the energy transition platform of NGP, with several existing venture investors also taking part.
details: Dandelion's systems are ground source heat pumps, which move heat between a home and the ground to provide heating and cooling instead of a gas furnace. A Series B1 is an extension-stage venture round in which investors buy shares in a growing private company. The company says it will use the money to expand in both retrofit and new-build housing and to develop a wider range of products for more customers and regions. It reports having completed its 1,000th installation. Breakthrough Energy Ventures, NEA, GV, Collaborative Fund and Building Ventures also participated.
context: The company says its commercial operations more than tripled in 2022 and points to Inflation Reduction Act tax credits as making geothermal heat pumps more affordable for homeowners. Backing from Lennar's venture arm links the company to a large homebuilder, which says it wants to lower the cost of geothermal systems for new homebuyers. NGP describes ground source heat pumps as having among the lowest emissions and operating costs of heating systems.

sources.title: Dandelion Energy Closes $70M Series B1 Funding Round to Scale Geothermal Heating and Cooling Solution to Meet Surging Demand

title: Longroad Energy closes financing for 152 MWdc Three Corners Solar project in Maine

buyers.name: U.S. Bank
buyers.role: lender and sole tax equity investor

summary: Longroad Energy has closed financing and started building the 152 MWdc Three Corners Solar project in Kennebec County, Maine. The project costs about US$200 million and is backed by debt from KeyBank and U.S. Bank, with U.S. Bank also providing tax equity.
details: The solar plant sits in the towns of Benton and Clinton and is expected to be finished in late 2023 or early 2024. KeyBank N.A. and U.S. Bank are the lenders, KeyBanc Capital Markets coordinated the loan, and U.S. Bank is the only tax equity investor, meaning it puts in money in exchange for the project's federal tax credits. EDF Energy Services will buy all the power under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to buy electricity at agreed terms, and use it to supply corporate customers in New England. The project will use First Solar modules, Nextracker trackers and Power Electronics inverters, and will connect to the Central Maine Power grid.
context: Longroad says the project will be the largest solar plant in Maine once built and that the offtake deal is the largest corporate PPA signed in the New England grid so far. The project has been in development for five years. U.S. Bank says this is the first deal on its new environmental finance debt platform, and KeyBanc says it is its 39th transaction with Longroad.

sources.title: Longroad Energy Completes Financing and Commences Construction of 152 MWdc Three Corners Solar Project

title: OYA Renewables and Oil Well Shares form Chrysalis Energy JV for 3 GW of Appalachian clean energy
summary: Canadian developer OYA Renewables and Appalachian oil and gas company Oil Well Shares have formed a joint venture called Chrysalis Energy. The venture plans to develop, build and operate more than 3 GW of solar, wind and storage projects on about 1.5 million acres in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia.
details: The projects would sit on land to which Oil Well Shares holds rights, mostly in one connected block, within the PJM region, the grid operator covering much of the US mid-Atlantic and Midwest. The partners will jointly own and run the assets, which may include community-scale and utility-scale solar, wind, battery storage and green hydrogen production, meaning hydrogen made with renewable power. The first phase is expected to be finished by 2030, with further development planned afterwards. The companies project that the work will lead to more than $3 billion in regional capital spending by 2030. No ownership split or deal value was disclosed.
context: The deal pairs a solar developer with a fossil fuel operator that holds a large land position, which OYA describes as possibly the largest private land inventory in PJM. The partners claim the venture will strengthen regional energy security and create local jobs. OYA says the proximity to the Great Lakes makes green hydrogen an option worth exploring.

sources.title: OYA Renewables and Appalachian Energy Innovator Oil Well Shares Sign Joint Venture for Landmark Clean Energy Development

title: Fengate acquires 160 MW Prairie Switch Wind project in Texas from Triple Oak Power and signs PPA with Meta
summary: Fengate Asset Management has bought the 160 MW Prairie Switch Wind project near Houston, Texas, from developer Triple Oak Power. Alongside the purchase, Fengate signed a long-term power purchase agreement with Meta covering all of the project's output.
details: The project is ready-to-build, meaning development and permitting work is done and construction can begin. It will use 48 GE Renewable Energy turbines rated at 3.4 MW each and is located near El Campo in Wharton County. Full operation is expected by the end of 2023. The power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity, covers 100 percent of production, though its length and price were not disclosed. No purchase price was stated.
context: Fengate says the deal fits its build-to-core approach, which means buying projects before construction and holding them as long-term operating assets. The investment is managed for Fengate's investors, including a fund owned by LiUNA's Pension Fund of Central and Eastern Canada. Meta says it has matched its global operations with renewable energy since 2020, and the project adds new wind supply to support that goal. The release also claims the project will bring tax and lease payments to the county while farming and ranching continue.

sources.title: Fengate acquires 160MW Prairie Switch Wind project in Texas and signs PPA with Meta

title: CIT arranges construction financing for Avantus' 147 MWdc Galloway 2 solar project in Texas
summary: CIT, a division of First Citizens Bank, acted as coordinating lead arranger of construction financing for Galloway 2, a 147 MWdc solar project in Concho County, Texas, developed by Avantus. Allianz Capital Partners bought a majority interest in the project and will co-own it with Avantus. The loan amount was not disclosed.
details: Galloway 2 is under construction next to the Galloway 1 solar plant, which CIT also helped finance in 2020, and is expected to start operating in 2023. Part of its output is sold under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to buy electricity at agreed terms, with EDF Energy Services. Tenaska led the tax equity investment, meaning it provides funding in exchange for the project's federal tax benefits. Tenaska Power Services Co. will act as the qualified scheduling entity, the party that handles the plant's communication and scheduling with the Texas grid operator.
context: The deal repeats the financing partnership between CIT and Avantus from the first Galloway project. Avantus says it continues to see strong demand for solar projects supplying low-cost power to consumers and businesses. The structure combines bank debt, tax equity and a long-term offtake contract, a common way US solar projects are funded.

sources.title: CIT Leads Construction Financing for Major New Texas Solar Project

title: Google signs 942 MW solar power purchase agreement with SB Energy in Texas
summary: SB Energy has agreed to sell Google about 75 percent of the output from four Texas solar projects under development, amounting to 942 MW. The four projects total 1.2 GW and will supply power matched to Google's data center in Midlothian and cloud region in Dallas.
details: The deal is a power purchase agreement, a long-term contract under which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a specific project. It covers the Orion 1-3 and Eiffel solar projects, which together have 1.2 GW of capacity and are expected to begin operating by mid-2024. The projects will mainly use U.S.-made First Solar modules produced at First Solar's Ohio factory. Contract length and price were not disclosed.
context: Google describes the agreement as its largest combined clean energy purchase in Texas so far, and says it supports its goal of running on carbon-free energy every hour of every day by 2030. SB Energy, backed by SoftBank and Ares-managed funds, says it plans to have 10 GW of renewable and storage projects operating or under construction by the end of 2025 and credits the Inflation Reduction Act with supporting its growth.

sources.title: SB Energy Inks 942 MW PPA with Google to Power Data Center

title: Ignis H2 Energy and GEOLOG invest in geothermal storage developer Sage Geosystems
summary: Houston-based Sage Geosystems has received an investment from Ignis H2 Energy and its sister company Geolog International as part of a strategic partnership. The size of the investment and the stake acquired were not disclosed.
details: Sage develops geothermal technology that uses standard oil and gas equipment, including a long-duration energy storage product it calls Battery+, which stores energy underground and can later run as baseload power, meaning steady round-the-clock output. Sage says it is currently prioritizing storage for utility grids. GEOLOG, founded in Milan in 1982, provides subsurface characterization and drilling optimization services, and is expected to support faster geological evaluation and international expansion. No advisers or deal terms were named.
context: The parties say the partnership will help bring geothermal storage and baseload power to major markets worldwide as growing wind and solar output leads to more curtailment, the cutting back of renewable generation the grid cannot absorb. Ignis says it aims to become a geothermal power producer in multiple countries, with a long-term goal of producing green hydrogen from geothermal energy.

sources.title: Sage Geosystems Announces Strategic Partnership and Investment from IGNIS H2 Energy and the Geolog Group to Advance Energy Storage Solutions Using Geothermal Technology

title: WEC Energy Group agrees to buy 80% of Invenergy's 250 MW Maple Flats solar project in Illinois
summary: WEC Energy Group has agreed to acquire an 80% ownership interest in the 250 MW Maple Flats Solar Energy Center in Clay County, Illinois, which is being developed by Invenergy. WEC expects its investment to total about $360 million.
details: The project is planned to have about 800,000 solar panels spread over 1,500 acres, with commercial operation expected in early 2024. Its output will be sold to an unnamed Fortune 100 company under a long-term power purchase agreement, which is a contract to buy electricity at agreed terms over many years. WEC expects the project to qualify for Production Tax Credits under the Inflation Reduction Act, a federal incentive paid per unit of electricity produced. The deal still needs regulatory approvals.
context: This is the first solar investment for WEC's Infrastructure segment, which already has existing or planned stakes in eight wind farms totaling more than 1.5 GW. The company says the deal shows growth opportunities for that business and broadens its mix of renewable assets.

sources.title: WEC Energy Group to acquire 80% ownership of Maple Flats Solar Energy Center

title: ENGIE North America acquires 6 GW US solar and storage development portfolio from Belltown Power
target: 33-project solar and battery storage development portfolio
summary: ENGIE North America has bought a portfolio of 33 solar and battery storage development projects totalling about 6 GW from developer Belltown Power U.S. The projects are spread across several US power markets. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio includes about 2.7 GW of solar, 0.7 GW of battery storage paired with solar, and 2.6 GW of stand-alone battery storage, giving roughly 3.3 GW of storage in total. The projects range from early to late stage of development, meaning they have not yet been built. They sit in the ERCOT (Texas), PJM (mid-Atlantic), MISO (Midwest) and WECC (Western) grid regions. Storage energy capacity in MWh and financial terms were not stated.
context: ENGIE reported 3.9 GW of installed renewable capacity in North America as of June 30, 2022, and says the deal expands its US pipeline and takes it into new areas. The company claims the storage projects will help balance the grid and improve reliability. For Belltown, a greenfield developer that builds projects from site selection onward, the sale is described as a milestone.

sources.title: ENGIE acquires 6 GW of solar and battery storage capacity projects from Belltown Power U.S. and significantly strengthens its renewable development pipeline

title: rPlus Energies signs PPA with PacifiCorp for 400 MW Green River solar-plus-storage project in Utah
summary: Developer rPlus Energies has signed a long-term power purchase agreement with utility PacifiCorp for the Green River Energy Center in Emery County, Utah. The project pairs 400 MWac of solar panels with a 200 MW battery system.
details: A power purchase agreement is a contract in which a buyer, here the utility, agrees to purchase the electricity a plant produces over many years. The project was put forward in PacifiCorp's 2020 All-Source Request for Proposals, a competitive tender, where it was shortlisted and selected. Sundt Construction will handle engineering, procurement and construction. Building is expected to start in early 2023, and the project is described as a roughly $750 million investment. The release does not state the contract length or the battery's energy capacity in MWh.
context: rPlus Energies says the project is the largest planned solar-plus-storage facility in Utah and one of the largest on PacifiCorp's system. The developer says the deal lifts its contracted renewable capacity to more than 1.2 GW since it was formed in late 2018. The project is located in a county where coal plants are expected to retire over the next ten to twenty years.

sources.title: rPlus Energies Signs Power Purchase Agreement with PacifiCorp for 400 MW Solar with 200 MW Battery Storage in Utah

title: Matrix Renewables closes US$217 million construction financing for Gaskell West 2 and 3 solar-plus-storage projects in California
target: Gaskell West 2 and Gaskell West 3 projects
summary: Matrix Renewables, a platform backed by TPG Rise, has closed US$217 million in debt financing for its Gaskell West 2 and 3 solar and storage projects in Kern County, California. The loans came from MUFG, HSBC, National Bank of Canada and Commonwealth Bank.
details: The two projects total 143 MWdc of solar capacity paired with an 80 MWh battery system and are well advanced in construction. The package combines a construction loan, a tax equity bridge loan (short-term funding repaid when tax equity investors, who invest in exchange for tax credits, put in their money) and a back-levered term loan (long-term debt secured at the owner level rather than directly on the project). It follows US$92 million of tax equity from Bank of America in June 2022. The projects sell their output under five long-term power purchase agreements with California utilities and cities. Cohn Reznick Capital and Norton Rose Fulbright advised Matrix, and Latham & Watkins advised the lenders.
context: Matrix describes this as its first non-recourse financing in the US, meaning lenders are repaid from project cash flows rather than from the parent company. The deal supports the company's US expansion, which includes a recently announced 4.6 GW solar development portfolio acquisition in the central US. Matrix reports a portfolio of 2.3 GW of operating, under-construction or near ready-to-build projects plus a 7.3 GW pipeline.

sources.title: MATRIX RENEWABLES CLOSES CONSTRUCTION FINANCING FOR GASKELL WEST PROJECT

title: Hershey signs 140 MW solar PPA with National Grid Renewables for Texas Copperhead project

advisors.name: Edison Energy
advisors.role: energy advisor to The Hershey Company

summary: The Hershey Company agreed to buy power from 140 MW of National Grid Renewables' Copperhead Solar & Storage Project in Falls County, Texas. The project combines 150 MW of solar with 100 MWh of battery storage and has started construction.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract to buy electricity from a specific project. The contract covers 140 MW of the 150 MW Copperhead solar plant, which sits in the ERCOT grid region of Texas and includes a 100 MWh Fluence Gridstack battery system. The plant will use First Solar Series 6 thin film modules and is being built by TIC, a Kiewit subsidiary acting as the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor. The contract length and price were not disclosed.
context: This is Hershey's second PPA with National Grid Renewables, following the Noble solar deal announced in 2021. Hershey says solar contracts are helping it toward targets of cutting Scope 1 and 2 emissions by more than 50 percent and Scope 3 by 25 percent by 2030. National Grid Renewables projects about $25 million in local economic impact over 25 years of operation.

sources.title: The Hershey Company Signs Second Solar Power Purchase Agreement with National Grid Renewables

title: Fundamental Renewables provides $100 million revolving development loan to Pivot Energy
summary: Fundamental Renewables, the clean energy investment arm of Fundamental Advisors, agreed to provide Denver-based Pivot Energy with a $100 million revolving development loan facility. The money will fund solar and storage projects across the United States.
details: The facility is revolving, meaning Pivot can borrow, repay and borrow again up to the limit, and it runs for a three-year term. It is meant to fund early development and initial construction of Pivot's pipeline of distributed generation solar projects, which are smaller systems located near where power is used, including commercial and community solar. Community solar lets multiple customers subscribe to a shared solar project, and the release mentions New York as one market. No project capacity figures or advisers were disclosed.
context: Pivot says the facility gives it financial flexibility to speed up development across its portfolio of commercial and community solar projects. Fundamental Renewables describes the deal as part of its focus on backing companies working on the clean energy transition and on making solar more accessible. Development-stage loans like this help developers move projects forward before long-term construction or permanent financing is arranged.

sources.title: Pivot Energy Secures $100 Million Revolving Loan Facility from Fundamental Renewables

title: Sabanci Renewables acquires 272 MW Cutlass Solar II project in Texas from Advanced Power
summary: Advanced Power has completed the sale of its full interest in Cutlass Solar II LLC to Sabanci Renewables, a wholly owned unit of Turkey's Sabanci Holdings. The project is a 272 MW solar plant in Fort Bend County, Texas. No price was disclosed.
details: Cutlass Solar II is a photovoltaic plant on a 1,100-acre site about 40 miles southwest of Houston, intended to serve the Houston and Freeport areas. Construction was expected to start in the fourth quarter of 2022, with commercial operation expected in 2024. The project will sell electricity and renewable energy credits into the ERCOT market, the Texas grid, rather than relying on a disclosed long-term contract. Advanced Power and Sabanci plan to keep working together during construction.
context: The deal is Sabanci's first US energy investment, and the buyer describes it as a landmark step toward building an international clean energy portfolio. For Advanced Power it is the second and final phase of its Cutlass Solar projects, after the first phase began operating in July 2022. The developer says it has an 8 GW renewables pipeline across several US markets, including further Texas solar projects with optional battery storage.

sources.title: Advanced Power Closes Sale of Cutlass Solar II to Sabanci Renewables

title: AboitizPower to take 60% of Mainstream's 90 MW Libmanan wind project in Philippines joint venture
summary: Mainstream Renewable Power and AboitizPower have signed a joint venture agreement to build the 90 MW Libmanan onshore wind project in the Philippines. Under the deal, AboitizPower's subsidiary Aboitiz Renewables plans to acquire a 60 percent stake in the project.
details: The Libmanan wind farm is located in Camarines Sur Province and has been under development by Mainstream and a local partner since 2017.
