The joint venture is structured through an investment agreement covering the proposed 60 percent stake purchase and still needs regulatory approval. The project is expected to reach financial close, meaning the point when all funding is secured and construction can begin, in 2023, with commercial operations targeted for 2025. No deal value was disclosed.
context: The project would be Mainstream's first wind farm in the Philippines, which the company describes as a priority market. AboitizPower aims to grow its renewables portfolio to 4,600 MW by 2030, and the partnership is also meant to cover a future development pipeline. The Philippine government targets 35 percent renewable electricity by 2030 and recently raised its annual renewable portfolio standard requirement from 1 to 2.5 percent.

sources.title: Mainstream Renewable Power and AboitizPower Enter Joint Venture Agreement for Initial 90 MW Wind Project in the Philippines

title: Mitsui affiliate MyPower acquires US community solar service provider Solstice Power Technologies
summary: MyPower Corp., an investment affiliate wholly owned by Japan's Mitsui & Co., has acquired all of Solstice Power Technologies, a US company that signs up and manages customers for community solar projects. No price was disclosed.
details: Solstice, founded in 2016 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, enrolls households and local organizations as subscribers to shared solar projects, offers financing approaches aimed at underserved communities, and runs subscriber management software. Community solar lets people who cannot install rooftop panels, such as renters, buy into a nearby solar project and receive bill savings. Solstice's nonprofit arm, Solstice Initiative, is excluded from the deal and will continue as an independent charity under a new name. The release does not name sellers, advisers or financial terms.
context: MyPower says the deal lets it expand further into the US community solar market and pair Solstice with its commercial clean energy offerings. Solstice says backing from Mitsui will help it enter new markets and develop new services. The release frames the purchase as a step toward wider access to clean energy for low- and moderate-income households.

sources.title: MyPower Corp. Acquires Solstice Power Technologies, Inc., a Prominent Service Provider Specialized in Customer Management for Community Solar in the U.S.

title: AboitizPower to take 60% stake in Mainstream's 90 MW Libmanan wind project in the Philippines
summary: Mainstream Renewable Power has signed a joint venture agreement with AboitizPower, through its unit Aboitiz Renewables, to build the 90 MW Libmanan onshore wind project in the Philippines. Under the deal Aboitiz Renewables plans to acquire a 60 percent stake in the project. No price was disclosed.
details: The Libmanan project is located in Camarines Sur Province and has been under development by Mainstream and a local partner since 2017. The joint venture is structured as an investment agreement under which Aboitiz Renewables would buy 60 percent of the project, and it still needs regulatory approval. The partners expect financial close, the point when all funding is committed and construction can start, in 2023, with commercial operations targeted for 2025. The partnership is also meant to cover a future development pipeline beyond this first project.
context: Mainstream says this would be its first wind farm in the Philippines, which it describes as a priority market. AboitizPower aims to grow its renewables portfolio to 4,600 MW by 2030, and the project contributes to that goal. The deal comes as the Philippine government raised its annual renewable portfolio standard from 1 to 2.5 percent and targets 35 percent renewable electricity by 2030 and 50 percent by 2040.

title: Ashtrom Renewable Energy signs deal to develop 476 MW solar pipeline in Greece with local partner
target: Five solar projects in Greece totaling about 476 MW
summary: Ashtrom Renewable Energy, a subsidiary of Israeli builder Ashtrom Group, has signed agreements with an unnamed local partner to develop five solar projects in Greece totaling about 476 MW. The company estimates the cost of building the projects at 335 million to 380 million euros.
details: The five projects are at an early stage of development and will be developed by the Greek partner. Ashtrom bases its cost estimate on 700,000 to 800,000 euros per MW, including grid connection. Payments to the partner are tied to development milestones, with most paid at late stages and after grid connection approval. Ashtrom also received a future right to take over several more of the partner's projects that are further along, which the partner expects to receive key construction permits within a year.
context: The deal marks Ashtrom's entry into Greece after starting operations in the US and Poland the previous year. The company says Greece offers rapid growth, high power prices and strong sunshine, and puts its total pipeline across the US, Israel, Poland and Greece at about 1.5 GW. Power from Greek projects can be sold through government tenders, long-term power purchase agreements or the open market.

sources.title: Ashtrom Group extends its renewable energy operations in Europe: Ashtrom Renewable Energy will establish projects of 476 MW capacity in Greece at an overall investment of up to €380M

title: GIP completes acquisition of Latin American solar platform Atlas Renewable Energy from Actis
summary: Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) has completed its purchase of Atlas Renewable Energy from investor Actis. Atlas owns 14 fully contracted solar assets totalling 2.3 GW of installed capacity in Brazil, Chile, Mexico and Uruguay. The price was not disclosed.
details: Atlas was founded in 2016 with Actis backing and describes itself as the second largest independent renewables developer in Latin America. Its 14 solar assets are fully contracted, meaning their power output is already sold under agreements with buyers, largely large corporate customers. The company says it grew installed capacity fivefold over about four and a half years. The release does not state the deal value, the stake size beyond a full acquisition, or any advisers.
context: GIP says the deal adds a large Latin American platform to its solar, wind and battery holdings in North America, Europe and Asia, and that it plans to expand Atlas into other technologies and markets. For Actis, the sale is its fifth renewable platform exit in the Americas, where it says it has built and owned more than 7 GW of contracted wind and solar capacity. The parties point to economic growth and the energy transition as drivers of rising demand for renewable power in the region.

title: Air Products plans about $500 million green liquid hydrogen plant in Massena, New York
summary: Air Products announced plans to invest roughly $500 million to build, own and operate a green liquid hydrogen plant in Massena, New York. The plant is designed to produce 35 metric tons of hydrogen per day and will be powered by a 94 MW allocation of hydroelectric power from the New York Power Authority.
details: The facility will sit on a greenfield site, meaning previously undeveloped land, and the investment also covers liquid hydrogen distribution and dispensing operations. In July 2022 the New York Power Authority board approved 94 MW of low-cost power from its St. Lawrence hydroelectric project for the plant. Commercial operation is targeted for 2026 to 2027 and the project is expected to create 90 jobs. The company says its budget assumes certain local and state incentives and benefits from the federal Inflation Reduction Act.
context: Air Products says market demand justifies the investment and plans to sell the hydrogen mainly to the New York mobility market and possibly northeast industrial users. The project supports New York's bid to become a regional clean hydrogen hub under a federal program. The company is also studying a northeast hydrogen fueling network that could serve its own truck fleet, which it plans to convert to fuel cell vehicles, and it claims the project could avoid more than six million tonnes of CO2 over its life if all output goes to heavy trucks.

sources.title: Air Products to Invest About $500 Million to Build Green Hydrogen Production Facility in New York

title: Greater Commercial Lending provides $25 million USDA-guaranteed loan for Aemetis dairy biogas project in California
target: Aemetis Biogas Central Dairy Digester Project
summary: Greater Commercial Lending has completed $25 million in long-term financing for the Aemetis Biogas Central Dairy Digester Project in Stanislaus County, California. The loan is guaranteed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture and supports dairy biogas digesters and a biogas pipeline that turn manure methane into renewable natural gas.
details: The project uses anaerobic digesters, sealed systems that break down manure without oxygen, at dairy farm lagoons to capture methane. Construction and testing of six digesters is scheduled to finish in the first quarter of 2023. A pipeline carries the biogas to the Aemetis Keyes ethanol plant, where it is upgraded into a low-carbon transportation fuel, and PG&E will move the fuel through its gas network for sale across California. The loan is backed by the USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP), meaning the government guarantees repayment to the lender.
context: Aemetis says that when fully built the project will link digesters at 66 dairy farms along a 40-mile pipeline and is designed to cut emissions by an estimated 6.8 million tonnes of CO2 over 10 years. The release notes that dairy lagoons account for about a quarter of California methane emissions. Both parties argue that government-guaranteed loans offer a low-cost, long-term funding route for such projects.

sources.title: Greater Commercial Lending Completes $25 Million in Financing for Dairy Farm Biogas Digesters and Pipeline to Produce Renewable Natural Gas

title: AB CarVal funds acquire 70 MW Pennsylvania solar portfolio from ReneSola Power
target: ~70 MW portfolio of three utility-scale solar projects in Pennsylvania
summary: ReneSola Power has completed the sale of a portfolio of about 70 MW of solar development projects in Pennsylvania to funds managed by AB CarVal Investors. The price was not disclosed.
details: The portfolio is made up of three ground-mounted utility-scale solar projects in Pennsylvania, within the PJM grid region, which is the transmission network operator covering much of the eastern US. The projects were sold at the Notice to Proceed stage, meaning they are ready to begin construction. AB CarVal will build the projects and keep them as long-term owner.
context: The sale fits ReneSola Power's strategy of selling projects once they reach the ready-to-build stage, and the company says these are its largest single-site project sales in the US so far. For AB CarVal, an alternative investment manager, the deal adds to clean energy investments it says exceed $3.0 billion since 2017.

sources.title: ReneSola Power Closes Sale of 70 MW of Solar Projects in Pennsylvania

title: ReneSola Power acquires 50 MWp operating Branston solar farm in UK from P&T Global Renewable Energy
summary: ReneSola Power, a NYSE-listed solar developer, has bought Project Branston, a 50 MWp operating solar farm near Lincoln in the United Kingdom, from P&T Global Renewable Energy. The deal closed on September 30, 2022. No price was disclosed.
details: The solar farm is in Branston, Lincoln, and has been producing power since October 12, 2020. The company says it currently generates about 1,011 MWh per MWp each year, a measure of how much electricity each unit of installed peak capacity produces. MWp means megawatts peak, the panels' maximum output under ideal conditions. The release does not describe the financing, offtake arrangements or advisers.
context: The acquisition marks ReneSola Power's entry into the independent power producer (IPP) business in Europe, meaning it will own the plant and earn revenue from selling its electricity rather than only developing and selling projects. The company says the asset will be profitable immediately, provide stable cash flow and reduce its reliance on project sales. It also expects the deal to strengthen its European position and add to shareholder value.

sources.title: ReneSola Power Acquires 50 MWp Fully Operational Solar Farm in the United Kingdom and Commences its IPP business in Europe

title: Enbridge completes acquisition of US renewable developer Tri Global Energy

advisors.name: Lazard
advisors.role: lead financial advisor to Tri Global Energy

advisors.name: Haynes and Boone
advisors.role: outside counsel to Tri Global Energy

summary: Canadian energy company Enbridge has completed its acquisition of Tri Global Energy, a Dallas-based developer of wind, solar and battery storage projects in the United States. The purchase price was not disclosed.
details: Tri Global Energy, founded in 2009, says it has developed 8.7 GW across 37 projects in Texas, Illinois, Indiana, Nebraska, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Wyoming. Its model is to originate and develop projects, meaning it finds sites and secures permits and contracts, and then sell them to long-term owners such as NextEra, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Engie. Ten of the Texas wind projects it developed are now operating. Lazard acted as lead financial adviser and Haynes and Boone as outside legal counsel to Tri Global Energy.
context: The deal gives Enbridge, a large oil and gas pipeline company, an established US renewable development team. The American Clean Power Association ranked Tri Global Energy tenth in the US for overall renewable development and first for onshore wind development in Texas in the second quarter of 2022. Tri Global's CEO said the combination would support continued growth.

sources.title: Tri Global Energy, a Leading U.S. Renewable Energy Developer, Acquired by Enbridge

title: Enbridge acquires US wind and solar developer Tri Global Energy for US$270 million
summary: Canadian energy company Enbridge has acquired Tri Global Energy, a US developer of wind and solar projects, for US$270 million in cash and assumed debt. The developer holds a pipeline of more than 7 GW of renewable projects in the US.
details: Beyond the upfront price, Enbridge may pay up to about US$50 million more if Tri Global's projects are successfully delivered, a structure known as contingent payments. The portfolio includes 3.9 GW of projects previously sold to operators, which are expected to earn development fees, and 3 GW of late-stage projects owned outright that Enbridge expects to enter service between 2024 and 2028. Earlier-stage projects make up the rest of the pipeline. Tri Global's development team will stay on after the deal. CIBC advised Enbridge on financial matters and Eversheds Sutherland acted as its legal counsel.
context: Tri Global, founded in 2009, describes itself as the third largest onshore wind developer in the US and says it has developed and sold over 6 GW of utility-scale projects. Enbridge, best known for oil and gas pipelines, says the deal will speed up its North American renewables growth and add to cash flow per share in the first year. The company expects rising state renewable targets and corporate demand for clean power to drive higher wind and solar investment over the next decade.

sources.title: Enbridge Enhances North American Renewables Business with Acquisition of Tri Global Energy

title: Enfinity Global agrees to buy 400 MW operating US solar portfolio from Capital Dynamics
target: 400 MW portfolio of 28 operating solar PV plants in California, North Carolina and Idaho
summary: Enfinity Global has signed a definitive agreement to buy a 400 MW portfolio of operating utility-scale solar plants in the United States from Capital Dynamics. The portfolio is made up of 28 solar PV plants located in California, North Carolina and Idaho. No price was disclosed.
details: All 28 plants are already operating and began commercial operation (COD, the date a plant starts selling power commercially) within the past five years. The plants sell their output under long-term power purchase agreements, which are contracts to sell electricity at agreed terms, with utility buyers. Barclays advised the seller, Capital Dynamics. The release does not give a closing date or deal value.
context: Enfinity Global says it has more than 5 GW of plants in operation, under construction or in development, and that this deal brings it a geographically spread set of operating assets. The company expects the US market to keep consolidating, which it believes favors long-term owners, and says it plans to pursue more US acquisitions. It also states its funding to date, excluding this deal, exceeds US$1 billion.

title: Ashtrom and Kenlov sign 20-year PPA with CPS Energy for 235 MWdc of Tierra Bonita solar project in Texas
summary: A project company jointly owned by Israel's Ashtrom Group and Kenlov Renewable Energy has signed a power purchase agreement with CPS Energy, the San Antonio municipal utility. CPS Energy will buy the output of about 235 MWdc, roughly 60% of the roughly 400 MWdc Tierra Bonita solar project in Texas, for 20 years at a fixed price.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract to sell electricity at agreed terms. Under this deal CPS Energy will take about 235 MWdc of output and the matching green certificates, which document that the power comes from renewable sources. The rest of the project's power and certificates will be sold on the open Texas market, known as merchant sales. The project covers about 9,000 dunams and has secured its main land rights and a grid connection agreement. The company expects construction to begin in the second quarter of 2023 and commercial operation at the end of 2024.
context: This is Ashtrom's first PPA in the US market, and the company says the contract with a utility rated Aa2 by Moody's should strengthen the project's financial footing. Tierra Bonita is part of a roughly 1,500 MW portfolio in Texas and Idaho that Ashtrom holds with Kenlov and that OnPeak Power is developing. Ashtrom says it is working on further PPAs and aims to grow its renewable investments mainly in the US and Europe.

title: Nexus Renewables closes US$5 million development credit facility with Scale Microgrid Solutions
summary: Toronto-based developer Nexus Renewables has closed a US$5 million asset-backed credit facility with Scale Microgrid Solutions, a Warburg Pincus portfolio company. The money will help Nexus move more than 100 MW of distribution-scale solar and storage projects toward construction readiness.
details: The facility is asset-backed, meaning the loan is secured against the developer's project assets. Proceeds will fund late-stage distribution-scale solar and energy storage projects, which are smaller systems connected to local grids, until they reach notice-to-proceed, the point at which construction can formally begin. The release does not name the project locations, their individual sizes or the storage capacity. The facility was provided through Scale's Capital Solutions platform.
context: Nexus says it has more than 1 GW of solar and storage projects under development and focuses on early-stage work before handing projects to capital partners for construction. Its chief executive describes the facility as a departure from traditional project finance that gives it more flexibility. Nexus claims the projects could supply more than 150,000 homes and avoid 120,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions.

sources.title: Nexus Renewables closes on $5m USD Development Financing Facility with Scale

title: Ojjo raises $40 million Series C led by NGP ETP to scale solar foundation system
summary: California-based Ojjo, which makes foundations for ground-mounted solar arrays, has closed a $40 million Series C equity round. The round was led by NGP ETP, the energy transition investment arm of NGP, with Ajax Strategies also taking part.
details: Ojjo sells its patented Earth Truss foundation hardware together with field engineering services and automated drilling machines called Truss Drivers to solar developers and EPC contractors, the firms that design and build projects. The company says its system has been contracted or built on more than 1.6 GW of solar projects, including all 967 MW of the Gemini Solar project in Nevada, with over 550 MW installed in Texas, Nevada and Oregon. A Series C is a later-stage venture funding round for a growing company. As part of the deal, NGP partner James Wallis joined Ojjo's board. Ojjo had previously raised $27 million across two earlier rounds, with investors including Cthulhu Ventures.
context: Ojjo plans to use the money to grow and deliver on what it describes as a 9 GW active project pipeline. The company claims its foundations need less steel and labor than conventional driven piles. Investors pointed to the US Inflation Reduction Act as a driver of steady domestic renewable growth that could benefit suppliers of solar hardware.

sources.title: Ojjo Secures $40 Million Series C Funding Round to Scale Next Generation Solar Foundations

title: Matrix Renewables acquires 4.6 GW US solar development portfolio from SolarStone and forms development JV
target: 4.6 GW utility-scale solar development portfolio in the central US
summary: Matrix Renewables, a renewable energy platform backed by TPG Rise, has secured a 4.6 GW portfolio of utility-scale solar projects in development across the central United States from SolarStone Partners. The two companies also signed a wider joint venture to develop further projects together. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of large, grid-scale solar projects at the development stage, meaning they are not yet built, spread across several central US states. Matrix and SolarStone will jointly carry the 4.6 GW portfolio through development and plan to originate new projects in other US markets under their joint venture. CohnReznick Capital acted as financial adviser and Norton Rose Fulbright as legal adviser to Matrix.
context: The deal adds a large block of projects to Matrix's US backlog, which the company says already includes 2.3 GW of operating, under-construction or near ready-to-build assets and a 7.3 GW pipeline across North America, Europe and Latin America. For SolarStone, which has mainly developed community solar projects, the partnership supports its stated push into utility-scale renewables.

sources.title: MATRIX RENEWABLES ACQUIRES A 4.6 GW US DEVELOPMENT PORTFOLIO FROM SOLARSTONE

title: Terra-Gen closes US$959 million financing for second phase of Edwards Sanborn solar and storage project in California
target: Edwards Sanborn Solar Storage facility, phase 2
summary: Terra-Gen has closed US$959 million of senior secured credit facilities for the second phase of its Edwards Sanborn solar and battery project in Kern County, California. This phase combines 410 MWac of solar with 1,786 MWh of battery storage.
details: The second phase has 410 MWac of solar nameplate capacity, of which 358 MWac can be delivered at the grid connection point, plus 1,786 MWh of batteries. The debt package consists of a US$460 million construction and term loan, a US$403 million tax equity bridge loan (short-term debt repaid once tax equity investors, who fund projects in exchange for tax credits, pay in), and a US$96 million construction and revolving letter of credit facility. U.S. Bank provides the tax equity commitment, while BNP Paribas, CoBank, ING and Nomura Securities lead the construction and term financing. Mortenson is the engineering, procurement and construction contractor, with First Solar supplying modules and LG Chem, Samsung and BYD supplying batteries. Terra-Gen expects the solar to come online in the third and fourth quarters of 2022 and the storage to be fully operational by the third quarter of 2023.
context: The first phase, financed in July 2021 with 345 MW of solar and 1,505 MWh of storage, is now operating. Terra-Gen says it is developing further phases adding over 2,000 MW of solar and storage on the CAISO grid, with financing starting in 2023, and expects the complete site to be the world's largest integrated solar and battery storage project. The site sits partly on land leased from Edwards Air Force Base, and the company says its offtake structure was well received by lenders.

sources.title: Terra-Gen Closes Financing for Second Phase of Edwards Sanborn Solar Storage Franchise in California

title: Prospect14 and investor group led by Jones Family Office form Ampliform solar JV in the US

advisors.name: Guggenheim Securities
advisors.role: financial advisor, structuring advisor, private placement agent and arranger

advisors.name: Sullivan & Cromwell LLP
advisors.role: counsel to investor group and Ampliform

summary: Solar developer Prospect14 has launched Ampliform, a joint venture with an investor consortium led by the Jones Family Office, alongside Barings and the George Kaiser Family Foundation. The venture will develop, build and run utility-scale solar and solar plus storage projects in the United States. It starts with more than 3 GW of projects in development, with a target pipeline above 10 GW by 2025.
details: Ampliform begins with over 3 GW of early- and mid-stage projects, and the first are expected to start construction in 2023. Prospect14 will supply greenfield origination, development and construction services, meaning it finds and prepares new sites from scratch. Greens Ledge Renewable Partners, whose team has power trading and plant optimization backgrounds, is investing and joining the leadership team. The equity commitment amount was not disclosed. Guggenheim Securities advised on the JV formation and arranged the financing, Sullivan & Cromwell advised the investors and Ampliform, and Jefferies and Greeneurlocker advised Prospect14.
context: The partners say they plan to own and operate the projects and to move toward a merchant model, which means selling power at market prices rather than under long fixed contracts. Prospect14 claims its data-driven siting and grid connection work, combined with the investors' trading expertise, sets the venture apart. Ampliform also intends to grow through acquisitions of solar projects and grid interconnection capacity.

sources.title: NEW JOINT VENTURE FORMED BY PROSPECT14 AND INVESTMENT AND OPERATING PARTNERS TO DEVELOP UTILITY-SCALE SOLAR PROJECTS

title: SunVest Solar acquires and energizes three 2 MWac community solar projects in Illinois
target: Three Illinois community solar projects in Glenwood, Mazon and Elba
summary: Wisconsin-based developer SunVest Solar has bought three community solar projects in Illinois from an unnamed developer and brought them into operation. Each site is 2 MWac, for 6 MWac in total. The price was not disclosed.
details: Community solar projects are local solar farms whose output is shared by subscribing homes and businesses. Two of the sites, in Glenwood and Mazon, sit in Commonwealth Edison's service area, and the third, in Elba, is in Ameren's area. The company says the Glenwood site is believed to be the first community solar project energized in Cook County. SunVest says it has acquired nearly 90 MWac of Illinois projects together with another developer, of which nearly 74 MWac are operating or have reached notice to proceed, meaning construction can formally begin.
context: SunVest describes these purchases as the first of many planned across the US and says it is pursuing community solar sites in 14 states. The projects rely on Illinois incentives such as solar renewable energy credits and the Climate and Equitable Jobs Act. The company says its financial partners position it to acquire more assets soon.

sources.title: SunVest Solar Acquires and Energizes Three Community Solar Projects in Illinois, First of Many Nationwide

title: SunPower takes minority stakes in solar dealers Renova Energy and EmPower Solar
summary: SunPower has made minority investments in two US residential solar installers, Renova Energy in California's Coachella Valley and EmPower Solar on Long Island, New York. The amounts and stake sizes were not disclosed.
details: Both companies join SunPower's Dealer Accelerator Program, launched in March 2022, which gives selected dealers capital and business strategy support. Participating dealers sell SunPower solar systems exclusively and also offer its SunVault home batteries and SunPower Financial loan products. Renova, with over 300 staff, installed about 11.5 MW of solar in 2021 across California and Arizona. EmPower installed 7.79 MW of distributed solar, meaning small systems on homes and businesses, in 2021.
context: SunPower says consumer demand for home solar is at a record high, helped by new federal incentives, and it wants local dealers to capture that demand while expanding sales of its products. The deals follow similar investments earlier in 2022 in Freedom Solar Power and Sea Bright Solar under the same program.

sources.title: SunPower invests in leading solar dealers Renova Energy and EmPower Solar

title: Clēnera closes construction and tax equity financing for 105 MWdc Apex Solar project in Montana

advisors.name: Paragon Energy Capital
advisors.role: exclusive tax equity advisor to Clēnera

summary: Clēnera, a US subsidiary of Israel's Enlight Renewable Energy, has closed construction and tax equity financing for its 105 MWdc Apex Solar project in Beaverhead County, Montana. Bank of America and NORD/LB are providing a construction loan, and Huntington National Bank is providing long-term tax equity financing. The amount was not disclosed.
details: Apex Solar is a utility-scale solar plant and the first project Clēnera will build in Montana. Its power will be sold to NorthWestern Energy under a long-term power purchase agreement, a contract to buy the output at agreed terms, while the renewable energy credits will be sold separately. Bank of America and NORD/LB fund construction through a loan, and after the plant starts operating Huntington will provide financing through a 25-year sale-leaseback, where the bank buys the plant and leases it back to Clēnera, combining tax benefits with long-term funding. Greenberg Traurig was legal counsel to Clēnera and Paragon Energy Capital was its tax equity advisor. Commercial operation is expected in the second quarter of 2023.
context: The companies say Apex Solar will be among the largest utility-scale solar projects in Montana. Clēnera describes its single-transaction approach to tax benefits and long-term financing as unusual in the US utility-scale market. Enlight claims the financing gives competitive pricing and a better return on equity, and Clēnera says it is working toward 12 GWdc of solar alongside a growing storage business.

sources.title: Clēnera, an Enlight Company, Closes on Financing for Montana Utility-Scale Solar Project

title: Fundamental Renewables secures $400 million credit facility led by Delaware Life

buyers.name: CDPQ American Fixed Income V Inc.

summary: Fundamental Renewables, the clean energy investment arm of Fundamental Advisors, has secured a $400 million credit facility. Delaware Life Insurance Company arranged the facility and is a lead lender, joined by a CDPQ subsidiary and East West Bank.
details: A credit facility is a pool of borrowing the company can draw on as needed rather than a single loan for one project. Fundamental Renewables plans to use the money to invest in solar and other renewable assets and to lend to clean energy developers across the United States. Delaware Life, part of Group 1001, said this is its fourth financing for Fundamental. The other lenders are CDPQ American Fixed Income V Inc., a wholly owned unit of Canadian pension investor CDPQ, and East West Bank.
context: The facility gives Fundamental Renewables more capital to offer developers flexible financing, which the company says will help it grow its platform. Fundamental says it has closed over $5 billion of renewable energy development and construction loans since starting its renewable strategy in 2015. The lenders presented their participation as part of their support for a lower carbon economy.

sources.title: Fundamental Renewables Secures $400 Million Credit Facility

title: BASF signs 12-year, 48 MW solar PPA with X-ELIO for Freeport, Texas site
target: Liberty Solar Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Plant
summary: Chemical maker BASF has agreed to buy 48 MW of solar power from X-ELIO under a 12-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity at agreed terms. The power will supply BASF's Verbund manufacturing site in Freeport, Texas.
details: The electricity will come from X-ELIO's 72 MW Liberty Solar Photovoltaic project in Houston, which is expected to start operating in 2024 and to produce about 137 GWh per year. The project will also include a 60 MW energy storage system, a battery that can hold power for later use. X-ELIO says the project involves more than $130 million of capital investment in Texas and up to 125 construction jobs. The release does not state the price or financial terms of the contract.
context: BASF says the deal means all of the Freeport site's expected purchased power will come from renewable sources, and it estimates, based on EPA figures, that it will offset more than 82,000 metric tons of CO2 per year. The company links the agreement to its targets of cutting greenhouse gas emissions 25% by 2030 versus 2018 and reaching net zero by 2050. For X-ELIO, the contract supports its strategy of selling renewable power to industrial customers.

sources.title: BASF and X-ELIO sign power purchase agreement to supply Freeport site with renewable energy

title: Pattern Energy and GPI close financing for 112 MW Ishikari offshore wind and storage project in Japan
summary: Pattern Energy and its Japanese affiliate Green Power Investment Corporation have completed financing for the 112 MW Ishikari Offshore Wind project in Hokkaido, Japan. The project includes a 100 MW, 180 MWh battery system, and full construction has started. The loan amount was not disclosed.
details: The wind farm sits about three kilometers off the coast in Ishikari Bay and will use 14 Siemens Gamesa 8 MW turbines designed for offshore conditions such as typhoons and earthquakes. The battery component can deliver 100 MW for under two hours, storing 180 MWh in total. The debt was jointly arranged by seven banks including MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho and the Development Bank of Japan. Hokkaido Electric Power Network will buy all of the output under a 20-year power purchase agreement, a long-term contract to buy electricity at agreed terms. Commercial operation is expected in December 2023.
context: Pattern Energy describes the project as Japan's largest combined offshore wind and storage facility and the first in the country to install an 8 MW offshore turbine. The company says the project follows more than 15 years of planning and that the bank group reflects strong demand for clean power. It brings Pattern's Japanese portfolio to eight facilities operating or under construction. Pattern Energy holds a majority interest in GPI.

sources.title: Pattern Energy Closes Financing of Japan's Largest Offshore Wind Power and Storage Project

title: Cypress Creek Renewables closes $216 million financing for Zier solar and storage project in Texas

buyers.name: NORD/LB
buyers.role: Coordinating lead arranger, lender and LC issuing bank

summary: Cypress Creek Renewables has closed $216 million in debt financing for its Zier Solar and Storage project in Kinney County, Texas. The project pairs a 208 MW solar farm with a 40 MW/80 MWh battery system. NORD/LB led the bank group with Rabobank, National Bank of Canada and the North American Development Bank.
details: The project combines 208 MW of solar generation with a battery that can deliver 40 MW for about two hours (80 MWh). The financing includes a construction-to-term loan, which funds building and then converts into a long-term loan once the plant operates, plus a tax equity bridge loan, which is short-term money covering the gap until tax equity investors (who invest in exchange for tax credits) fund the project. Letter of credit facilities, a form of bank guarantee, were also provided. Construction started at the same time as financial close, the point when funding becomes available.
context: This is the first solar-plus-storage project Cypress Creek has developed in Texas, where it says it has developed close to 2 GW of solar. The company expects the project to power more than 30,000 homes in its first year and to support grid reliability in Texas. NORD/LB says this is the fourth deal it has led as coordinating arranger for Cypress Creek in the past 12 months.

sources.title: Cypress Creek Renewables Closes Financing for Texas Solar and Storage Project

title: TIU Canada and Siksika Nation form joint venture for Gleichen Solar project in Alberta
summary: Solar producer TIU Canada has signed an agreement with the Siksika Nation to set up a joint venture for renewable energy projects. The first project is the Gleichen Solar development on 72 acres in Wheatland County, Alberta, within Siksika Nation traditional territory.
details: The agreement was signed on June 1, 2022 by TIU Canada director Vlad Lizunov and Shane Breaker, interim CEO of SRDL, acting for the Siksika Nation. The partners plan to jointly build solar generation facilities in Alberta, starting with the Gleichen Solar site. The release does not state the project's capacity, cost or ownership split. Formal approvals and power purchase agreements, which are long-term contracts to sell the electricity, are expected in the following months.
context: The Siksika Nation says the partnership is a way to enter the solar industry and build future growth on its own territory. TIU Canada, which says it has managed solar projects since 2016 and operates 45 MW, expects the project to bring jobs, clean power and investment to Alberta.

sources.title: Joint Venture Agreement on Solar Energy Signed with Siksika Nation

title: Amp Energy closes KeyBank debt and U.S. Bank tax equity for 61 MW community solar-plus-storage portfolio
target: 13-project community solar plus storage portfolio in Massachusetts and New York
summary: Amp Energy has closed financing for a 13-project community solar portfolio with battery storage in Massachusetts and New York, valued at US$155 million. KeyBank led the construction and term loans and U.S. Bank provided tax equity.
details: The portfolio totals 61 MW of solar and 6.5 MWh of storage, with most projects due to start commercial operation in 2022 and the rest in the second quarter of 2023. Three projects include DC-coupled batteries, meaning the batteries connect directly to the solar side before power is converted for the grid. These batteries will be run by Amp's Amp X software to maximize fixed revenues under the Massachusetts SMART incentive program while also trading in ISO New England wholesale markets. Tax equity is an investment by a bank that receives the project's federal tax credits in return for funding, and construction and term debt covers building costs and then longer-term repayment. Community solar lets customers who cannot install rooftop panels subscribe to a shared solar farm.
context: This is the fourth deal among Amp, KeyBank and U.S. Bank since 2017. Amp says the financing takes its total tax equity and debt raised in the US community solar market past US$500 million. The company also says its US business has passed 200 MW of operating and under-construction assets, with about 500 MW more planned over the next two to three years.

sources.title: Amp Energy Secures Tax Equity and Debt Financing for $155M Community Solar Plus Storage Portfolio in Repeat Transactions with U.S. Bank and KeyBank

title: SM Investments gets SEC approval to buy remaining 81% of geothermal steam producer PGPC's parent

sellers.name: Related parties of SM Investments Corporation

target: Allfirst Equity Holdings Inc (holding company of Philippine Geothermal Production Company, Inc)
summary: SM Investments Corporation received Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission approval to acquire an 81% stake in Allfirst Equity Holdings, the parent of Philippine Geothermal Production Company, from related parties. The deal is valued at P15.76 billion and will lift SMIC's ownership of PGPC to 100%.
details: SMIC will pay for the stake by issuing 17.44 million new shares to the sellers, about 1.4% of its outstanding shares, rather than paying cash. PGPC runs the Tiwi and Mak-Ban geothermal steam fields in the Philippines, which have operated since 1979 and supply enough underground steam to generate roughly 300 MW of electricity. The company also holds several undeveloped greenfield concession areas, meaning sites licensed for future geothermal steam production, which it plans to develop.
context: PGPC reported 2021 revenue of US$99.4 million and net income of US$48.8 million, which SMIC says equals 1.2% of its revenue and would add 5.5% to its 2021 net income. SMIC, a conglomerate focused on retail, banking and property, describes the deal as accretive and a strategic fit that supports its sustainability goals. Tiwi is described as the first commercial-scale geothermal steam field in Southeast Asia.

sources.title: SMIC receives approval to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production Company (PGPC)

title: Natixis arranges about US$360 million financing for CC&L Infrastructure and CarbonFree Chilean PMGD solar portfolio

buyers.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
buyers.role: Lead placement agent, sole bookrunner, underwriter and green coordinator

target: Portfolio of 53 PMGD solar photovoltaic projects in Chile

advisors.name: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking
advisors.role: Lead placement agent and green issuance coordinator

summary: Natixis CIB arranged roughly US$360 million of debt for a portfolio of 53 small-scale solar plants in Chile owned by CC&L Infrastructure and CarbonFree Technology. The portfolio is expected to total about 360 MWdc. Most of the money comes from a US private placement bond that refinances existing bank loans.
details: The package has three parts: a US$19 million letter of credit facility, a US$71 million bridge loan to pay for construction still under way, and a private placement of about US$270 million. A private placement is a bond sold directly to a small group of institutional investors rather than on a public exchange. Its proceeds will mainly refinance existing bank debt and repay the bridge loan once construction ends. The projects run under Chile's PMGD regime for distributed generation, which lets small plants sell power at a regulated stabilized price. Once all are operating, the sponsors say the plants will produce more than 750,000 MWh per year.
context: The parties describe it as the largest PMGD portfolio financed so far in Chile by both capacity and project count. Natixis says it is its twelfth PMGD financing in three years, bringing its total in the segment to about US$1.5 billion. CC&L Infrastructure presents the deal as the payoff of a multi-year strategy of aggregating small projects to secure long-term financing, and Natixis says several US institutional investors took part despite a more difficult market.

sources.title: Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking leads CC&L Infrastructure and CarbonFree US$360 million hybrid bond private placement and debt financing for largest PV PMGD portfolio financed to date in Chile

title: Pivot Energy acquires Maryland community solar developer SGC Power
summary: Denver-based Pivot Energy, which is owned by investor ECP, has acquired SGC Power, a community solar developer headquartered in Maryland. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: SGC Power finds sites and develops and designs community solar projects, meaning local solar farms or rooftop systems whose power is shared by nearby subscribers while landowners earn lease income. Since its founding in 2008 the company says it has been involved in more than 285 projects totaling about 2,845 MW across over 31 states and territories. SGC Power will keep operating as a business unit under the Pivot Energy brand, and its daily activities are said to remain unchanged. The release does not name the sellers, a price or advisers.
context: Pivot says the deal will help it scale early-stage greenfield development, add products and widen its national footprint. SGC is expected to gain access to new markets through Pivot's development and long-term ownership capabilities. The companies describe community solar as the fastest growing part of the solar industry, with programs active in 21 states and the District of Columbia.

sources.title: Pivot Energy Announces Acquisition of Maryland-Based Community Solar Developer SGC Power

title: Liberty completes acquisition of Wisconsin dairy RNG developer Sandhill Advanced Biofuels
summary: Liberty, a subsidiary of Algonquin Power & Utilities, has completed its purchase of Sandhill Advanced Biofuels, a developer of renewable natural gas projects on dairy farms. Sandhill's portfolio consists of four projects in Wisconsin. No price was disclosed.
details: The projects use anaerobic digesters, which are sealed tanks where bacteria break down manure and release methane, plus upgrading systems that clean the gas so it can be injected into the natural gas pipeline network. Once all four sites run, they are expected to produce about 500 MMBTU (million British thermal units) of renewable natural gas per day, aimed at the transportation sector. Two sites are already operating and the other two are expected to start in 2023. Separately, Liberty joined more than forty partners in a New York-led consortium preparing a bid for a regional clean hydrogen hub, which is not a transaction in itself.
context: The release describes this as the company's first investment in renewable natural gas outside its regulated utility business. Algonquin says the move adds to its wind, solar and hydro holdings and responds to corporate customers seeking renewable energy. The company also expects the projects to give farmers extra income and help cut greenhouse gas emissions.

sources.title: Liberty completes acquisition of Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) platform and partners on Hydrogen Hub project

title: Evergy agrees to buy 199 MW Persimmon Creek wind farm in Oklahoma from Scout Clean Energy and Elawan

advisors.name: McDermott Will & Emery LLP
advisors.role: legal advisor to Scout Clean Energy

summary: US utility Evergy has agreed to acquire the 199 MW Persimmon Creek wind farm in western Oklahoma from Scout Clean Energy and its joint venture partner Elawan Energy. The total consideration is about US$250 million.
details: Persimmon Creek has been operating since 2018 and uses 80 General Electric turbines spread over 17,000 acres in Dewey, Ellis and Woodward counties. Its output will be used to serve customers in Evergy's service area in Kansas and Missouri. Although the release describes the sale as completed, it also says closing is expected in the first quarter of 2023, subject to conditions including regulatory approvals. McDermott Will & Emery advised Scout and Morgan, Lewis & Bockius advised Evergy.
context: The purchase adds owned wind generation to Evergy's portfolio, which the utility says will bring long-term benefits to its customers. For Scout, a portfolio company of investment manager Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners, the sale monetises an operating asset while it develops a pipeline it puts at over 15 GW across 24 states. Elawan Energy is part of the ORIX Group.

sources.title: Scout Clean Energy Sells Persimmon Creek Wind Farm to Evergy

title: Live Oak Bank provides about $6.6 million permanent debt for two CVE community solar projects in Acushnet, Massachusetts
target: Two community solar projects in Acushnet, Massachusetts
summary: CVE North America has closed roughly $6.6 million of permanent debt financing from Live Oak Bank for two community solar projects in Acushnet, Massachusetts. The two plants have a combined capacity of 4.2 MW.
details: Permanent debt is long-term lending that replaces short-term construction funding once projects are running. The two Acushnet plants qualify as community solar under the state's SMART incentive program, in which local homes and businesses subscribe to a share of a nearby solar farm and receive bill credits for the power it produces. With these additions, CVE's Massachusetts portfolio financed with Live Oak over the past two years totals nine operating plants with more than 37 MW. CVE says the plants serve over 800 local subscribers through its Halo brand.
context: The company says the financing gives it more flexibility to grow in Massachusetts and other US community solar markets. CVE reports about 250 MW of projects in development, including more than 70 MW starting construction in New York State in 2022, and aims to exceed 450 MW in the US by 2026. CVE North America is part of France-based CVE Group.

sources.title: CVE North America and Live Oak Bank close permanent debt financing of two more community solar farms in Massachusetts

title: Enfinity Global secures $242 million long-term financing for 70 MW of operating Japanese solar plants

buyers.name: Nomura
buyers.role: initial lead arranger and sole bookrunner

target: Three operational utility-scale solar PV plants in Japan (70 MW)
summary: Enfinity Global has raised $242 million (about 29 billion yen) in long-term debt for three recently completed solar plants in Japan with a combined 70 MW. Nomura and Aozora Bank arranged the financing.
details: The three utility-scale solar PV plants, which include the Kurokawa project, are already built and operating. Their power is sold for 18 years under Japan's feed-in tariff (FIT) program, a government scheme that pays a fixed price for renewable electricity. Nomura acted as initial lead arranger and sole bookrunner, meaning it structured the loan and placed it with lenders, while Aozora Bank acted as lead arranger and agent, handling administration of the loan. Because the plants are completed, the deal is long-term financing of operating assets rather than construction funding.
context: The deal follows Enfinity Global's earlier 2022 acquisition of a 250 MW Japanese solar portfolio with an enterprise value of $1 billion, which the company says made it one of the industry leaders in Japan. The company presents the financing as support for Japan's goal of carbon neutrality by 2050. The long FIT contracts provide predictable revenue that lenders typically rely on for such loans.

sources.title: Enfinity Global closes $242 million of long term financing for three operational solar power plants in Japan

title: CIT arranges financing for Swell Energy's California commercial behind-the-meter storage pipeline
target: Pipeline of over 100 behind-the-meter commercial energy storage projects in California
summary: CIT, a division of First Citizens Bank, acted as sole lead arranger of financing for a subsidiary of Swell Energy. The funds support development of more than 100 battery storage projects on commercial properties across California. The loan amount and capacity were not disclosed.
details: The projects are behind-the-meter systems, meaning batteries installed on the customer's side of the electricity meter to cut that site's own power bills rather than selling into the grid. They sit on commercial properties throughout California and are still being developed. The projects benefit from California's Self-Generation Incentive Program, a state incentive that partly aims to bring storage to underserved communities. As sole lead arranger, CIT's Power and Energy business structured and organized the financing for the Swell subsidiary that is the borrower.
context: Swell Energy says the small commercial segment, which it calls ultra-light commercial, is a large untapped market for storage. CIT describes itself as a leading financier of battery storage and says it hopes to work with Swell again. The deal shows lenders financing aggregated portfolios of small distributed storage projects.

sources.title: CIT Serves as Sole Lead Arranger of Financing for Swell Energy's Commercial Behind-The-Meter Energy Storage Projects

title: Cypress Creek Renewables acquires 100 MW early-stage New York solar project from Carson Power
target: 100 MW solar project near Rochester, New York
summary: Cypress Creek Renewables has bought a 100 MW solar project near Rochester, New York, from developer Carson Power. The project joins Cypress Creek's development portfolio in the NYISO market, the grid region run by the New York Independent System Operator. Financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The project is at an early stage of development and is expected to start operating in 2026. Carson Power will stay on as co-developer, handling permits and land approvals (entitlement) and community engagement. Cypress Creek will lead the main development work, including finding a buyer for the power (offtake), procuring equipment and arranging financing. Carson Power's CEO said the goal is to bring the project to notice to proceed, the point at which construction can begin.
context: Cypress Creek says it has developed more than 11 GW of solar and storage nationally and has more than 35 projects operating in New York, with 55 more in development there. The company describes the deal as the start of a relationship in which it provides development capital to Carson Power, a New York City developer expanding from community solar into utility-scale solar and storage.

sources.title: Cypress Creek Renewables Acquires 100MW Solar Asset from Carson Power

title: SolaREIT provides $12.2 million in land financing to Norbut Solar Farms for New York community solar
target: Land under four community solar projects in New York
summary: SolaREIT, a solar real estate investment fund based in Maryland, signed land agreements worth $12.2 million with developer Norbut Solar Farms. The deals cover more than 500 acres in New York that host four community solar projects totalling over 84 MW.
details: The transaction involves the land beneath four community solar projects in New York, meaning solar farms whose output is shared by multiple local subscribers rather than a single owner. SolaREIT finances the land holdings so the developer does not have to tie up its own capital in land or lease payments. The release does not break down the capacity by project or give expected construction dates. SolaREIT previously offered a product that lets developers pay landowners up front for up to 30 years of lease payments.
context: Norbut Solar Farms says the capital raised will support expansion of its early-stage development work across New York. SolaREIT argues that land and lease costs are a major burden for community solar developers and that its model frees up capital and lowers costs. The fund launched in late 2020.

sources.title: SolaREIT Closes on $12 Million in Land Deals with Norbut Solar Farms

title: ECP completes acquisition of Borrego's solar and storage development business, now New Leaf Energy
target: New Leaf Energy (Borrego's solar and energy storage development business)
summary: Borrego has completed the spin-off and sale of its solar and energy storage development arm to investor ECP. The business will run independently under ECP as New Leaf Energy, with a pipeline of about 450 projects in the United States. No price was disclosed.
details: New Leaf Energy, based in Lowell, Massachusetts, holds a pipeline of more than 8.5 GW of solar and 7 GW / 28 GWh of energy storage projects. It focuses on distributed generation, meaning smaller systems connected close to where power is used, as well as utility-scale projects. Core markets include New York, Massachusetts, Maine, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Delaware and Illinois, with utility-scale work also planned in California, Arizona and Colorado. The existing development leadership team, led by CEO Dan Berwick, will run the company. J.P. Morgan Securities acted as exclusive financial adviser to Borrego and Covington Burling provided legal counsel.
context: ECP says New Leaf Energy becomes its 11th renewable platform and its fourth focused on solar. Borrego says it will now concentrate on its engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) and third-party operations and maintenance businesses. The deal separates early-stage project development from Borrego's construction and service activities.

sources.title: Borrego Completes Spin Off and Sale of Solar and Energy Storage Development Business to ECP

title: Idemitsu Renewables closes $61M tax equity and debt financing for 73 MW Luciana Solar in California
summary: Idemitsu Renewables, the US arm of Japan's Idemitsu Kosan, has completed funding of about $61 million in tax equity and debt financing for its 73 MW Luciana Solar Project in Tulare County, California. Morgan Stanley Renewables supplied the tax equity and Rabobank supplied the debt.
details: The Luciana project is a utility-scale solar plant that started commercial operation in May 2022 and is owned and operated by Idemitsu Renewables. Tax equity is investment from a party that receives the project's federal tax benefits in return for funding, and here it came from Morgan Stanley Renewables Inc. Rabobank provided the loan portion of the financing. The release does not break down the $61 million between the two sources. The plant's output is directed to Northern California, and the company says it matches the power needs of more than 20,000 homes.
context: The project adds to Idemitsu Renewables' operating assets in California and Colorado alongside a development pipeline across several US grid regions. The company presents the financing as evidence of its ability to take projects from early development through to operation, and both Morgan Stanley and Rabobank said they had worked with or hope to keep working with Idemitsu.

sources.title: Idemitsu Renewables Completes Funding of $61M Tax Equity and Debt Financing for Luciana Solar project

title: Cypress Creek Renewables acquires 400 MW Texas storage portfolio from Black Mountain Energy Storage
target: Four standalone energy storage projects in Texas (400MW/600MWh)
summary: Cypress Creek Renewables has bought four standalone battery storage projects in Texas from developer Black Mountain Energy Storage. The portfolio totals 400 MW of power capacity and 600 MWh of storage. No price was disclosed.
details: The portfolio consists of four projects of 100 MW each, spread across the ERCOT market, the grid that serves most of Texas. Based on the stated totals, the batteries can discharge at full power for about one and a half hours. The projects are still in development, and Cypress Creek will handle the remaining permitting, engineering, procurement, financing and construction, then operate them. The projects are expected to enter service in 2024. The sale was arranged through the LevelTen Energy Asset Marketplace, an online platform that matches project sellers with buyers.
context: The deal expands Cypress Creek's storage holdings in Texas, where the company says it has developed 5 GW of solar and storage. Cypress Creek argues that standalone batteries, which are not paired with a solar or wind plant, can improve grid reliability in ERCOT by supplying power on demand. For Black Mountain, a developer founded in 2021, the sale hands off early-stage projects to a larger firm to build and run.

sources.title: Cypress Creek Renewables Acquires 400MW from Black Mountain Energy Storage

title: MasTec agrees to acquire renewable construction contractor IEA for about $1.1 billion

advisors.name: Fried Frank Harris Shriver & Jacobson LLP

summary: Infrastructure contractor MasTec has signed a definitive agreement to buy all shares of Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives (IEA), an Indianapolis-based builder of utility-scale wind and solar projects. The cash-and-stock deal values IEA at $14.00 per share, with total consideration of about $1.1 billion including IEA's estimated net debt.
details: IEA shareholders will get $10.50 in cash plus 0.0483 of a MasTec share per IEA share, which MasTec says is a 34% premium to IEA's July 22, 2022 closing price. MasTec expects to issue about 2.8 million new shares and has committed bridge financing (a short-term backup loan) from Bank of America and J.P. Morgan, though it plans to seek other debt to fund the cash part. Holders of about 35% of IEA stock have agreed to vote in favor, and closing is expected in late fourth quarter 2022 subject to shareholder and Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust approval. J.P. Morgan Securities, Fried Frank and Holland & Knight advise MasTec, while Lazard and Gibson Dunn advise IEA.
context: IEA says it has completed more than 260 utility-scale wind and solar projects in North America and has almost 6,000 employees, including a union-based workforce. MasTec says the deal will add scale to meet expected growth in renewable power demand and pair IEA's generation construction with its own grid transmission work. MasTec expects the deal to add to its 2023 adjusted earnings per share and projects IEA 2023 revenue of $2.6 to $2.7 billion.

sources.title: MasTec to Acquire Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives, Inc. ("IEA"), a Premier Renewable Energy and Infrastructure Services Provider

title: CIT and Siemens Financial Services arrange $88 million for Aypa Power's 173 MW Wolf Tank storage project in Texas
summary: CIT, a division of First Citizens Bank, arranged $88 million in financing for the 173 MW Wolf Tank stand-alone battery storage project in Webb County, Texas. The borrower is an affiliate of Aypa Power, a Blackstone portfolio company.
details: Wolf Tank Storage is a stand-alone merchant battery facility, meaning it sells power and grid services at market prices rather than under a long-term fixed contract. It sits in the south region of ERCOT, the Texas grid operator. Construction is under way and completion is expected in the first quarter of 2023. Siemens Financial Services acted as joint lead arranger alongside CIT. The storage energy capacity in MWh was not disclosed.
context: Aypa Power says battery storage helps integrate renewable generation and keep electricity flowing reliably. CIT says the project will support renewable power and grid reliability in South Texas, and the deal adds to its activity as a lender to U.S. battery and renewable projects.

sources.title: CIT Serves as Lead Arranger of $88 Million Financing for Texas Battery Energy Storage System

title: Polar Racking acquires Axsus Solar tracker business from Magna Closures
summary: Polar Racking, a Canadian maker of mounting systems for solar panels, has acquired Axsus Solar, the solar division of Magna Closures Inc. No price was disclosed.
details: The main product gained is the Axsus Sol-X, a single-axis tracker, which is a mounting system that slowly turns solar panels to follow the sun during the day and so produce more power than fixed panels. Polar says the Sol-X has fewer parts, installs quickly and needs less ground preparation. Axsus staff in engineering, quality control and project management join Polar, and former Axsus team member Robert Souliere becomes Polar's Director of Operations and Construction. Financial terms and advisers were not named.
context: The deal adds trackers to a product line that already includes ground-mount and carport systems, at a time when Polar says buyers increasingly prefer trackers over fixed-tilt designs. Polar states the combined teams have more than 3 GW of installed systems and that it has a pipeline of about 10 GW. The company expects the deal to support further growth across North America and the Caribbean.

sources.title: Polar Racking Deepens its Leadership in PV Mounting Systems with the Acquisition of Axsus Solar

title: Omega Energia acquires FGE Goodnight wind project in Texas from FGE Power

advisors.name: Karbone Capital Markets
advisors.role: former tax equity financing advisor to FGE Power

summary: Austin-based developer FGE Power has sold full ownership of its FGE Goodnight wind project in Texas to Brazilian renewable energy company Omega Energia. The first two phases total 531 MW. No price was disclosed.
details: The project includes Goodnight I and Goodnight II, each sized at 265.5 MW. Construction on Goodnight I began alongside the sale, and Goodnight II is expected to start construction soon, with both phases able to reach commercial operation by the end of 2023. Goodnight I will use Vestas V136-4.5MW turbines, and Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives is the EPC contractor, meaning the firm handling engineering, procurement and construction. A third phase of more than 200 MW is in early development, and whether it is built depends on decisions by the new owner.
context: FGE Power says that once the third phase is complete, the overall project would be the largest operating wind farm in Texas. The release presents the deal as an example of foreign investors taking part in the US renewable energy market. Omega Energia describes itself as Latin America's largest renewable energy company, and its CEO pointed to the project's wind measurement work and transmission solution as strengths.

sources.title: FGE Power Announces Sale of FGE Goodnight Wind Farm Project to Omega Energia

title: Whetstone Power and Rosemawr acquire 30 MW operating solar plant in Alamosa, Colorado
target: 30 MW-ac operating solar facility in Alamosa, Colorado
summary: Whetstone Power and Rosemawr Sustainable Infrastructure Management, the sustainable infrastructure arm of Rosemawr Management, have acquired a 30 MW-ac solar plant already in operation in Alamosa, Colorado. The seller and price were not disclosed.
details: The plant's entire electricity output is under contract to Public Service Company of Colorado, a subsidiary of Xcel Energy. Whetstone Power Operations, a wholly-owned Whetstone subsidiary, will handle operations, maintenance and asset management. The facility currently uses high concentrating solar systems, which focus sunlight onto small cells, and the buyers plan to replace them over the longer term with standard photovoltaic panels, possibly adding battery storage while reusing much of the existing infrastructure. FTI Capital Advisors acted as sell-side adviser.
context: The deal adds an operating, fully contracted asset to the partnership between Whetstone and Rosemawr, an investment firm that reports about $1.3 billion in assets under management and investments in more than 90 energy projects across 14 states. The planned refurbishment points to the buyers' intention to modernise an older solar technology site rather than build from scratch.

sources.title: Whetstone Power and Rosemawr Announce Acquisition of 30 MW operating solar facility in Colorado

title: Infinity Group and Africa Finance Corporation agree to buy Lekela Power from Actis and Mainstream
summary: Actis and a consortium led by Mainstream Renewable Power have agreed to sell Lekela Power, an African wind power producer, to Infinity Group and Africa Finance Corporation. The deal values Lekela at an enterprise value of about US$1.5 billion, meaning the combined worth of its equity and debt. Lekela owns more than 1 GW of operating wind farms in South Africa, Egypt and Senegal.
details: Lekela operates five wind farms in South Africa totalling 624 MW, one in Egypt of 252 MW and one in Senegal of 159 MW, and holds development opportunities in Ghana, Senegal and Egypt. It was set up in 2015 as a joint venture owned 60% by Actis and 40% by Mainstream Renewable Power Africa Holdings, a consortium including Mainstream, IFC and IFC-managed funds, Rockefeller Brothers Fund, Ascension Investment Management and Sanlam. Mainstream holds a 13.52% net stake and expects net proceeds of about US$90 million, subject to closing adjustments. The sale needs regulatory approvals and other usual conditions and is expected to close later in 2022.
context: Lekela describes itself as Africa's largest pure-play renewable independent power producer, a company that owns plants and sells their electricity. For Mainstream, majority-owned by Aker Horizons, the sale follows its June 2022 exit from the Chilean joint venture Aela Energía to Innergex, and the company presents it as the conclusion of its partnership strategy with Actis.

sources.title: Aker Horizons: Mainstream Renewable Power Signs Agreement for the Sale of African Renewable Energy IPP

title: Clean Energy Systems agrees to acquire idled Madera biomass plant in California for carbon removal conversion
summary: Clean Energy Systems has signed an agreement to buy the idled Madera Biomass Power Plant in Madera County, California. The company plans to turn the plant into a biomass carbon removal and storage facility. The price, seller and plant capacity were not disclosed.
details: Once converted, the facility would gasify local agricultural waste into a synthesis gas that is burned with pure oxygen to make electricity and possibly hydrogen. The resulting carbon dioxide would be injected deep underground for permanent storage, and the company expects to capture more than 99% of the process carbon. CES projects the plant would remove about 600,000 tons of CO2 per year and consume about 400,000 tons of farm waste annually. The deal depends on further due diligence, meaning more detailed checks of the asset, and closing is expected in early 2023.
context: Biomass carbon removal and storage, or BiCRS, aims for net-negative emissions because plants absorb CO2 as they grow and that carbon is then stored rather than released. CES says the project would support California's plan to phase out agricultural burning in the San Joaquin Valley by 2025 and improve local air quality. The company is developing similar projects in Fresno and Kern Counties.

sources.title: CLEAN ENERGY SYSTEMS ENTERS INTO AN AGREEMENT TO ACQUIRE THE MADERA BIOMASS POWER PLANT

title: ReNew refinances US$525 million of 2024 dollar bonds with Indian project debt
summary: Indian renewable power producer ReNew Energy Global has refinanced US$525 million of dollar bonds due in 2024 using amortising project loans from an unnamed Indian nonbank lender. The company says it is the first Indian renewable energy firm to retire dollar bonds this way.
details: The bonds, known as RPVIN 6.67% 24s, were issued in 2019 and were due to mature in 2024. They were replaced with amortising project debt, meaning the loan is repaid gradually over its life rather than in one lump sum at the end. According to the company, the new financing lowers the rupee interest cost by 200 basis points (2 percentage points), fixes the rate for three years and extends maturity to the end of fiscal year 2027. The lender was described only as an Indian nonbank financial company.
context: ReNew presents the deal as evidence of its access to domestic debt markets and as a way to reduce the risk of having to refinance near-term debt during a period of rising interest rates. The company says the move did not draw on its growth capital. ReNew reports its gross portfolio has grown to about 12.8 GW from 10.2 GW at the start of 2022.

sources.title: ReNew Becomes First Indian Renewable Energy Company To Refinance Dollar-Denominated Bonds

title: Meijer signs renewable purchase agreement for NextEra's Lacy Creek wind project in Texas
summary: Midwestern retailer Meijer has signed a renewable product purchase agreement with a subsidiary of NextEra Energy Resources to buy most of the output of the Lacy Creek Wind Energy Center in Texas. The 108-turbine project is expected to supply Meijer with about 800,000 MWh of renewable electricity per year.
details: Lacy Creek is under construction across 60,000 acres in Glasscock and Sterling counties, Texas, and is expected to be finished in late 2022. It will use 108 wind turbines, though the release does not state its capacity in megawatts. Under the agreement, Meijer will buy the majority of the electricity the project produces, and the release does not give the contract length or price. A renewable purchase agreement of this kind is a long-term contract in which a buyer commits to purchase power or its environmental attributes from a specific project.
context: Meijer says the deal advances its goal of cutting absolute carbon emissions by 50 percent by 2025. It follows a March 2022 virtual power purchase agreement with Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions for a solar project in Navarro County, Texas, and the company expects both projects to begin producing energy by the end of 2022. NextEra said the wind project will bring jobs and tax revenue to the host counties.

sources.title: Meijer Invests in Wind Energy, Makes Significant Strides Toward its Goal of Reducing 50 Percent of Absolute Carbon Emissions by 2025

title: Meijer signs renewable purchase agreement for Lacy Creek wind project with NextEra Energy Resources

advisors.name: Schneider Electric
advisors.role: renewable procurement adviser to Meijer (solar project)

summary: Midwestern retailer Meijer has signed a renewable product purchase agreement with a subsidiary of NextEra Energy Resources for most of the output of the Lacy Creek Wind Energy Center in Texas. The deal is expected to supply about 800,000 MWh of renewable electricity to Meijer each year.
details: Lacy Creek is a 108-turbine wind farm under construction on about 60,000 acres in Glasscock and Sterling counties, Texas, with completion expected in late 2022. Under the agreement, a long-term contract to buy power or its renewable attributes, Meijer will take the majority of the energy the project generates. The release does not state the contract length, price or project capacity in megawatts. Schneider Electric is named as Meijer's adviser, though the release says its support related to the retailer's earlier solar deal.
context: Meijer says the deal advances its goal of cutting absolute carbon emissions by 50 percent by 2025. It follows a March 2022 virtual power purchase agreement with Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions for a solar project in Navarro County, Texas, and Meijer expects both projects to start producing energy by the end of 2022. NextEra says the project will bring jobs and tax revenue to the host counties.

sources.title: Meijer Invests in Wind Energy, Makes Significant Strides Toward its Goal of Reducing 50 Percent of Absolute Carbon Emissions by 2025

title: Honeywell Ventures joins Electric Hydrogen's US$198 million Series B round
summary: Honeywell Ventures, the venture investment arm of Honeywell, has invested in Electric Hydrogen's Series B financing round. The round, which also included other investors and banks, brought total funding to US$198 million. Electric Hydrogen is a US company developing electrolyzers that make green hydrogen.
details: A Series B round is a company's second major round of outside equity funding, usually used to grow beyond early development. Electric Hydrogen builds electrolyzers, machines that use electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, producing green hydrogen when the power comes from wind or solar. The company says the money will fund scaling up its high-throughput electrolyzer and manufacturing technology and large pilot projects for industrial and infrastructure uses. Honeywell's individual contribution was not disclosed. Electric Hydrogen was founded in 2020 and is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston.
context: Honeywell says the investment will help it better understand the electrolyzer market and could pair with its catalyst coated membrane technology, which it claims improved electrolyzer efficiency in lab tests. Electric Hydrogen says it targets heavy industries such as steel, ammonia and freight that are hard to run on electricity directly. Its other backers include Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Amazon Decarbonization Fund, Equinor Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Rio Tinto.

sources.title: HONEYWELL VENTURES TO MAKE INVESTMENT IN ELECTRIC HYDROGEN

title: Canadian Solar sells 345 MWp Suntop and Gunnedah solar farms in New South Wales to CalEnergy
summary: Canadian Solar has completed the sale of two solar farms, Suntop and Gunnedah, with a combined 345 MWp of capacity in New South Wales, Australia. The buyer is CalEnergy Resources (Australia), a subsidiary of Northern Powergrid Holdings Company. No price was disclosed.
details: The two projects have reached substantial completion, meaning construction is essentially finished, and are expected to produce more than 700,000 MWh of electricity per year. Both have long-term offtake agreements, which are contracts to sell their power, with an unnamed global technology company. MWp refers to peak direct-current output of the solar panels. Alongside the sale, the two companies signed a multi-year development services agreement to work together on Canadian Solar's Australian project pipeline.
context: The sale continues Canadian Solar's model of developing projects and selling them to long-term owners. The company says it has now taken seven Australian development projects to notice-to-proceed, the point where construction can begin, and is growing a multi-gigawatt solar and storage pipeline there. For CalEnergy, the deal expands its renewable portfolio in Australia and sets up a framework for further projects with Canadian Solar.

sources.title: Canadian Solar Completes Sale of Two Solar Farms Totaling 345 MWp in New South Wales, Australia

title: Onward Energy agrees to buy 1,171 MW operating US solar portfolio from Global Atlantic
target: 1,171 MW operating solar portfolio (11 projects in 8 US states)
summary: Onward Energy has signed a binding agreement to buy all of the cash equity interests in a 1,171 MW portfolio of operating solar projects from Global Atlantic Financial Group. The portfolio spans 11 projects across 8 US states. No price was disclosed.
details: The assets are already operating, meaning they are built and producing power. Onward is buying 100% of the cash equity, which is the ownership stake held by the main equity investor, as distinct from other financing such as debt or tax equity. Onpeak Capital acted as financial adviser and Mayer Brown as legal adviser to Global Atlantic, while Milbank advised Onward. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2022, subject to customary conditions.
context: Onward says this is the largest renewable investment in its history and will take its portfolio of solar, wind and gas assets to more than 6 GW. Global Atlantic, a life insurer majority-owned by KKR, built the portfolio over about seven years and says it intends to keep growing its presence in solar investment.

sources.title: ONWARD ENERGY TO ACQUIRE A 1,171 MW OPERATING SOLAR PORTFOLIO FROM GLOBAL ATLANTIC

title: Fundamental Renewables expands Birch Creek Development credit facility to $250 million
summary: Fundamental Renewables, the clean energy investment arm of Fundamental Advisors, agreed to enlarge its existing credit facility to US solar developer Birch Creek Development to $250 million. The money will support development and construction of utility-scale solar projects in the United States, along with acquisitions.
details: A credit facility is a loan arrangement that lets a borrower draw money as needed up to a set limit.
