Birch Creek plans to use the funds for development and construction of utility-scale solar projects, strategic acquisitions in key markets, and buying solar modules. The developer says it has a pipeline of more than 5 GW of utility-scale solar at various stages across the MISO and PJM grid regions, Texas and the Southeast. The release does not state the loan terms, interest rate or maturity.
context: Birch Creek, formed in 2019, says it has financed over 700 MW of projects since then, and the two firms describe a working relationship of about three years. The company says the larger facility will let it build out its current pipeline and pursue new opportunities. Securing panel supply is presented as a central part of its growth plan.

sources.title: Birch Creek Development Secures $250 Million Loan Facility from Fundamental Renewables

title: Enlight agrees to acquire and co-develop 525 MW solar and wind portfolio in Croatia
target: 525 MW portfolio of five solar and wind projects in Croatia
summary: Israeli developer Enlight Renewable Energy has signed an agreement to acquire and jointly develop a 525 MW portfolio of renewable projects in Croatia. The portfolio includes four solar projects and one wind project. The seller and the price were not disclosed.
details: The five projects are at various stages of development, meaning they have not yet been built. Four solar projects add up to 386 MW and one wind project accounts for 139 MW. Enlight expects construction to begin between the end of 2023 and 2025, provided each project successfully completes its development phase. The deal is structured as an acquisition combined with joint development, so Enlight will continue developing the projects alongside a partner that the release does not name.
context: Enlight says the deal broadens its Croatian business beyond its operating Lukovac wind farm into large-scale solar. The company describes the portfolio as one of the largest and most advanced in Croatia, and points to Croatia's plan to raise the renewable share of electricity to over 36% by 2030 and 66% by 2050. The acquisition adds to Enlight's roughly 1.2 GW portfolio across Hungary, Kosovo, Serbia and Croatia, of which 316 MW is operating.

sources.title: Enlight to Acquire 525 MW Portfolio of Solar and Wind Projects in Croatia

title: Nelnet takes controlling stake in Midwest solar EPC firm GRNE Solar

sellers.name: GRNE Solutions, LLC
sellers.role: target and seller of solar assets

summary: Nelnet, a US financial services and technology company, acquired a controlling interest in affiliates of GRNE Solar, a Midwest solar engineering, procurement and construction firm. It also bought a set of solar assets from a GRNE affiliate. The deal closed on July 1, 2022, with no price disclosed.
details: GRNE designs and builds residential, commercial and utility-scale solar systems in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Nebraska and Missouri, with Colorado planned, and its projects usually range from 1 MW to 5 MW. An EPC firm is the contractor that designs a project, buys the equipment and builds it. The solar assets Nelnet bought include some that already produce power and others still under construction, though their size was not given. GRNE's co-founders Jess Baker and Eric Peterman will keep leading the company and hold a minority ownership share. GRNE has more than 80 employees across seven offices.
context: The purchase extends Nelnet's renewable energy arm beyond tax equity investing, where an investor funds solar projects in exchange for their federal tax credits, into building projects itself. Nelnet says its renewable unit has funded or committed to over 1.5 billion dollars of solar construction since 2018 and holds more than 240 million dollars in over 200 solar projects. The company says combining construction, financing and community solar subscription services will create a distinctive offering.

sources.title: Nelnet Acquires Solar Construction Firm GRNE Solutions

title: GEF Capital Partners completes acquisition of renewable heating oil producer Lifecycle Renewables

advisors.name: Boenning & Scattergood
advisors.role: exclusive financial advisor to Lifecycle Renewables and WindSail Capital Group

summary: Sustainability-focused private equity firm GEF Capital Partners has completed its acquisition of Lifecycle Renewables, a Massachusetts company that turns used cooking oil into renewable heating oil. The price was not disclosed.
details: Lifecycle Renewables collects used cooking oil from restaurants and other foodservice businesses and processes it into a heating fuel sold as LR100, which the company says cuts greenhouse gas emissions by up to 80% versus fossil heating oil. Its customers include district energy systems (networks that heat multiple buildings from a central plant), universities and hospitals. The company was founded in 2008, is based in Tewksbury, Massachusetts, and runs processing plants across the Northeastern United States. Boenning & Scattergood acted as exclusive financial adviser to Lifecycle Renewables and to WindSail Capital Group, which had backed the company since 2017. The deal was led by GEF Capital managing partner Daniel Prawda and co-led by vice president Catherine Lien.
context: GEF Capital says the investment is meant to help Lifecycle Renewables raise production and expand beyond the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic into wider North American markets. The buyer presents the company as a low-cost way for institutions to cut heating emissions toward Net Zero goals. The deal reflects investor interest in biofuels made from waste feedstocks.

sources.title: GEF Capital Partners Completes Acquisition of Lifecycle Renewables to Accelerate Growth

title: LyondellBasell signs 216 MW of Texas wind and solar PPAs with ENGIE and Buckeye Partners
target: Limestone wind project and Files solar project
summary: Chemical maker LyondellBasell has signed its first two US power purchase agreements, covering a combined 216 MW of renewable capacity in Texas. The deals are with ENGIE North America for wind power and Buckeye Partners for solar power.
details: A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract to buy electricity from a specific project. The ENGIE deal covers 100 MW from the Limestone wind project in Navarro and Limestone counties, runs for 12 years and is estimated to supply about 377,000 MWh a year, with operations expected to start in late 2022. The Buckeye deal covers 116 MW from the Files solar project in Hill County near Dallas, runs for 10 years and is estimated to supply about 251,000 MWh a year, with operations expected in the second quarter of 2023. Both projects were under construction at the time of the announcement.
context: LyondellBasell aims to source at least half of its electricity from renewables by 2030 and to reach net zero scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2050. The company estimates the two contracts will cut its carbon dioxide emissions by about 225,000 metric tons a year. It says electricity use accounts for roughly 15 percent of its scope 1 and 2 emissions.

sources.title: LyondellBasell Announces Renewable Energy Power Purchase Agreements

title: Ameren Missouri to acquire 200 MW Huck Finn Solar Project from EDF Renewables under build-transfer deal
summary: Ameren Missouri, a subsidiary of Ameren Corporation, plans to acquire the 200 MW Huck Finn Solar Project in central Missouri from EDF Renewables. The deal uses a build-transfer agreement and financial terms were not disclosed.
details: The solar plant is planned for the border of Audrain and Ralls counties in Missouri. Under a build-transfer agreement, EDF Renewables develops and builds the project and then hands ownership to Ameren Missouri once it is complete. The company expects the plant to supply power equal to the needs of about 40,000 homes and to create more than 250 construction jobs. Subject to timely regulatory approvals, it could start producing power as early as 2024.
context: Ameren Missouri says the project will be its largest solar facility and more than 25 times larger in output than the biggest existing solar site in Missouri. It forms part of the utility's plan to add 2,800 MW of renewable generation by 2030 and follows Ameren bringing forward its companywide net-zero carbon goal to 2045. It is the ninth solar facility the company has announced or put in service since 2019, with the nine together exceeding 360 MW.

sources.title: Ameren Missouri plans to acquire its largest-ever solar facility to power thousands of homes

title: SinglePoint subsidiary Boston Solar acquires solar finance firm Ecodaptive
summary: The Boston Solar Company, a subsidiary of SinglePoint Inc., has acquired Ecodaptive Inc., a Delaware company that structures financing for clean energy projects. Ecodaptive is developing the SunRAYS rooftop solar program in Massachusetts. No purchase price was disclosed.
details: SunRAYS places solar panels on small commercial, multi-family and single-family rooftops under a roof lease, meaning building owners rent out their roof space and receive an upfront payment plus ongoing lease payments while the panels feed power directly into the local grid. According to the release, a framework agreement of more than 100 million US dollars is in place with a project buyer to acquire SunRAYS projects installed in Massachusetts, which SinglePoint describes as an asset finance facility to scale a pilot program. Ecodaptive will support Boston Solar's commercial division. Boston Solar co-founder Daniel Mello Guimaraes, now SinglePoint's executive vice president of EPC services, will lead further small acquisitions of solar engineering, procurement and construction businesses.
context: SinglePoint says the deal adds vertical integration, meaning it brings solar financing in-house alongside installation work. The company's CEO claims it could be a significant competitive advantage. The release argues that rooftop distributed solar avoids the long grid connection delays faced by large utility-scale projects.

sources.title: SinglePoint Inc. Subsidiary, The Boston Solar Company, Acquires Ecodaptive Inc., a Clean Energy Investment Facilitator

title: Bank of America affiliate provides $92 million tax equity for Matrix Renewables' Gaskell West 2 and 3 solar-plus-storage projects
target: Gaskell West 2 and Gaskell West 3 projects

advisors.name: CohnReznick Capital
advisors.role: exclusive financial advisor to Matrix Renewables

summary: Matrix Renewables has signed a $92 million tax equity financing with an affiliate of Bank of America for its Gaskell West 2 and 3 projects in Kern County, California. The projects combine 143 MWdc of solar with an 80 MWh battery system.
details: Tax equity is a form of investment where a party with large tax bills, here a Bank of America affiliate, funds part of a project in return for the federal tax credits and other tax benefits it generates. The two projects are under construction and are expected to begin commercial operation in late 2022. Their output is sold under five long-term power purchase agreements, which are fixed contracts to sell electricity, with California utilities and cities. CohnReznick Capital acted as exclusive financial adviser to Matrix and Norton Rose Fulbright also advised the company.
context: This is the first US tax equity deal for Matrix Renewables, which is backed by TPG and its impact investing platform TPG Rise. The company describes Gaskell as its flagship solar project and says it aims to become a leading renewable platform across North America, Europe and Latin America. It reports a portfolio of 2.3 GW of operating, under-construction or near ready-to-build projects plus a 3 GW pipeline.

sources.title: MATRIX RENEWABLES SIGNS TAX EQUITY FINANCING FOR GASKELL WEST PROJECT

title: NYSERDA awards CS Energy three New York solar projects totaling 270 MW AC

buyers.name: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA)
buyers.role: procuring agency and offtaker under the Renewable Energy Standard

target: Stern Solar, York Run Solar and Yellow Barn Solar projects
summary: CS Energy was selected by NYSERDA for three utility-scale solar projects in upstate New York in the agency's fifth annual Renewable Energy Standard solicitation. The projects total 270 MW AC, or 365 MW DC, and are planned to start construction in 2025.
details: The awards cover Stern Solar (19.99 MW AC) in Rensselaer County, York Run Solar (90 MW AC) in Chautauqua County and Yellow Barn Solar (160 MW AC) in Tompkins County. AC capacity is what the plant delivers to the grid, while the larger DC figure is the combined rating of the panels. All three will use bifacial panels, which capture light on both sides, mounted on single-axis trackers that follow the sun. Construction is expected to begin in 2025 and finish in 2026, and the company estimates output of over 500,000 MWh per year. The release does not state contract terms, pricing or financing.
context: The three projects were among 22 chosen from more than 50 bidding facilities in a competitive state procurement. CS Energy, an engineering, procurement and construction firm owned by American Securities, presents the awards as strengthening its position in the New York solar market. The largest project sits under 10 miles from the Cayuga coal plant, retired in 2019, and NYSERDA says the full award group brings its large-scale renewables program to 8,000 MW of solar.

sources.title: CS Energy Secures Large-Scale Solar Portfolio in New York

title: Volvo Energy takes 10% stake in UK second-life battery storage firm Connected Energy
summary: Volvo Energy, a business area of Sweden's Volvo Group, is investing about SEK 50 million for a 10 percent stake in Connected Energy, a UK company that builds energy storage systems from used electric vehicle batteries. Volvo Energy is one of five new investors joining the funding round.
details: Connected Energy reuses batteries that have finished their life in vehicles, known as second-life batteries, in stationary commercial storage systems. It is based in Newcastle upon Tyne, has a technical centre in Norfolk and runs sixteen operational systems in the UK, Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands, the largest at Cranfield University in Bedfordshire. The other new investors are Caterpillar Venture Capital, the Hinduja Group, Mercuria and OurCrowd. Existing backers Engie New Ventures, Macquarie and the Low Carbon Innovation Fund remain shareholders. The release does not state the total size of the round.
context: Volvo says the investment is meant to help scale up second-life battery storage and give it an outlet for the growing number of batteries it expects to come back from Volvo Group vehicles. Connected Energy claims to be one of only a few companies worldwide to have shown that used vehicle batteries can work in commercial storage systems. The deal reflects automakers seeking circular uses for batteries before recycling.

sources.title: Volvo Energy invests in Connected Energy for second life battery business

title: Recurrent Energy acquires two 200 MWh Texas storage projects from Black Mountain Energy Storage
target: Two standalone energy storage projects in ERCOT South Load Zone
summary: Recurrent Energy, the US development arm of Canadian Solar, has bought two standalone battery storage projects in development from Black Mountain Energy Storage. The projects sit in the South Load Zone of the Texas ERCOT grid and together are expected to store up to 400 MWh. No price was disclosed.
details: Each project is expected to hold up to 200 MWh of energy and both are still in development. They are expected to reach notice to proceed, the point when full construction is authorized, in 2023 and to start operating in the second quarter of 2024. The batteries will run as merchant projects, meaning they will sell power and services at market prices rather than under a long-term fixed contract. Recurrent will finish permitting and design, buy equipment, raise project financing and build the plants. The deal was arranged through the LevelTen Asset Marketplace, an online platform for buying and selling clean energy projects.
context: Canadian Solar describes ERCOT as one of the fastest growing storage markets, driven by demand for flexible capacity, and the deal adds to Recurrent's 15.5 GWh early to mid-stage storage pipeline. The seller says the project locations should see strong price swings that batteries can profit from, and that it has about 3 GW more of ERCOT storage projects in development. The release notes the South Zone is attractive for storage due to plentiful coastal wind and solar.

sources.title: Recurrent Energy Expands ERCOT Storage Pipeline with Acquisition of 400 MWh of Standalone Storage Projects Under Development

title: Babcock Power Renewables agrees to buy assets of wind service firm Renewable Concepts and R. Tinsley Projects
target: Substantially all assets of Renewable Concepts Inc. and R. Tinsley Projects Inc.
summary: A subsidiary of Babcock Power Renewables, part of Babcock Power Inc., has signed a definitive agreement to buy substantially all the assets of Renewable Concepts Inc. and its affiliate R. Tinsley Projects Inc. Renewable Concepts is a US company that maintains and repairs wind turbines. No price was disclosed.
details: Renewable Concepts was founded in 2008 by Rob Tinsley and offers maintenance, engineering, construction and repair services for wind turbines. The deal is an asset purchase, meaning the buyer takes over the business's assets rather than buying the company's shares. The release does not give a purchase price, closing date or advisers.
context: Babcock Power, which mainly supplies equipment and services to the power generation industry, says the purchase will widen its range of clean energy products and services. The company presents the deal as a way to serve what it describes as growing demand for clean energy by adding wind turbine service expertise.

sources.title: Babcock Power Renewables LLC, a Babcock Power Inc. company, acquires substantially all of the assets of Renewable Concepts Inc. and R. Tinsley Projects Inc.

title: Atlas Renewable Energy acquires 378 MW Juramento wind project in Brazil from Voltalia
summary: Atlas Renewable Energy has bought the development rights to the Juramento wind project in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais from French power producer Voltalia. The project is planned at 378 MW across 63 turbines. It is Atlas's first wind project in Brazil.
details: Juramento is a development-stage project, meaning it has not yet been built, and is expected to produce about 1,650 GWh of electricity per year. Unlike Atlas's Alpaca wind portfolio in Chile, it does not yet have a power purchase agreement, which is a long-term contract to sell its electricity to a buyer. Atlas says it is offering the output to large energy consumers in Brazil. The deal structure is to be reviewed and finalised by Brazil's competition authority CADE in the coming days. No price was disclosed.
context: The acquisition follows Atlas's recent announcement of a power purchase agreement with Enel Energía Chile for its 417 MW Alpaca wind portfolio, making Juramento its second wind project. The company says the deal widens its range of clean energy offerings for corporate customers across its markets. Atlas claims the project will avoid roughly 123,750 tonnes of CO2 emissions per year.
